qa_results.bill_summary: Requires architectural paint producers or a representative organization to submit a Paint Stewardship Program plan by July 1, 2025. Requires the Department of the Environment to review and approve submitted plans and annual reports. Establishes a uniform paint stewardship assessment added to the purchase price of all architectural paint sold in Maryland. Prohibits producers and retailers from selling architectural paint unless participating in an approved program, beginning January 1, 2026, or later. Requires program implementation within six months after plan approval to provide convenient statewide postconsumer paint collection. Directs the Department to complete a program cost-benefit review and submit a report by December 1, 2028.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment; Office of Recycling
qa_results.stakeholders: producers, distributors, and retailers of architectural paint; consumers of architectural paint; local governments
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund expenditures from the State Recycling Trust Fund increase by $70,212 in FY 2026 and $64,307 in FY 2027 for contractual personnel, fully offset by plan review and annual report review fee revenues. State and local government expenditures increase minimally beginning in FY 2026 from paint stewardship assessments on paint purchases. Local waste management costs potentially decrease beginning in FY 2026 due to diverted paint collection.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDE is the primary regulatory and implementing agency for the Paint Stewardship Program, responsible for reviewing and approving program plans, assessing compliance, collecting plan and report review fees into the State Recycling Trust Fund, and submitting an evaluation report.

The Comptroller is statutorily designated to account for the State Recycling Trust Fund, which will receive new revenues from paint stewardship plan review fees, annual report review fees, and penalties.
The State Treasurer holds and invests the State Recycling Trust Fund, which receives additional revenues and handles disbursements associated with the Paint Stewardship Program.
MES coordinates with MDE's Office of Recycling on solid waste and recycling studies and reports under the amended sections of the Environment Article and was consulted as an information source.
The Governor's Office receives required reporting, including the comprehensive cost-benefit evaluation of the Maryland Paint Stewardship Program due by December 1, 2028.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes Baltimore City or counties to establish a subclass of real property for vacant and abandoned property. Covers vacant lots or improved property cited as vacant and unfit for habitation or other authorized use. Authorizes local governing bodies to set a special property tax rate for that subclass. Requires enacting jurisdictions to report annually by December 1 on rates, revenues, and property reuse. Directs reports to the Department of Housing and Community Development and the General Assembly. Takes effect June 1, 2024, applicable to taxable years beginning after June 30, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Mayor and City Council of Baltimore City; county governing bodies; Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
qa_results.stakeholders: owners of vacant lots or improved property cited as vacant and unfit for habitation or other authorized use; Baltimore City; Maryland county governments
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Indeterminate effect on Baltimore City and county property tax revenues depending on the special property tax rates set locally. State finances are not affected, and local reporting mandates can be absorbed with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates that any county or Baltimore City that enacts a special property tax rate for vacant and abandoned property must report annually by December 1 to the Department of Housing and Community Development on the rate, property counts, revenue changes and uses, and the viability of adaptive reuse for those properties.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits institutions of higher education in the State that receive State funds from considering legacy preferences or donor preferences in admissions. Defines donor preference as an admissions preference based on a familial relationship to an institutional donor. Defines legacy preference as an admissions preference based on a familial relationship to an institutional alumnus. Authorizes covered institutions to ask applicants about familial ties to alumni solely to collect data. Takes effect July 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Institutions of higher education in Maryland receiving State funds
qa_results.stakeholders: Applicants to Maryland colleges and universities, alumni, institutional donors, and institutions of higher education that receive State funds
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material fiscal impact on State public four-year institutions of higher education, which can implement the prohibition with existing resources. Local community colleges experience no fiscal impact because they do not consider legacy status or donor preferences for admission.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly applies to all institutions of higher education in Maryland receiving State funds, requiring the University System of Maryland's constituent institutions to eliminate legacy and donor preferences from their admissions standards.
As an independent public state university receiving State funds, Morgan State University must comply with the prohibition against considering legacy and donor preferences in admissions.
As an independent public four-year institution receiving State funds, St. Mary's College of Maryland is directly subject to the bill's restrictions on undergraduate admissions policies.
The Maryland Higher Education Commission is the state's regulatory and coordinating body overseeing postsecondary education standards and policies across public and private colleges in Maryland.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits a person from committing the common law crime of indecent exposure. Prohibits committing indecent exposure with prurient intent when knowing or reasonably should know a minor is present. Applies that prohibition if the minor is at least two years old and over four years younger. Subjects indecent exposure to misdemeanor penalties of up to three years imprisonment, a $1,000 fine, or both. Subjects violations involving minors to misdemeanor penalties of up to five years imprisonment, a $10,000 fine, or both.
qa_results.responsible_party: Judiciary; Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
qa_results.stakeholders: individuals charged with or convicted of indecent exposure; minors; state and local correctional facilities
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal increase in State general fund revenues and expenditures; minimal increase in local revenues and expenditures due to the new monetary and incarceration penalties.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill codifies common law indecent exposure and creates an enhanced misdemeanor offense, impacting caseloads, trial proceedings, and fine collections handled across the District Court and circuit courts.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes an offense punishable by up to five years of imprisonment and supervises individuals on probation or parole, creating potential fiscal and operational impacts on state correctional facilities.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Public Defender provides legal defense services to indigent defendants who face prosecution and potential incarceration under the new criminal offense provisions.

As the primary state law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police is responsible for enforcing state criminal statutes and investigating violations of indecent exposure laws within state jurisdiction.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Housing Innovation Pilot Program and the Housing Innovation Fund in the Department of Housing and Community Development. Authorizes the department to provide low- or no-interest loans to local housing authorities and county governments for mixed-income, cross-subsidized housing. Requires local housing authorities to provide a dollar-for-dollar match before drawing down program funds. Directs the department to select three projects in different jurisdictions, prioritizing projects that maintain 99-year affordability and public ownership. Authorizes the Governor to include a $5,000,000 appropriation to the fund for each of fiscal years 2026 through 2029.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development
qa_results.stakeholders: local housing authorities, county governments, private housing developers, and low- and moderate-income households
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures increase by $10.17 million in FY 2025, reflecting $10.0 million in general obligation bond expenditures restricted in the capital budget to capitalize the fund and $170,535 in general fund administrative expenses. Special fund revenues and loan expenditures increase by $10.0 million in FY 2025 and an assumed $5.0 million annually from FY 2026 through FY 2029 from reallocated rental housing funds. Local revenues and expenditures increase significantly for county governments and housing authorities that receive loan funds, provide matching funds, and operate housing projects.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly establishes the Housing Innovation Pilot Program and the Housing Innovation Fund within DHCD. The department is tasked with administering the fund, creating program regulations and application processes, evaluating projects, coordinating with local housing authorities, and awarding low- or no-interest loans.
The bill explicitly mandates that the State Treasurer hold the Housing Innovation Fund separately and invest the moneys of the fund in the same manner as other state money.
The bill specifically designates that the Comptroller of Maryland must account for the newly established Housing Innovation Fund.
The bill authorizes the Governor to include an annual appropriation of up to $5,000,000 in the operating or capital budget bill for the Housing Innovation Fund for fiscal years 2026 through 2029.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the establishment of a condominium regime on residential leasehold property owned by an affordable housing land trust. Adds affordable housing land trusts to the entities permitted to hold the reversionary fee simple estate for residential condominiums. Maintains existing exceptions for the State, charter home rule counties, municipal corporations, and the Washington Metropolitan Area Transit Authority. Takes effect October 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Clerks of the Circuit Court
qa_results.stakeholders: affordable housing land trusts, low- and moderate-income homebuyers, and residential condominium developers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DHCD is the primary state agency responsible for affordable housing and homeownership initiatives; the bill expands options for creating affordable homeownership opportunities through affordable housing land trusts establishing condominium regimes.
The Secretary of State oversees the registration and regulation of residential condominium regimes in Maryland under the Maryland Condominium Act.
The circuit court clerks, supported by the Administrative Office of the Courts, maintain the local land records where condominium declarations, bylaws, and plats must be recorded.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires local property tax collectors to include an insert promoting the Homeowner Protection Program with each property tax bill. Requires the State Tax Sale Ombudsman to design the insert and provide it to each collector. Directs the insert to describe program assistance for low-income, elderly, and disabled homeowners facing tax sale foreclosure. Requires the State Department of Assessments and Taxation to maintain a website for voluntary donations to the program. Credits all donations collected through the website to the Homeowner Protection Fund. Takes effect July 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation; State Tax Sale Ombudsman
qa_results.stakeholders: Low-income, elderly, and disabled homeowners facing tax sale foreclosure; Maryland property taxpayers; local property tax collectors
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Indeterminate increase in special fund revenues to the Homeowner Protection Fund beginning in FY 2025 from voluntary online donations. Local government expenditures increase beginning in FY 2025 to print and mail property tax bill inserts, with reported local estimates ranging from $3,200 to $70,000 annually.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill facilitates funding and public awareness for the Homeowner Protection Program, which assists vulnerable homeowners in avoiding tax sale foreclosure and remaining in their homes. This aligns closely with DHCD's mission of supporting homeownership and housing stability, and DHCD was consulted during the legislative review.

The bill relates to tax sale processes and the Homeowner Protection Program, which interacts with the judicial tax sale foreclosure and redemption proceedings administered through the state court system. AOC was consulted as an information source on the legislation.

The Maryland Tax Court adjudicates disputes regarding property tax assessments and taxing authorities, and was consulted as an information source regarding the bill's property tax and tax sale provisions.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes a duty for charter counties to affirmatively further fair housing through housing and urban development programs. Requires housing elements of comprehensive plans enacted or amended on or after January 1, 2025, to include a fair housing assessment. Requires charter counties amending plans on or after January 1, 2024, to incorporate prior federal fair housing assessments by reference. Directs the Maryland Department of Planning and the Department of Housing and Community Development to provide technical assistance upon request. Specifies that the requirement neither mandates nor prohibits any specific action by a county to affirmatively further fair housing.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Planning; Department of Housing and Community Development
qa_results.stakeholders: charter counties, Baltimore City, certain code counties exercising planning powers, and county residents seeking fair housing opportunities
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State requirements can be handled within existing budgeted resources with no impact on state revenues. The bill has no direct material fiscal impact on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill was requested by the Maryland Department of Planning and explicitly tasks the department, upon request of a county and in consultation with DHCD, with providing technical assistance to charter counties for the purpose of developing the housing element of their comprehensive plans to affirmatively further fair housing.

The bill requires the Maryland Department of Planning to consult with the Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) when providing technical assistance to counties developing the fair housing elements of their comprehensive plans.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the common name of the northern snakehead as the Chesapeake Channa in State law. Renames the commercial northern snakehead license to include Chesapeake Channa. Permits archery fishing for Chesapeake Channa in Anne Arundel County waters subject to departmental regulations. Requires the Department of Natural Resources to adopt implementing regulations on or before January 1, 2025. Mandates that the Department refer to the fish as Chesapeake Channa across all applicable publications.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
qa_results.stakeholders: Commercial fishers, seafood dealers, and recreational anglers targeting northern snakeheads
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Department of Natural Resources can implement the bill using existing resources. There is no local government fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the Natural Resources Article and requires the Department of Natural Resources to adopt regulations establishing the common name of northern snakehead as 'Chesapeake Channa', update commercial licensing, and use the new name in all department publications.

The Department of Agriculture oversees the promotion and marketing of Maryland agricultural and seafood products, and was consulted on the bill regarding the marketability and commercial impact of renaming the species.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the State Highway Administration to expand its pollinator habitat plan with specific policies and procedures. Mandates policies to encourage pollinator-friendly native plants and develop roadside habitats under relevant safety standards. Requires the Administration to establish public education and communication procedures regarding roadside pollinator habitats. Directs the Administration to evaluate and apply for beneficial federal funding for pollinator habitats and invasive species control. Requires annual website updates of the plan beginning October 1, 2024, listing habitat locations and sizes.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Highway Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland motorists, bicyclists, pedestrians, community associations, and native plant and pollinator conservation groups
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Transportation Trust Fund expenditures increase minimally, likely by less than $50,000 annually (preliminarily estimated at $35,000 in fiscal 2025 for informational signage and outreach events). Federal fund revenues may increase if the State Highway Administration applies for and receives federal pollinator habitat grants.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly applies to the State Highway Administration (SHA), requiring it to expand its pollinator habitat plan to include specific policies on native plants, habitat maintenance along highways, and public education. SHA must also track and apply for relevant federal funding and update its published plan annually.
SHA is a modal administration within MDOT, and implementation costs associated with public signage, events, and roadside pollinator habitat management impact the Transportation Trust Fund.

The bill amends the Agriculture Article concerning pollinator habitat plans, which are established in consultation with the Maryland Department of Agriculture and must align with MDA's managed pollinator protection plan and noxious weed control laws.
DNR is a co-entity named in Section 2-1801 that established and maintains a pollinator habitat plan and may consult with SHA on best management practices and native plant habitat creation.
MES is also named in Section 2-1801 as one of the state entities that established and maintains a pollinator habitat plan under the statute being amended.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals an exemption that permitted qualified health plans on the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange to omit pediatric dental benefits. Requires all qualified health plans offered through the Exchange to provide essential pediatric dental benefits. Repeals Exchange authority to mandate that children enrolling in a qualified health plan obtain separate essential pediatric dental coverage. Excludes Affordable Care Act plans sold outside the Exchange from these requirements. Applies to all health benefit plans issued, delivered, or renewed on or after January 1, 2025.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Health Benefit Exchange; Maryland Insurance Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Health insurance carriers offering plans through the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange, and consumers and children enrolled in exchange coverage
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not substantively change State activities or operations and has no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends Title 31 of the Insurance Article governing the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange (MHBE), mandating that all qualified health plans (QHPs) certified and sold through the Exchange include pediatric dental benefits and repealing related discretionary authority of MHBE.

This was introduced as a departmental bill requested by the Maryland Insurance Administration (MIA), which regulates health insurance carriers, approves premium rates and plan forms, and oversees compliance with state insurance benefit mandates.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the financial assistance eligible fund managers may provide from the Small, Minority, and Women-Owned Businesses Account. Authorizes eligible fund managers to provide financial assistance in the form of loans or grants. Caps standard grants at $10,000 and requires them to accompany a loan of any amount. Preserves authority to provide emergency grants up to $50,000 in declared disaster or emergency areas. Applies the revised assistance structure to clean energy businesses supported by the Strategic Energy Investment Fund.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Commerce
qa_results.stakeholders: small, minority, women-owned, and veteran-owned businesses; eligible fund managers, including local economic development corporations
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No direct effect on State revenues into or expenditures from the Small, Minority, and Women-Owned Businesses Account, and the Department of Commerce can administer changes with existing budgeted resources. Local economic development entities serving as eligible fund managers may experience shifts in revenues and expenditures as grant pairings reduce future loan repayments.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly governs the Small, Minority, and Women-Owned Businesses Account (SMWOBA), which is administered under the authority of the Department of Commerce. Commerce requested this departmental legislation to allow eligible fund managers to award grants of up to $10,000 in conjunction with loans.

SMWOBA receives funding from the Strategic Energy Investment Fund (SEIF), which is managed by MEA, to provide financing to clean energy businesses. The bill alters the forms of financial assistance that fund managers can deploy using SEIF funds.

qa_results.bill_summary: Aligns State health insurance laws with federal requirements under the Affordable Care Act and the No Surprises Act. Updates definitions of emergency medical conditions and emergency services to include behavioral health and crisis facilities. Prohibits carriers from requiring prior authorization or restricting emergency condition determinations solely by diagnosis codes. Applies provider designation and emergency service coverage protections to all grandfathered health benefit plans. Adds plan cost-sharing errors to triggering events for small employer special enrollment periods. Authorizes the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange to establish expanded annual open enrollment dates if federally permitted.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration; Maryland Health Benefit Exchange
qa_results.stakeholders: health insurance carriers, health maintenance organizations, health care providers, and insured individuals and small business employees in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not materially affected by changes in State agency activities, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This is a departmental bill requested by the Maryland Insurance Administration to conform State insurance law with federal regulations, requiring the Insurance Commissioner to adopt conforming regulations regarding grandfathered plans, essential health benefits, medical loss ratios, and coverage of emergency services.

The bill directly amends provisions governing the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange and SHOP Exchange, altering the criteria for special enrollment periods due to material errors and authorizing the Exchange to establish an expanded open enrollment period and alternate coverage effective dates.

The bill amends the Health - General Article to revise statutory definitions of emergency medical conditions and emergency services applicable to health maintenance organizations regulated under State health laws.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the person responsible for issuing building permits to include the estimated cost of construction when submitting permit copies. Mandates submitting the permit and cost estimate immediately to the supervisor of assessments of the relevant county. Helps state assessors determine the valuation of real property improvements more accurately. Takes effect July 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation
qa_results.stakeholders: Local government building permit offices, county supervisors of assessments, and real property owners
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state fiscal impact. Local fiscal impact is minimal, as many local jurisdictions already collect and report estimated construction costs as part of the permitting process.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires local permit offices to provide estimated construction costs to the county supervisor of assessments to facilitate more accurate real property valuations and improvement assessments. The Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board hears appeals regarding real property valuations following initial determinations by these supervisors of assessments.
The Maryland Tax Court adjudicates appeals concerning assessments of real property resulting from initial decisions by local supervisors of assessments and the Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits a public adjuster from soliciting clients within 24 hours after covered loss or between 8:00 p.m. and 8:00 a.m. Alters the contract rescission period to 10 business days for insureds under 65 and seven for older insureds. Requires public adjuster contracts to include statements detailing these rescission rights and solicitation restrictions. Requires public adjusters to notify the Insurance Commissioner within one business day when contracting within 72 hours of loss. Expands fraudulent insurance acts by home repair contractors paying deductibles to include any damage, not only weather damage. Takes effect October 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration; Maryland Insurance Commissioner
qa_results.stakeholders: public adjusters, insured property owners, home repair and remodeling contractors, and property and casualty insurers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal state impact; the Maryland Insurance Administration can implement the bill using existing budgeted resources. There is no effect on local revenues or expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 36 is a departmental bill requested by the Maryland Insurance Administration (MIA). It amends the Insurance Article regarding public adjuster solicitation restrictions, contract rescission terms, required notices to the Insurance Commissioner, and definitions of fraudulent insurance acts.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore City from requiring new motor vehicle off-street parking for certain developments. Applies to developments that include residential use located near specified mass transit stations. Restricts mandates within a 0.25-mile radius of present or planned MARC, Baltimore MTA Light Rail, Red Line, or Metro stations. Defines "Red Line" as a rail transit facility connecting Security Boulevard and Johns Hopkins Bayview Medical Center. Takes effect October 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Mayor and City Council of Baltimore City
qa_results.stakeholders: Residential developers, property owners, and businesses developing residential projects near transit stations in Baltimore City
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State or Baltimore City local government finances, though it may reduce development costs for qualifying projects.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill prohibits mandatory off-street parking requirements near transit stations operated or planned by MTA, including MARC, Baltimore Light Rail, Baltimore Metro, and the Red Line, directly impacting transit-oriented development around MTA facilities.

MDOT is the parent department of the Maryland Transit Administration and oversees statewide transportation infrastructure, transit planning, and station-area coordination. MDOT was also an information source for the bill's fiscal note.

MDP provides technical assistance, land use policy guidance, and growth management oversight to local jurisdictions. The bill amends the Land Use Article regarding local zoning and parking requirements around mass transit, and MDP served as an information source for the fiscal note.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Maryland Department of Health to reimburse residential service agencies for personal assistance services only if provided by employees. Excludes personal assistance services delivered by individuals classified as independent contractors from state reimbursement. Conditions Medicaid reimbursements on agencies employing rather than independently contracting with personal care aides. Protects homecare workers by linking agency reimbursement to employee classification and statutory protections. Establishes an effective date of January 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: residential service agencies; personal care aides and homecare workers; Medicaid recipients receiving personal assistance services
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No impact on Medicaid revenues or expenditures if residential service agencies transition personal care aides to employee status prior to the effective date. Indeterminate operational impact and administrative costs for the Maryland Department of Health if noncompliant agencies must be disenrolled as Medicaid providers. No local fiscal effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly governs the Maryland Department of Health (MDH) and its Medicaid program, prohibiting the department from reimbursing residential service agencies (RSAs) for personal assistance services unless the care is provided by an individual classified as an employee.

The bill addresses worker misclassification in the homecare sector by requiring personal care aides to be classified as employees rather than independent contractors, which intersects with the Department of Labor's jurisdiction over state labor laws and employment standards.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals exceptions allowing tobacco product and electronic smoking device sales to active-duty military members under age 21. Updates mandatory retail signage to reflect the universal minimum sales age of 21. Authorizes the Maryland Department of Health to reallocate projected unspent county cancer grant funding between counties during the fiscal year. Transfers payment responsibility for emergency medical treatment of abused or neglected children to the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy. Repeals the requirement for the Secretary of Health to annually convene an expert panel on child abuse and neglect. Requires the State Council on Child Abuse and Neglect to coordinate with the Child Abuse Medical Providers Initiative.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy; State Council on Child Abuse and Neglect
qa_results.stakeholders: Retailers and distributors of tobacco products and electronic smoking devices; active-duty military members ages 18 to 20; county health departments; abused and neglected children and their parents or guardians
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State operations and finances are not materially affected. Local grant revenues and expenditures are affected to the extent that the Maryland Department of Health reallocates projected unspent cancer grant funding among counties during the fiscal year, though specific amounts cannot be estimated.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDH is the primary sponsor and subject of this departmental legislation. The bill authorizes MDH to reallocate unspent local cancer grant funds, removes MDH's statutory duty to pay emergency medical costs for child abuse/neglect examinations, repeals the Secretary's requirement to convene an annual expert panel on child abuse and neglect, and streamlines tobacco counter-marketing reporting requirements.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill statutorily transfers responsibility to GOCPP as the payor of last resort for emergency medical treatment charges incurred on behalf of an abused or neglected child, and authorizes the Executive Director of GOCPP to adopt implementing regulations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters statutory duties and reporting requirements of the State Council on Child Abuse and Neglect (SCCAN), requiring it to coordinate with the Maryland CHAMP Initiative and incorporate child abuse and neglect diagnosis and treatment data into its annual report while repealing an existing expert panel.

The bill specifies that MDH must collaborate and consult with the Office of the Comptroller in developing ongoing strategies for enforcing prohibitions on tobacco product sales to individuals under 21, and the agency oversees tobacco regulation and compliance.

DHS oversees the State's child protective services and local departments of social services, which are referenced in the amended Family Law provisions regarding determining medical assistance eligibility for abused and neglected children receiving emergency treatment.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes governing bodies of counties and municipalities to designate local highways on which a person may operate an unregistered golf cart. Limits operation to highways with posted speed limits of 30 miles per hour, or 35 miles per hour in Golden Beach Patuxent Knolls. Allows daytime operation with required lighting devices, or anytime operation with approved headlights, taillights, and brake lights. Restricts the number of occupants to the number of seats installed in the golf cart. Requires drivers to hold a valid driver's license and keep the cart as far right as feasible. Repeals separate local statutory authorizations previously enacted for specific jurisdictions across the State.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration; governing bodies of counties and municipalities
qa_results.stakeholders: Golf cart operators, licensed drivers, and county and municipal governments in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Motor Vehicle Administration (referenced in the Maryland Vehicle Law as 'the Administration') administers motor vehicle registration and driver licensing. The bill amends vehicle registration exemptions and tasks the Administration with approving required lighting devices on golf carts operated on designated public roadways.

The Department of Transportation oversees the state's transportation framework and is the parent department of the Motor Vehicle Administration, which is tasked with vehicle registration exemptions and equipment approvals under the bill.

The Maryland State Police enforces the Maryland Vehicle Law statewide, including rules regarding driver's license possession, equipment compliance, and traffic safety rules for vehicles operated on public highways.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the sale, barter, or exchange of legally acquired mounted specimens of game birds or game mammals from a decedent's estate. Excludes migratory game birds from this authorization. Applies only when the original owner is deceased. Requires the specimen to be personal property of an estate being liquidated or distributed.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
qa_results.stakeholders: Personal representatives and heirs of decedents' estates, auctioneers, estate liquidators, and purchasers of mounted game specimens
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State finances and has no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 45 was introduced as a Departmental bill by the Department of Natural Resources (DNR). It amends Title 10 of the Natural Resources Article, which DNR is responsible for implementing and enforcing regarding game birds, mammals, and wildlife conservation.

The Register of Wills is responsible for overseeing the administrative probate and timely distribution or liquidation of decedents' estates and personal property, which this bill directly affects by authorizing the sale, barter, or exchange of mounted specimens held in an estate.
The Administrative Office of the Courts supports Maryland's judicial branch, which includes the Orphans' Courts that oversee decedent estate disputes and probate administration.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the authorized uses of the Maryland Pediatric Cancer Fund to support only pediatric cancer research and administrative expenses. Repeals prior authorization allowing fund expenditures for pediatric cancer prevention and treatment grants. Establishes the Pediatric Cancer Research Commission to oversee competitive research grants to public and private entities. Limits the combined annual distribution for fund administration and promotional accounts to 5% of the fund. Requires the commission to develop review criteria, establish award standards, and evaluate grant recipient progress.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Pediatric Cancer Research Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: pediatric cancer researchers, eligible physicians, hospitals, laboratories, educational institutions, childhood cancer organizations, and pediatric cancer patients and caregivers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures increase by $52,900 in FY 2025, increasing to $69,000 by FY 2029 for a part-time physician program manager to support the commission. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health is the primary implementing agency. The Secretary of Health administers the Maryland Pediatric Cancer Fund, serves on the Pediatric Cancer Research Commission, provides administrative and staffing support, adopts implementing regulations, and submits required annual reports.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a new entity, the Pediatric Cancer Research Commission, charged with developing criteria, reviewing applications, and overseeing the award of competitive pediatric cancer research grants.
The Governor is responsible for appointing members to the newly established Pediatric Cancer Research Commission and possesses statutory authority to fill vacancies and remove members for cause.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and managing the appointment process for the multiple members of the newly formed Pediatric Cancer Research Commission.

The bill statutorily requires each member of the Pediatric Cancer Research Commission to disclose to the State Ethics Commission whether they are employed by or hold a financial interest in any entity that may apply for state-funded pediatric cancer research grants.

The bill mandates that multiple scientists and physicians from the University of Maryland serve on the Commission and allows university faculty and research institutions to apply for research grant funding from the Fund.

qa_results.bill_summary: Entitles State employees to paid parental bereavement leave following the death of a child or infant or a stillbirth. Applies to all employees across the Executive, Judicial, and Legislative branches and public institutions of higher education. Authorizes up to 10 days of paid leave within 60 days after the death of a child. Authorizes up to 60 days of paid leave within 60 days after a stillbirth or an infant's death. Prohibits appointing authorities from requiring eligible employees to use other available paid leave. Requires the Secretary of Budget and Management to adopt implementing regulations.
qa_results.responsible_party: Secretary of Budget and Management
qa_results.stakeholders: State employees in the Executive, Legislative, and Judicial branches, temporary State employees, and employees of public institutions of higher education who experience a stillbirth or the death of a child
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State operations and finances are not expected to be materially affected, although agency expenditures may increase minimally in limited instances to provide overtime coverage for employees on leave. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DBM serves as the central personnel agency for the State Personnel Management System, and the bill explicitly mandates that the Secretary of Budget and Management adopt regulations governing parental bereavement leave.
The bill explicitly applies to all employees in the Judicial Branch of state government and units with independent personnel systems, which the Administrative Office of the Courts administers.

The bill specifically applies to all employees of public institutions of higher education, requiring USM to implement parental bereavement leave across its institutions and independent personnel systems.
MDOT operates an independent personnel system covering transportation employees across its modal administrations and must implement and track the new paid leave provisions.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the State Tax Sale Ombudsman to contract with a vendor to operate an installment payment program for taxes. Authorizes Baltimore City, counties, and municipal corporations to establish installment payment programs for residential property taxes in arrears. Exempts residential property transfers to an heir or legatee from tax prepayment requirements if entered into a payment plan. Exempts land transfers from tax prepayment requirements when a grantee assumes an existing tax payment plan. Prohibits tax collectors from taking collection actions against participants compliant with an installment payment plan.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Tax Sale Ombudsman; State Department of Assessments and Taxation
qa_results.stakeholders: Heirs and legatees inheriting residential real property, homeowners with delinquent or current property taxes, property grantees assuming tax payment plans, and local tax collectors
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by at least $67,271 in FY 2025, rising to at least $89,900 by FY 2029 for program oversight personnel. State and local property tax revenues are not materially affected in total, though collection timing may shift. Local government expenditures and penalty or interest revenues may be affected if local installment payment programs are established.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill impacts the Clerks of the Circuit Court (supported by the Administrative Office of the Courts), who record property deeds and land records. Under the bill, clerks must record instruments transferring property ownership to an heir, legatee, or grantee without requiring full prepayment of taxes upon presentation of an affidavit verifying an installment payment plan.

The Register of Wills is responsible for the administration of decedents' estates and probate proceedings. The bill directly impacts estate settlement and probate property transfers by permitting residential real property to be transferred from a decedent's estate to an heir or legatee under an approved tax payment plan rather than requiring all taxes to be settled prior to recordation.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Maryland Commission on Veterans and Military Families to develop a statewide strategic plan. Requires the Commission to study and recommend actions to make Maryland the best state for veterans and military families. Directs the Commission to identify key performance indicators comparing quality of life metrics with other states. Requires consultation with the Office of Military and Federal Affairs and the Maryland Military Installation Council. Mandates a final report with legislative and budgetary recommendations to the Governor and General Assembly by December 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Commission on Veterans and Military Families; Maryland Department of Veterans Affairs
qa_results.stakeholders: Military veterans, reserve service members, and military families in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $74,200 in FY 2025 for contractual staff support and operating expenses to assist the commission and produce the report. No effect on state revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Maryland Commission on Veterans and Military Families, designating the Secretary of Veterans Affairs (now Veterans & Military Families) as the chair and requiring the department to staff the commission, resulting in a general fund expenditure increase of $74,237 in FY 2025.

The bill explicitly requires the Commission to consult with the Office of Military and Federal Affairs and the Maryland Military Installation Council, both housed within the Department of Commerce, during the development of the study and recommendations.
The Adjutant General, or the Adjutant General's designee, is designated as an ex officio member of the newly created Commission.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a new temporary state commission tasked with studying and developing recommendations for a statewide strategic plan to support veterans and military families.
The Governor is tasked with appointing five members to the Commission, and the Commission must submit its final report and recommendations to the Governor by December 1, 2024.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the statutory definition of disability governing rehabilitation services in the State. Defines disability as any physical or mental impairment constituting or resulting in a substantial impediment to employment or independent living. Repeals language describing disability as a defect or infirmity incapacitating an individual totally or partially. Conforms Maryland rehabilitation law to definitions established under federal rehabilitation statutes. Takes effect July 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education; Division of Rehabilitation Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals with physical or mental impairments seeking or receiving rehabilitation services in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The altered definition conforms State law to federal rehabilitation standards and does not affect governmental finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 60 amends the Education Article regarding the definition of 'disability' for vocational rehabilitation services administered by the Division of Rehabilitation Services (DORS), which is an operational division within the Maryland State Department of Education.

The Department of Disabilities coordinates statewide policies and employment services for Maryland residents with disabilities and works across agencies to align rehabilitation and employment opportunities.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases the timeframe for investigating and issuing a written decision on certain State employee discrimination or harassment complaints. Extends the statutory deadline from 30 days to 60 days after receiving a complaint. Applies to complaints filed by Executive Branch employees or job applicants alleging nonmerit actions or unlawful harassment. Requires an equal employment officer to investigate the complaint and recommend a decision. Requires the head of the principal unit to issue the written decision. Authorizes an additional 30-day extension if the complainant provides written authorization to the investigating officer.
qa_results.responsible_party: Equal employment officers; fair practices officers; heads of principal units of State government
qa_results.stakeholders: Executive Branch State employees and applicants for State employment
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact, as the procedural changes do not directly affect governmental finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DBM serves as the central personnel agency for the State of Maryland, managing state employee policies, overseeing equal employment and fair practices officers, and administering the appeals process for state employee personnel and harassment complaints under the State Personnel and Pensions Article.

MCCR enforces Maryland's anti-discrimination laws in employment, and the bill directly governs investigations of state employee complaints alleging harassment under § 20–606(a)(5) of the State Government Article.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands eligibility for an optional local property tax credit on dwelling houses of disabled veterans. Includes honorably discharged veterans declared by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs to have a 100% nonpermanent service-connected disability. Excludes disabled veterans who qualify for a separate statutory property tax exemption from receiving the credit. Authorizes counties and municipal corporations to enact local laws limiting eligibility solely to veterans with permanent disabilities. Applies to all taxable years beginning after June 30, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Mayor and City Council of Baltimore City; governing bodies of Maryland counties and municipal corporations
qa_results.stakeholders: Honorably discharged veterans with a 100% nonpermanent service-connected disability, surviving spouses, and county and municipal governments
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on State finances. County and municipal property tax revenues may decrease beginning in fiscal 2025 if local jurisdictions adopt the expanded credit criteria; specific revenue loss figures are unavailable because impact depends on local enactment and tax rates.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill expands eligibility for property tax credits available to disabled veterans. While the tax credit is administered at the local government level, the Department of Veterans and Military Families is responsible for advocating for veterans and providing information and assistance to help them secure state and local benefits and services.
The Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board provides administrative review and hears disputes concerning real property valuations, exemptions, and property tax credits across Maryland jurisdictions.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes Baltimore City, counties, and municipal corporations to grant property tax credits against local property taxes for specified properties. Covers residential property owned by and serving as the primary dwelling of a local public school system employee. Includes apartment or condominium buildings whose owners made health or safety improvements on or after July 1, 2024. Applies to apartment or condominium buildings used on or after July 1, 2024, for local housing programs serving homeless individuals or families. Permits local governing bodies to determine the credit amounts, durations, and additional eligibility criteria.
qa_results.responsible_party: Mayor and City Council of Baltimore City; governing bodies of Maryland counties and municipal corporations
qa_results.stakeholders: Public school employees who own primary dwellings in their school system's county, owners of apartment and condominium buildings making health or safety improvements or providing housing for homeless individuals and families, and county and municipal governments.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal effect. Local property tax revenues may experience a potentially significant decrease beginning in fiscal year 2025 to the extent local jurisdictions enact the authorized tax credits. Local expenditures are not directly affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill authorizes local jurisdictions to establish property tax credits for residential property owned and occupied by public school employees in the county where they work, touching upon workforce retention and support for local school systems overseen by MSDE.

The bill aligns with DHCD's mission of promoting safe housing and homeless solutions by authorizing local tax credits for apartment and condominium buildings undergoing health and safety improvements or serving local homeless housing programs.
PTAAB hears appeals and resolves disputes relating to real property assessments, tax exemptions, and property tax credits administered across Maryland jurisdictions.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases the maximum civil penalty from $50,000 to $125,000 per violation for unauthorized insurers. Raises the maximum civil penalty for licensed insurance producers from $500 to $5,000 per violation. Increases the maximum civil penalty for licensed public adjusters from $500 to $5,000 per violation. Maintains the minimum statutory civil penalty of $100 per violation for each category. Authorizes the Maryland Insurance Commissioner to impose these penalties in addition to or instead of license sanctions.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration; Maryland Insurance Commissioner
qa_results.stakeholders: unauthorized insurers, licensed insurance producers, licensed public adjusters, and Maryland insurance policyholders
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues increase, likely minimally, beginning in fiscal 2025 to the extent increased penalties are assessed. State expenditures are not affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 67 is a departmental bill requested by the Maryland Insurance Administration (MIA). It directly increases the maximum civil penalties that the Maryland Insurance Commissioner and MIA may impose on unauthorized insurers, insurance producers, and public adjusters who violate state insurance law.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires continuing care retirement community providers to post their most recent disclosure statement on their website. Increases the required frequency of open meetings between providers and subscribers from annually to quarterly. Directs providers to present an aggregated, deidentified summary of internal grievances at the final quarterly meeting each year. Requires the Maryland Department of Aging to collect annual grievance records from providers and report to the General Assembly. Mandates written reoccupancy status reports when entrance fee refunds remain unpaid after nine months.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Aging
qa_results.stakeholders: Continuing care retirement community providers, continuing care subscribers, resident associations, and subscribers' beneficiaries
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures and revenues are not affected, as the Maryland Department of Aging can implement the reporting and data collection requirements with existing budgeted resources. Local governments are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends Title 10 of the Human Services Article, which the Department of Aging administers. The department is tasked with collecting annual internal grievance reports from continuing care retirement community (CCRC) providers, reviewing disclosure statements, and submitting an annual summary report to the General Assembly.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands eligibility for the Teacher Development and Retention Program to include students at all Maryland community colleges. Delays initial stipend awards to the 2024–2025 through 2026–2027 school years. Shifts educator internship stipends to the 2027–2028 through 2029–2030 school years. Extends the termination date of the pilot program by one year to June 30, 2030. Requires the Maryland Higher Education Commission to conduct an internal program evaluation by July 1, 2029. Authorizes the Teacher Development and Retention Fund to cover program administrative expenses.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Higher Education Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland community college students pursuing teaching careers, teacher candidates, public schools and publicly funded prekindergarten programs, and Maryland community colleges
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures decrease by an estimated $1.0 million through FY 2029 by replacing the requirement for an independent evaluation consultant with an internal evaluation by MHEC. Special fund expenditures for stipends are shifted back by one year, utilizing existing funding without requiring new appropriations. No effect on State revenues, and local finances are not directly affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MHEC directly administers the Teacher Development and Retention Program and its special fund. The bill expands program eligibility to all Maryland community colleges, shifts the award periods and termination date, allows special funds to cover administrative costs, and tasks MHEC directly with conducting the program evaluation rather than hiring an outside consultant.

MHEC administers the Teacher Development and Retention Program and the associated fund, establishes eligibility criteria through the Office of Student Financial Assistance, and is specifically directed by the bill to conduct the program effectiveness evaluation.

The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) identifies the high-needs schools, grade levels, and content areas experiencing teacher shortages where stipend recipients must complete their service obligations, and previously executed an MOU transferring program funds to MHEC.
Under the reenacted provisions of the bill, the State Treasurer is statutorily required to hold the Teacher Development and Retention Fund separately and invest its moneys.
Under the reenacted provisions governing the Teacher Development and Retention Fund, the Comptroller is responsible for accounting for the special fund.
The bill requires MHEC to report the results of the comprehensive evaluation of the Teacher Development and Retention Program to the Governor on or before January 1, 2030.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes licensed pharmacists to order and administer influenza, COVID-19, and emergency vaccines to individuals at least 3 years old. Permits qualifying pharmacists to administer ACIP-recommended or FDA-approved vaccines to individuals at least 7 years old. Allows pharmacists meeting specified credentials to administer CDC-recommended travel vaccines to adults. Requires pharmacists to complete approved practical training, maintain CPR certification, and complete immunization-related continuing education. Mandates reporting all administered vaccinations to the ImmuNet Program and referring minor patients to pediatric primary care providers when appropriate.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Pharmacy; Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: licensed pharmacists, individuals age 3 and older seeking vaccinations, small business pharmacies, and pediatric primary care providers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on State operations or finances, and no direct effect on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the Health Occupations Article governing pharmacist scope of practice for administering vaccines. The Maryland Department of Health (MDH), along with the State Board of Pharmacy, Board of Physicians, and Board of Nursing housed within it, is responsible for establishing regulatory criteria, written protocols, and receiving vaccination records through the ImmuNet system.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters governance, contracting procedures, and reporting deadlines for the Maryland Environmental Service. Expands the definition of municipality to include the District of Columbia and the United States or its units. Authorizes the Board Secretary, with Board approval, to appoint an employee as Deputy Secretary. Allows the Service to provide project proposals rather than proposed contracts following service requests. Establishes that the Service generally has no obligation to provide services before contract execution. Sets November 15 annual deadlines for financial audits and activity reports while repealing an unauthorized spending audit requirement.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Environmental Service
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland Environmental Service; municipalities; the District of Columbia; federal agencies; private entities contracting for Maryland Environmental Service projects
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material impact on State or local finances. The Maryland Environmental Service experiences modest administrative efficiencies and potential minimal savings from repealed auditing and modified reporting requirements.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This departmental bill directly amends the governing statutes of the Maryland Environmental Service, altering board governance delegation, contracting procedures, and annual auditing and reporting deadlines.

Under the amended provisions of the bill, the Maryland Environmental Service is statutorily required to submit copies of its annual independent financial audit and board recommendations to the Department of Budget and Management.
The bill alters the annual reporting deadline by which the Maryland Environmental Service must submit its annual report of activities and financial audit to the Governor.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires each hospital and urgent care center in Maryland to implement an evidence-based sepsis protocol by January 1, 2025. Mandates that hospital protocols comply with Centers for Disease Control and Prevention sepsis guidelines. Directs specialty psychiatric hospitals to establish screening procedures and transfer processes for affected patients. Requires periodic training for direct care staff and updated training following substantive protocol changes. Obligates facilities to provide their sepsis protocols to the Maryland Department of Health upon request.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Hospitals, urgent care centers, specialty psychiatric hospitals, healthcare staff, and patients with sepsis, severe sepsis, or septic shock
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Department of Health can oversee protocol implementation using existing budgeted resources. There is no effect on State revenues and no material impact on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Health - General Article to require hospitals and urgent care centers to implement evidence-based sepsis protocols and submit these protocols to the Maryland Department of Health upon request. MDH is responsible for oversight and regulatory enforcement.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Health, in consultation with county boards of education, to establish a public school bronchodilator policy. Authorizes trained school nurses and designated school personnel to administer bronchodilators to students experiencing asthma symptoms or respiratory distress. Prohibits personnel from administering a bronchodilator to a prekindergarten student without a diagnosis and a prescription. Requires public schools to store stock bronchodilators and modes of delivery, including inhalers with spacers. Directs the Maryland State Department of Education to develop training identifying symptoms of asthma, respiratory distress, and anaphylaxis. Authorizes nonpublic schools to adopt a similar bronchodilator policy and obtain standing orders.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Maryland State Department of Education; county boards of education
qa_results.stakeholders: Public and nonpublic school students, school nurses, designated school personnel, local school systems, and local health departments
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $32,200 in FY 2025 for MDH contractual support to establish the bronchodilator policy. Local school system and local health department expenditures increase by an indeterminate amount to conduct paid training and maintain stock supplies of bronchodilators and spacers.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health (MDH) is mandated by the bill to establish the statewide policy for public schools regarding the availability and administration of bronchodilators in consultation with county boards, and to consult on the development of related training. MDH also incurs an estimated $32,208 in general fund expenditures in FY 2025 to hire contractual support to develop this policy.

The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) is required to identify or develop paid professional development training for school personnel to recognize and differentiate symptoms of asthma, respiratory distress, and anaphylaxis. MSDE must also develop standard incident recording and reporting forms and collect incident reports from public schools.

qa_results.bill_summary: Grants immediate vesting rights in the State Retirement and Pension System to the State Superintendent of Schools. Adds the State Superintendent of Schools to the statutory list of qualifying officials who vest immediately. Applies to the specific retirement system plan in which the superintendent holds membership. Takes effect June 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Retirement Agency
qa_results.stakeholders: State Superintendent of Schools
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No discernible effect on State pension liabilities or contribution rates because the bill affects only one member at a time. No effect on revenues or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This departmental bill was requested by the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) and directly benefits the head of the agency, granting the State Superintendent of Schools immediate vesting rights in the State Retirement and Pension System.

The Maryland State Retirement Agency manages and administers the State Retirement and Pension System (SRPS), including tracking and applying vesting rules and benefit eligibility for state officials such as the State Superintendent of Schools.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Insurance Commissioner to allow small employer business entities to be represented by authorized non-attorney individuals. Authorizes representation by corporate officers, partners, limited liability company members, or designated employees. Requires qualifying business entities to provide proof of small employer status to the Commissioner. Requires designated employees to submit a sworn power of attorney confirming authority to bind the entity. Prohibits representation by disbarred or suspended lawyers and hiring outside entities for appearance services.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Commissioner; Maryland Insurance Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Small business employers, including corporations, partnerships, limited liability companies, and sole proprietorships participating in hearings before the Maryland Insurance Administration
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State operations or finances, and has no local effect. Small business employers may experience reduced costs by avoiding the need to retain counsel for administrative hearings.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This is a departmental bill requested by the Maryland Insurance Administration that directly alters the procedural requirements for administrative hearings conducted by the Insurance Commissioner, allowing qualifying small employer business entities to be represented by designated non-attorney individuals.

Administrative Law Judges at the Office of Administrative Hearings conduct hearings delegated by or held on behalf of the Maryland Insurance Administration and must apply the new representation rules for qualifying small businesses.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services to assist incarcerated individuals in accessing federal Pell Grants. Directs the department to consult with all University System of Maryland institutions, Morgan State University, and Goucher College. Directs consultation with Anne Arundel Community College, Hagerstown Community College, and Wor-Wic Community College. Requires the department to set goals and establish tracking systems for incarcerated individuals in postsecondary education programs. Requires the department to track earned college credits and forward the data to the Maryland Higher Education Commission. Mandates that the Maryland Higher Education Commission assist the department in creating the tracking systems.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services; Maryland Higher Education Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Incarcerated individuals in Maryland correctional facilities, the Maryland Higher Education Commission, all University System of Maryland institutions, Morgan State University, Anne Arundel Community College, Hagerstown Community College, Wor-Wic Community College, and Goucher College
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State agencies and participating public institutions of higher education can implement the bill using existing resources. Local community colleges can likewise implement the requirements within existing resources. Any future marketing funding in the state budget is discretionary because the bill does not mandate a specific amount. State and local revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS is the primary implementing agency tasked with assisting incarcerated individuals in accessing federal Pell Grants, consulting with higher education institutions, adopting regulations, setting goals for postsecondary education participation, establishing tracking systems, and reporting credit attainment data to MHEC.
MHEC is statutorily required to assist DPSCS in developing tracking systems for incarcerated individuals in postsecondary education and will receive credit completion tracking data from DPSCS.
MHEC is statutorily required to assist DPSCS in developing tracking systems for incarcerated individuals in postsecondary education and will receive credit completion tracking data from DPSCS.
All USM institutions are expressly enumerated in the statute as higher education institutions that DPSCS must consult with to assist incarcerated individuals in accessing federal Pell Grants.
Morgan State University is specifically named in the statute as an institution of higher education that DPSCS must consult with to assist incarcerated individuals in accessing federal Pell Grants.
The bill directs the Governor to include an appropriation in the annual state budget bill to fund DPSCS's marketing of postsecondary education programs and implementation of tracking systems.

DBM assists the Governor with state budget formulation and execution, which is implicated by the statutory language requesting annual budget appropriations for marketing and tracking systems under the bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Limits a residential tenant's liability for rent to two months after vacating due to a qualifying mental disorder. Requires the mental disorder to make continued habitation unfeasible or unsustainable, or require a higher level of care. Authorizes licensed professional counselors, therapists, or psychologists, alongside physicians, to sign the required medical certification. Requires the written certification to state that the condition will outlast the lease termination date. Mandates that tenants provide landlords with the certification and written termination notice before vacating.
qa_results.responsible_party: Judiciary (Administrative Office of the Courts); District Court of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: residential tenants, residential landlords, and licensed physicians, professional counselors, therapists, and psychologists
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Administrative Office of the Courts supports the District Court of Maryland, which adjudicates landlord-tenant disputes and breach-of-lease actions where this statutory limitation of rent liability would be raised as a defense or claim.

The bill references statutory definitions of mental disorders under the Health - General Article and relies on health professionals (such as licensed psychologists and physicians) credentialed by health occupations licensing boards housed within the Maryland Department of Health.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals the authority of the Division of Correction to arrange agricultural employment for inmates in certain camps. Eliminates provisions applying to inmates of camps in Queen Anne's County or other counties with similar camps. Removes requirements for employers to pay prevailing wages and provide security for agricultural inmate labor. Removes statutory authority allowing employers to sell produce harvested by inmate workers. Takes effect July 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Division of Correction
qa_results.stakeholders: inmates in correctional camps in Queen Anne's County and neighboring counties, agricultural employers, and the Division of Correction
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Not expected to have a material impact on State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly repeals statutory provisions governing the Division of Correction (a division of DPSCS) regarding arranging agricultural employment for inmates in certain camps.
The State Highway Administration is explicitly referenced in the repealed statutory provision, which carved out an exception for inmates needed or utilized by SHA for emergency road maintenance.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals the approval requirement for adding federal Recommended Uniform Screening Panel core conditions to Maryland's newborn screening system. Requires the Maryland Department of Health to implement testing for core conditions within 18 months of federal addition. Mandates legislative reporting if procurement delays prevent implementing testing within required statutory timeframes. Authorizes the Department to screen for conditions recommended by the State Advisory Council and approved by the Secretary. Requires the Department to implement testing for infantile Krabbe disease within one year after federal panel inclusion.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Newborn infants in Maryland, parents and guardians, healthcare providers, and the Maryland Department of Health public health laboratory.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Potential significant increase in special fund expenditures and matching fee revenues for the Maryland Department of Health beginning as early as fiscal 2026. Medicaid expenditures (split equally between general and federal funds) may increase to cover higher screening fees and potential follow-up testing.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health (MDH) is the primary implementing agency responsible for the statewide Newborn Screening Program and operating the state public health laboratory that conducts the testing. MDH must implement testing for core RUSP conditions and infantile Krabbe disease within specific statutory timeframes, submit delay reports to legislative committees if necessary, adjust screening fees, and manage the fiscal impact on the state Medicaid program.

Statute designates that all fees collected under the newborn screening subtitle are paid by the Secretary of Health to the Comptroller, who is responsible for distributing them into the Newborn Screening Program Fund.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the statutory role and authorities of the State Advisory Council on Hereditary and Congenital Disorders regarding the approval and recommendation of newborn screening conditions.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits selling or distributing baby food containing toxic heavy metals exceeding U.S. Food and Drug Administration limits. Permits selling or distributing baby food manufactured before January 1, 2026. Requires baby food manufacturers to test representative samples of final products monthly at a proficient laboratory. Requires manufacturers to provide test results to the Maryland Department of Health on request. Requires manufacturers, beginning January 1, 2026, to publish test results online and include label QR codes. Directs consumers to report noncompliant baby food to the department.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Baby food manufacturers, processors, and packers; food retailers and distributors; consumers and young children in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $27,700 in FY 2025 and range from $25,500 to $28,600 annually in future years for the Maryland Department of Health to hire a part-time contractual employee to review test results and handle consumer reports. Local health department expenditures may increase minimally if local inspections of retail food establishments are required. State and local revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health (MDH) is the primary state agency responsible for implementing and enforcing the bill. MDH is authorized to request and review laboratory test results from baby food manufacturers, receives consumer reports of baby food exceeding FDA heavy metal limits, and incurs direct general fund expenditures to hire staff to manage compliance and complaint intake.
