qa_results.bill_summary: Expands the crime of sexual solicitation of a minor to include violations concerning child pornography production or distribution. Prohibits soliciting a minor or a law enforcement officer posing as a minor for unlawful child pornography activities. Prohibits soliciting the consent of a parent, guardian, custodian, or undercover officer for such activities. Subjects violators to existing felony penalties of up to 10 years imprisonment for a first offense. Authorizes penalties of up to 20 years imprisonment for a second or subsequent offense.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary; Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services; Office of the Public Defender
qa_results.stakeholders: Minors and their parents or guardians; law enforcement officers posing as minors or guardians; individuals accused or convicted of sexual solicitation of a minor
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State or local finances or operations. Any increase in court caseloads, public defender workloads, or correctional expenditures is expected to be minimal and absorbable within existing resources.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill expands felony offenses related to sexual solicitation of a minor to include solicitation with the intent to violate child pornography laws, which carries prison sentences of up to 10 or 20 years served in state correctional facilities managed by DPSCS.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: OPD represents indigent defendants in criminal proceedings and would provide legal representation in prosecutions resulting from the expanded scope of felony sexual solicitation offenses.
The Maryland Judiciary and court system will adjudicate criminal charges, pretrial hearings, and sentencing proceedings arising under the expanded criminal prohibition.

As the primary state law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police investigates child exploitation and internet crimes, including conducting undercover operations where officers pose as minors or parents/guardians as specifically referenced in the statute.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits a passenger from riding on a motorcycle seat behind the operator unless able to firmly position their feet on footrests. Exempts a motorcycle passenger who cannot firmly position their feet on the footrests due to a permanent physical disability. Establishes that violations constitute a misdemeanor subject to a maximum fine of $500. Takes effect October 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of State Police; Maryland Department of Transportation; District Court of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: motorcycle operators and motorcycle passengers in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Potential minimal increase in State general fund revenues from District Court fines. Enforcement and caseload adjustments can be absorbed using existing budgeted resources. No material effect on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Motor Vehicle Administration is responsible for driver licensing, vehicle regulations, and assessing points on driver's licenses for moving violations of the Maryland Vehicle Law, including motorcycle safety violations.

The Maryland Department of Transportation oversees the state's transportation network and vehicle administration laws, and this bill amends Title 21 of the Transportation Article regarding motorcycle passenger safety.
The Maryland State Police is responsible for enforcing traffic and vehicle laws on Maryland highways, including issuing citations for moving and passenger safety violations on motorcycles.
The Administrative Office of the Courts supports the District Court, which processes citations, collects fines, and adjudicates contested misdemeanor traffic violations arising from this bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Health to study expanding coverage under the Maryland Healthy Smiles Dental Program. Directs the department to examine covering removable full and partial dentures with minimal benefit restrictions. Mandates studying per-patient reimbursement for provider house calls and extended care facility calls. Evaluates setting reimbursement rates at least 60% of average commercial rates or benchmark charges. Requires soliciting input from dental professional organizations and low-income oral health advocacy groups. Requires reporting the findings to specified legislative committees by December 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: enrollees in the Maryland Healthy Smiles Dental Program; dental care providers; low-income Maryland residents
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Department of Health can complete and report on the study using existing budgeted resources. There is no effect on state revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates the Maryland Department of Health (MDH) to conduct a feasibility study on coverage for certain dental services (dentures, house calls, and extended care facility calls) and provider reimbursement rates under the Maryland Healthy Smiles Dental Program, and submit a report to the General Assembly by December 1, 2024.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes an individual to petition for expungement of probation before judgment records for driving while impaired or under the influence. Prohibits filing the expungement petition within 15 years after discharge from probation. Requires the Motor Vehicle Administration to mandate Ignition Interlock System Program participation for additional drunk driving offenders. Deems program participation to begin on the day the ignition interlock system is installed in the participant's vehicle. Requires the Administration to report participant data annually to the Governor and General Assembly beginning December 1, 2028.
qa_results.responsible_party: Motor Vehicle Administration; Maryland Judiciary
qa_results.stakeholders: individuals convicted of or granted probation before judgment for drunk driving offenses; authorized ignition interlock service providers; commercial driver employers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: General fund expenditures increase by up to $997,600 in FY 2025 for the Judiciary to hire 17 clerks to process expungements, with future year annualization. Transportation Trust Fund revenues increase by $279,900 in FY 2025 and approximately $373,190 annually thereafter from program participation and licensing fees. Local law enforcement agencies and record custodians may experience increased operational costs to process court expungement orders.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The MVA is the primary implementing agency for the Ignition Interlock System Program (IISP). The bill expands mandatory participation in the program to individuals granted probation before judgment for certain drunk driving offenses, alters the program start date calculation, and requires MVA to collect and submit annual reports on program participants to the Governor and the General Assembly.

The bill allows individuals granted probation before judgment for certain drunk driving offenses to petition the District Court and circuit courts for expungement after 15 years, requiring the Judiciary to hire additional clerical personnel with an estimated general fund fiscal impact of approximately $1 million to $1.3 million annually.

MDOT is the parent department of the Motor Vehicle Administration. The bill directly impacts Transportation Trust Fund revenues via increased interlock participation fees and restricted license fees resulting from expanded mandatory enrollment.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS oversees the Criminal Justice Information System (CJIS), which acts as the central repository for criminal records and is responsible for processing court-ordered expungements of police and criminal records under the bill.
OAH conducts administrative hearings for individuals facing driver's license suspensions or modifications related to drunk driving and ignition interlock requirements.
MSP is a primary law enforcement agency maintaining arrest and citation records for impaired driving offenses that are subject to court expungement orders under the bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: OPD represents indigent defendants charged with drunk driving offenses who will be subject to expanded mandatory interlock participation and may later seek expungement under the bill's provisions.
The bill mandates that the Motor Vehicle Administration submit an annual report directly to the Governor on ignition interlock system participants beginning in December 2028.
DNR's Natural Resources Police enforce traffic and conservation laws and serve as custodians of law enforcement records that may be subject to expungement orders under the bill.
As the repository for historical state and court records, the State Archives is impacted by record expungement and redaction mandates for eligible historic cases.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases compensation and scholarship amounts for members of the Baltimore County Board of Education. Sets the annual compensation for nonstudent members other than the board chair at $16,500. Entitles the chair of the county board to receive $17,500 annually as compensation. Grants a $10,000 higher education scholarship to a student member who completes a full term. Delays compensation increases until the beginning of the next term of office following the effective date. Takes effect July 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Baltimore County Board of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: Elected, appointed, and student members of the Baltimore County Board of Education and Baltimore County Public Schools
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Baltimore County expenditures increase by $39,250 in FY 2027, phased up to $102,500 by FY 2030 as terms turn over. County revenues and State finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Department of Education provides statewide leadership and oversight for the 24 local school systems, including Baltimore County Public Schools. While the bill directly affects local board compensation and student scholarships with solely local fiscal impact, it amends statutory provisions within the Education Article governing local school board governance.

qa_results.bill_summary: Regulates the alteration and removal of submerged aquatic vegetation across tidal waters of the State. Expands Department of Natural Resources plan approval requirements to include trimming vegetation. Reduces the allowable width of permit-exempt navigation strips from 60 feet to 20 feet. Restricts dock and marina owners to trimming or cutting rather than complete eradication. Mandates that exempt entities use best harvesting methods and report activity locations and dates to the department. Prohibits using chemicals to trim, harvest, cut, or eradicate submerged aquatic vegetation under statutory exemptions.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
qa_results.stakeholders: owners and renters of piers, docks, ramps, and marinas on State tidal waters; public utility companies; telecommunications carriers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Department of Natural Resources can handle the bill's requirements with existing budgeted resources. The bill does not materially affect State or local finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 109 is a departmental bill requested by DNR. It directly amends Section 4-213 of the Natural Resources Article, which DNR administers, modifying requirements for obtaining approval or submitting notifications to the Department for the trimming, alteration, and removal of submerged aquatic vegetation.

MDE regulates tidal wetlands and waterways through its Wetlands and Waterways Program. The bill clarifies the boundaries between DNR-regulated submerged aquatic vegetation trimming and activities regulated by MDE (such as dredging, filling, and shoreline alterations).

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires a person doing public business to file a registration statement with the State Board of Elections. Sets the registration deadline within 15 business days after award of a qualifying contract. Mandates disclosing beneficial ownership of 5% or more and updating this information under State Board regulations. Requires filing an initial political contribution statement within 15 business days after the registration filing. Repeals the requirement that businesses with State contracts file beneficial ownership lists with the Secretary of State. Authorizes the State Board of Elections to impose late fees and civil penalties for reporting violations.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Elections; Board of Public Works; Secretary of State
qa_results.stakeholders: businesses contracting with Maryland State or local governmental entities for $200,000 or more; State and local procurement entities
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues for the Fair Campaign Financing Fund may increase minimally beginning in fiscal 2025 from late filing fees and civil penalties. Affected State agencies and local governments can implement the administrative changes within existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Board of Elections is the primary implementing agency for the bill. It is responsible for receiving registration statements and beneficial ownership disclosures from persons doing public business, adopting regulations, notifying filers of deficiencies, and assessing late fees and civil penalties.

The bill was requested by the Secretary of State and repeals the requirement under State Finance and Procurement law that businesses doing $200,000 or more in public business file beneficial ownership disclosures with the Secretary of State, transferring this reporting function entirely to the State Board of Elections.

The bill directly impacts the Board of Public Works by requiring contractors awarded contracts subject to BPW approval to certify to the Board that they have filed the required initial contribution statement with the State Board of Elections.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits an adult directly supervising a minor from allowing the minor to ride a horse without an approved, properly secured helmet. Applies to riding on highways, public horse-riding paths or trails, and specified public equestrian facility grounds. Defines horses to include donkeys, mules, and ponies. Exempts minors crossing highways between private land, engaging in agricultural practices, or belonging to Amish or Mennonite communities. Exempts certain minors receiving medical therapy services who require approved alternative helmets. Treats a violation involving an adult supervising multiple minors simultaneously as a single violation.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of State Police; Maryland Department of Transportation
qa_results.stakeholders: Minors riding horses, adult supervisors of minor equestrians, commercial equestrian facility operators, and state and local law enforcement agencies
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Potential minimal increase in general fund revenues from fines of up to $500 for violations. Potential indeterminate decrease in Maryland Department of Health expenditures if traumatic head injuries are reduced. Local finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the Maryland Vehicle Law within the Transportation Article regarding rules of the road and helmet requirements for equestrian riding on highways and public paths.

As the primary law enforcement agency responsible for enforcing the Maryland Vehicle Law and traffic safety on state highways, the Maryland State Police is responsible for enforcing this new requirement and issuing citations.

The bill explicitly applies to equestrian riding on public horse-riding paths and trails, which are largely situated within state parks and public lands managed and patrolled by DNR and the Natural Resources Police.
The District Court within the judicial system is responsible for processing citations, collecting fines (up to $500), and adjudicating violations of this provision under the Maryland Vehicle Law.

The fiscal note identifies a potential expenditure reduction for MDH (through Medicaid and the Developmental Disabilities Administration) to the extent the helmet mandate prevents traumatic brain injuries among minors.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires a commitment unit to include the telephone number of the Maryland Crime Victims Resource Center in release notifications. Applies this requirement when a sentenced defendant or child respondent is released from confinement. Mandates inclusion of this contact information in notifications sent to a victim, victim's representative, or witness. Defines release from confinement to include work release, home detention, or other authorized release from a facility. Takes effect October 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services; Department of Juvenile Services
qa_results.stakeholders: crime victims, victims' representatives, witnesses, and the Maryland Crime Victims Resource Center
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local government finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As a principal commitment unit retaining custody of sentenced adult defendants, DPSCS is directly responsible for issuing release notifications and must include the required contact information for the Maryland Crime Victims Resource Center.

As the commitment unit retaining custody of committed or detained youth (child respondents), DJS is directly responsible for issuing release notifications and must include the telephone number of the Maryland Crime Victims Resource Center.
The Judiciary issues commitment orders and interfaces with victim notification processes, although court operations are not materially affected by the change in notice contents.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Maryland Geological Survey Fund as a special, nonlapsing fund within the Department of Natural Resources. Directs the Fund to finance survey operations, long-term budgeting, procurements, and equipment purchases. Specifies the Fund consists of State budget appropriations, interest earnings, and other accepted revenues. Requires the State Treasurer to invest Fund money and credit all interest earnings to the Fund. Authorizes the Department of Natural Resources to use Fund money for eligible direct and indirect administrative costs. Sets the effective date as October 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland Geological Survey and its clients, including local governments, nonprofit organizations, and private companies.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Overall special fund revenues and expenditures for the Department of Natural Resources are not materially affected. Accrued balances will retain minor interest earnings rather than transferring them to the General Fund. Special fund spending may be delayed across fiscal years to finance larger projects and equipment replacements.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 117 directly establishes the Maryland Geological Survey Fund within the Department of Natural Resources (DNR) and designates DNR as the administrator of the fund to support the survey's projects, equipment purchases, and operational costs.

The bill explicitly requires the State Treasurer to hold the Maryland Geological Survey Fund separately and invest the fund's moneys, with net interest earnings credited to the fund rather than the General Fund.
The bill mandates that the Comptroller of Maryland account for the newly established Maryland Geological Survey Fund.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands HIV and syphilis testing and reporting requirements for pregnant women, newborns, and health care providers. Requires health care providers to test pregnant women for HIV and syphilis at delivery unless the patient declines. Mandates HIV testing of newborns when the mother's HIV status is unknown. Requires hospitals to determine a mother's syphilis serologic status before discharging the newborn. Excludes HIV reporting records from discovery or admission in criminal, civil, or administrative actions. Increases maximum criminal fines for unauthorized disclosure of confidential HIV and AIDS reporting information.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: pregnant women, newborns, health care providers, hospitals, and medical laboratories
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State Medicaid expenditures increase by an estimated $783,600 in FY 2025 (85% federal funds, 15% general funds) for additional testing, increasing to $1,175,876 by FY 2029. Testing costs are expected to be offset by significant but indeterminate long-term savings from early disease detection and treatment. Local health departments face a minimal workload increase handleable with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 119 is a departmental bill requested by the Maryland Department of Health (MDH). It alters HIV and syphilis testing and reporting requirements, authorizes MDH to adopt rules and regulations, manages the HIV registry, and impacts MDH Medicaid expenditures for screening pregnant women and newborns.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation to provide loans up to $10,000 per seasonal full-time job. Requires seafood processing loan recipients to report annually for three consecutive years on jobs created or retained. Expands Maryland Watermen's Microloan Program eligibility to State residents holding commercial licenses issued by the Potomac River Fisheries Commission. Adds a Maryland residency requirement to the definitions of beginner waterman and generational waterman. Repeals statutory loan limits of $7,000 minimum and $15,000 maximum for the microloan program.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland commercial watermen, licensed seafood dealers, and seafood processing businesses
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: MARBIDCO nonbudgeted revenues and expenditures increase beginning in FY 2025 due to increased lending under the oyster processing loan program. Microloan program adjustments reallocate existing funds without altering overall State funding levels. No local effect.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Agricultural & Resource-Based Industry Development Corp.
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MARBIDCO directly administers the Maryland Watermen's Microloan Program and the Maryland Oyster Shucking House Loan Fund. The bill alters loan qualification metrics, definitions of eligible watermen, seasonal job provisions, loan reporting requirements, and limits for these programs.

The bill references commercial tidal fish licenses issued by DNR, and existing loan forgiveness mechanisms for seafood processing loans require verification by and returns of oyster shells/spat-on-shell to DNR.

The bill expands loan eligibility under the Maryland Watermen's Microloan Program to Maryland residents holding commercial fishing licenses issued by the Potomac River Fisheries Commission (PRFC), an interstate compact agency.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the criteria for supervised individuals to accrue earned compliance credits under the Division of Parole and Probation. Excludes monthly supervision fees from the requirement that individuals remain current on court-ordered restitution, fines, and fees. Allows qualifying individuals on probation, parole, or mandatory release to earn 20-day monthly supervision reductions despite unpaid fees. Maintains requirements that individuals avoid new arrests, follow no-contact conditions, and fulfill community supervision obligations. Takes effect October 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Division of Parole and Probation; Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals under active probation, parole, or mandatory release supervision by the Division of Parole and Probation who owe monthly supervision fees
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Potential speculative decrease in State general fund revenues from uncollected monthly supervision fees. Likely reduces caseloads for the Division of Parole and Probation and collections workload for the Central Collection Unit. Specific dollar estimates are unavailable.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS is the primary implementing agency. The bill alters the criteria under which its Division of Parole and Probation (DPP) awards earned compliance credits, allowing supervised individuals to earn credits toward reducing their period of active supervision without being current on monthly supervision fees, which directly impacts DPP caseloads and operations.

The Central Collection Unit (CCU) resides within DBM. By shortening active supervision periods and potentially reducing the cumulative outstanding supervision fee balances transferred to CCU upon case closure, the bill is anticipated to decrease CCU's collection workload.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the clerk of the circuit court of each county to keep electronic records of military discharge papers. Expands the recordation requirement from Armed Forces members to all individuals who served in the uniformed services. Requires the clerk to redact an individual's Social Security number from any portion of the record. Allows public inspection of discharge records recorded at least 70 years earlier without requiring good cause or kinship. Repeals the good cause requirement for relatives obtaining certified copies of records recorded at least 70 years prior.
qa_results.responsible_party: Clerk of the Circuit Court of each county
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals who served in the uniformed services of the United States, their relatives, and individuals seeking access to military discharge records
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Judiciary can implement the bill with existing resources. State revenues and local operations and finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly governs the recordation, electronic indexing, redaction, and inspection of military discharge records maintained by the clerks of the circuit courts across Maryland, which are supported and administered by the Administrative Office of the Courts.
The bill directly impacts the handling, privacy, and public availability of military discharge papers and service records for Maryland veterans and their families.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Nonoccupational Postexposure Prophylaxis (nPEP) Standing Order Program within the Maryland Department of Health. Authorizes licensed pharmacists registered with the program to dispense nPEP medication under a standing order without a prescription. Requires pharmacists to screen patients, verify exposure occurred within 72 hours, and follow federal CDC clinical guidelines. Mandates patient referral to a departmental disease intervention specialist for ongoing treatment. Requires the department to adopt regulations addressing specific populations, including sexual assault victims and pediatric patients. Authorizes the department to collect administrative fees, exempting individuals qualifying under the rape victim prevention program.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; State Board of Pharmacy
qa_results.stakeholders: Licensed pharmacists in Maryland, individuals with potential nonoccupational exposure to HIV (including sexual assault victims and pediatric patients), and primary care providers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Indeterminate general fund revenue increase to the extent the Maryland Department of Health collects administrative fees. Potential near-term increase in Medicaid expenditures and federal matching funds from higher nPEP utilization, likely offset by savings from prevented HIV infections. MDH can implement the program with existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health (MDH) is the primary implementing agency for the bill. MDH is tasked with administering the Nonoccupational Postexposure Prophylaxis (nPEP) Standing Order Program, adopting regulations with the advice and approval of the State Board of Pharmacy, collecting administrative fees, establishing training and educational guidelines, managing patient referrals to departmental disease intervention specialists, and collecting program data.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill references the Program for Preventing HIV Infection for Rape Victims established under § 11-1008 of the Criminal Procedure Article, which is administered by the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy, exempting qualifying victims under that program from fees collected under the new standing order program.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires local jurisdictions with at least 150,000 residents to submit an annual housing permit report by July 1. Directs jurisdictions to report to the Department of Housing and Community Development and the Department of Planning. Covers building and development permit applications containing a residential housing component considered during the prior calendar year. Specifies reporting metrics including application counts, processing times, approved units, and expedited review procedures. Mandates that covered local jurisdictions publish the report publicly on their websites. Takes effect October 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development; Maryland Department of Planning
qa_results.stakeholders: local jurisdictions with at least 150,000 residents, residential housing developers, and the public
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State agencies can implement the reporting requirements with existing resources. Expenditures may increase for certain local jurisdictions to modify software systems and compile required data, such as an estimated one-time programming cost of $10,000 in Charles County.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 131 requires qualifying local jurisdictions to annually report data regarding residential building and development permit applications directly to the Department of Housing and Community Development.

HB 131 designates the Maryland Department of Planning as a recipient of the annual local jurisdiction reports on residential development permit applications, integrating with existing local planning reporting under the Land Use Article.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits employers from taking or threatening adverse actions against employees who exercise statutory rights under specified labor and wage laws. Prohibits employers from hindering or delaying the Commissioner of Labor and Industry in enforcing covered employment standards. Authorizes the Commissioner to investigate violations on their own initiative or upon receiving a written complaint. Requires the Commissioner to attempt mediation within 90 days and issue compliance orders for unresolved violations. Authorizes civil enforcement actions by the Attorney General or affected employees when employers fail to comply within 30 days. Prohibits groundless or malicious complaints and bad-faith proceedings, establishing administrative penalties up to $1,000.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor; Office of the Attorney General
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland employers and employees covered under state wage, equal pay, minor employment, workplace fraud, and living wage laws
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $225,049 in FY 2025 for the Maryland Department of Labor to hire 2.5 positions and update database software, with annualized expenditures between $209,300 and $237,000 through FY 2029. State general fund revenues increase minimally from civil and administrative penalties. Local governments face no material fiscal effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill is a departmental initiative for the Department of Labor. The Commissioner of Labor and Industry within the department is directly responsible for investigating complaints, mediating disputes, issuing orders, assessing civil penalties, and enforcing anti-retaliation provisions across multiple employment standards laws.

The bill explicitly authorizes the Commissioner of Labor and Industry to ask the Attorney General to bring civil enforcement actions on behalf of employees when employers fail to comply with orders. The fiscal note also includes funding for a part-time Assistant Attorney General.

Employer orders and administrative penalties issued by the Commissioner are subject to the contested case provisions of the State Government Article, requiring the Office of Administrative Hearings to conduct administrative hearings and train administrative law judges on the new statutory provisions.

The bill authorizes civil enforcement actions and private causes of action in the District Court and circuit courts for violations and enforcement of Commissioner orders, potentially affecting judicial caseloads.

qa_results.bill_summary: Provides civil immunity to administrative, educational, and support staff of public, private, and parochial schools. Protects staff from civil liability for personal injury or property damage resulting from intervening in student disturbances. Applies when staff members intervene in an altercation between students or another student disturbance. Requires staff to act in an official capacity and intervene in a reasonably prudent manner. Excludes conduct that is grossly negligent, willful, wanton, or intentionally tortious.
qa_results.responsible_party: Judiciary
qa_results.stakeholders: Administrative, educational, and support staff of public, private, and parochial schools; students; and parents or guardians
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill provides civil immunity to school staff members (administrative, educational, or support staff) who intervene in student altercations or disturbances, which directly impacts public school personnel and operational policies overseen by the department.

As the agency tasked with comprehensive school safety approaches, training, and resources for school staff dealing with altercations and emergencies, changes to educator intervention liabilities directly align with its core mission.
The bill amends the Courts and Judicial Proceedings Article to establish a statutory civil immunity defense in personal injury and property damage lawsuits arising from educator intervention.
The Treasurer's Office administers the State Insurance Trust Fund and manages tort claims and liability coverage for state-operated educational institutions and state employees.
As a state agency operating public schools, its instructional and support staff will be covered by the new civil immunity provisions when responding to student disturbances.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands utility billing notice and disclosure requirements in residential leases to include gas and electric services. Requires landlords who collect utility payments to state tenant payment responsibilities in a written lease. Authorizes landlords of buildings with six or more units to provide prior-year utility costs instead of bill copies. Requires landlords of buildings with five or fewer units who collect utility payments to provide bill copies. Exempts utility services paid directly to providers and utilities allocated through a ratio utility billing system.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General (Consumer Protection Division)
qa_results.stakeholders: Residential landlords and residential tenants in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local government operations and finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division enforces statutory requirements governing residential leases, landlord-tenant relations, and unfair or deceptive trade practices involving utility billing disclosures.

The Department of Human Services houses the Office of Home Energy Programs (OHEP), which assists low-income households with utility costs. Although the provisions mandating landlord acceptance of OHEP funds were struck during the legislative process, DHS was consulted on the bill and works closely with tenants affected by utility billing and assistance.
The Department of Housing and Community Development oversees state rental housing programs and tenant-landlord policy initiatives related to housing affordability and stability.
The Maryland Judiciary handles residential landlord-tenant disputes in the District Court, where lease compliance and utility payment notice requirements may be raised in legal proceedings.

qa_results.bill_summary: Renders contracts for the sale or resale of condominium units unenforceable without specified disclosures concerning asbestos. Requires initial sale contracts to disclose vendor knowledge of asbestos on the site, its location, and abatement history. Requires resale certificates to state whether the council of unit owners knows of health or building code asbestos violations. Mandates resale unit owners disclose any known presence of asbestos and any abatement performed during their occupancy. Takes effect October 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Secretary of State
qa_results.stakeholders: Condominium developers, condominium unit owners, condominium purchasers, and condominium councils of unit owners
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Secretary of State is responsible for the statutory oversight and registration of condominiums in Maryland, including the registration and review of condominium public offering statements referenced in the bill.

The Office of the Attorney General, through its Consumer Protection Division, enforces state consumer disclosure laws and handles complaints related to mandatory disclosures in residential real estate and condominium sales.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters provisions of the Public Employee Relations Act governing collective bargaining procedures and administration. Defines an interested employee organization as an existing representative or a petitioner meeting showing of interest requirements. Requires public employers to provide electronic notice within five days of any mandatory employee check-in event. Clarifies that appointed deputy directors are primarily responsible for their respective labor relations subject areas. Directs deputy directors to provide unfair labor practice investigation information directly to the Board.
qa_results.responsible_party: Public Employee Relations Board
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland public employers, public employees, and public employee organizations
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. Changes are procedural and handled with existing agency resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This departmental legislation was requested by PERB and directly alters the Public Employee Relations Act governing PERB's operations, defining interested employee organizations, clarifying deputy director responsibilities across executive, school, and higher education sectors, and updating procedures for unfair labor practice investigations.

As the state's central personnel agency, DBM oversees state employee policies and collective bargaining administration, and noted operational and human resources impacts regarding the bill's altered notice timeline requirements for new employee check-in events.

OAH conducts administrative hearings on unfair labor practice complaints referred by PERB under the statute; the bill amends statutory requirements concerning information provided to OAH and requires training of Administrative Law Judges on the bill's substantive aspects.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes certain health occupations boards to adopt regulations establishing reciprocity for individuals licensed or certified in another state. Applies only to boards that lack existing statutory authority to issue licenses or certifications by reciprocity. Requires the other state to offer similar reciprocity to individuals licensed or certified in Maryland. Mandates that applicants hold substantially equivalent credentials, maintain good standing, submit an application, and pay required fees. Takes effect July 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Health Occupations Boards
qa_results.stakeholders: Out-of-state licensed or certified health care professionals seeking Maryland licensure or certification, and Maryland health care boards and practitioners
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Potential minimal increase in special fund expenditures for any health occupations board choosing to implement reciprocity due to application processing costs. Special fund revenue impact is indeterminate, as fee levels and applicant volume remain unknown. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 146 is a departmental bill from the Maryland Department of Health (MDH). It directly affects the health occupations boards housed within MDH by authorizing those without existing statutory authority to adopt regulations establishing reciprocal licensure and certification.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes claimants who purchase tobacco tax stamps to receive a refund for stamps lost due to theft. Requires claimants to submit a detailed police report and a notarized affidavit under penalty of perjury. Mandates that claimants notify the Comptroller and return refunds if stolen property is recovered. Subjects claimants who submit false refund claims to a fine equal to double the refund received. Authorizes the Comptroller to adopt regulations to administer the refund process.
qa_results.responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Claimants who purchase tobacco tax stamps, including licensed cigarette wholesalers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues decrease by an indeterminate amount beginning as early as fiscal 2024 due to refund issuances. Revenue losses may be partially offset by fines collected for false claims. The Comptroller's Office can administer the changes using existing budgeted resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland administers the state tobacco tax, receives and processes refund claims for stolen tobacco tax stamps, collects required documentation and affidavits, and is authorized to adopt implementing regulations and impose fines for false claims.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the prohibition on destroying medical records, laboratory reports, and X-ray reports from five years to seven years. Bars destroying records of a minor patient until seven years after the patient attains the age of majority. Requires destruction notices to be delivered by both first-class mail and email to the patient or guardian. Requires health care providers to make records available for retrieval within 60 days before the proposed destruction date. Repeals the option to provide notice of record destruction through local newspaper publication upon practice closure.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Health care providers, patients, parents and guardians of minor patients, and health care facilities
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local expenditures may increase minimally to retain medical records for a longer duration, but the Maryland Department of Health and local health departments can handle the changes within existing budgeted resources. Revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the Health - General Article regarding medical record retention and destruction mandates for health care providers and facilities regulated by MDH. It tasks the Secretary of Health with adopting regulations, impacts health occupation licensing boards under MDH, and requires MDH to update record retention schedules across its state-operated facilities and hospitals.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Charles County Board of Education to fill a board vacancy within 90 days after it occurs. Authorizes the board to leave a vacancy unfilled if it occurs in an election year for that seat. Requires the board to provide live video streaming of public applicant interviews through its website. Mandates complete and unedited archived video recordings of each livestreamed interview meeting on the website. Takes effect July 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Charles County Board of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: Charles County Board of Education, applicants for vacant school board seats, and Charles County residents
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal effect. The Charles County Board of Education can implement live streaming and video archiving using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Education Article concerning the vacancy and public meeting procedures for the Charles County Board of Education. While the bill directly governs the local school board and has no state fiscal impact, the Maryland State Department of Education provides overarching leadership and regulatory oversight for the state's 24 local school systems.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits health care providers or their representatives from charging fees for medical record copies requested by a patient's attorney. Applies when records are used to file or appeal Social Security disability income or Social Security benefit claims. Requires the attorney to provide documentation confirming representation of the patient. Takes effect October 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Health care providers, patients filing or appealing Social Security disability income or benefit claims, and attorneys representing those patients
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material impact on State finances or operations. Local government revenues may decrease to the extent local health departments charge fees for copies of medical records, while expenditures are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Health - General Article regarding medical record fees charged by health care providers, directly impacting health care regulations and local health departments overseen by the Maryland Department of Health.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Public Defender was consulted as an information source for this bill, as it relates to legal representation, record retrieval, and fee exemptions for indigent clients and legal representatives.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the State Department of Assessments and Taxation to accept late property tax credit applications from Homeowner Protection Program enrollees. Extends the application deadline to three years after April 15 of the applicable taxable year for program participants. Requires the department to adjust homestead tax assessments for eligible seniors at least 70 years old who missed prior deadlines. Specifies that homeowners receiving this homestead assessment recalculation are not due reimbursements for prior property taxes paid. Authorizes two-year retroactive assessment calculations for seniors at least 70 years old who apply by May 31, 2025.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation; Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Homeowners enrolled in the Homeowner Protection Program and homeowners at least 70 years of age
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase beginning in fiscal 2025 due to retroactive homeowners' property tax credits, while Annuity Bond Fund revenues decrease from additional homestead property tax credits. Local property tax revenues and supplemental credit funding also decrease, but specific statewide figures are indeterminate as costs depend on enrollment.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Under the amended provisions of Tax - Property § 9-104, the Comptroller is statutorily directed to pay property tax credits due to eligible homeowners upon certification by the State Department of Assessments and Taxation, and the Comptroller's Office was consulted in the fiscal analysis of the bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes standards and procedures for installing and using electric vehicle recharging equipment in cooperative housing corporations. Expands the definition of electric vehicle recharging equipment in condominiums and homeowners associations to include electric bicycles. Voids cooperative covenants, lease provisions, and bylaws that prohibit or unreasonably restrict installing or using such equipment. Requires unit owners, lot owners, and cooperative members to provide insurance certificates prior to installation and maintain continuous coverage. Directs the Department of Housing and Community Development to post equipment requirements, contractor information, and dispute resolution resources online.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development
qa_results.stakeholders: members and governing bodies of cooperative housing corporations; unit owners and councils of unit owners in condominiums; lot owners and governing bodies of homeowners associations
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures for the Department of Housing and Community Development increase by $41,700 in fiscal 2025 to hire one part-time development officer, with expenditures increasing to $52,500 by fiscal 2029. Revenues are unaffected and local government operations and finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Department of Housing and Community Development to expand its common ownership community website with guidance on electric vehicle recharging equipment, provide information on certified contractors and insurers, designate a departmental point of contact, and provide dispute resolution resources. The fiscal note also identifies a direct general fund expenditure impact for DHCD to hire staff to fulfill these duties.

qa_results.bill_summary: Exempts qualifying applicants from paying the identification card issuance fee upon presenting designated documentation. Extends the fee exemption to recently released individuals, homeless individuals, and certain youths under State care. Extends the expiration period of certain learner's instructional permits from 180 days to one year. Maintains driver's license validity for certain federal contractors and their dependents during absences from the State. Keeps qualifying licenses in effect for 30 days following the licensee's return to Maryland.
qa_results.responsible_party: Motor Vehicle Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: applicants for identification cards who are homeless, recently incarcerated, or receiving State care; licensed drivers seeking additional license classes; federal agency and armed forces contract employees serving outside Maryland and their dependents
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on Transportation Trust Fund finances or operations. Computer reprogramming changes are handled with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Motor Vehicle Administration is the primary implementing agency responsible for issuing identification cards, learner's instructional permits, and driver's licenses, and will administer the fee exemptions and term extensions mandated by the bill.
The Maryland Department of Transportation is the parent department of the Motor Vehicle Administration and requested this departmental legislation.
Youth under the care of the Department of Juvenile Services are granted a fee exemption for identification cards when presenting appropriate documentation.
Youth between 15 and 20 years old participating in approved Department of Human Services programs are exempted from identification card fees upon presenting documentation.
Individuals currently under the care of the Maryland Department of Health are exempted from identification card fees upon presenting documentation.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Individuals released from correctional facilities within the prior 60 days are exempted from identification card fees upon presenting documentation.
The agency serves as an information source regarding programs and documentation for individuals experiencing homelessness who qualify for the identification card fee exemption.

qa_results.bill_summary: Mandates the withholding of 20% of State aid for highway user revenues and disparity grants for delinquent local jurisdictions. Triggers this reduction if a county, municipality, or special taxing district misses its audit deadline by two calendar years. Directs the Comptroller to order the discontinuance upon notice from the Department of Legislative Services. Requires reinstatement of current fiscal year funds promptly after the jurisdiction submits the audit report. Reverts forfeited prior-year disparity grants to the General Fund and highway user revenues to the Transportation Trust Fund.
qa_results.responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland; Department of Legislative Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland counties, municipalities, and special taxing districts
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Potential decrease in State general fund and Transportation Trust Fund expenditures beginning in FY 2027 to the extent withheld aid reverts to the State. Noncompliant counties, municipalities, and special taxing districts face a 20% reduction in highway user revenues and disparity grants; specific dollar amounts are indeterminate because they depend on local compliance.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Comptroller, upon notice from the Department of Legislative Services, to order the discontinuance of 20% of State aid for local highway user revenues and disparity grants for noncompliant local jurisdictions, and to order the reinstatement of those funds once compliance is achieved.

Local governments and taxing districts are statutorily required to submit their annual audit reports directly to the Legislative Auditor in the prescribed manner and format, which triggers the compliance and penalty provisions under the bill.

The bill impacts the distribution of local highway user revenues, with any discontinued and non-reinstated highway user funds reverting back to the State's Transportation Trust Fund (TTF), decreasing TTF expenditures.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Secretary of State Police to determine the manner, format, and payment methods for specified occupational applications. Applies to private detectives and agencies, security guards and agencies, security systems technicians and agencies, special police, and railroad police. Requires applicants to submit fingerprints in a format approved by state and federal authorities instead of physical forms. Alters insurance documentation requirements for security guard agency applicants employing one or more security guards. Takes effect June 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of State Police
qa_results.stakeholders: private detectives, private detective agencies, security guards, security guard agencies, security systems technicians, security systems agencies, special police officers, and railroad police officers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues decrease minimally by approximately $9,500 annually beginning in FY 2025 due to a 3% vendor fee for automated electronic payment processing. The Department of State Police can manage administrative and operational transitions with existing budgeted resources. No local government fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Maryland State Police is the primary implementing agency for this departmental bill, which authorizes the Secretary of State Police to modernize and automate the application, licensing, certification, and payment processes for private detectives, security guards, security systems technicians, special police officers, and railroad police officers.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly involves the Criminal Justice Information System Central Repository (CJIS-CR), an entity housed within DPSCS, regarding the submission and formatting of fingerprint records and processing of state and national criminal history background checks for applicants.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes a person towing or removing a vehicle from a parking lot to notify the insurer of record electronically. Applies this authorization when the tower and insurer of record agree in writing or by electronic communication. Retains the requirement to send notice by certified and first-class mail absent such an agreement. Requires towers to provide notice within seven days after vehicle removal, excluding days the business is closed. Takes effect October 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Transportation; Motor Vehicle Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Towing businesses and vehicle insurers of record
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends provisions within the Maryland Vehicle Law regarding towing notification procedures. Under current law (§ 21-10A-04), the MVA is statutorily required to maintain and make available to towers a database of insurer contact addresses for notification purposes.
MDOT is the parent department over the Motor Vehicle Administration and oversees the administration of the Maryland Vehicle Law governing towing regulations and vehicle records.
MIA regulates motor vehicle insurers doing business in the State, whose notification requirements and communication standards following vehicle tows are impacted by this legislation.
As the state's automobile insurer of last resort, MAIF acts as an insurer of record and may enter into electronic notification agreements with towing companies under the bill's provisions.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires hospitals to provide oral and written educational resources on safe sleep environments before discharging newborn infants. Directs hospitals to ask parents or legal guardians to describe the infant sleep environment they will provide at home. Mandates that hospitals inform parents or legal guardians of suffocation risks and document that educational materials were provided. Requires each hospital to establish a process by January 1, 2025, to distribute resources and maintain confirmation records. Requires the Maryland Department of Health, in consultation with local health officers, to develop a county-by-county safe sleep resource list.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; local health departments
qa_results.stakeholders: Hospitals; parents and legal guardians of newborn infants; newborn infants
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $19,444 in FY 2025 for contractual staff to develop the initial county-by-county resource list. Local health departments can provide annual resource updates using existing budgeted resources. Revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the Health - General Article and mandates that the Maryland Department of Health develop and maintain a county-by-county list of resources for parents to obtain safe sleep environment items, resulting in a direct operational and fiscal impact of $19,400 in FY 2025.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Motor Vehicle Administration to issue special disabled veteran registration plates to certain disabled armed forces veterans. Applies to veterans between 50% and 99%, inclusive, service-connected disabled as classified by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs. Restricts plate assignment to Class A passenger, Class E 1-ton truck, Class M multipurpose, and Class D motorcycle vehicles. Requires the Administration to charge standard registration fees and surcharges without imposing additional fees for the plates. Prohibits charging replacement plate fees to a spouse or prior joint owner upon vehicle ownership transfer.
qa_results.responsible_party: Motor Vehicle Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: armed forces veterans with a 50% to 99% service-connected disability and their spouses or joint vehicle owners
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on Transportation Trust Fund revenues or expenditures. Newly qualifying individuals remain subject to standard registration fees, replacement fee exemptions have negligible impact, and required software reprogramming can be handled with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MVA is the primary implementing agency tasked with establishing, manufacturing, verifying eligibility for, and issuing the special disabled veteran registration plates, as well as promulgating any necessary regulations.
MDOT is the parent department of the Motor Vehicle Administration and oversees the Transportation Trust Fund, which receives registration revenues affected by the bill's provisions.

DVMF advocates for Maryland veterans and assists them in accessing state benefits and recognition programs, which include specialized motor vehicle registration options for service-connected disabled veterans.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Department of Human Services to use food supplement funding to offset federal Summer Electronic Benefit Transfer administrative costs. Allows the department to establish application deadlines and notification dates for county food supplement matching funds. Alters application requirements and requires counties to coordinate communication plans with the department. Sets the Human Services Careers Scholarship service obligation to 15 months for each awarded academic year. Requires scholarship recipients to enter into a written agreement with the Maryland Higher Education Commission. Authorizes the Commission to determine repayment amounts if a recipient fails to complete the service obligation.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Human Services; Maryland Higher Education Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Children and low-income households receiving food supplement benefits, county governments administering food supplement programs, and recipients of the Pilot Program for Human Services Careers Scholarship.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Alters the authorized uses of existing budgeted funds without materially affecting state or local revenues or expenditures. The Department of Human Services and the Maryland Higher Education Commission can implement the changes with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 183 is a departmental bill requested by the Department of Human Services (DHS). It alters the administration and application timelines for the Summer SNAP for Children program, authorizes DHS to use funds to offset administrative costs of the federal Summer EBT program, and modifies targeted positions and service obligations within DHS under the Pilot Program for Human Services Careers.

The bill directly impacts MHEC and its Office of Student Financial Assistance, requiring MHEC to enter into written agreements with recipients of the Pilot Program for Human Services Careers Scholarship, determine repayment terms upon failure to complete service obligations, and adjust scholarship awards.

As the state's higher education regulatory and student financial assistance coordinating agency (also listed as MHEC), the commission is tasked with administering scholarship agreements, prorating repayments, and setting scholarship conditions under the Pilot Program for Human Services Careers Scholarship.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes an Eastern Shore code county to set a hotel rental tax rate up to 6%. Requires the unanimous consent of the county commissioners to establish the rate. Distinguishes Eastern Shore code counties from other code counties capped at 5%. Takes effect July 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: County Commissioners of Eastern Shore Code Counties
qa_results.stakeholders: Hotel and lodging guests in Eastern Shore code counties, hotel operators in Caroline, Kent, Queen Anne's, and Worcester counties, and Eastern Shore county and municipal governments
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on state finances. If the maximum 6% rate is adopted, annual county revenues increase by approximately $501,000 across Caroline, Kent, Queen Anne's, and Worcester counties, and annual municipal revenues increase by approximately $5.4 million (primarily in Ocean City). Local expenditures are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is the state's chief tax administrator and was consulted on the fiscal analysis of the bill. While hotel rental taxes are administered and collected locally with no direct state fiscal impact, the bill involves Maryland tax statutes and tax policy.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires residential service agencies providing certain Medicaid services to submit annual wage reports to the Maryland Department of Labor. Applies to personal assistance services under Community First Choice, Community Options, Community Personal Assistance Services, and other Department-administered programs. Excludes personal care services provided through the Developmental Disabilities Administration. Mandates annual reports by September 1, beginning in 2025, detailing average, lowest, and highest personal care aide wage rates. Requires the Department of Health to report on operationalizing the federal Ensuring Access to Medicaid Services rule within 180 days.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor; Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: residential service agencies; personal care aides; Medicaid home- and community-based services recipients
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not materially affected; the Maryland Department of Labor and the Maryland Department of Health can administer the reporting requirements using existing budgeted resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 189 directly tasks the Maryland Department of Labor with establishing the form and manner for, and annually receiving, wage rate reports for personal care aides from residential service agencies.

HB 189 applies to Medicaid home- and community-based personal care services administered by MDH and mandates that MDH submit a report to legislative committees regarding the federal Ensuring Access to Medicaid Services rule, the process to review aide wage reports, and the impact on Medicaid reimbursement rates.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes Anne Arundel County and municipalities located in Anne Arundel County to decrease highway speed limits. Sets the minimum allowable decreased speed limit at 15 miles per hour. Requires local authorities to perform an engineering and traffic investigation before decreasing any speed limit. Prohibits local authorities from implementing new speed monitoring systems on highway portions with decreased limits. Takes effect October 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Anne Arundel County; municipalities located in Anne Arundel County
qa_results.stakeholders: motorists driving in Anne Arundel County; Anne Arundel County government; municipal governments within Anne Arundel County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues may increase minimally from additional speeding citations. Local expenditures in Anne Arundel County and its municipalities increase to the extent that engineering and traffic investigations are conducted. Local revenues may increase if speed limits are reduced on roadways with existing speed cameras, but specific figures are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Under Maryland transportation law, any alteration of a maximum speed limit by a local authority on a state highway or its extension is not effective until approved by the State Highway Administration.

As the parent department overseeing state transportation policy, highways, and the State Highway Administration, MDOT monitors statutory changes governing speed limits and roadway safety across jurisdictions.
The District Court of Maryland processes traffic citations and court hearings resulting from enforced speed limit violations, which may see a minimal caseload adjustment.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes a Purple Alert Program within the Department of State Police to assist in locating certain missing individuals. Applies to missing individuals with specified cognitive impairments, mental disorders, intellectual or developmental disabilities, brain injuries, or hearing loss. Requires the Department of State Police to adopt guidelines, train local law enforcement agencies, and recruit broadcasters. Directs the Department of State Police to consult with the State Highway Administration regarding dynamic highway message signs. Requires consulting with the Maryland State Department of Education to develop a search program for high school students. Mandates that caregivers immediately notify law enforcement when a missing individual is found.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of State Police; State Highway Administration; Maryland State Department of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: Missing individuals with cognitive impairments, mental disorders, intellectual or developmental disabilities, brain injuries, or hearing loss; caregivers; local law enforcement agencies; and Maryland high school students.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local government requirements can be absorbed using existing budgeted resources. There is no effect on state or local revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Maryland State Police is the primary implementing agency directed to establish and administer the Purple Alert Program, create guidelines and procedures, train local law enforcement, and coordinate alert dissemination.

The bill explicitly requires the Department of State Police to consult with the Maryland State Department of Education to develop a program allowing high school students to assist in searches consistent with student service-learning guidelines.

The bill explicitly requires the Department of State Police to consult with the State Highway Administration to establish a plan for displaying Purple Alert information to the public via statewide dynamic message signs.
As the parent department of the State Highway Administration, the Department of Transportation oversees the state's transportation infrastructure and signage systems used to broadcast Purple Alerts.

The Purple Alert Program specifically covers individuals with intellectual, developmental, cognitive, or mental disabilities, and the bill permits consultation with disability stakeholders to develop regulations and procedures.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill specifically includes missing individuals who are deaf, deafblind, hard of hearing, or late-deafened as eligible for a Purple Alert, aligning directly with this office's mission and advocacy population.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Secretary of Labor to exempt furloughed federal civilian employees from active work search requirements during a federal shutdown. Applies during a full or partial federal government shutdown caused by a lapse in federal appropriations. Requires the furloughed employee to remain able to work, available for work, and work-attached. Defines a furloughed employee as one temporarily barred from working and placed in a temporary nonpay status. Takes effect July 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor
qa_results.stakeholders: Furloughed federal civilian employees
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material fiscal impact. The Maryland Department of Labor can administer the exemption with existing budgeted resources. Benefit payouts from the Unemployment Insurance Trust Fund are reimbursed when employees receive federal back pay, resulting in no net effect on trust fund balances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 197 is a departmental bill directly affecting the Maryland Department of Labor. It authorizes the Secretary of Labor to exempt furloughed federal civilian employees from the active work search requirement for unemployment insurance benefits eligibility during a federal government shutdown, easing the administrative burden on the Department's Division of Unemployment Insurance.

qa_results.bill_summary: Suspends through fiscal year 2027 the required withholding of operating grants when the transit authority's budget increases over three percent. Reinstates the thirty-five percent grant withholding requirement for budget increases exceeding three percent beginning in fiscal year 2028. Requires withholding thirty-five percent of grants if the board chairman serves over two years or repeats jurisdictional representation. Requires withholding thirty-five percent of grants if an operational Purple Line is omitted from posted transit station maps.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Transportation
qa_results.stakeholders: Washington Metropolitan Area Transit Authority (WMATA); Washington Suburban Transit District; transit riders in Montgomery and Prince George's counties
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures increase by an estimated $223.7 million in FY 2025 ($150.0 million in general funds and $73.7 million in Transportation Trust Fund special funds) by temporarily pausing the 35% operating grant withholding requirement. Additional indeterminate expenditure increases may occur in FY 2026 and FY 2027. Revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the Secretary of Transportation with providing operating grants and enforcing the statutory withholding provisions concerning WMATA. The legislation also has an immediate, significant fiscal impact on the Transportation Trust Fund.

WMATA is an interstate compact entity operating across Maryland, Virginia, and Washington, D.C. The bill alters operating assistance conditions and governance/station mapping requirements that directly affect this interstate compact.

The bill carries significant general fund expenditure implications ($150 million in FY 2025 via the Dedicated Purpose Account) and impacts state budget planning and execution across multiple fiscal years.

MTA is the modal transit administration within MDOT responsible for state transit initiatives, including the development and operation of the Purple Line, which is explicitly cross-referenced as a condition for station map inclusion under the bill's withholding provisions.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters requirements and definitions governing Maryland community schools and community school coordinators. Requires the Director of Community Schools to create a common needs assessment tool and an evaluation form. Directs community school coordinators to use the common tool and submit annual evaluations to State authorities. Requires coordinators to review implementation plans at least once every three years. Authorizes the State Department of Education to comment on implementation plans and requires online publication of needs assessments. Expands wraparound services to include hearing care, therapists, and transportation to off-site learning opportunities.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education; Accountability and Implementation Board
qa_results.stakeholders: students and families in community schools, community school coordinators, and local school systems
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal impact, as existing agency resources can handle implementation. Local school systems may experience indeterminate administrative cost increases associated with community school coordinator evaluations, but net community school expenditures are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 200 directly impacts the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE). The bill requires the Director of Community Schools within MSDE to create a common needs assessment tool and evaluation form, authorizes MSDE to review and provide comments on community school implementation plans, mandates MSDE to make submitted evaluations publicly available, and requires MSDE to jointly submit a report to the General Assembly regarding the appropriate use of grant funds.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires state education agencies to develop mental health training guidelines for athletic coaches. Directs the Maryland State Department of Education to collaborate with health and athletic partners on public school guidelines. Directs the Maryland Higher Education Commission and the Maryland Department of Health to develop higher education guidelines. Identifies indicators of mental illness and behavioral distress, including depression, trauma, violence, youth suicide, and substance abuse. Mandates that public schools and public higher education institutions offering athletic programs train all participating coaches. Takes effect July 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education; Maryland Higher Education Commission; Maryland Department of Health; Maryland Public Secondary Schools Athletic Association
qa_results.stakeholders: Public school athletic coaches, intercollegiate athletic coaches, student athletes, local school systems, and Maryland public institutions of higher education
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local expenditures may increase minimally for public schools, local school systems, and public institutions of higher education to provide required coach trainings, though costs are largely absorbable. State agencies can develop training guidelines using existing resources. Revenues are not affected.
