Exempts retained program funds from statutory reversion to the General Fund.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment
qa_results.stakeholders: Local subdivisions and residents of underserved or overburdened communities in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No direct State fiscal effect because the authorized appropriation of up to $20.0 million annually beginning in fiscal 2026 aligns with existing planned capital expenditures. Overall local government finances are not directly affected, but grant distributions among individual local jurisdictions will shift to meet the 40% funding mandate for underserved or overburdened communities.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The comprehensive flood management grant program is housed within and administered by the Maryland Department of the Environment, which must implement the requirement that at least 40% of grant funding be directed to underserved or overburdened communities.
The bill authorizes the Governor to include an appropriation of up to $20,000,000 in the annual State budget for the grant program beginning in fiscal year 2026.
The Department of Planning consults with MDE on adopting regulations for the program, reviews flood control operations with MDE, and processes grant applications through the State clearinghouse.
The Board of Public Works is statutorily required to approve certain grants and uses of State debt under the comprehensive flood management grant program.
The Maryland Department of Emergency Management is tasked with reviewing and approving local emergency response plans associated with automated flood warning project grants under the program.
As the state's budget agency, DBM oversees executive budget development and manages capital and operating appropriations that may incorporate the authorized grant funding.

qa_results.bill_summary: Directs the Comptroller to distribute $500,000 annually from unclaimed property funds to the Tax Clinics for Low-Income Marylanders Fund. Increases the annual mandated budget appropriation for the CASH Campaign of Maryland to $800,000 beginning in fiscal year 2026. Requires the CASH Campaign to allocate $150,000 of that appropriation to grants for on-demand or mobile tax clinics. Specifies that mobile clinic grants must serve senior populations, rural communities, or under-resourced communities, including new American populations. Requires designated law school and legal service tax clinics to coordinate annually with the CASH Campaign.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Comptroller; Office of the Governor
qa_results.stakeholders: Low-income Maryland taxpayers, senior populations, rural communities, new American populations, University of Maryland School of Law, University of Baltimore School of Law, Maryland Volunteer Lawyers Service, and the CASH Campaign of Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: General fund revenues decrease by $500,000 annually beginning in FY 2025 as unclaimed property funds are redirected to the Tax Clinics for Low-Income Marylanders Fund. General fund expenditures increase by $300,000 annually beginning in FY 2026 to increase the CASH Campaign mandated appropriation from $500,000 to $800,000. Special fund and higher education revenues and expenditures increase by matching distribution amounts. Local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill was requested by the Office of the Comptroller. The Comptroller is the administrator of the State's abandoned property funds and is tasked with distributing $500,000 annually to the Tax Clinics for Low-Income Marylanders Fund, which the Comptroller directly administers and accounts for.

Two-thirds of the Tax Clinics for Low-Income Marylanders Fund is statutorily distributed to constituent institutions of the University System of Maryland (the University of Maryland School of Law and the University of Baltimore School of Law), resulting in a direct increase of $333,333 in higher education revenues and expenditures annually.
The bill requires the State Treasurer to hold the Tax Clinics for Low-Income Marylanders Fund separately and invest the money in the fund in the same manner as other State funds.

The bill establishes and increases statutory budget mandates affecting general fund expenditures ($300,000 annually starting in FY 2026 for the CASH Campaign), which DBM must incorporate into the state budget process and fiscal planning.
The bill statutorily requires the Governor to include an increased annual budget appropriation of $800,000 for the CASH Campaign in the annual budget bill starting in FY 2026.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the State Board of Individual Tax Preparers to publish ethical and professional conduct rules by January 1, 2026. Grants authorized Field Enforcement Bureau employees peace officer powers to enforce tax preparation laws. Requires the Board and the Comptroller to notify each other within five business days of certain enforcement actions. Prohibits willfully preparing income tax returns or refund claims without being licensed or registered. Establishes a misdemeanor fine of up to $5,000 for each unauthorized return prepared. Directs collected penalty fines into the Tax Clinics for Low-Income Marylanders Fund.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Individual Tax Preparers; Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: individual tax preparers, income tax return preparers, low-income Maryland taxpayers, and legal tax clinic programs
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $32,300 in FY 2025 only for one-time Judiciary computer programming costs. Special fund revenues for the Tax Clinics for Low-Income Marylanders Fund increase minimally beginning in FY 2025 from fine revenues. No local government fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill was requested by the Office of the Comptroller and grants peace officer enforcement powers to authorized employees of its Field Enforcement Bureau regarding income tax preparation laws. It also mandates reciprocal notification between the Comptroller and the State Board of Individual Tax Preparers and directs penalty fines to the Comptroller-administered Tax Clinics for Low-Income Marylanders Fund.

The State Board of Individual Tax Preparers is housed within the Maryland Department of Labor. The bill requires the Board to publish a code of ethics and rules of professional conduct, investigate violations, and coordinate enforcement actions by notifying the Comptroller and the Field Enforcement Bureau of disciplinary proceedings and unregistered practice.

The bill creates a new misdemeanor criminal offense for unauthorized tax preparation, requiring one-time judiciary programming updates estimated at $32,300 in fiscal 2025 to update case management and citation systems.

Fines collected under the bill's new penalty provisions are distributed to the Tax Clinics for Low-Income Marylanders Fund, which directly funds tax legal clinics operated by University System of Maryland member institutions (University of Maryland School of Law and University of Baltimore School of Law).

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals obsolete statutory provisions governing income tax revenue distributions to municipalities for fiscal year 1990. Removes the associated payment timing requirement for those outdated distributions. Conforms individual income tax revenue distribution provisions to reflect the repeal. Corrects a statutory cross-reference regarding the tax credit for catalytic revitalization projects. Takes effect July 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Comptroller
qa_results.stakeholders: individuals, nonprofit organizations, and business entities claiming catalytic revitalization project tax credits, and Maryland municipalities
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact; the bill makes only technical and nonsubstantive corrections to the Tax-General Article.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This is a departmental bill requested by the Comptroller's Office to make technical corrections and repeal obsolete statutory provisions regarding the Comptroller's distribution of income tax revenues.

The bill updates a cross-reference in the tax code regarding the catalytic revitalization project tax credit, which is codified under the Housing and Community Development Article administered by the department.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Comptroller to disclose tax information to certain persons, governmental entities, or tax compliance organizations. Alters the definition of tax information to include digital advertising gross revenues tax returns and specified filings. Requires the Comptroller to execute binding written data use agreements before releasing information to specified entities. Mandates continuous supervision by the Comptroller over designated recipients of confidential tax data. Prohibits officers and employees of recipient entities from disclosing received tax information without explicit authorization. Establishes misdemeanor penalties of up to a $1,000 fine and six months imprisonment for unauthorized disclosures.
qa_results.responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland taxpayers, tax compliance organizations, governmental entities receiving tax data, and employees handling confidential tax information
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Potential increase in State general and special fund revenues, as well as local revenues, beginning as early as fiscal 2025 due to enhanced tax compliance and auditing activities; specific figures are unavailable. Operational requirements and enforcement are handled using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 454 is a departmental bill requested by the Comptroller. It expands the Comptroller's authority to disclose tax information to external tax compliance organizations and governmental entities to assist with compliance and audit activities, and mandates that the Comptroller execute and enforce binding data use agreements and supervise recipients.

The bill mandates that recipients of tax information under § 13-203(c)(14), which includes the Maryland Department of Health, enter into binding written data use agreements prescribed by the Comptroller and remain subject to Comptroller supervision.

As an authorized recipient of tax information under § 13-203(c)(14), the Department of Human Services is subject to the new statutory requirement to enter into a binding data use agreement with the Comptroller and comply with specified data security supervision.

The State Department of Education is listed under § 13-203(c)(14) as an authorized recipient of certain tax information and is newly required under subsection (g) to enter into a binding data use agreement and be supervised by the Comptroller regarding data security.

As an entity authorized to receive tax information under § 13-203(c)(14), HSCRC must enter into a formal, binding data use agreement governing the use and security of that data and be subject to Comptroller supervision.

The Maryland Small Business Retirement Savings Board, which administers MarylandSaves, is an authorized recipient under § 13-203(c)(15) and is now statutorily required under subsection (g) to enter into a binding data use agreement and adhere to Comptroller data security oversight.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires electronic filing of various State tax and fee returns administered by the Comptroller. Applies electronic filing mandates to specified business and excise tax returns for periods beginning after December 31, 2026. Mandates electronic filing for corporate, pass-through entity, and withholding income tax returns for tax years after 2026. Requires individual income tax electronic filing after 2029, exempting seniors and taxpayers under specified income thresholds. Exempts persons with disabilities, religious prohibitions, or approved special needs from electronic filing mandates. Prohibits tax preparers and software companies from charging separate electronic filing fees beginning January 1, 2030.
qa_results.responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Individual taxpayers, businesses, corporations with at least 15 employees, pass-through entities, fee-collecting entities, tax return preparers, and tax software developers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Potential minimal increase in State general fund revenues beginning in fiscal 2030 from civil penalties of $500 to $1,000 imposed on tax return preparers and software companies. The Comptroller's Office can implement the requirements with existing resources and expects operational efficiencies from reduced paper processing. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 455 is a departmental bill requested by the Comptroller that mandates electronic filing for various taxes and fees collected and administered by the agency, establishes waiver procedures and exemptions, and authorizes the Comptroller to enforce civil penalties against tax preparers or software companies violating electronic filing fee restrictions.

The bill amends provisions in the Environment Article governing the electronic filing and remittance of both the tire recycling fee and the Bay Restoration Fee, programs and funds overseen in conjunction with the Department of the Environment.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires synthetic turf producers and sellers to provide maintenance and cost disclosures to customers before sales. Mandates disclosing typical lifespan maintenance along with standard costs for turf removal, replacement, and disposal. Defines synthetic turf as plastic tufted carpet of at least 5,000 square feet used for sports fields. Directs the Maryland Department of the Environment to study synthetic turf and the State synthetic turf industry. Requires the department to consult with industry representatives, local governments, school systems, and higher education facilities. Mandates submission of a final report with findings to specified legislative committees by July 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment
qa_results.stakeholders: producers and sellers of synthetic turf; purchasers of synthetic turf; local governments, county school systems, higher education facilities, and professional sports organizations with synthetic turf fields
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $59,400 in FY 2025 and $63,900 in FY 2026 for the Maryland Department of the Environment to hire one contractual specialist to conduct the study. State expenditures terminate at the end of FY 2026. Local governments and public higher education institutions can consult on the study using existing budgeted resources. Revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of the Environment is the primary implementing agency tasked with conducting a comprehensive study on synthetic turf, existing turf fields, and the synthetic turf industry in Maryland in consultation with key stakeholders, and submitting a report to the General Assembly by July 1, 2026.

As operators of higher education athletic and recreational facilities with synthetic turf fields, the University System of Maryland is explicitly identified among the higher education users to be consulted by the Department of the Environment during the study.

As an independent public higher education institution that utilizes athletic facilities, Morgan State University is included among the higher education facilities consulted by the Department of the Environment for the synthetic turf study.

As a public higher education institution operating sports facilities, St. Mary's College of Maryland is identified among the higher education users to be consulted by the Department of the Environment in conducting its study.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits courts and parties from disclosing certain court filings to a nonparty in criminal or juvenile delinquency cases. Applies on notice that an electronic or paper filing contains identifying information of a minor victim. Requires the court or disclosing party to redact all identifying information before disclosure or inspection. Permits unredacted disclosure only if the court finds clear and convincing evidence of good cause. Defines a minor victim as an individual who was a minor when the crime or delinquent act occurred.
qa_results.responsible_party: Judiciary
qa_results.stakeholders: Minor victims of crimes and delinquent acts, parties in criminal and juvenile delinquency cases, court clerks, and nonparties requesting court records
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal general fund expenditure increase and operational impact for the Judiciary to handle redaction of minor victim identifying information in District and circuit court filings. Local revenues are unaffected, with potential operational impacts on circuit courts.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the Judiciary and court operations by requiring courts to redact identifying information of minor victims from electronic and paper filings, including charging documents, before disclosing or allowing inspection by nonparties, necessitating changes to court clerk workflows and public document access systems.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As defense counsel and a party in criminal and juvenile delinquency cases across the state, the Office of the Public Defender is subject to the bill's restrictions prohibiting the disclosure or inspection of court filings containing a minor victim's identifying information to nonparties without redaction.

The bill governs court filings and procedures in juvenile delinquency cases involving minor victims, directly impacting the juvenile justice proceedings and records with which the Department of Juvenile Services interacts.

The Office of the Attorney General represents the State in criminal appeals and specific criminal prosecutions, making it a party subject to the bill's requirements when handling court filings containing identifying information of minor victims.

qa_results.bill_summary: Renames the State Advisory Council on Quality Care at the End of Life. Designates the body as the State Advisory Council on Serious Illness Care. Updates statutory references concerning the development of Medical Orders for Life-Sustaining Treatment forms. Requires the Office of the Attorney General to consult the renamed council on certain healthcare plans. Maintains existing council membership, duties, and joint administrative staffing by the Department of Aging and Attorney General.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Advisory Council on Serious Illness Care; Maryland Department of Aging; Office of the Attorney General
qa_results.stakeholders: Marylanders receiving serious illness or end-of-life care, healthcare providers, and members of the State Advisory Council on Serious Illness Care
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on State or local finances or operations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly renames a statutory state advisory council, changing the State Advisory Council on Quality Care at the End of Life to the State Advisory Council on Serious Illness Care.

The Department of Aging jointly provides staff support and technical assistance to the Advisory Council, the Secretary serves on the council, and the agency receives formal recommendations from the council.

The Office of the Attorney General jointly provides staff support and technical assistance to the Advisory Council, the Attorney General serves on the council, and the OAG consults with the council on end-of-life and serious illness plans.
The advisory council is codified under the Health - General Article, the Secretary of Health is a statutory member, and the council provides health policy recommendations to the department.
The Secretary of Disabilities or designee is designated by statute as a member of the Advisory Council.
The Governor appoints the chair and 17 members of the Advisory Council and may assign duties to the council.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and appointing the chair and the 17 appointed members to this advisory council.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the statutory definition of "practice audiology" to include evaluating, diagnosing, managing, and treating auditory or vestibular conditions. Authorizes prescribing, ordering, selling, dispensing, or externally fitting sound processors for osseo-integrated devices and cochlear implants. Permits conducting health screenings and removing non-impacted cerumen and foreign bodies from the external auditory canal. Allows ordering cultures, bloodwork, and radiographic imaging, plus ordering and performing in-office nonradiographic external canal imaging. Excludes surgical procedures, osseo-integrated device surgery, cochlear implant surgery, and performing radiographic imaging.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Examiners for Audiologists, Hearing Aid Dispensers, Speech-Language Pathologists, and Music Therapists
qa_results.stakeholders: Licensed audiologists and individuals receiving audiological care in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on revenues. The State Board of Examiners for Audiologists, Hearing Aid Dispensers, Speech-Language Pathologists, and Music Therapists can adopt updated regulations using existing budgeted resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health houses the State Board of Examiners for Audiologists, Hearing Aid Dispensers, Speech-Language Pathologists, and Music Therapists, which is the primary regulatory body responsible for implementing the bill, regulating the audiology profession, and updating relevant regulations regarding the scope of practice.

The Maryland School for the Deaf provides specialized education and support services to deaf and hard-of-hearing students, frequently utilizing and coordinating audiological services, cochlear implants, and sound processors impacted by the revised scope of practice definition.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases the maximum civil penalty from $5,000 to $10,000 for each knowingly misclassified employee. Applies this increased penalty to employers violating the Workplace Fraud Act. Requires the Commissioner of Labor and Industry to refer specified tax complaints to enforcement agencies. Triggers these referrals upon clear and convincing evidence of workplace fraud or prevailing wage violations. Mandates referrals to the Comptroller, relevant State's Attorneys, and three federal departments. Takes effect October 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Commissioner of Labor and Industry
qa_results.stakeholders: Employers in Maryland (specifically construction and landscaping businesses), contractors and subcontractors on public works projects, and misclassified workers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: General fund revenues may increase minimally beginning in FY 2025 due to higher civil penalties and improved tax compliance. General fund expenditures may increase if referrals require additional compliance staff at the Comptroller's Office (estimated at $88,000 to $100,000 annually per position). Local finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor (via the Commissioner of Labor and Industry) is the primary enforcement agency responsible for administering the Workplace Fraud Act and State Prevailing Wage Law, assessing the increased civil penalties, and referring complaints alleging tax violations to designated state and federal authorities.

The bill explicitly mandates that the Commissioner of Labor and Industry refer complaints alleging certain tax violations under the Tax - General Article to the Comptroller, which may require additional compliance staff and could lead to increased tax assessments and collections.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Commission to Advance Lithium-Ion Battery Safety in Maryland. Requires the Office of the State Fire Marshal to provide staff for the Commission. Directs the Commission to study best practices for preventing, detecting, and suppressing lithium-ion battery fires. Requires recommendations regarding battery reuse, recycling, decommissioning, and extended producer responsibility. Mandates an interim report by December 1, 2024, and a final report by December 1, 2025.
qa_results.responsible_party: Commission to Advance Lithium-Ion Battery Safety in Maryland; Office of the State Fire Marshal
qa_results.stakeholders: Lithium-ion battery manufacturers, battery recyclers, vehicle dismantlers, electric utilities, first responders, and emergency response personnel
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $64,700 in FY 2025 and $27,600 in FY 2026 for the Office of the State Fire Marshal to hire one contractual position to staff the Commission. State revenues are not affected, and local government finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the State Fire Marshal, which operates under the Maryland Department of State Police, is designated as the primary entity responsible for staffing the Commission and incurs a direct fiscal impact for contractual personnel to manage operations and reporting.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a new temporary advisory and study body, the Commission to Advance Lithium–Ion Battery Safety in Maryland, tasked with studying safety, fire prevention, and recycling standards and submitting reports.

The Director of MEA is tasked with appointing three commission members (including an MEA representative and battery manufacturing industry representatives), and the commission's work directly intersects with clean energy and grid-scale storage safety.

The Secretary of the Environment appoints a member to the commission, and the commission's duties include examining recycling facility fire safety, battery reuse and recycling, and the viability of extended producer responsibility.
The Chairman of the PSC appoints a representative to the commission, which is tasked with reviewing lithium-ion battery safety in utility applications and grid-scale storage.
The Secretary of Natural Resources appoints a representative to the commission from the Power Plant Research Project (PPRP), which is housed within the department.
The commission is statutorily required to submit its final report of findings and recommendations to the Governor by December 1, 2025.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters postelection procedures for canvassing, reviewing, and certifying election results across Maryland. Requires local boards of canvassers to investigate errors in election documents in consultation with the State Administrator. Authorizes state election authorities to reject inaccurate canvass statements when supported by clear and convincing evidence. Authorizes members of the Board of State Canvassers to appoint designated deputies to serve in their stead. Requires the Governor to issue certificates of electors and publish election proclamations on the State Board website.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Elections; State Administrator of Elections; Board of State Canvassers; local boards of canvassers; Governor
qa_results.stakeholders: Registered voters, candidates for public office, presidential electors, local election officials, and members of the Board of State Canvassers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly governs postelection procedures, requiring the State Administrator to consult with local boards of canvassers on record errors, review dissents, submit dissents to the Board of State Canvassers, and transmit certified results. It also grants the State Board authority to review and reject inaccurate canvass statements and adopt regulations governing election result certification.

The bill specifically alters the statutory duties of the Governor upon receipt of election returns, requiring the Governor to ascertain and enumerate votes consistent with returns received, issue and transmit certificates of electors under federal law (3 U.S.C. § 5), and issue proclamations.

The Secretary of State is a statutory member of the Board of State Canvassers, and the bill modifies the Board's procedures and explicitly authorizes the Secretary of State to appoint the Deputy Secretary of State as a designee to serve on the Board.

The Comptroller serves as a member of the Board of State Canvassers, and the bill alters the Board's procedures and explicitly authorizes the Comptroller to appoint the Chief Deputy Comptroller to serve on the Board.

The State Treasurer is a member of the Board of State Canvassers, and the bill updates provisions regarding the designation of the deputy treasurer to serve on the Board and alters the Board's canvassing schedule and duties.

The Attorney General serves as a member of the Board of State Canvassers, and the bill modifies the Board's procedures and explicitly authorizes the Attorney General to appoint the Deputy Attorney General to serve on the Board.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the School Mapping Data Program in the Maryland Center for School Safety. Requires the Interagency Commission on School Construction to adopt uniform facility mapping standards for public schools. Authorizes local school systems, in consultation with local law enforcement agencies, to apply for program grants. Authorizes the School Safety Subcabinet to award mapping data grants from the Safe Schools Fund. Requires public record custodians to deny inspection of school mapping data under the Public Information Act.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Center for School Safety; School Safety Subcabinet; Interagency Commission on School Construction
qa_results.stakeholders: Local school systems, public charter schools, local law enforcement agencies, first responders, and Maryland public school students and staff
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No net impact on State finances, as agencies implement the program within existing budgeted resources. Using the Safe Schools Fund for mapping grants may reduce funding available for other authorized school safety programs. Local school system revenues and expenditures increase only to the extent that systems apply for and receive grants.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the School Mapping Data Program within the Maryland Center for School Safety (MCSS) and authorizes its School Safety Subcabinet to administer grants from the Safe Schools Fund to local school systems.
The bill mandates that the Interagency Commission on School Construction adopt uniform facility mapping standards for public schools and consult with MCSS on program compliance.

The Maryland Center for School Safety is housed as an independent unit within the Maryland State Department of Education, and the program directly impacts public school systems overseen by the department.

The Maryland Department of Emergency Management is explicitly granted statutory authority to inspect and utilize school emergency plans and mapping data in the performance of official emergency response duties.
The Department of State Police is designated as an authorized entity to inspect school emergency mapping data and plans for official public safety duties, and serves on the School Safety Subcabinet.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The department is specifically authorized by the bill under the Public Information Act exception to inspect school safety evaluations, emergency plans, and mapping data in the performance of official duties.
The Comptroller is statutorily designated to account for the Safe Schools Fund in conjunction with the Executive Director of the Maryland Center for School Safety.
The State Treasurer holds and invests the moneys of the Safe Schools Fund, which is authorized to disburse grants for the School Mapping Data Program.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Open-Source Phonics Matching Grant Program within the Maryland State Department of Education. Authorizes qualifying nonprofit organizations, higher education institutions, and public libraries to apply for matching grants. Requires funded materials to enable adults to tutor students and align with the science of reading. Directs the Department to periodically review learning materials and report biennially on program effectiveness. Requires the Governor to include an annual appropriation of $150,000 in the State budget.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: Nonprofit organizations, institutions of higher education, and public libraries producing or distributing open-source phonics materials, adult tutors, and Maryland students
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $150,000 annually beginning in FY 2025. Funding is discretionary in FY 2025 and becomes a mandated appropriation beginning in FY 2026. Local school system operations and finances are not directly affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 475 establishes the Open-Source Phonics Matching Grant Program within the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE). MSDE is responsible for administering the program, processing applications, disbursing grants, reviewing phonics materials for alignment with the science of reading, and reporting biennially to the General Assembly.
The bill mandates an annual appropriation of $150,000 in the state budget for the grant program, which impacts DBM's budget formulation and fiscal planning responsibilities.
The bill mandates that the Governor include a $150,000 appropriation for the Open-Source Phonics Matching Grant Program in the annual budget bill.

Public libraries are explicitly defined as eligible 'open-source phonics organizations' authorized to apply for and receive matching grant funds, and the Maryland State Library Agency was consulted on the implementation of the bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Exempts forensic genetic genealogical DNA analysis and search from statutory restrictions when identifying specified minors. Applies the exemption to searches conducted solely to identify a deceased individual under 18 years of age. Extends the exemption to missing individuals under age 18 reported to a State law enforcement agency. Relieves qualifying searches from standard judicial authorization and third-party consent requirements. Takes effect October 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of State Police; local law enforcement agencies; Judiciary of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Law enforcement agencies, genetic genealogists, and families of deceased or missing children
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local finances are not anticipated to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary state law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police investigates missing persons and unidentified deceased individuals. The bill directly impacts their investigative procedures by exempting forensic genetic genealogical DNA searches conducted for identifying deceased or missing minors from standard Title 17 judicial authorization and protocol requirements.

Under existing law, forensic genetic genealogical DNA analysis and search (FGGS) generally requires judicial authorization, affidavits, and regular progress reports submitted to the court. Exempting searches conducted to identify deceased or missing minors reduces the need for court-issued orders and reporting in these specific circumstances.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Office of the Public Defender monitors changes to the Criminal Procedure Article and the handling, retention, and chain of custody of forensic DNA and genealogical records, which may intersect with criminal investigations or juvenile proceedings.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel on statutory interpretation and criminal procedure to state agencies and law enforcement entities regarding compliance with DNA search and privacy statutes.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes a person to receive a raffle ticket for each antlerless deer hunted during certain qualifying raffle programs. Limits eligibility to raffle programs held during the month of January. Requires the raffle program to have the hunting of antlerless deer as its objective. Requires the program to have operated at least once between January 1, 2020, and January 30, 2024. Exempts qualifying raffle participants from general statutory prohibitions against bartering or exchanging wild game mammals.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
qa_results.stakeholders: Deer hunters, organizers of qualifying antlerless deer hunting raffle programs, agricultural businesses, and hunting equipment retailers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State or local operations or finances. It may have a potential meaningful economic impact on small businesses, including hunting supply retailers and farms.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Natural Resources Article regarding hunting and the barter or exchange of game mammals, specifically creating an exception to allow hunters to receive raffle tickets for hunting antlerless deer during qualifying programs. The Department of Natural Resources is the primary agency responsible for managing wildlife populations, establishing hunting seasons, and enforcing state hunting and conservation laws.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires sellers of residential property located within one mile of a National Priorities List Superfund site to provide a disclosure addendum. Mandates that the addendum identify the Superfund site and provide specified U.S. Environmental Protection Agency website links. Requires the addendum to include the federal definition of an NPL Superfund site. Authorizes buyers to void the contract of sale within five days after signing and dating the contract upon written notice. Requires a full refund of any money paid to the seller upon contract rescission. Takes effect October 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Seller of residential real property
qa_results.stakeholders: Buyers and sellers of residential real property located within 1 mile of a National Priorities List Superfund site
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDE administers Maryland's Superfund program, which oversees the assessment and remediation of hazardous waste and contaminated sites, including those designated on or evaluated for the National Priorities List.

The Maryland Department of Labor regulates real estate brokers, salespersons, and transactions through the Maryland Real Estate Commission, which oversees adherence to statutory real estate contract disclosure requirements.
The Office of the Attorney General enforces consumer protection statutes related to deceptive trade practices and disclosure mandates in residential real estate transactions.
The Judiciary and state court system may handle civil disputes and litigation arising from real estate contract rescissions, failure to provide mandated disclosures, or refund claims under the bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the State income tax subtraction modification for donations to qualified charitable entities through tax year 2026. Allows individuals and corporations to subtract up to $1,000 in eligible donations from income. Applies to donations of diapers, hygiene products for infants or children, and feminine personal hygiene products. Includes cash specifically designated to purchase those qualifying hygiene items. Requires donors to file proof of donation value and the entity's name with their tax return. Sunsets the subtraction modification on June 30, 2027.
qa_results.responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Taxpayers who donate eligible hygiene products or designated cash, and qualified charitable entities including diaper banks, homeless shelters, domestic violence shelters, and religious organizations.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues decrease by an estimated $250,000 annually in FY 2025 through FY 2027. Local income tax revenues decrease by an estimated $165,000 annually across the same period. Small additional revenue reductions may affect special funds from corporate income tax filings.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 490 directly extends the income tax subtraction modification for donations to diaper banks and other qualified charitable entities through tax year 2026. The Comptroller of Maryland is the primary implementing agency tasked with administering the tax subtraction, adopting regulations, processing tax filings, and managing the registration of qualified charitable entities.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Baltimore County School Board Nominating Commission to publish candidate names on its website before interviews begin. Requires Commission meetings involving action on a candidate for appointment to be open to the public. Mandates that meetings involving candidate interviews or deliberations be held without the public in attendance. Requires the Commission to record all meetings held without the public in attendance. Requires the Commission to provide a recording for public inspection within 48 hours of receiving a request.
qa_results.responsible_party: Baltimore County School Board Nominating Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: candidates for appointment to the Baltimore County Board of Education, the Baltimore County School Board Nominating Commission, and Baltimore County residents
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State effect. Baltimore County can record meetings and fulfill public inspection requests using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Baltimore County School Board Nominating Commission's statutory purpose is to select and recommend nominees to the Governor for gubernatorial appointment to the Baltimore County Board of Education. While the procedural changes apply directly to the Commission, the resulting recommendations directly inform the Governor's executive appointment responsibilities.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in managing appointments to state and local boards and commissions, including reviewing candidate slates submitted for gubernatorial appointment to local boards of education.

The Maryland State Department of Education oversees the state's public education system and the governance structures codified in the Education Article of the Maryland Annotated Code, although the bill places administrative requirements directly on the local nominating commission.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals force or the threat of force as a necessary element of second-degree rape. Establishes that engaging in vaginal intercourse or a sexual act without consent constitutes second-degree rape. Defines consent as the clear and voluntary agreement to engage in vaginal intercourse, a sexual act, or sexual contact. Requires determining consent based on the totality of circumstances, including words and conduct of both parties. Clarifies that relationship history, manner of dress, and submission from fear or coercion do not constitute consent. Requires the Maryland Judiciary to submit annual reports on sexual crime charges and convictions through April 2029.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary
qa_results.stakeholders: Victims of sexual offenses, individuals accused of sexual crimes, defense attorneys, and state prosecutors
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by at least $7,000 in FY 2025 for Judiciary information technology costs. General fund expenditures may also increase significantly for the Office of the Public Defender and the Division of Correction depending on the bill's impact on prosecutions, convictions, and incarceration. Local government operations and finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill statutorily mandates that the Maryland Judiciary compile and submit an annual report to the General Assembly regarding charges and convictions for specified sexual crimes disaggregated by modality, jurisdiction, and offender demographics. The fiscal note identifies direct IT expenditures for the Judiciary to implement these reporting requirements.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The alteration of the elements of second-degree rape by removing the requirement of force or threat of force is anticipated to increase caseloads and operational costs for the agency in representing indigent defendants.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters the statutory elements of felony second-degree rape, which may lead to increased convictions and longer sentences served in State correctional facilities managed by DPSCS.

As the State's primary law enforcement agency, MSP investigates allegations of sexual assault and rape and will need to apply the redefined legal standards of consent and second-degree rape in investigations and charging decisions.
The OAG represents the State in criminal appeals, which will involve defending convictions obtained under the revised statutory definition of consent and altered elements of second-degree rape.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases the fee for a nonresident sika deer stamp from $25 to $200. Maintains the existing fee for a resident sika deer stamp at $10. Requires nonresident hunters to pay the higher fee before hunting sika deer in Maryland. Takes effect July 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
qa_results.stakeholders: Nonresident hunters seeking to hunt sika deer in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues to the Wildlife Management and Protection Fund increase by an estimated $332,200 annually beginning in FY 2025. Federal fund revenues from conservation matching grants increase by an estimated $996,500 annually beginning in FY 2026. State expenditures are not directly affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Natural Resources (DNR) administers hunting licensing and wildlife conservation in Maryland. The bill increases the nonresident sika deer stamp fee from $25 to $200, which directly generates an estimated $332,200 in annual special fund revenue for DNR's Wildlife Management and Protection Fund and enables approximately $996,500 in annual federal matching grant funds for DNR's Wildlife and Heritage Service.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the annual reporting requirements for the Access to Counsel in Evictions Program administered by the Maryland Legal Services Corporation. Requires the Corporation to report program data to the Governor and General Assembly annually by August 31. Mandates reporting on attorney payments per case, geographic case distribution, and case disposition data. Requires reporting the allocation of State and federal funds to each designated organization. Requires reporting the number of covered individuals provided legal representation for multiple cases. Terminates these reporting provisions on June 30, 2027.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Legal Services Corporation
qa_results.stakeholders: Covered residential tenants, designated legal services organizations, and attorneys participating in the Access to Counsel in Evictions Program
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No direct effect on State or local finances. The Maryland Legal Services Corporation can administer the revised reporting requirements using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates that the Maryland Legal Services Corporation submit an expanded annual report detailing the performance, financials, and case outcomes of the Access to Counsel in Evictions Program directly to the Governor by August 31 each year.

The Access to Counsel in Evictions Program operates within the state court system on eviction, holdover, and breach of lease proceedings overseen by the Judiciary. The Administrative Office of the Courts was consulted as an information source regarding court case tracking and dispositions.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires each owner of a private dental office to designate a licensed dentist as the supervising dentist. Requires the supervising dentist to complete registration required by the State Board of Dental Examiners. Mandates that the supervising dentist be responsible for all infection control activities within the office. Requires the owner to immediately designate an interim supervising dentist if the supervisor relinquishes responsibility. Authorizes the Board to charge a fee for registering a supervising dentist. Excludes the statutory responsibilities of a supervising dentist from the definition of practicing dentistry.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Dental Examiners
qa_results.stakeholders: Owners of private dental offices and licensed dentists
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State Board of Dental Examiners special fund revenues increase by an estimated $1,500 in fiscal 2025 and $2,000 annually thereafter from registration fees when supervising dentists change. Board expenditures are not affected as implementation can be handled with existing budgeted resources. No local fiscal effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill regulates infection control activities in private dental offices and requires registration of supervising dentists through the State Board of Dental Examiners, which is a regulatory licensing board within the Maryland Department of Health.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases the maximum civil fine that a charter county may impose to enforce local laws from $1,000 to $5,000. Increases the maximum criminal fine from $1,000 to $5,000 for enforcing an ordinance, resolution, bylaw, or regulation. Maintains the maximum imprisonment penalty of six months for criminal violations. Takes effect October 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Charter county governments
qa_results.stakeholders: Charter counties and individuals or entities subject to enforcement of charter county ordinances, resolutions, bylaws, or regulations
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not materially affected. Charter county revenues may increase to the extent counties exercise authority to raise civil and criminal fines up to the new $5,000 limit, but the overall fiscal impact cannot be reliably estimated. Local expenditures are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Administrative Office of the Courts supports the Maryland Judicial Branch. The Judiciary provided input on the bill noting that an increase in maximum criminal fines from $1,000 to $5,000 could potentially result in an increase in demands for jury trials in local criminal enforcement cases, though no significant operational or fiscal impact is anticipated.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Governor to appropriate $1,000,000 annually to the Maryland Department of Planning for the Maryland Humanities Council. Directs the Council to fund the Marilyn Hatza Memorial Strengthening the Humanities Investment in Nonprofits for Equity Grantmaking Initiative. Requires the Council to provide general operating grants to small and mid-size humanities, arts, cultural, and educational nonprofit organizations. Mandates that the Council consider geographic and racial diversity when awarding one-time or multiyear grants. Requires the Council to submit an annual report on grant distribution and outcomes to the Department by December 31.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Planning; Maryland Humanities Council
qa_results.stakeholders: Small and mid-size humanities, arts, cultural, and educational nonprofit organizations in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $1.0 million annually beginning in fiscal 2025 to fund the grant program. Revenues are not affected. The Maryland Department of Planning can implement the bill with existing budgeted resources, and local finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly names the Department of Planning as the administering agency to receive the $1,000,000 annual state appropriation, disburse the grant to the Maryland Humanities Council, and receive annual accountability reports from the Council.

As the state agency responsible for developing the Governor's annual budget and managing state appropriations, DBM is directly involved in incorporating and overseeing the authorized $1,000,000 annual general fund appropriation.
The bill explicitly authorizes the Governor to include a $1,000,000 appropriation in the annual executive budget bill for the SHINE Grantmaking Initiative.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes Morgan State University and St. Mary’s College of Maryland to use webinar, computer-based, or online sexual harassment training. Applies this option to mandatory sexual harassment prevention training for employees. Requires any such training to include an evaluative component. Mandates that the evaluative component ensure employee engagement and assess comprehension of training objectives. Takes effect October 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Morgan State University; St. Mary's College of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Employees and supervisors at Morgan State University and St. Mary's College of Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are unaffected as changes can be handled with existing budgeted resources. The bill has no effect on State revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 506 specifically authorizes Morgan State University to provide required biennial sexual harassment prevention training to its employees via webinar, computer-based, or online formats with an evaluative component.

House Bill 506 specifically authorizes St. Mary's College of Maryland to provide required biennial sexual harassment prevention training to its employees via webinar, computer-based, or online formats with an evaluative component.

DBM serves as the central personnel agency for the State of Maryland and oversees state employee personnel policies, training standards, and statewide Equal Employment Opportunity compliance enforcement.
The Maryland Commission on Civil Rights coordinates with state agencies and higher education institutions to implement required employee sexual harassment prevention training standards.

The bill amends the subsection of the Annotated Code that previously applied exclusively to the University System of Maryland to extend the same online training flexibility to Morgan State University and St. Mary's College of Maryland.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the governing bodies of Allegany County, Garrett County, and their municipalities to grant a property tax credit. Limits the credit to newly constructed residential dwellings occupied as the purchaser's principal residence. Requires qualifying dwellings to have building permits issued on or after June 1, 2024. Requires dwellings to feature a qualifying sprinkler system, on-site sewage disposal system, or fixed broadband internet connectivity. Caps the property tax credit at $10,000 over up to five taxable years. Authorizes local governing bodies to establish credit amounts, additional eligibility criteria, and application procedures.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governing Body of Allegany County; Governing Body of Garrett County; Municipal corporations located in Allegany County and Garrett County
qa_results.stakeholders: Purchasers of newly constructed residential homes in Allegany County and Garrett County; governing bodies of Allegany County, Garrett County, and municipalities within those counties
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on State revenues or expenditures. Local property tax revenues in Allegany County, Garrett County, and qualifying municipalities decrease beginning as early as fiscal 2025 to the extent the optional credit is enacted; local expenditures are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill relates to incentives for the construction and purchase of housing and residential development in Maryland. While provisions requiring the Department of Housing and Community Development to administer a state income tax credit were amended out of the final enacted legislation, the subject matter directly relates to the department's core mission of supporting homeownership and housing access, and the department served as an information source on the bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands the definition of abuse to include labor trafficking of a child by any individual for child protection proceedings. Extends child abuse and neglect reporting and investigation requirements to suspected child labor trafficking cases. Requires local departments of social services to refer suspected child labor trafficking victims to regional navigators. Broadens the Safe Harbor Regional Navigator Grant Program to serve youth victims of labor trafficking. Mandates that grantee services coordinated under the program include housing as a basic living need.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Human Services; local departments of social services
qa_results.stakeholders: Child victims of labor trafficking, local departments of social services, mandatory reporters of child abuse, and victim service providers under the Safe Harbor Regional Navigator Grant Program.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local operations or finances. Although it expands the scope of the Safe Harbor Regional Navigator Grant Program to include labor trafficking victims, it does not mandate additional State grant funding.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Local departments of social services must investigate reports of child abuse/neglect involving labor trafficking and refer suspected victims to regional navigators. Additionally, DHS is statutorily required to report annually on child labor trafficking reports, dispositions, and referrals.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Administers the Safe Harbor Regional Navigator Grant Program, which this bill expands to encompass services, grant allocations, coordination, and biennial reporting for youth victims of labor trafficking.
The bill alters the definition of abuse to include labor trafficking for Child in Need of Assistance (CINA) cases, directly impacting proceedings adjudicated in the state's juvenile courts.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Represents children and indigent parents in CINA proceedings affected by the expanded abuse definition, and is explicitly named as a partner entity coordinating with the Safe Harbor Regional Navigator Grant Program.
DJS is explicitly enumerated in the statute as an interagency partner coordinating with the Safe Harbor Regional Navigator Grant Program to identify and serve youth victims of trafficking.
Receives required annual reports from DHS and biennial evaluation reports regarding the Safe Harbor Regional Navigator Grant Program's services to trafficking victims.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands eligibility for funding under the Business Facade Improvement Program to include certain community development organizations. Requires eligible community development organizations to serve at least one sustainable community and apply for program funds. Directs the Department of Housing and Community Development to develop application processes and award criteria for applicants. Requires recipient community development organizations to distribute grants to qualified businesses in sustainable communities. Mandates that recipient organizations establish a grant application process and rating criteria for qualified businesses.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development
qa_results.stakeholders: Community development organizations, political subdivisions with sustainable communities, and qualified businesses seeking facade improvements
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected, as the Department of Housing and Community Development can administer the expansion with existing budgeted resources. Local governments may receive fewer funds to the extent that community development organizations apply for and receive program funding.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the Business Facade Improvement Program administered by the Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD), requiring the department to expand eligible funding recipients to include community development organizations and update its application and evaluation criteria accordingly.
The bill reenacts a statutory provision requiring the Governor to include an annual appropriation of $5,000,000 for the Business Facade Improvement Program in the state budget bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires commercial fish packers, fish dealers, and licensed commercial fishers to submit required reports under Department of Natural Resources regulations. Replaces statutory provisions requiring paper forms prescribed or provided by the Department. Requires individuals holding an angler's license for nontidal waters to submit any reports required under Department regulations. Requires individuals holding a Chesapeake Bay and coastal sport fishing license to submit any reports required under Department regulations. Takes effect July 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
qa_results.stakeholders: Commercial fish packers, fish dealers, licensed commercial fishers, and recreational anglers holding nontidal or Chesapeake Bay and coastal sport fishing licenses
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No direct effect on State or local finances. Any future costs associated with expanding electronic reporting systems will depend on how regulations are implemented.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 512 directly affects the Department of Natural Resources (DNR) by granting it regulatory authority over reporting requirements for commercial fish packers, dealers, commercial harvesters, and recreational anglers licensed under the Natural Resources Article.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters civil penalties and revenue distribution for violations recorded by highway work zone speed control systems. Sets the civil penalty at $80 on June 1, 2024. Establishes a tiered penalty structure ranging from $60 to $500 starting January 1, 2025. Doubles civil penalties when workers are present in the work zone at the time of the violation. Distributes net camera revenues between the Department of State Police and the Transportation Trust Fund. Authorizes local political subdivisions to implement work zone speed control systems and retain fine revenues.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of State Police; State Highway Administration; Maryland Department of Transportation; District Court
qa_results.stakeholders: motorists traveling through Maryland highway work zones, highway construction and maintenance workers, State and local law enforcement agencies
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues increase by an estimated $15.8 million in FY 2025 due to higher and tiered penalties, while special fund expenditures increase by $4.2 million for system expansion and administration, yielding a net state impact of $11.7 million. Local government revenues and expenditures also increase as political subdivisions deploy work zone speed control systems.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: SHA is a primary implementing agency for the work zone speed control systems program, receives significant fine revenue for program administration and system preservation, jointly adopts program regulations with the Maryland State Police, and must submit annual reports on testing new technologies.

MSP is a primary agency operating and enforcing work zone speed control systems, receives dedicated cost-recovery funding and 25% of remaining fine revenues for replacement vehicles and outfitting equipment, and jointly adopts regulations with SHA.

MDOT is the parent department of SHA and MVA; 75% of net revenues are deposited into MDOT's Transportation Trust Fund for highway/work zone safety and system preservation, and MDOT is statutorily required to submit an annual expenditure report to the Governor and General Assembly.
The District Court of Maryland (supported by the AOC) prescribes the uniform citation forms for work zone speed control systems and processes and collects fine revenues from contested citations.
The Comptroller is statutorily mandated to receive civil fines collected from State-controlled work zone speed control systems and distribute them to the designated special fund.
MVA handles vehicle registration holds and flag fees for individuals who fail to pay or contest work zone speed control citations.
The bill represents an Administration priority stemming from executive workgroup recommendations and requires SHA and MDOT to submit recurring annual reports directly to the Governor.

The legislation directly results from recommendations of the Governor's Work Zone Safety Work Group chaired by the Lieutenant Governor, and the Lt. Governor's Office prepared the small business impact statement for the bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Workgroup to Study the Fiscal and Operational Viability of Public–Private Partnerships for Calvert County Public Schools. Requires the Calvert County Board of Education to provide staff for the Workgroup. Directs the Workgroup to study public–private partnerships for financing, constructing, maintaining, and operating county schools. Requires recommendations on using partnerships for new school construction and lower-cost school rehabilitation. Mandates a final report to specified State and local officials by December 31, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Calvert County Board of Education; Workgroup to Study the Fiscal and Operational Viability of Public–Private Partnerships for Calvert County Public Schools
qa_results.stakeholders: Calvert County Public Schools, Calvert County public school students and personnel, and Calvert County taxpayers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State operations and finances are not materially affected. Calvert County Public Schools expenditures may increase by an indeterminate amount for temporary staffing or consultant services to support the Workgroup; local revenues are unaffected. Specific cost estimates are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly designates the Chair of the Interagency Commission on School Construction (or the Chair's designee) as a member of the Workgroup and requires the Workgroup to submit its findings and recommendations to the Commission by December 31, 2024.

The bill designates the Executive Director of the Maryland Stadium Authority (or the Executive Director's designee) as a member of the Workgroup studying public-private partnerships for school construction.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a temporary state advisory workgroup—the Workgroup to Study the Fiscal and Operational Viability of Public-Private Partnerships for Calvert County Public Schools—which operates until June 30, 2025.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes any person to submit a complaint alleging an advertising violation to the State Real Estate Commission anonymously. Eliminates the requirement that an advertising violation complaint be made under oath. Requires every complaint alleging an advertising violation to be accompanied by documentary or other evidence. Maintains the requirement that all complaints be in writing and state specifically the underlying facts. Takes effect October 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Real Estate Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Licensed real estate professionals and individuals filing complaints alleging real estate advertising violations
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State finances or operations. Additional staff may be required if the State Real Estate Commission receives a meaningful number of additional complaints. There is no local fiscal effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Real Estate Commission is housed within the Maryland Department of Labor's Division of Occupational and Professional Licensing. The bill directly alters complaint procedures regarding advertising violations handled by the Commission.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the State Department of Education and the Maryland Department of Health jointly to develop State guidelines for student telehealth appointments. Applies these guidelines to appointments during the school day on public middle and high school premises. Directs the State Board of Education to adopt the guidelines. Requires each county board of education to adopt and implement a student telehealth policy before the 2025–2026 school year. Mandates publishing the policy in student handbooks and making school personnel aware of its requirements. Clarifies that schools are not required to construct new space or building additions.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education; Maryland Department of Health; State Board of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: public middle and high school students, parents, school personnel, and health care providers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $100,000 in fiscal 2025 only for contractual support to develop guidelines. Local school boards can adopt and implement policies using existing resources, though local school systems may face operational space and staffing challenges.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) is designated as a primary implementing agency alongside the Maryland Department of Health to jointly develop State guidelines for school health services regarding student telehealth access, adopt the guidelines through the State Board of Education, and provide technical assistance to local boards.

The Maryland Department of Health is explicitly tasked alongside the Department of Education with jointly developing State guidelines for school health services regarding student participation in telehealth appointments during the school day.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the restriction on orphans' court judges practicing law during a term of office. Repeals existing county-specific exceptions to the practice restriction. Prohibits an orphans' court judge from acting as an attorney in matters related to estate administration or minor guardianship. Prohibits judges from preparing estate plans or estate planning documents that might come within the court's jurisdiction. Applies this unified prohibition across all Maryland counties and Baltimore City.
qa_results.responsible_party: Judiciary (Administrative Office of the Courts); Orphans' Court
qa_results.stakeholders: Judges of the orphans' court, attorneys in Maryland, and individuals seeking estate planning or estate administration services
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Administrative Office of the Courts provides administrative, legal, and operational support to Maryland's judicial branch, which includes the oversight and policy administration concerning the state's courts and judges such as Orphans' Court judges.

The Register of Wills serves as the Clerk to the Orphans' Court and oversees the administration of decedents' estates, the exact subject matter and judicial body governed by this bill's practice restrictions.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals the requirement for the Maryland Parole Commission to assess a monthly $50 supervision fee on parolees. Eliminates the Division of Parole and Probation's authority to require parolees to pay for drug or alcohol abuse testing. Abolishes statutory provisions allowing parole revocation based on failure to pay supervision or testing fees. Retains supervision fees and testing payment requirements for individuals placed on probation by a court. Takes effect October 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Parole Commission; Division of Parole and Probation; Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
qa_results.stakeholders: individuals on parole or mandatory supervision under the Division of Parole and Probation
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues decrease by at least $53,931 in FY 2025 and by at least $71,908 annually thereafter from the repeal of supervision fees. General fund expenditures increase, potentially significantly, starting in FY 2025 to fund drug and alcohol testing contracts previously offset by supervisees. Central Collection Unit special fund revenues and expenditures also decrease. Local finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS is the primary implementing agency. The bill directly impacts two of its units, the Maryland Parole Commission and the Division of Parole and Probation, by repealing parole supervision fees and supervisee payments for drug and alcohol testing, resulting in reduced fee collections and increased department expenditures to cover vendor testing contracts.

The Central Collection Unit (CCU), housed within DBM, will experience decreases in both special fund revenues and operating expenditures because unpaid parole supervision fees will no longer be referred to CCU for debt collection.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the termination date of the Live Near Your School program and a related homebuyer assistance program. Continues the programs within the Community Development Administration through September 30, 2030. Authorizes financial assistance for degree-seeking students and recent graduates purchasing homes near their public institutions. Removes proposed statutory budget mandates for program funding from fiscal 2026 through 2030. Takes effect July 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Community Development Administration; Department of Housing and Community Development
qa_results.stakeholders: current students and recent graduates of Maryland public institutions of higher education purchasing homes near their schools
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on State or local finances or operations because both programs remain inactive absent funding or institutional partners.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) by extending the statutory authorization and termination date of the Live Near Your School program and related homebuyer assistance program administered by the Community Development Administration within DHCD until September 30, 2030.

Under the extended statutory provisions of the Live Near Your School and homebuyer assistance programs, public institutions of higher education, including USM member institutions, are authorized to coordinate with DHCD and provide matching funds for students and recent graduates purchasing homes.

As an independent public institution of higher education, Morgan State University is eligible to participate as an institutional partner and provide matching assistance funds under the extended programs.

As a public institution of higher education, St. Mary's College of Maryland is eligible to coordinate with DHCD and provide matching funds for qualifying students or recent graduates purchasing homes near the college under the extended program.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires local jurisdictions to allow increased density and mixed-use development for qualified affordable housing projects. Prohibits local legislative bodies from barring qualifying manufactured homes or modular dwellings in single-family residential zones. Limits the number of local public hearings that may be required for qualified projects. Prohibits local jurisdictions from imposing unreasonable development limitations on qualified projects. Establishes the Historic Property Revitalization Director within the Department of Housing and Community Development. Requires developers of projects in nonresidential zones to obtain department approval for a public health impact assessment.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
qa_results.stakeholders: affordable housing developers, low- and moderate-income households, buyers and manufacturers of modular and manufactured housing, and local zoning authorities
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $73,700 in FY 2025 and up to $148,100 by FY 2029 to fund the Historic Property Revitalization Director position. Local government expenditures may increase or accelerate if higher density accelerates infrastructure strain, alongside potential administrative costs for project reviews, partly offset by development-related fees.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DHCD is the primary implementing agency for the bill, which establishes the Historic Property Revitalization Director within DHCD, requires DHCD to review and approve public health impact assessments for certain qualified affordable housing projects, and utilizes DHCD's Multifamily Rental Financing Program Guide standards.

The bill explicitly requires the newly established Historic Property Revitalization Director to work directly with the DGS Office of Real Estate during the disposition process of relevant state-owned property.

The bill statutorily tasks the Historic Property Revitalization Director to collaborate with the Department of Commerce and the Smart Growth Subcabinet to identify state and federal financing mechanisms and programs to support property redevelopment.

The bill impacts statewide land use and zoning policy and interfaces with historic property preservation and the Smart Growth Subcabinet, both of which are core functions housed or coordinated within the Maryland Department of Planning.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
