agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires the new Director to support the work of and regularly consult with the Smart Growth Subcabinet on property inventories, stabilization studies, economic prospects, and annual reporting to the General Assembly.

The bill establishes qualified project density bonuses specifically around passenger rail stations (including MARC, Light RailLink, and Metro SubwayLink), directly impacting transit-oriented development around MDOT infrastructure.

MTA operates the MARC train lines, Baltimore Metro SubwayLink, and Baltimore Light RailLink stations specifically designated in the bill to determine eligibility for transit-oriented affordable housing density increases.
This is a key Administration priority bill sponsored on behalf of the Governor to address the state's housing shortage by adjusting state land disposition and local zoning density standards.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires each public institution of higher education to adopt a student withdrawal policy for extenuating circumstances. Defines extenuating circumstances to include illness, injury, hospitalization, and mental health and wellness. Mandates a policy provision refunding tuition and fees paid by the student for the semester of withdrawal. Applies when extenuating circumstances inhibit the student's ability to acquire an education, as defined in policy. Takes effect July 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland public institutions of higher education
qa_results.stakeholders: Students at Maryland public institutions of higher education who withdraw due to extenuating circumstances, as well as public four-year institutions and local community colleges.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local higher education revenues decrease, potentially significantly, due to refunding tuition and fees to qualifying withdrawing students. Expenditures are not materially affected as institutions can develop policies using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: USM and its constituent institutions are directly subject to the bill's requirement to adopt an extenuating circumstances withdrawal policy and provide refunds for tuition and fees, which could result in a significant decrease in higher education revenues.

As an independent public four-year university, Morgan State University is directly required to establish the withdrawal and refund policy mandated by the bill and may experience reduced tuition and fee revenue.

As a public honors college and independent state agency, St. Mary's College of Maryland must adopt the required withdrawal policy and issue tuition and fee refunds for qualifying extenuating circumstances, directly impacting institutional revenue.

MHEC serves as the statewide regulatory and coordinating body for Maryland's public and private institutions of higher education and provided information regarding institutional policies and implementation.
Serves as the coordinating and regulatory agency establishing statewide postsecondary policies for Maryland's public institutions of higher education affected by the withdrawal and refund mandates.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the governing body of Anne Arundel County to establish a Student Loan Assistance Repayment Program for Educators. Requires the program to assist eligible Anne Arundel County Public School System educators with higher education loan repayment. Limits eligibility to educators who earn below county-set income limits and commit to at least five years of service. Requires the Anne Arundel County Public School System to administer the program. Mandates annual county funding separate from the county appropriation to the school board's operating budget.
qa_results.responsible_party: Anne Arundel County Public School System; Anne Arundel County
qa_results.stakeholders: Educators employed by the Anne Arundel County Public School System, including classroom teachers, education support professionals, education-related service providers, and certified specialists
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state fiscal effect. Anne Arundel County expenditures increase if the county chooses to establish and fund the program, with specific costs depending on annual county appropriations. Local revenues are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill defines eligible educators under the local student loan repayment program to include specialists eligible for certification from the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE), which oversees Maryland's public school systems and teacher certification.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Department of Human Services to establish and maintain a decentralized supply of new luggage for children in foster care. Mandates that the department provide new luggage to a child entering, moving placements within, or exiting foster care. Prohibits the department from using disposable bags or trash bags to transport any items of a child in foster care. Specifies that provided luggage becomes the child's property and cannot be reclaimed by the department or retained by foster parents. Requires the department to report annually by December 1 to the General Assembly regarding luggage inventory and bag usage.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Human Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Children in foster care, foster parents, and local departments of social services
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by at least $120,500 in FY 2025 to purchase luggage and update the MD THINK reporting platform. Ongoing annual luggage expenditures are estimated at at least $84,500 beginning in FY 2026, which may be offset by donations. Local departments of social services can implement the bill with existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 542 directly mandates the Department of Human Services (DHS) to establish, maintain, and distribute a decentralized supply of new luggage for children in foster care, prohibits the use of trash or disposable bags, requires recordkeeping and annual reporting to the General Assembly, and results in direct general fund expenditures for luggage purchases and MD THINK IT platform modifications.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes a five-year statute of limitations for prosecuting the crime of sexual extortion. Establishes a 10-year statute of limitations for prosecuting the crime of stalking. Authorizes the State to institute a criminal prosecution for revenge porn at any time. Classifies revenge porn as a penitentiary misdemeanor for purposes of in banc review under the Maryland Constitution. Prohibits public inspection of visual representations depicting victims in court records from revenge porn cases, subject to specified exceptions.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary; Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services; State's Attorneys
qa_results.stakeholders: Victims and defendants in cases involving sexual extortion, stalking, or revenge porn
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal potential increase in State and local revenues and expenditures beginning in fiscal 2026 due to additional fines and incarceration costs from extended prosecution timelines; specific dollar estimates are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters the statute of limitations for criminal offenses prosecuted in the District Court and circuit courts, clarifies in banc review provisions for certain misdemeanor offenses, and establishes confidentiality restrictions and access rules for court records containing visual representations of victims.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill extends or eliminates statutes of limitations for sexual extortion, stalking, and revenge porn, which may increase convictions and result in additional individuals being sentenced to State correctional facilities.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill's expansion of timeframes to prosecute sexual extortion, stalking, and revenge porn may increase criminal defense caseloads for indigent defendants represented by the Office of the Public Defender.

The bill explicitly authorizes the Attorney General or their designee to access and inspect confidential court records involving visual representations in revenge porn prosecutions, and the office represents the State in appellate proceedings, including points reserved for in banc review.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands the Nancy Grasmick Public School Professional Award to include eligible public school nurses. Requires qualifying nurses to be employed by a county school system or a local health department. Directs the Office of Student Financial Assistance to grant priority participation to qualified nurse applicants. Mandates that the office publicize the loan repayment program to recruit and retain public school nurses.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Higher Education Commission; Office of Student Financial Assistance
qa_results.stakeholders: public school nurses, county school systems, and local health departments
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $753,000 in FY 2025, reflecting a $750,000 contingent budget appropriation to fund loan repayment awards for approximately 115 school nurses and $3,000 for one-time software upgrades. State revenues are unaffected, and there is no direct local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MHEC (through its Office of Student Financial Assistance) is the primary implementing agency responsible for administering the Janet L. Hoffman Loan Assistance Repayment Program and the Nancy Grasmick Public School Professional Award, updating the Maryland College Aid Processing System (MDCAPS), and publicizing the award to eligible public school nurses.

MHEC (through its Office of Student Financial Assistance) is the primary implementing agency responsible for administering the Janet L. Hoffman Loan Assistance Repayment Program and the Nancy Grasmick Public School Professional Award, updating the Maryland College Aid Processing System (MDCAPS), and publicizing the award to eligible public school nurses.

MSDE oversees the state's public education system and 24 local school systems where these public school nurses are deployed; the bill aims to address recruitment and retention of health professionals in public schools.

The bill defines eligible public school nurses as registered nurses licensed under the Health Occupations Article (regulated by the Maryland Board of Nursing under MDH) or those employed by local health departments providing school health services.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Task Force on Responsible Use of Natural Psychedelic Substances. Requires the Maryland Cannabis Administration to provide staff for the Task Force. Directs the Task Force to study existing laws, public benefits, potential risks, and healthcare practitioner barriers. Requires recommendations on establishing a Maryland Natural Psychedelic Substance Access Program and transitioning from criminalizing nonviolent psychedelic offenses. Mandates the Task Force submit findings and recommendations to the Governor and General Assembly by July 31, 2025.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Cannabis Administration; Task Force on Responsible Use of Natural Psychedelic Substances
qa_results.stakeholders: Patients with conditions treatable by psychedelic substances, healthcare practitioners and facilitators, researchers, and individuals convicted of or incarcerated for nonviolent psychedelic offenses
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are not materially affected because the Maryland Cannabis Administration can provide staff support using existing budgeted resources. Task force member expense reimbursements are minimal and absorbable. State revenues and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Cannabis Administration (MCA) is designated as the primary staffing agency for the Task Force on Responsible Use of Natural Psychedelic Substances, and the Director of the MCA serves as an ex officio member.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a temporary state body, the Task Force on Responsible Use of Natural Psychedelic Substances, to study and issue recommendations regarding psychedelic policy and regulation.
The Secretary of Health (or designee) is designated as an ex officio member of the Task Force, which addresses medical, clinical, and public health aspects of psychedelic substances.
The Secretary of Disabilities (or designee) serves as an ex officio member of the Task Force examining access and therapeutic uses of psychedelic substances.
The Secretary of Veterans Affairs (now Veterans & Military Families) or designee is designated as an ex officio member of the Task Force, relevant to veteran mental health and trauma therapies.
The Governor appoints numerous members to the Task Force, designates the Task Force chair, and receives the final report and recommendations.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting and appointing the required members from specific disciplines and backgrounds to the Task Force.
A representative of the University System of Maryland is listed as one of the eligible academic appointees to serve on the Task Force.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires agencies issuing automated enforcement citations and notices to use the recipient's current Motor Vehicle Administration mailing address. Requires using the recipient's current residential address on file if a mailing address is unavailable. Applies to red light, speed, school bus, work zone, railroad crossing, bus lane, and vehicle height monitoring systems. Covers Maryland Transportation Authority notices of toll due and toll violation citations. Takes effect October 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Motor Vehicle Administration; Maryland Transportation Authority; Department of State Police; Baltimore City Department of Transportation; local law enforcement agencies
qa_results.stakeholders: Registered motor vehicle owners receiving automated traffic citations or video toll notices; state and local law enforcement agencies and contractors operating automated enforcement systems
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local finances are not materially affected. The Motor Vehicle Administration can implement necessary computer reprogramming changes using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires automated enforcement citations and notices (and video toll notices) across Maryland to be mailed using the current mailing address or residential address on file with the Administration (MVA), requiring MVA to provide and maintain this data and adjust system programming as necessary.

The bill directly amends Section 21-1414 of the Transportation Article governing the Maryland Transportation Authority, requiring the Authority or its agent to use the specified MVA mailing or residential address records when issuing notices of toll due and civil citations for unpaid video tolls.

As the parent cabinet department overseeing the Motor Vehicle Administration and highway safety administration, MDOT is impacted by operational and technical requirements ensuring automated enforcement systems conform to statutory address standards.

The bill directly applies to work zone speed control systems (§ 21-810), requiring State police departments or their contractors issuing citations and warning notices to send them to the MVA mailing or residential address.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the sales and use tax exemption for aircraft parts and equipment through June 30, 2030. Applies the exemption to materials, parts, or equipment used to repair, maintain, or upgrade eligible aircraft. Covers aircraft under 12,500 pounds or heavier aircraft primarily used in interstate or foreign commerce. Repeals the requirement for the Comptroller to report annually on lost revenue and aviation technician employment.
qa_results.responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Aviation repair and maintenance businesses, aircraft owners, and aircraft parts suppliers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund and special fund (Blueprint for Maryland's Future Fund) revenues continue to decrease through fiscal 2030 from the extended tax exemption; however, specific revenue loss estimates cannot be determined. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller administers the state sales and use tax and is directly affected by the bill, which extends the sales and use tax exemption on certain aircraft parts and equipment through 2030 and repeals the requirement that the Comptroller submit an annual report to the General Assembly regarding the revenue lost and impact on aviation technician employment.

The Maryland Aviation Administration is tasked with fostering the economic viability and vitality of aviation within the state. While the agency has no direct administrative duties under the bill, extending the sales tax exemption for aircraft repair, maintenance, and upgrade equipment directly affects the economic competitiveness of Maryland's aviation services and maintenance industry.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes statutory caps on fees that the Department of Natural Resources may set by regulation for tree expert licenses. Limits tree expert examination fees to $45, initial license fees to $55, and renewal fees to $100. Authorizes the department to suspend or revoke a license if the licensee fails to maintain required insurance. Requires the Secretary of Natural Resources to submit an annual licensing report to the General Assembly by November 1 each year. Authorizes the department to adopt regulations to implement tree expert licensing provisions.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
qa_results.stakeholders: licensed tree experts, applicants for tree expert licensure, and businesses employing licensed tree experts
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues to the Forest and Park Reserve Fund likely increase minimally beginning in fiscal 2025 from anticipated regulatory fee increases. The Department of Natural Resources plans to use the revenue to partially fund a regulatory position. Local governments are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 561 directly impacts the Department of Natural Resources (DNR) as the primary regulatory and licensing agency for tree experts. The bill establishes maximum statutory caps on tree expert examination, initial licensing, and renewal fees set by DNR, requires DNR to submit an annual report to the General Assembly, authorizes DNR to adopt implementing regulations, and empowers the department to suspend or revoke licenses for failure to maintain required insurance.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases the nonresident annual fee for a special Chesapeake Bay and coastal sport fishing license from $50 to $100. Maintains the existing $50 annual fee for resident applicants. Authorizes any person on the registered boat to sport fish in designated tidal and coastal waters. Requires the Department of Natural Resources to issue a complimentary fishing license to the purchasing boat owner. Takes effect October 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Natural Resources
qa_results.stakeholders: Nonresident recreational boat owners and anglers fishing in Maryland tidal and coastal waters
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund (Fisheries Research and Development Fund) revenues increase by $359,500 in FY 2025 and by $460,900 annually thereafter. State expenditures and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Natural Resources (DNR) administers the special Chesapeake Bay and coastal sport fishing license program, issues the licenses, and collects the license fees, which are deposited into DNR's Fisheries Research and Development Fund, generating an estimated revenue increase of approximately $460,900 annually.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Department of State Police to publish an annual report on suspected homicide investigations of incarcerated individuals. The mandate applies to investigations of deaths occurring while individuals are in Division of Correction custody. Requires the Department to report the number of completed investigations for the preceding calendar year. Requires reporting the number of cases referred for prosecution following those completed investigations. Mandates posting the report online and submitting it to the Governor and General Assembly by December 31 annually.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of State Police
qa_results.stakeholders: Incarcerated individuals in the custody of the Division of Correction, their families, and Department of State Police investigators
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures and revenues are not materially affected; the Department of State Police can implement the reporting requirements using existing budgeted resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Department of State Police to track completed homicide investigations of individuals in the custody of the Division of Correction, publish an annual report on its website, and submit the report to the Governor and General Assembly.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The investigations and subsequent reporting required by the bill pertain specifically to deaths of individuals in the custody of the Division of Correction, which is an administration within the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services.
The Department of State Police is statutorily required to submit the annual report detailing completed investigations and case referrals for prosecution directly to the Governor.

qa_results.bill_summary: Regulates how controllers and processors collect, maintain, and process consumer personal data and sensitive data. Authorizes consumers to access, correct, delete, or obtain their personal data and opt out of certain processing. Prohibits the sale of sensitive data and restricts the use of geofencing near specified healthcare facilities. Requires controllers to provide privacy notices, conduct data protection assessments, and contractually bind processors. Makes violations unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices enforceable by the Consumer Protection Division.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General, Consumer Protection Division
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland consumers; businesses and entities that control or process personal data of at least 35,000 Maryland consumers, or at least 10,000 Maryland consumers while deriving more than 20% of gross revenue from personal data sales; third-party data processors
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: General fund expenditures for the Office of the Attorney General, Consumer Protection Division likely increase, at least minimally, beginning in fiscal 2026 for enforcement. Exact costs are indeterminate and depend on complaint volume. The bill's penalty provisions are not expected to materially affect State or local revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Consumer Protection Division of the Office of the Attorney General is the primary regulatory and enforcement authority for the Maryland Online Data Privacy Act. Violations constitute unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act, and the agency is responsible for reviewing data protection assessments, issuing notices of violation, and initiating enforcement actions.

The Judiciary may adjudicate civil enforcement actions and penalty proceedings brought by the Office of the Attorney General for violations of the Act, though impact is minimal since private rights of action for damages are excluded.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires public community colleges to consider nonremedial English as a Second Language and English language learner courses for credit. Qualifies these courses for world language or humanities electives credit toward a student's associate degree. Requires these credits to transfer to any public institution of higher education in the State. Prohibits public institutions of higher education from denying the transfer of these credits for any reason. Requires private nonprofit institutions of higher education to review and consider transferring these credits.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Higher Education Commission; public community colleges; public institutions of higher education; private nonprofit institutions of higher education
qa_results.stakeholders: Community college students taking English as a Second Language or English language learner courses, Maryland public community colleges, public institutions of higher education, and private nonprofit institutions of higher education
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Public four-year institutions and local community colleges can implement the credit transfer and evaluation requirements using existing resources. Higher education and community college revenues are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MHEC is responsible for establishing transfer procedures and developing and implementing the statewide transfer agreement with public institutions of higher education, which must now incorporate transferability of non-remedial ESL and English language learner courses.

As the state's coordinating board for higher education, the commission oversees statewide transfer policies and articulation agreements between community colleges and four-year institutions impacted by the bill.

USM institutions are public institutions of higher education required under the statewide transfer agreement to accept transferable ESL and English language learner course credits earned at Maryland community colleges without denial.

As an independent public four-year university, Morgan State must comply with the statewide transfer agreement and is prohibited from denying the transfer of non-remedial ESL course credits from Maryland community colleges.

As a public senior higher education institution, St. Mary's College is subject to the updated statewide transfer agreement requirements and cannot deny qualifying ESL course credits transferred from community colleges.

qa_results.bill_summary: Modifies the Family and Medical Leave Insurance Program by altering implementation timelines, benefit calculations, and administrative procedures. Delays the start date for required contributions to July 1, 2025, and benefit payments to July 1, 2026. Requires the Secretary of Labor to set the initial total contribution rate by February 1, 2025. Authorizes employers to satisfy program requirements through private plans consisting of employer-provided benefits or authorized insurance. Prohibits employers offering private plans from deducting more than 50% of the set contribution rate from employees. Authorizes the Department to adopt regulations establishing application and renewal fees for private employer plans.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland employers, covered employees, participating self-employed individuals, and private insurers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues decrease by up to $915.5 million in FY 2025 and $457.8 million in FY 2026 due to delayed contributions. Special fund expenditures decrease by up to $869.4 million in FY 2026 due to delayed benefit payments. State employer expenditures across all funds decrease by up to $26.1 million in FY 2025 and $8.9 million in FY 2026. General fund expenditures decrease by $12.4 million in FY 2025 for community service provider reimbursements. Beginning in FY 2026, special fund revenues increase from private employer plan fees and assessed appeal costs.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor is the primary agency administering and enforcing the Family and Medical Leave Insurance (FAMLI) Program. The bill directly alters program deadlines, contribution schedules, benefit calculation rules, private plan authorization and fees, and enforcement processes managed by the department.

The Department of Health is required to reimburse certain healthcare and community service providers for the employer share of FAMLI contributions; delaying the program implementation results in an expenditure reduction for the department of over $12 million in FY 2025.

As the principal personnel and budget agency for the State, DBM oversees state employee benefits and budget impacts. The delay in required employer contributions for state personnel significantly reduces state employer expenditures across state agencies in FY 2025 and FY 2026.
The bill regulates private employer plans providing paid family leave benefits, including plans that provide coverage through insurers authorized and licensed by the Maryland Insurance Commissioner.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases the Citizens Committee for the Enhancement of Communities Surrounding Baltimore–Washington International Thurgood Marshall Airport to 12 members. Requires delegates representing legislative district 12A to recommend one member for appointment by the Secretary. Requires the delegate representing legislative district 12B to recommend one member for appointment by the Secretary. Retains existing appointment recommendation requirements for legislative delegations representing districts 13 and 32. Requires members to represent community associations located within or within two miles of the certified noise zone.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Transportation
qa_results.stakeholders: Community associations and residents situated within or within two miles of the Baltimore–Washington International Thurgood Marshall Airport certified noise zone, and state legislators representing legislative districts 12A and 12B
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State operations or finances and has no local fiscal effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters the membership of the Citizens Committee for the Enhancement of Communities Surrounding BWI Thurgood Marshall Airport, whose members are appointed by the Secretary of Transportation and which is staffed and funded through the Maryland Department of Transportation.
As the modal unit within MDOT that owns and operates BWI Thurgood Marshall Airport, MAA works directly with surrounding communities and the certified airport noise zones addressed by this committee.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters the statutory composition and membership of an executive advisory committee established to evaluate livability issues in communities near BWI airport.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the membership of the Criminal Injuries Compensation Board from five to seven members. Expands eligibility criteria, covered crimes, and reimbursable expenses for crime victims and their dependents. Increases maximum award limits for funeral expenses, mental health counseling, property repair, and emergency awards. Repeals requirements for victims to report crimes within 48 hours and fully cooperate with law enforcement. Authorizes claimants to petition the Board for reconsideration and seek judicial review. Authorizes the Governor to include appropriations in the annual budget bill for the compensation fund.
qa_results.responsible_party: Criminal Injuries Compensation Board; Governor's Office of Crime Prevention, Youth, and Victim Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Victims of crime, surviving dependents and household members of victims, victim service organizations, and law enforcement agencies
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase significantly beginning in FY 2026 to support expanded Board operations and compensation awards, including $975,585 in administrative costs in FY 2026. Special fund revenues and expenditures increase correspondingly, and federal fund revenues and expenditures increase beginning in FY 2028 from federal matching funds. The total cost of additional victim compensation awards cannot be reliably estimated. Local government operations and finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Criminal Injuries Compensation Board (CICB) is housed directly within GOCPP. The bill significantly alters the composition, powers, and claim review procedures of the Board, expands compensation award eligibility, and increases GOCPP's administrative responsibilities and staffing requirements.

The bill authorizes the Governor to include an appropriation in the annual budget bill to ensure an adequate balance in the Criminal Injuries Compensation Fund, and requires the Governor's approval for appointments made to the Board.

The bill authorizes claimants to file petitions for judicial review of Board reconsideration decisions in court, and court costs collected in criminal and traffic cases continue to serve as a key revenue source for the Criminal Injuries Compensation Fund.
The bill explicitly mandates that the State Treasurer shall separately hold and invest the Criminal Injuries Compensation Fund.
The bill explicitly designates the Comptroller to account for the Criminal Injuries Compensation Fund.
The bill explicitly provides that the Criminal Injuries Compensation Fund is subject to audit by the Office of Legislative Audits.

State Police are subject to requests from the Board for investigative materials to verify crimes and are required under statute to provide Board-supplied victim compensation information when crime reports are filed.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes each county to establish an assisted outpatient treatment program by July 1, 2026. Requires the Maryland Department of Health to establish a program in any county that does not establish one. Permits specified individuals to petition a circuit court to order assisted outpatient treatment for an eligible adult. Requires multidisciplinary care coordination teams to develop comprehensive, recovery-oriented outpatient treatment plans for respondents. Requires the Office of the Public Defender to provide legal representation for indigent respondents in program proceedings. Terminates the assisted outpatient treatment program provisions on June 30, 2030.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Behavioral Health Administration; Office of the Public Defender
qa_results.stakeholders: individuals with serious and persistent mental illness; county governments; local behavioral health authorities and core service agencies; behavioral health care providers; Office of the Public Defender
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $3.0 million in FY 2025 under a contingent budget appropriation, and by at least $291,700 in FY 2026 for Maryland Department of Health personnel and Judiciary IT programming. Indeterminate, potentially significant additional state expenditures continue through FY 2030 for state-operated county programs, Medicaid outpatient services, and Office of the Public Defender legal representation and expert witness costs. Local government expenditures and revenues increase from FY 2026 through FY 2030 to the extent counties choose to establish local programs and provide billable services.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health (MDH) and its Behavioral Health Administration (BHA) are tasked with primary implementation oversight. MDH must establish clinical and operational standards for Assisted Outpatient Treatment (AOT) programs and care coordination teams, establish and operate programs in any county that does not opt to do so, and submit comprehensive annual reports to the General Assembly. The department also receives substantial dedicated funding and incurs ongoing personnel and operational costs.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Criminal Procedure Article to mandate that the Office of the Public Defender (OPD) provide legal representation for indigent individuals in all AOT proceedings. The court must formally notify OPD's Mental Health Division of petition filings, and the agency incurs significant fiscal and staffing impacts to hire mental health attorneys, support personnel, and retain expert witnesses.

Circuit courts are responsible for receiving AOT petitions, sealing filings from public case search, scheduling hearings, issuing findings and orders, and adjudicating treatment plan modifications. The Administrative Office of the Courts incurs direct fiscal impacts of at least $133,209 for required programming modifications to the Judicial Information System.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes a Study on the Establishment of a Homeless Shelter Licensing Program in the Department of Housing and Community Development. Requires the Department to hire one new full-time permanent employee to conduct the study in consultation with political subdivisions. Directs the study to review current habitability and admissions standards of homeless shelters in the State. Requires the study to recommend basic habitability and admission standards for Maryland homeless shelters. Mandates recommendations for a plan to establish a homeless shelter licensing program within the Department. Requires reporting findings and recommendations to designated legislative committees and the Department by July 1, 2025.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development
qa_results.stakeholders: Homeless shelters in Maryland, homeless individuals and shelter residents, and local political subdivisions.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $77,933 in FY 2025 to hire one permanent full-time employee to conduct the study, with ongoing costs in future years. Revenues are not affected. Local government finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly establishes the Study on the Establishment of a Homeless Shelter Licensing Program within the Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD), mandates DHCD to hire a full-time permanent employee to conduct the study, and requires reporting to the Assistant Secretary of DHCD's Homeless Solutions Division.

The Department of Human Services is Maryland's primary social service agency assisting individuals facing homelessness; recommendations on standards and licensing of homeless shelters directly intersect with its service population and emergency shelter network.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases disaster service leave for Executive Branch employees from 15 to 30 days in any 12-month period. Requires employees to obtain approval from their appointing authority before taking disaster service leave. Authorizes appointing authorities to waive approval requirements or increase disaster service leave days during prolonged disasters. Increases the paid leave allowed for uniformed services training or active duty from 15 to 30 days. Authorizes the Secretary of Budget and Management to provide the uniformed services leave by regulation.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Budget and Management
qa_results.stakeholders: Executive Branch employees; State employees serving in the armed forces reserves or organized militia; State agencies
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances and operations are not materially affected overall. Limited agencies may incur minimal overtime costs to provide coverage for employees on leave, but these costs can likely be absorbed with existing resources. No local fiscal effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the State Personnel and Pensions Article regarding leave policies, authorizing the Secretary of Budget and Management to provide by regulation up to 30 days of paid leave for uniformed services training or active duty.

Identified in the fiscal note as one of the agencies likely to experience an operational impact and potential overtime costs to maintain coverage when personnel use extended uniformed services or disaster service leave.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Identified in the fiscal note as likely to experience an increase in overtime expenditures to cover mandatory staffing and facility coverage when employees utilize the expanded leave allowances.

Oversees the Maryland Military Department and organized militia, whose members directly benefit from the expansion of paid uniformed services leave from 15 to 30 days for military training and service.
Administers the State Retirement and Pension System, which calculates and awards service credits to members whose state employment is interrupted by uniformed service.
This bill was an Administration initiative ('Time to Serve Act of 2024') affecting personnel policies across the entire Executive Branch of state government.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires each principal department and independent unit in the Executive Branch to catalog all issued permits, licenses, and certificates. Mandates submission of the catalog to the Governor on or before October 1, 2024. Directs each entity to post application processes and processing times on its website by December 1, 2024. Requires annual website updates of this information beginning October 1, 2025. Establishes the Government Efficiency Commission to monitor processing efficiency and recommend improvements. Requires the commission to report findings and recommendations annually beginning December 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Principal departments and independent units of State government; Office of the Governor; Government Efficiency Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Applicants for State permits, licenses, and certificates, including Maryland businesses and individuals; Maryland Executive Branch departments and independent units
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are not materially affected, as affected entities and the Office of the Governor are expected to implement the requirements using existing budgeted resources. Travel expense reimbursements for commission members are minimal and absorbable. Local government finances and operations are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires all principal departments and independent units to submit their permit, license, and certificate catalogs to the Governor, requires the Governor to designate the chair of the new Government Efficiency Commission and appoint business representatives, and designates the Office of the Governor to provide staff support for the commission.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill formally creates a new advisory body within the executive branch, the Government Efficiency Commission, tasked with compiling catalog data, reviewing statutory and regulatory processes, and making annual recommendations to improve permitting and licensing efficiency.

The Secretary of Information Technology (or designee) serves as a statutory member of the Government Efficiency Commission. Additionally, DoIT manages the statewide OneStop licensing portal and the bill requires reporting on information technology systems used for permitting and manual tasks remaining.

The Secretary of Labor (or designee) is a statutory member of the Government Efficiency Commission. Furthermore, MD Labor is one of the state's largest licensing entities, overseeing dozens of professional licensing boards and commissions directly subject to the catalog and website reporting mandates.

The Secretary of Health (or designee) is a statutory member of the Government Efficiency Commission. MDH also oversees numerous health facility permits and 20 health occupational licensing boards that must compile and publish permit and license processing catalogs.

The Secretary of the Environment (or designee) is a designated member of the Government Efficiency Commission. MDE is also highlighted in the fiscal note as a primary permitting agency responsible for numerous environmental, water, mining, and waste discharge permits subject to the cataloging and reporting requirements.

The Secretary of Transportation (or designee) is designated as a member of the Government Efficiency Commission. MDOT and its modal administrations also issue numerous vehicle, highway access, hauling, and aviation permits and licenses required to be cataloged under the bill.

MSDE is specifically highlighted in the fiscal note regarding an estimated $200,000 cost to procure a contractor to catalog and build web pages for its educator and childcare provider licensing and certification systems.
The Chief Performance Officer, who leads or operates within the Governor's Office of Performance Improvement, is a designated statutory member of the Government Efficiency Commission.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Special Secretary of Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs (or designee) is a statutory member of the Government Efficiency Commission to represent business equity interests in permitting and licensing reform.
The Secretary of Commerce (or designee) is designated as an ex officio member of the Government Efficiency Commission to support its mission of enhancing economic competitiveness.

The Secretary of Housing and Community Development (or designee) is a statutory member of the Government Efficiency Commission and must catalog any permits, certificates, or licenses issued by the department.
The Secretary of Planning (or designee) is designated as a statutory member of the Government Efficiency Commission.
The Director of the Maryland Energy Administration (or designee) serves as a statutory member of the Government Efficiency Commission.

MDA is explicitly highlighted in the fiscal note as a major regulatory entity that issues extensive permits, licenses, and registrations (such as pesticides, food quality, and nutrient management) required to be cataloged and tracked online.

DNR is highlighted in the fiscal note as an executive department that issues numerous licenses and permits (hunting, fishing, boating, waterways, forestry) that must be cataloged and reported on its website under the bill.

MSP and the Office of the State Fire Marshal are noted in the fiscal note as entities that issue regulated licenses and certifications (such as firearms, security services, and electrical inspectors) subject to the bill's cataloging mandates.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Pava LaPere Innovation Acceleration Grant Program in the Maryland Technology Development Corporation. Establishes the Baltimore Innovation Initiative Pilot Program within the Maryland Innovation Initiative. Requires $50,000 grants to qualifying student- or faculty-founded start-ups in the Baltimore-Columbia-Towson metropolitan statistical area. Requires qualifying applicants to use at least 20% of the award to hire third-party consultants. Requires a $1,500,000 appropriation for the pilot program in fiscal years 2025 and 2026. Repeals the $1,000,000 annual mandated appropriation for the Business Telework Assistance Grant Program.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Technology Development Corporation; Maryland Innovation Initiative; Department of Commerce
qa_results.stakeholders: student and faculty entrepreneurs and technology start-ups in the Baltimore-Columbia-Towson metropolitan statistical area; public and private colleges and universities in the Baltimore metropolitan region; small businesses seeking telework assistance
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Net general fund expenditures increase by $1.0 million annually from FY 2025 through FY 2027 and decrease by $0.5 million annually beginning in FY 2028. Nonbudgeted revenues and expenditures increase by $850,000 annually from FY 2025 through FY 2027 from participating higher education institution contributions. Higher education expenditures increase by $325,000 annually from FY 2025 through FY 2027 for participating State institutions.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: TEDCO is the primary implementing agency tasked with establishing, administering, and adopting regulations for both the Pava LaPere Innovation Acceleration Grant Program and the Baltimore Innovation Initiative Pilot Program, as well as reporting to the General Assembly.
The bill repeals the annual $1,000,000 mandated appropriation for the Business Telework Assistance Grant Program, which is housed within and administered by the Department of Commerce.

Multiple USM institutions (including Towson University, UMBC, UMB, Coppin State, and University of Baltimore) are designated as eligible universities under the Baltimore Innovation Initiative Pilot Program, requiring annual contributions of up to $50,000 to participate and submit proposals for funding.

Morgan State University is explicitly designated as an eligible university under the Baltimore Innovation Initiative Pilot Program, allowing it to participate, contribute up to $50,000 annually, and submit project proposals for grant funding.

DBM is responsible for the state budget process, which is impacted by the repeal of a $1.0 million annual funding mandate and the creation of mandated general fund appropriations for the new programs.
The bill was introduced by request of the Administration and requires the Governor to include appropriations for the new innovation programs in the annual executive budget bills.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Center for Firearm Violence Prevention and Intervention in the Maryland Department of Health. Requires the Secretary of Health to appoint an executive director to direct center planning and personnel. Directs the center to consult with specified state agencies and solicit recommendations from impacted communities and experts. Mandates submitting a preliminary public health state plan to reduce firearm violence by May 1, 2025. Requires submitting a quadrennial state strategic plan for firearm violence reduction beginning May 1, 2029.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: communities disproportionately impacted by firearm violence, local health departments, health care professionals, and community and faith-based organizations
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures increase by $2,171,387 in FY 2025, comprising a $2.0 million contingent general fund appropriation and $171,387 in federal funds for three personnel and contractual services. Annual general fund expenditures are estimated at $8.0 million in FY 2026 and $10.0 million beginning in FY 2027. Local health department revenues and expenditures increase beginning in FY 2026 to the extent they receive grants from the center.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 583 establishes the Center for Firearm Violence Prevention and Intervention within the Maryland Department of Health. The Secretary of Health appoints the executive director, and the department receives dedicated general and federal fund allocations to staff and operate the Center.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates that the Center work in consultation with the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy (formerly Crime Prevention, Youth, and Victim Services) to ensure a multidepartmental approach to firearm violence reduction and to facilitate cross-jurisdictional data and information sharing.
The Center is statutorily required to work in consultation with the Maryland State Police to ensure a comprehensive, whole-of-government approach to reducing firearm violence.

The Governor receives the preliminary State Plan and recurring four-year State Strategic Plans for Firearm Violence Reduction from the Center, and is authorized to include an appropriation for the Center in the annual budget bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands workers' compensation occupational disease presumptions to include thyroid, colon, and ovarian cancer for specified first responders. Covers paid and volunteer firefighters, fire fighting instructors, rescue squad members, advanced life support unit members, and fire marshals. Requires an individual to complete at least 10 years of cumulative service in the State. Requires the cancer to stem from toxic substance contact encountered in the line of duty. Mandates that the disease result in partial or total disability or death to qualify for compensation.
qa_results.responsible_party: Workers' Compensation Commission; Chesapeake Employers' Insurance Company
qa_results.stakeholders: Paid and volunteer firefighters, fire fighting instructors, rescue squad members, advanced life support unit members, sworn members of the Office of the State Fire Marshal, the State, and local governments
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures may increase, likely minimally, beginning in FY 2025 from expanded claim eligibility. Local government expenditures and Chesapeake Employers' Insurance Company expenditures likely increase, potentially significantly, due to increased workers' compensation benefit payments and premium adjustments; specific figures cannot be reliably estimated.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Commission administers the state's Workers' Compensation Law and adjudicates claims arising from occupational diseases, including the expanded cancer presumptions established by this bill for first responders.

IWIF (operating as Chesapeake Employers' Insurance Company) serves as the third-party administrator for State of Maryland employee workers' compensation claims and will experience increased expenditures and claim payouts under the expanded presumptions.
Sworn members of the Office of the State Fire Marshal, which is organized within the Department of State Police, are explicitly covered under the bill's expanded occupational disease presumptions.
The MAA operates BWI Marshall Airport and employs airport firefighters and rescue personnel who are State employees eligible for the expanded cancer presumptions under the bill.
MDOT is the parent department of the Maryland Aviation Administration, whose airport fire and rescue personnel are covered by the bill's expanded occupational disease presumptions.
This is an Administration bill proposed on behalf of the Governor to expand health protections and workers' compensation coverage for first responders.
The Subsequent Injury Fund reviews and handles workers' compensation claims involving combined disabilities and pre-existing conditions, and served as an informational source on the legislation.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits a person from knowingly and willfully threatening harm against an election official or an immediate family member. Applies the prohibition when threats stem from the election official's role in administering the election process. Prohibits knowingly sending, delivering, parting with, or making a prohibited threat for delivery. Defines election officials to include state and local board members, staff, counsel, directors, election judges, and pages. Establishes misdemeanor penalties of imprisonment not exceeding three years, a fine not exceeding $2,500, or both.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Elections; local boards of elections; Office of the State Prosecutor
qa_results.stakeholders: Election officials, including State Board of Elections members and staff, local election board members and staff, county election directors, board counsel, election judges, election day pages, their immediate family members, and individuals prosecuted under the law
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Department of Legislative Services indicates the bill will not materially affect State or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates criminal protections specifically for election officials, including the State Administrator, State Board members, staff, counsel, and local election personnel administering the election process under the Election Law Article.
The Office of the State Prosecutor is responsible for investigating and prosecuting criminal violations of Maryland election laws and public integrity matters.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a new misdemeanor carrying penalties of up to three years of imprisonment, requiring legal defense services from OPD for qualifying indigent defendants charged under the statute.
The Judiciary and court system will process, hear, and adjudicate new misdemeanor criminal charges and citations initiated under this legislation.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The agency oversees incarceration and probation supervision for individuals convicted of misdemeanors carrying sentences of up to three years imprisonment.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the Class C (Weinberg Center) beer, wine, and liquor license in Frederick County to include New Spires Arts Stages. Expands the licensed premises to the New Spires Arts Stages facility. Authorizes the facility manager or a municipal official designated by the Mayor of Frederick to sign the license application. Allows the sale of beer, wine, and liquor from one hour before to one hour after qualifying events. Covers performances, facility fundraisers, and events hosted by outside groups renting either facility. Takes effect July 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Frederick County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Weinberg Center for the Arts, New Spires Arts Stages, outside groups renting either facility, and patrons in Frederick County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Frederick County revenues decrease by approximately $375 annually beginning in fiscal 2025 as the permanent license replaces multiple per diem licenses. Any additional local enforcement activity can be handled using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is responsible for the overarching regulation and taxation of the alcohol industry in the state. While this bill specifically amends a local alcoholic beverage license administered by the Frederick County Board of License Commissioners with no direct state fiscal impact, it relates to the broader statutory framework of alcoholic beverage regulation overseen by the Comptroller.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes a manufacturer's limited beer, wine, and liquor permit in Frederick County. Authorizes the Board of License Commissioners to issue the permit to eligible distillery and brewery license holders. Permits holders to allow licensed caterers or contracted parties to provide third-party alcoholic beverages during private events. Prohibits permit holders from having a direct or indirect pecuniary interest in the caterer or contracted party. Prohibits public patrons on the licensed premises from entering the private event area during events. Requires permit holders to obtain Board approval before each event.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Frederick County
qa_results.stakeholders: Holders of Class 1 distillery licenses and Class 5 brewery licenses in Frederick County, licensed caterers, and private event hosts
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Frederick County revenues increase by approximately $4,500 annually beginning in fiscal 2025 from permit fee collections. Frederick County can handle enforcement using existing budgeted resources. No State fiscal effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill concerns alcoholic beverages manufacturer licenses (Class 1 distilleries and Class 5 breweries) and the Alcoholic Beverages Article. While the permit is authorized and issued locally by the Frederick County Board of License Commissioners, the Comptroller has general statutory authority over the regulation and oversight of the alcohol industry and state-level manufacturer licenses in Maryland.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Board of License Commissioners for Frederick County to issue a municipal golf course license to a designated city official. Requires the recipient to be an official of the City of Frederick designated by the Mayor. Authorizes the Board to transfer the license to a different designated city official upon request of the city. Authorizes the license holder to sell beer, wine, and liquor for on-premises consumption at the municipal golf course.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Frederick County
qa_results.stakeholders: City of Frederick officials, municipal golf course managers, and patrons of municipal golf courses in the City of Frederick
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state fiscal impact. The bill does not materially affect Frederick County finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland oversees state sales and use tax collection and broad regulation of the alcoholic beverages industry in Maryland. The bill involves local alcoholic beverage licensing and notes that designated agents are responsible for collecting and remitting sales and use tax.

qa_results.bill_summary: Exempts specified applicants for employment in Dorchester County from statutory prohibitions against mandatory polygraph examinations. Applies to applicants for employment as paramedics or emergency medical technicians within the county Emergency Medical Services Division. Covers applicants seeking employment as 9-1-1 center dispatcher specialists at the Dorchester County 9-1-1 Center. Includes applicants for employment as correctional officers at the Dorchester County Detention Center. Takes effect October 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Dorchester County Department of Emergency Services; Dorchester County Department of Corrections
qa_results.stakeholders: Applicants for employment as paramedics, emergency medical technicians, 9-1-1 center dispatcher specialists, or correctional officers in Dorchester County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal effect. The bill has no material effect on Dorchester County finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends § 3-702 of the Labor and Employment Article, which is administered and enforced by the Commissioner of Labor and Industry within the Maryland Department of Labor regarding employment standards and polygraph prohibitions.

The underlying statute (§ 3-702) authorizes the Office of the Attorney General to initiate legal actions on behalf of applicants or employees for violations of the polygraph prohibition at the request of the Commissioner of Labor and Industry.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases the number of resident circuit court judges in Prince George’s County from 24 to 25. Adds one courtroom clerk and one law clerk to support the new judgeship. Requires Prince George’s County to fund an administrative assistant and related operating expenses. Addresses judicial workload certifications indicating critical need in the county. Takes effect July 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary
qa_results.stakeholders: Litigants and residents in Prince George’s County, the Circuit Court for Prince George’s County, and circuit court judicial staff
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $361,459 in FY 2025 for one judge and two support staff positions, increasing to $493,400 by FY 2029. Prince George’s County expenditures increase starting in FY 2025 to fund an administrative assistant and operating expenses. Revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Administrative Office of the Courts provides administrative, operational, and financial support to Maryland's judicial branch. The bill directly impacts the Judiciary by adding a circuit court judgeship in Prince George's County along with associated staff positions (courtroom clerk and law clerk), increasing State general fund expenditures.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and recommending candidates for judicial appointments to fill newly created judgeships across the state.
The Governor holds executive constitutional authority to appoint judges to newly established judicial vacancies prior to election.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes publication requirements for legal advertisements and legal notices in Dorchester County. Requires Dorchester County to publish and distribute mandated notices through both print and digital formats. Starts the required publication period once the first notice appears in print or digital format. Authorizes placement in an accessible local digital publication if no qualified print and digital publication exists. Expands the general definition of a qualifying newspaper to include publications offered in digital formats.
qa_results.responsible_party: Dorchester County
qa_results.stakeholders: Dorchester County government, publishers of local print and digital newspapers, and residents of Dorchester County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal effect. The bill is not anticipated to materially affect Dorchester County operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill governs legal advertisements and notices required pursuant to court orders, judgments, or decrees in Dorchester County, which directly intersects with judicial proceedings and court-ordered notices overseen and supported by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

qa_results.bill_summary: Renames the Law Enforcement Cadet Apprenticeship Program to the Public Safety Apprenticeship Program in the Maryland Department of Labor. Expands program eligibility to public safety agencies, including correctional units and state and local law enforcement agencies. Authorizes start-up grants up to $200,000 and stabilization grants up to $5,000 for each enrolled apprentice. Requires the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission to develop mental health wellness policies for law enforcement and correctional facilities. Establishes the Workgroup on Growing Engagement in the Law Enforcement and Corrections Workforce to study workforce shortages.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor; Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: public safety agencies, correctional units, state and local law enforcement agencies, correctional and law enforcement officers, and public safety apprentices
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local public safety agencies may receive expanded grant awards under the existing $750,000 annual mandated appropriation. The Maryland Department of Labor and the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission can implement the act with existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill renames and expands the Law Enforcement Cadet Apprenticeship Program within the Maryland Department of Labor into the Public Safety Apprenticeship Program, authorizing the department to administer start-up and stabilization grants and adopt implementation regulations. Additionally, the Secretary of Labor serves on the newly established Workgroup.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission (MPTSC), housed within DPSCS, is mandated to develop mental health wellness policies for law enforcement agencies and correctional facilities, report annually on their implementation, and staff the new Workgroup. Furthermore, the Secretary of Public Safety and Correctional Services is a member of the Workgroup.

The Secretary of State Police is a designated member of the Workgroup on Growing Engagement in the Law Enforcement and Corrections Workforce, and the department is directly affected by the law enforcement mental health wellness policies and eligible for the apprenticeship program.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill statutorily creates the Workgroup on Growing Engagement in the Law Enforcement and Corrections Workforce to examine staffing shortages and recruitment strategies in law enforcement and corrections.
The Governor designates the Chair of the newly established Workgroup and receives annual reports from both the Workgroup and the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission.
The State Superintendent of Schools (or designee) is designated as a member of the Workgroup on Growing Engagement in the Law Enforcement and Corrections Workforce.
The Secretary of Higher Education (or designee) is designated as a member of the Workgroup on Growing Engagement in the Law Enforcement and Corrections Workforce.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits discrimination based on military status in housing, employment, and residential real estate transactions. Defines military status as being a member of the uniformed services, a reserve component, a veteran, or a dependent. Prohibits employers, employment agencies, and labor organizations from discriminating or harassing individuals based on military status. Bars discriminatory practices in selling, renting, advertising, or financing residential dwellings based on military status. Preserves the Attorney General's independent civil rights enforcement authority.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Commission on Civil Rights; Office of the Attorney General
qa_results.stakeholders: Uniformed service members, military reservists, veterans, and military dependents; employers, employment agencies, and labor organizations; residential property owners, landlords, real estate brokers, and residential lenders
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal increase in State general fund expenditures for the Maryland Commission on Civil Rights to investigate additional discrimination complaints, with specific totals unavailable (estimated at $80,000 annually per additional investigator needed); no material impact on local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Commission on Civil Rights (MCCR) is the primary state agency responsible for investigating and enforcing statutory prohibitions against discrimination in employment and housing, which HB 598 expands to include military status.

The bill explicitly clarifies and preserves the authority of the Attorney General under Title 20, Subtitle 10, Part III of the State Government Article to investigate, prosecute, and remediate civil rights violations, which includes discriminatory actions prohibited by this bill.

The bill establishes legal protections against housing and employment discrimination for uniformed service members, reservists, veterans, and their dependents, aligning directly with the agency's mission to advocate for and support military families.
The Office of Administrative Hearings conducts administrative hearings for contested discrimination complaints certified for litigation by the Maryland Commission on Civil Rights.
The state court system may adjudicate civil actions, appeals, or petitions for relief arising from alleged housing or employment discrimination based on military status.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Maryland Community Investment Corporation as an independent instrumentality of the State. Directs the corporation to qualify as a community development entity and apply for federal New Markets Tax Credits. Authorizes the corporation to make equity investments and provide financial assistance in low-income communities. Requires the corporation to establish an investment committee and appoint an advisory committee prioritizing Maryland businesses. Expands eligible uses of the Strategic Demolition and Smart Growth Impact Fund to include credit enhancement.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Community Investment Corporation; Department of Housing and Community Development
qa_results.stakeholders: Low-income communities, businesses and revitalization projects located in low-income communities, community development organizations, and local governments
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $800,000 annually beginning in FY 2025 to support the corporation's operations. Nonbudgeted revenues and expenditures may increase significantly beginning as early as FY 2026 from private investments in New Markets Tax Credits and resulting project financing. Local governments benefit from increased flexibility in utilizing the Strategic Demolition and Smart Growth Impact Fund.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DHCD is heavily involved in the bill: the Secretary serves on the Board of Directors of the newly established Maryland Community Investment Corporation (MCIC), DHCD may provide staff support, the $0.8 million initial general fund appropriation is passed through DHCD's budget, and the bill amends DHCD's Strategic Demolition and Smart Growth Impact Fund.
The Secretary of Commerce (or designee) is an ex officio member of the MCIC Board of Directors, and the Department may provide staffing and technical assistance to the corporation.
The Attorney General acts as the legal advisor to MCIC and is statutorily required to assign Assistant Attorneys General to the corporation and designate one as General Counsel.
The Comptroller (or designee) serves on the Board of Directors of the MCIC and is responsible for accounting for the Strategic Demolition and Smart Growth Impact Fund.
The Secretary of Planning (or designee) serves as a member of the Board of Directors of the MCIC.
The Secretary of General Services (or designee) serves as a member of the Board of Directors of the MCIC.

The Governor appoints two voting members of the MCIC Board of Directors, possesses removal authority for those members, and receives annual and quarterly operational and financial reports from the corporation.
The State Treasurer holds and invests the money of the Strategic Demolition and Smart Growth Impact Fund, whose eligible uses are amended by the bill.

Board members, officers, employees, and members of the investment and advisory committees of MCIC are subject to the Public Ethics Law and required to make conflict-of-interest financial disclosures directly to the State Ethics Commission.

The bill authorizes MCIC to make investments pursuant to agreements with the Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System under Section 21-123.2 of the State Personnel and Pensions Article.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits exhibition driving on any highway or private property used for driving by the public in general. Expands the authority to designate special event zones and enforce related driving prohibitions statewide. Increases driver's license point assessments to eight points, or 12 points if serious bodily injury results. Subjects violators to a maximum penalty of 60 days imprisonment, a $1,000 fine, or both. Increases penalties to one year imprisonment and a $1,000 fine when violations cause serious bodily injury. Establishes affirmative defenses for actions taken reasonably for safety or during a permitted parade.
qa_results.responsible_party: Motor Vehicle Administration; State Highway Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: motor vehicle drivers, vehicle passengers, event spectators, local governments, and law enforcement agencies
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal increase in general fund revenues from higher fines and new offenses beginning in fiscal 2025. Potential minimal increase in State and local expenditures due to incarceration penalties. The Motor Vehicle Administration, State Highway Administration, and Judiciary can handle implementation within existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters point assessments under Title 16 of the Transportation Article, requiring the MVA to assess 8 or 12 points on driver's licenses for racing, speed contests, and exhibition driving violations, as well as administer license actions.
The bill authorizes the State Highway Administration statewide to designate areas on State highways as special event zones and lower speed limits to ensure public safety.

As the umbrella department overseeing both the Motor Vehicle Administration and the State Highway Administration, MDOT oversees state transportation policy, highway safety, and the enforcement framework established in the Transportation Article.

MSP is the primary law enforcement agency responsible for enforcing traffic and criminal laws on state highways and will enforce the expanded prohibitions on exhibition driving, speed contests, and special event zone violations.

The bill introduces incarceration penalties that eliminate prepayment options for racing and exhibition driving offenses, thereby requiring mandatory court appearances and increasing the Judiciary's trial workload.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes incarceration penalties of up to 60 days or 1 year, potentially increasing commitments and detention costs at state-operated correctional facilities, such as the Baltimore Pretrial Complex.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Because the bill establishes possible terms of imprisonment for offenses that previously carried only fines, indigent individuals charged under these statutes may become eligible for legal representation by the Public Defender.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits employment discrimination on the basis of sexual orientation under the State Equal Pay for Equal Work law. Bars employers from paying lower wages based on sexual orientation for comparable work in the same establishment. Prohibits employers from providing less favorable career tracks or advancement opportunities based on sexual orientation. Permits wage differentials based on non-discriminatory seniority, merit, or bona fide business-related factors. Forbids employers from reducing another employee's wage to achieve statutory compliance. Takes effect October 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor; Commissioner of Labor and Industry
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland employees, private employers including small businesses with fewer than 15 employees, and state and local government employers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on state or local revenues.
