Enforcement can be handled with existing resources, and state and local governments already prohibit employment discrimination based on sexual orientation. Employers with fewer than 15 employees are newly prohibited from discrimination based on sexual orientation.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor, specifically through the Commissioner of Labor and Industry, is the primary agency responsible for enforcing the State's Equal Pay for Equal Work law, investigating wage disparity and employment opportunity complaints, conducting mediation, and referring cases for legal action.

The Maryland Commission on Civil Rights is the primary state entity tasked with enforcing anti-discrimination statutes in employment, including protections involving sexual orientation and gender identity.

The Office of the Attorney General is authorized under the Equal Pay for Equal Work statute to file actions for injunctive relief and damages on behalf of employees upon request by the Commissioner of Labor and Industry.

The Administrative Office of the Courts supports the circuit courts where legal actions for damages and injunctive relief under the Equal Pay for Equal Work law may be filed by aggrieved employees or the State.

The Department of Budget and Management serves as the central personnel and human resources agency for the State government, ensuring state employment practices, classifications, and compensation policies comply with nondiscrimination laws.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires covered entities offering online products reasonably likely to be accessed by children to complete data protection impact assessments. Mandates default privacy settings offering a high level of privacy for children using those online products. Prohibits processing children's personal data unnecessarily, profiling children by default, and employing dark patterns to manipulate choices. Authorizes covered entities to permit parents or guardians to monitor children's online activity without signaling the child. Establishes civil penalties of up to $2,500 for negligent violations and $7,500 for intentional violations per affected child.
qa_results.responsible_party: Division of Consumer Protection of the Office of the Attorney General
qa_results.stakeholders: Children under age 18 in Maryland, parents and legal guardians, and covered commercial entities that provide online products or services.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: General fund expenditures increase, at least minimally, for the Consumer Protection Division within the Office of the Attorney General beginning in FY 2025 to handle enforcement. General fund revenues may increase minimally from civil penalties.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division is the primary regulatory and enforcement agency for the bill. It is responsible for requesting and reviewing data protection impact assessments, issuing violation notices, allowing cure periods, and bringing enforcement actions and civil penalty proceedings under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act.

The state court system would adjudicate any civil enforcement actions or injunctions pursued by the Consumer Protection Division, though fiscal and operational impacts on court dockets are expected to be minimal since the bill explicitly bars private rights of action.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes a comprehensive regulatory framework for recreational vehicle manufacturers, distributors, factory branches, and dealers. Requires recreational vehicle manufacturers, distributors, and factory branches to obtain licenses and post surety bonds with the Motor Vehicle Administration. Requires written dealer agreements that designate agreement duration, exclusive sales areas, and good cause standards for contract termination. Establishes warranty reimbursement requirements, claim resolution timelines, and mutual indemnification obligations between dealers and warrantors. Prohibits manufacturers and distributors from coercing dealers and regulates dealer ownership transfers and inventory repurchases. Authorizes the Administration to suspend or revoke licenses and impose civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation.
qa_results.responsible_party: Motor Vehicle Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: recreational vehicle manufacturers, distributors, factory branches, dealers, and warrantors
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not materially affected because the Motor Vehicle Administration can handle licensing and enforcement with existing budgeted resources. Special fund revenues from licensing fees and penalties are expected to remain substantially unchanged. Local government finances are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Motor Vehicle Administration (MVA) is the primary regulatory body tasked with implementing and enforcing the bill. MVA is responsible for licensing recreational vehicle manufacturers, distributors, and factory branches, establishing annual license fees, administering surety bond requirements, and taking enforcement actions (including license suspension/revocation and fines).

MVA is a modal administration within the Maryland Department of Transportation (MDOT). The bill establishes regulatory frameworks affecting MDOT's operations, and licensing and fine revenues impact the Transportation Trust Fund.

The bill provides that dealers, manufacturers, distributors, factory branches, or warrantors are entitled to administrative hearings to contest licensing actions or fines imposed by MVA, which are adjudicated by Administrative Law Judges at the Office of Administrative Hearings.

qa_results.bill_summary: Exempts specified community college students from Maryland Community College Promise Scholarship grade point average requirements. Covers applicants in noncredit vocational certificate programs, noncredit licensure or certification courses, or registered apprenticeship programs. Exempts these applicants from submitting federal or State student financial aid applications. Requires financial aid applications only when enrolling in a noncredit program eligible for a federal Pell Grant. Establishes eligibility for qualifying applicants who reside in Maryland or graduated from a Maryland high school. Takes effect July 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Higher Education Commission; Maryland community colleges
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland community college students enrolling in noncredit vocational certificate programs, noncredit courses leading to licensure or certification, or registered apprenticeship programs; Maryland community colleges
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No direct effect on State or local expenditures or revenues. Expanded eligibility does not alter statutory funding levels, but may increase the scholarship waiting list or reduce award amounts if demand exceeds the annual appropriation. Community colleges can update application criteria using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Higher Education Commission (MHEC) oversees postsecondary education and student financial assistance programs in Maryland. It allocates funding for the Maryland Community College Promise Scholarship program to community colleges, conducts outreach to high school counselors, and reports annually on the program's implementation.

As the state's coordinating board for higher education and administrator of state financial aid programs, the Commission allocates funding for the Maryland Community College Promise Scholarship program and oversees compliance and reporting.

The Maryland Department of Labor oversees workforce development, adult learning, and registered apprenticeship programs, which are directly affected by the bill's expanded scholarship eligibility and exemption provisions.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes collective bargaining rights and procedures for full-time and part-time employees of covered county public library systems and the Enoch Pratt Free Library. Excludes public library systems in Baltimore, Montgomery, and Prince George's counties, as well as confidential, management, and temporary employees. Limits each covered library system to not more than two bargaining units, separating non-supervisory and supervisory employees. Requires employers and certified exclusive representatives to negotiate in good faith over wages, hours, and terms of employment. Establishes representation and impasse procedures through neutral decision makers and mediators from the Federal Mediation and Conciliation Service. Prohibits strikes, work stoppages, secondary boycotts, and lockouts, subjecting violators to specific disciplinary and decertification penalties.
qa_results.responsible_party: Boards of Trustees of Public Library Systems; County Public Library Systems; Enoch Pratt Free Library
qa_results.stakeholders: Full-time and part-time employees of covered county public library systems and the Enoch Pratt Free Library, public library employers and boards of trustees, employee organizations, and county funding bodies.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund retirement expenditures may increase minimally beginning in fiscal 2029 if collective bargaining increases eligible employee salaries. Local public library expenditures may increase significantly due to costs for outside mediators, potential employee wage increases, and non-State retirement contributions.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a statewide collective bargaining framework for employees across Maryland's county public library systems by enacting Subtitle 9 under Article - Education, which directly relates to the public library systems overseen and coordinated by the Maryland State Library Agency.

The State pays retirement benefits for eligible local public library employees through the State Retirement and Pension System. Higher compensation resulting from collective bargaining will lead to increased retirement liabilities and State expenditures administered by the agency.

As the primary state body charged with centralizing and standardizing public sector labor relations in Maryland, the expansion of collective bargaining rights to public library personnel intersects with PERB's policy domain, although the dispute and mediation procedures under the bill utilize the Federal Mediation and Conciliation Service.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals the Electronic Transactions Protection Act. Removes statutory provisions establishing the Electronic Transaction Education, Advocacy, and Mediation Unit within the Office of the Attorney General. Eliminates formal statutory mandates for the unit to handle complaints, educate consumers, and investigate electronic commerce violations. Takes effect October 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General
qa_results.stakeholders: consumers engaging in electronic transactions and the Office of the Attorney General
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No substantive effect on State activities, operations, or finances, as the statutory unit was never funded and the Consumer Protection Division already handles these functions. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 611 repeals the Electronic Transactions Protection Act, which established the statutory framework for the Electronic Transaction Education, Advocacy, and Mediation Unit within the Office of the Attorney General.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes a recreational oyster license for Maryland residents at least 16 years old to harvest oysters. Removes statutory daily catch limits for clams and aligns clam harvesting with Department of Natural Resources regulations. Sets a $10 annual application fee and directs a portion of revenues toward replenishing public oyster bars. Mandates complimentary licenses for qualifying disabled veterans, former prisoners of war, and blind individuals. Provides discounted licenses for Purple Heart recipients. Authorizes owners and residents of waterfront property bordering tidal waters to harvest oysters without a license after registering.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland residents recreationally harvesting oysters or clams, waterfront property owners and their resident family members, commercial agents selling licenses, and military veterans
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues increase annually beginning in FY 2025 from the $10 license fee, estimated illustratively at $100,000 per 10,000 licenses issued. Special fund expenditures increase correspondingly to replenish public fishery oyster bars, though total amounts are indeterminate.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Natural Resources is the primary implementing agency for this legislation. The bill tasks the department with establishing and administering a recreational oyster license program, developing application forms, setting regulations for clam and oyster harvesting, authorizing sales agents, collecting license fees, and utilizing a portion of fee revenues to replenish public fishery oyster bars.

qa_results.bill_summary: Decreases the annual fee for a stadium beer, wine, and liquor license in Harford County from $10,000 to $7,000. Applies the lower fee to licenses issued to owners, lessees, or concession managers of professional baseball stadiums. Maintains existing operational restrictions on alcohol sales and service during baseball games. Takes effect July 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Harford County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Owners, lessees, and concession managers of professional baseball stadiums in Harford County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Harford County revenues decrease by $3,000 annually beginning in fiscal 2025 due to the reduced license fee. County expenditures are not affected. State operations and finances are not affected.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits consumer reporting agencies from including specific non-conviction and expunged criminal records in consumer reports. Applies the ban to proceedings where the consumer was falsely accused, acquitted, or exonerated. Extends the prohibition to charges resulting in a nolle prosequi or lacking a guilty verdict or plea. Bans consumer reporting agencies from reporting any expunged criminal records concerning a consumer. Prohibits consumer reporting agencies from relying on those records to determine a consumer's creditworthiness.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of Financial Regulation
qa_results.stakeholders: consumer reporting agencies and consumers with expunged or non-conviction criminal records
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Office of Financial Regulation can enforce the bill with existing resources. State revenues and local government operations and finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Labor houses the Office of Financial Regulation (OFR), which regulates financial institutions and consumer reporting agencies and is responsible for investigating and enforcing violations of state consumer credit laws.
The Office of the Attorney General houses the Consumer Protection Division, which has jurisdiction to investigate and enforce consumer protection provisions under the Commercial Law Article.

The Administrative Office of the Courts maintains and manages the judiciary's criminal case proceedings, dispositions, and expungement records that are referenced and restricted from consumer reports under the bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Transfers administration of the Next Generation Scholars of Maryland Program from the State Department of Education to the Maryland Higher Education Commission. Requires the Department to assist the Commission with application reviews and nonprofit organization selections. Directs the Commission to collaborate with the Department to publicize the program and participating entities. Establishes that the Department remains responsible for identifying eligible local school systems. Clarifies that required financial aid literacy assistance includes guidance on leveraging federal, State, and institutional aid. Applies the administrative alterations beginning in fiscal year 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Higher Education Commission; Maryland State Department of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: Students eligible for Guaranteed Access Grants or free or reduced-price meals under the National School Lunch Program, participating nonprofit organizations, and local school systems
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Beginning in FY 2026, $5.0 million in mandated annual special fund revenues and expenditures transfer from MSDE to MHEC with no net fund effect. Assuming special funds are not used for administrative expenses, MHEC general fund expenditures increase by $223,700 in FY 2026 for 1.5 positions and MDCAPS system upgrades, and between $157,600 and $171,800 annually thereafter. MSDE can fulfill its collaborative duties using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates the Maryland Higher Education Commission as the new primary administrator of the Next Generation Scholars of Maryland Program and its associated special fund, transferring administrative responsibilities, grantmaking authority, and regulatory oversight to the agency beginning in fiscal year 2026.

The bill designates the Commission as the new primary administrator of the Next Generation Scholars of Maryland Program and the Next Generation Scholars of Maryland Program Fund, requiring it to award grants, review applications, adopt regulations, and report annually to the General Assembly.

The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) is relieved of primary administration of the program and its fund, but is statutorily required to assist the Commission with application reviews and nonprofit selection, collaborate on program publicity, identify eligible school systems, and co-author the annual implementation report.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands educational training topics required annually for trustees on the Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System. Adds training on investments, retirement administration and operations, and other topics deemed appropriate by the Board Chairman. Requires the Board to provide an annual report summary and system modifications on the State Retirement Agency's website. Directs the Board to make personal benefit statements available to members and retirees through a secure access participant portal. Specifies that portal information must include vested benefits, vesting dates, and the present value of any annuity.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System
qa_results.stakeholders: Members and retirees of the State Retirement and Pension System; trustees on the Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No direct effect on State or local governmental finances; the State Retirement and Pension System may experience administrative efficiencies.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 625 directly impacts the State Retirement and Pension System (SRPS) and the Maryland State Retirement Agency by revising the mandatory annual educational training topics for the Board of Trustees and authorizing the agency to fulfill annual benefit reporting requirements via its website and a secure participant online portal.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters waiver requirements for reciprocal licensure of clinical marriage and family therapists licensed in another state, territory, or jurisdiction. Requires the State Board of Professional Counselors and Therapists to waive specific degree, experience, and examination requirements under certain conditions. Requires applicants to have no past or pending disciplinary history and submit copies of current out-of-state licenses. Prohibits the Board from requiring applicants to pass a national certification examination. Authorizes the Board to require applicants to pass an examination on Maryland statutory requirements.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Professional Counselors and Therapists
qa_results.stakeholders: clinical marriage and family therapists licensed or certified in another state, territory, or jurisdiction seeking licensure in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The change is procedural in nature and does not affect governmental finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Professional Counselors and Therapists operates within the Maryland Department of Health and is directly responsible for administering the licensure, regulations, and waiver requirements for clinical marriage and family therapists.

qa_results.bill_summary: Updates the definition of Consumer Price Index in State pension law. Replaces the 1967 base year index with the 1982–1984 index. Applies the updated index to cost-of-living adjustment calculations for State Retirement and Pension System retirees. Takes effect October 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Retirement and Pension System
qa_results.stakeholders: retirees of the State Retirement and Pension System
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is technical in nature and has no material effect on State or local governmental operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 629 directly amends the statutory definition of the Consumer Price Index (CPI) utilized by the State Retirement and Pension System (SRPS) to calculate annual cost-of-living adjustments for retirees, which is administered directly by the Maryland State Retirement Agency.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals the benefit cap on transferred service credit when an individual retires within five years after transferring systems. Updates the member contribution rate calculation for transferring service into the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System. Grants up to 10 years of service credit in the Employees' Pension System for qualifying contractual Department of Legislative Services employees. Requires eligible employees to submit a claim by December 31, 2024, and deposit unpaid member contributions before retirement. Reduces a member's retirement allowance if the required member contributions are not paid prior to retirement.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System
qa_results.stakeholders: Members of the State Retirement and Pension System transferring service credit, members transferring credit into the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System, and qualifying contractual employees at the Department of Legislative Services
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No discernible effect on State pension liabilities or contribution rates, as the service credit purchase provisions are expected to apply to only two individuals and employee contributions mitigate costs. Conforms other provisions to current practice with no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Retirement Agency administers the State Retirement and Pension System (SRPS). This bill directly alters SRPS service credit transfer rules, corrects contribution rate provisions for the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System, and requires the Board of Trustees to process claims for contractual service credit.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes a Class GSF (golf simulator facility) alcoholic beverages license in Harford County. Authorizes the Board of License Commissioners for Harford County to issue the license to eligible public facilities with at least five simulator bays. Permits the license holder to sell beer, wine, and liquor for on-premises consumption if food is continuously offered during alcohol sales. Requires annual gross sales of at least 50% from simulator bay rentals and at least 15% from food. Prohibits annual gross sales from alcoholic beverages from exceeding 35% of total gross sales. Sets the annual license fee at $1,500.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Harford County
qa_results.stakeholders: golf simulator facility owners, operators, and patrons in Harford County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Harford County revenues increase by $1,500 in fiscal 2025 and annually thereafter for each Class GSF license issued or renewed. County expenditures for enforcement can be handled with existing resources. No state fiscal effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller regulates the alcohol industry and collects state alcohol and sales taxes in Maryland. Although this legislation specifically authorizes the local Harford County Board of License Commissioners to issue a Class GSF license with no direct state fiscal impact, it relates to the regulation and retail sale of alcoholic beverages.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Governing Board of the Maryland Longitudinal Data System Center to send student information to the United States Census Bureau. Defines student information to include student Social Security numbers, programs of study, enrollment, and educational institution names. Allows data sharing to support national research on earnings and postsecondary employment outcomes. Takes effect October 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governing Board of the Maryland Longitudinal Data System Center; Maryland Longitudinal Data System Center
qa_results.stakeholders: Students and graduates of Maryland educational institutions, postsecondary educational institutions, researchers, and the United States Census Bureau
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures can be absorbed using existing resources if the Governing Board authorizes sending the data. State revenues and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly applies to the Maryland Longitudinal Data System Center by authorizing its Governing Board to send student information to the United States Census Bureau for research projects such as the Post-Secondary Employment Outcomes project.

The Maryland Longitudinal Data System Center is administratively housed within the Maryland State Department of Education, and the department is one of the primary providers of the student information managed by the center.

The bill amends Section 24-703.2 of the Education Article, which establishes data-sharing and matching protocols between the Center and the Comptroller, and the Comptroller served as an information source during legislative review.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes a performing arts nonprofit organization beer, wine, and liquor license in Harford County. Authorizes the Board of License Commissioners to issue the license for up to three designated locations. Authorizes license holders to sell or serve alcohol during, before, and after performances and related receptions. Prohibits selling or issuing more than 750 tickets to any performance where alcohol is served. Requires license holders to offer snacks at all times when selling alcohol and maintain transaction records. Sets the annual license fee at $750.
qa_results.responsible_party: Harford County Board of License Commissioners; Comptroller of Maryland; Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Performing arts nonprofit organizations in Harford County, patrons of performing arts events in Harford County, and licensed alcoholic beverage wholesalers and retailers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal effect. Harford County revenues increase by at least $750 annually beginning in FY 2025 from license fees and potentially additional revenue from penalties. Additional local enforcement activities can be handled with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly grants the Comptroller the authority to inspect and audit alcoholic beverages records maintained by license holders, require reports under oath, and suspend licenses for up to 30 days without a hearing for noncompliance with record-keeping provisions.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the governing body of Allegany County or a municipal corporation in the county to grant a property tax credit. Limits the credit to property owned by Evergreen Heritage Center Foundation, Inc., or Evergreen Heritage Center Holdings, LLC. Applies the credit against imposed county or municipal corporation property taxes. Takes effect June 1, 2024. Applies to all taxable years beginning after June 30, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Allegany County; municipal corporations in Allegany County
qa_results.stakeholders: Evergreen Heritage Center Foundation, Inc.; Evergreen Heritage Center Holdings, LLC; Allegany County; municipal corporations in Allegany County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Allegany County property tax revenues may decrease by approximately $5,300 annually beginning in fiscal 2025 to the extent the credit is granted. County expenditures and State finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 636 authorizes Allegany County and its municipalities to grant an optional local property tax credit for property owned by the Evergreen Heritage Center Foundation or Holdings. As the administrative appellate body that hears disputes concerning real property valuations, exemptions, and property tax credits, the Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board could have jurisdiction over potential disputes regarding the application or administration of this credit.

qa_results.bill_summary: Consolidates the Maryland income tax subtraction modifications for volunteer police personnel and volunteer fire, rescue, and emergency services personnel. Increases the subtraction modification for qualifying police auxiliary and reserve volunteers from $5,000 to $7,000 beginning in tax year 2024. Requires bona fide Maryland police agencies to maintain volunteer activity records and provide qualification reports to members by February 15. Mandates police agencies submit annual qualification reports to the Comptroller and the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services by October 1. Imposes a $1,000 fine for knowingly making false statements or reports under the program.
qa_results.responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland; Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services; Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: qualifying police auxiliary and reserve volunteers, bona fide Maryland police agencies, and Maryland local governments
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues decrease by $21,000 annually beginning in FY 2025 due to the increased subtraction amount. Local income tax revenues decrease by $14,000 annually beginning in FY 2025. The Comptroller's Office can implement the changes using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the state's tax administration agency, the Comptroller oversees the implementation of personal income tax subtraction modifications and is statutorily designated to receive annual certification reports containing names and Social Security numbers of qualifying public safety volunteers.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates that bona fide police agencies and the Maryland State Firemen's Association submit annual reports to the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services listing qualifying individuals. Additionally, the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission, which operates under DPSCS, is responsible for approving police auxiliary and reserve volunteer programs.

As Maryland's primary state law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police is a bona fide police agency subject to the record-keeping and reporting requirements if utilizing qualifying auxiliary or reserve volunteer personnel.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes a comprehensive legal framework governing pet insurance policies and certificates in the State. Requires pet insurers to disclose policy exclusions, waiting periods, benefit schedules, and claim calculation methods to consumers. Mandates a 10-day policy cancellation window with a pro rata premium refund if no claim was filed. Prohibits waiting periods for accident-related conditions and caps non-accident waiting periods at 30 days. Prohibits marketing separate wellness programs as pet insurance or during pet insurance sales and negotiations. Requires the Maryland Insurance Administration to develop informational pet insurance materials for veterinary practitioners by June 1, 2025.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Pet insurers, pet insurance producers, pet owners purchasing pet insurance policies, and veterinary practitioners in Maryland.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal increase in Maryland Insurance Administration special fund revenues in FY 2025 only from rate and form filing fees. Enforcement can be handled using existing budgeted resources. No effect on local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Insurance Administration is the primary regulator responsible for implementing and enforcing the statutory framework for pet insurance, reviewing policy forms and rates, handling consumer disclosures, and developing informational materials for veterinary practitioners.

The bill references definitions under the Agriculture Article governing veterinary practitioners, whom the Department of Agriculture licenses and regulates via the State Board of Veterinary Medical Examiners, and who may receive and display pet insurance informational materials.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires employers to disclose the wage range, benefits, and other compensation in all job postings. Applies to positions for work physically performed at least in part in the State. Directs employers to disclose this information to applicants before compensation discussions if no posting was provided. Mandates employers to set disclosed wage ranges in good faith using specified criteria. Prohibits retaliation against applicants or employees who exercise rights under these wage disclosure provisions. Requires employers to maintain compliance records for each position for at least three years.
qa_results.responsible_party: Commissioner of Labor and Industry; Maryland Department of Labor
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland employers, job applicants, and current employees seeking promotions or transfers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $98,800 in FY 2025 for the Maryland Department of Labor to handle investigations and legal support, with ongoing expenditures in future years. Local government operational costs may increase minimally for disclosure and recordkeeping compliance.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Labor's Division of Labor and Industry is the primary implementing and enforcement agency for the bill. The Commissioner of Labor and Industry is required to develop a compliance form for employers, investigate complaints, issue compliance orders, and assess civil penalties for wage transparency violations.

As the State's central personnel agency overseeing State government employee resources, hiring, job classifications, and salary structures, DBM is responsible for ensuring executive branch job postings and recruitment processes comply with the bill's wage range and benefit disclosure requirements.

The OAG provides legal representation and counsel to the Department of Labor, assists in interpreting the statute, and may be requested by the Commissioner of Labor and Industry to initiate court enforcement actions against non-compliant employers.
The Office of Administrative Hearings adjudicates contested administrative enforcement cases delegated by the Maryland Department of Labor when civil penalties or orders are appealed by employers.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Labor to submit an apprenticeship mentoring ratio report to the General Assembly by October 1, 2024. Mandates that the report analyze ratios for all nontraditional apprenticeable occupations outside of the building trades. Requires the department to identify occupations that could safely operate with higher than one-to-one mentorship ratios. Directs the report to detail five-year waiver request outcomes and reasons for any denied requests. Requires recommended strategies to streamline ratio expansion for newly registered nontraditional occupations to meet Apprenticeship 2030 Commission goals.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor
qa_results.stakeholders: sponsors, employers, journeypersons, and apprentices in nontraditional apprenticeable occupations outside the building trades
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact; the Maryland Department of Labor can complete the required study and report using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Maryland Department of Labor (MDL) and its Maryland Apprenticeship and Training Council to analyze nontraditional apprenticeship mentoring ratios and submit a comprehensive report to the General Assembly by October 1, 2024.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes a beer, wine, and liquor tasting permit in St. Mary’s County. Authorizes the St. Mary’s County Board of License Commissioners to issue the permit to Class A license holders. Allows on-premises consumption of beer, wine, and liquor for tasting purposes only. Sets permit fees at $200 for 26 days, $250 for 52 days, and $300 for 365 days. Limits individual daily consumption amounts across all offerings of beer, wine, and liquor. Requires 26-day and 52-day permit holders to notify the board at least seven days before an event.
qa_results.responsible_party: St. Mary's County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Class A alcoholic beverages license holders and retail alcohol consumers in St. Mary's County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state fiscal effect. St. Mary's County revenues increase depending on the number of tasting permits issued, while local enforcement activities can be handled with existing county resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a local beer, wine, and liquor tasting permit administered by the St. Mary's County Board of License Commissioners, with no direct state fiscal effect. However, the Comptroller of Maryland oversees state regulation of the alcoholic beverage industry and enforcement of alcohol-related laws.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes a nonprofit performing arts theater beer and wine license in St. Mary's County. Authorizes the Board of License Commissioners to issue the license to seated theaters operated by nonprofit organizations. Allows the license holder to sell or serve beer and wine at retail for on-premises consumption. Restricts sales from one hour before to one hour after regular or fundraising performances. Authorizes the license holder to purchase beer and wine from a retail license holder or licensed wholesaler. Sets the annual license fee at $300.
qa_results.responsible_party: St. Mary's County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: nonprofit performing arts theaters in St. Mary's County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: St. Mary's County revenues may decrease by approximately $350 annually beginning in fiscal 2025 as theaters substitute per diem licenses for the annual license. St. Mary's County expenditures are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland oversees and regulates the state's alcoholic beverage industry. Although this legislation creates a local license administered by the St. Mary's County Board of License Commissioners with no state fiscal impact, it amends the state Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article and governs the retail sale and wholesale purchasing of alcoholic beverages.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires State regulations to set the minimum age for child care teachers at 18 years old. Applies the age standard to registered large family child care homes and licensed child care centers. Prohibits disqualifying an individual from being a child care teacher solely for being 18 years old. Takes effect July 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Education; Maryland State Department of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: large family child care homes, child care centers, and 18-year-old child care teacher applicants
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland State Department of Education can implement the bill with existing resources, with no effect on State revenues or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Education and the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) are responsible for regulating, licensing, and registering child care centers and large family child care homes, and are tasked with updating regulations to reflect the minimum age requirement of 18 for child care teachers.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes protected judicial officers and household members to request removal of their personal information from online publication. Requires governmental entities and persons to remove the specified personal information within 72 hours after receiving a written request. Establishes civil remedies and creates a misdemeanor penalty of up to 18 months imprisonment and a $5,000 fine for violations. Establishes the Judicial Address Confidentiality Program to shield participants' residential addresses and real property records from public inspection. Establishes the Task Force to Ensure the Safety of Judicial Facilities to identify courthouse security standards and deficiencies.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of Information Privacy in the Administrative Office of the Courts; Administrative Office of the Courts
qa_results.stakeholders: Current and retired Maryland and federal judges, magistrates, District Court commissioners, and their co-residing household family members, as well as state and local governmental entities and individuals or entities publishing records online.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances and operations are not materially affected; the Judiciary can establish the Office of Information Privacy and staff the task force using existing budgeted resources. Local government finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates the Office of Information Privacy within the Administrative Office of the Courts to administer the Judicial Address Confidentiality Program, handle requests to protect and remove court personnel's personal information, and staff the Task Force to Ensure the Safety of Judicial Facilities.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a statutory body, the Task Force to Ensure the Safety of Judicial Facilities, to study courthouse security and report findings and legislative recommendations.
The Superintendent of the Maryland State Police (or designee) is designated by statute as a member of the Task Force to Ensure the Safety of Judicial Facilities.

The Secretary of General Services (or designee) is named as a member of the Task Force to Ensure the Safety of Judicial Facilities, leveraging DGS's role overseeing state facility management and Capitol Police security.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Secretary of Public Safety and Correctional Services (or designee) is appointed as a statutory member of the Task Force to Ensure the Safety of Judicial Facilities.
The Secretary of Budget and Management (or designee) is designated as a member of the Task Force to Ensure the Safety of Judicial Facilities.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Public Defender (or designee) is designated as a member of the Task Force to Ensure the Safety of Judicial Facilities.
The bill amends real property provisions intersecting with the Address Confidentiality Program administered by the Secretary of State to incorporate the new Judicial Address Confidentiality Program.

The Governor is tasked with appointing multiple members to the Task Force to Ensure the Safety of Judicial Facilities, including local county leaders, sheriffs, chiefs of police, and a MACo representative.

qa_results.bill_summary: Lowers the qualifying age from 62 to 60 for household eligibility to receive a State-provided SNAP supplemental benefit. Increases the guaranteed minimum monthly SNAP benefit for eligible households from $40 to $50. Requires the State to provide a supplement whenever a qualifying household receives less than $50 monthly in federal benefits. Takes effect October 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Human Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Low-income Maryland households with an individual who is at least 60 years old receiving Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program benefits
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $4.2 million in fiscal 2025, which was budgeted contingently, and by an estimated $3.9 million annually beginning in fiscal 2026. Local finances are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Human Services (DHS) directly administers the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) and the State-funded supplemental benefit. DHS will be responsible for implementing the expanded eligibility for individuals aged 60 and older and increasing the minimum benefit level to $50 per month, which incurs a direct general fund expenditure impact.

The Department of Aging oversees advocacy, nutrition, and supportive programs for older adults across Maryland. Expanding food assistance eligibility down to age 60 and increasing the monthly benefit directly impacts the population and nutrition services the department advocates for and coordinates with.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the annual salary of the Sheriff of Anne Arundel County. Sets the salary equal to that of a captain in the Anne Arundel County Police Department at step 20. Maintains the prior annual salary of $133,000 through calendar year 2024. Applies the salary adjustment beginning at the start of the next term of office. Takes effect October 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Anne Arundel County Government
qa_results.stakeholders: Sheriff of Anne Arundel County and Anne Arundel County taxpayers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Anne Arundel County expenditures increase by a minimum of $20,100 in fiscal 2027 and by at least $34,400 annually thereafter once the new term of office begins. State finances and county revenues are unaffected.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the calculation of workers' compensation benefits for occupational hearing loss. Adds the 4,000 hertz frequency threshold to the measurement and calculation of occupational deafness. Requires employers to provide compensation for hearing loss caused by industrial noise at that frequency. Modifies the age-related deduction for nonoccupational hearing loss found in the population. Sets the deduction to the lesser of years over age 50 or years since last injurious exposure.
qa_results.responsible_party: Workers' Compensation Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Covered employees experiencing work-related hearing loss, employers, and workers' compensation insurers including Chesapeake Employers' Insurance Company
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local expenditures increase minimally beginning in fiscal 2025 due to modified occupational deafness calculations. Chesapeake Employers' Insurance Company expenditures and revenues also increase minimally to cover additional liabilities.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Commission is the primary regulatory and adjudicative body responsible for administering Maryland's Workers' Compensation Law and will be directly responsible for evaluating and calculating occupational deafness claims under the bill's updated frequency thresholds and formula.

Operating as the Chesapeake Employers' Insurance Company and third-party administrator for State of Maryland employee workers' compensation claims, the agency faces direct operational and fiscal impacts from increased compensability and higher average benefit payouts for hearing loss claims.

The Subsequent Injury Fund investigates and pays workers' compensation claims involving pre-existing conditions and liabilities that combine with workplace injuries, directly interacting with modified hearing loss thresholds and nonoccupational deduction calculations.

The Treasurer's Office administers the State Insurance Trust Fund, which funds workers' compensation benefits for state employees and will absorb a minimal increase in claim costs under the revised hearing loss calculations.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands Maryland's Right to Try Act to cover individualized investigational treatments tailored to a patient's genetic profile. Broadens patient eligibility from individuals with terminal illnesses to those with life-threatening or severely debilitating illnesses. Authorizes manufacturers operating in eligible facilities to provide these treatments and charge patients for manufacturing costs. Repeals the prohibition against manufacturers profiting from providing eligible patients with investigational treatments. Authorizes health insurance carriers, third-party administrators, and government agencies to cover treatment costs. Prohibits State officials and health occupations boards from blocking patient access or disciplining participating providers.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General; Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Patients with life-threatening or severely debilitating illnesses; manufacturers of individualized investigational treatments; treating physicians and licensed health care providers; health insurance carriers and third-party administrators
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates the Office of the Attorney General to develop an informed consent form that complies with the revised statutory requirements under the Right to Try Act.

The bill amends the Health - General Article and places specific restrictions on the Maryland Department of Health and health occupations boards regarding disciplinary actions or actions against a provider's Medicare certification related to individualized investigational treatments.

The bill references health insurance carriers, third-party administrators, and Title 15 of the Insurance Article, permitting coverage for individualized investigational treatments and related services, which falls under MIA's regulatory oversight.

The bill permits government agencies to cover the costs of individualized investigational treatments (without mandating coverage), which could affect the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program administered by DBM.

The bill clarifies provisions regarding civil liability and the absence of a private cause of action against manufacturers and healthcare providers complying with the subtitle in good faith, which minimally impacts the state judicial system.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands the principles of public higher education in Maryland to include promoting diversity and inclusion. Requires each public senior higher education institution, excluding University of Maryland Global Campus, to adopt an annual recruitment policy. Directs institutions to identify communities of interest with historically underrepresented groups, demographics, or geographic areas. Requires each covered institution to complete targeted recruitment and outreach efforts in those communities annually. Mandates annual reporting on outreach efforts and admission data to State officials beginning August 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: University System of Maryland; Morgan State University; St. Mary's College of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Prospective college students from historically underrepresented groups, demographics, or geographic areas in Maryland; public senior higher education institutions (excluding University of Maryland Global Campus)
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Indeterminate, potentially material increase in State higher education expenditures for some public four-year institutions to hire outreach staff and comply with reporting requirements; some institutions may absorb costs within existing resources. No effect on State revenues or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Constituent institutions of the University System of Maryland (with the exception of UMGC) are directly mandated to develop, adopt, and annually update policies for targeted recruitment and outreach in communities of interest, carry out those activities, and submit annual reports.

As a public senior higher education institution, Morgan State University is directly required to adopt and annually update outreach policies for communities of interest, conduct specified recruitment efforts, and report annually on its outcomes and plans.

As a public four-year higher education institution, St. Mary's College of Maryland is directly subject to the bill's requirements to establish targeted recruitment and outreach policies, perform outreach in communities of interest, and submit annual reports.
Public senior higher education institutions are required to submit an annual report by August 1 each year directly to the Governor on communities of interest, outreach efforts, and admissions data.

MHEC establishes statewide policies and coordinating principles for public higher education in Maryland, and the bill amends the statutory principles of public higher education under Section 10-202 of the Education Article.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Radiation Emergency Response Program within the Maryland Department of the Environment. Designates the department as the lead State agency and an off-site response organization for nuclear incidents. Requires owners of qualifying nuclear power plants to remit two annual fees for each facility. Deposits a $300,000 annual fee into the newly established Radiation Emergency Response Fund. Transfers an additional $60,000 annual fee to the Maryland Department of Emergency Management. Authorizes the Maryland Department of the Environment to increase fees annually by up to 3%.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment; Maryland Department of Emergency Management
qa_results.stakeholders: Owners and operators of nuclear power plants affecting Maryland, including Constellation Energy, and the general public
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues and expenditures for the Maryland Department of the Environment increase by $600,000 annually beginning in FY 2025 from fees assessed on two nuclear power plants. An additional $120,000 in collected fees is transferred annually to the Maryland Department of Emergency Management, replacing an existing funding agreement with no net fiscal impact on that agency. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDE is the primary implementing agency tasked with establishing and administering the Radiation Emergency Response Program and the Radiation Emergency Response Fund, serving as the lead state agency for protective actions during nuclear incidents, and collecting fees from nuclear power plant owners.

MDEM receives transferred fee revenues ($60,000 per nuclear power plant) for radiological emergency response preparedness activities and is required to incorporate MDE's technical emergency radiation response plan into the State Emergency Management Program.
The State Treasurer is statutorily required to hold the newly created Radiation Emergency Response Fund separately and invest its moneys with interest credited back to the fund.
The Comptroller is statutorily designated to account for the newly established Radiation Emergency Response Fund.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Maryland Aerospace and Technology Commission within the Department of Commerce. Directs the Commission to promote innovation in space exploration and commercial aerospace opportunities. Requires the Commission to designate aerospace and technology zones and determine their boundaries. Mandates that the Commission develop and annually update an aerospace economic development strategic plan. Requires the Department of Commerce to provide staff support to the Commission. Requires the Commission to submit an annual activity and strategic plan report by October 1.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Commerce; Maryland Aerospace and Technology Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland aerospace and aviation businesses, aerospace researchers, institutions of higher education, and workforce trainees in the aerospace sector
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures for the Department of Commerce increase by $161,400 in FY 2025 for one program manager and a consultant, followed by ongoing costs between $103,600 and $117,900 annually through FY 2029. State revenues and local finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 685 establishes the Maryland Aerospace and Technology Commission within the Department of Commerce. Commerce is responsible for providing staff support (including hiring a program manager), the Secretary of Commerce serves on the Commission, and the department incurs general fund expenditures to support the Commission's operations and consulting needs.

The bill mandates that the President of the University of Maryland Baltimore County (UMBC) and the President of the University of Maryland, College Park (UMCP)—both constituent institutions of USM—or their designees, serve as members of the Maryland Aerospace and Technology Commission.

The Governor appoints four members of the Commission with the advice and consent of the Senate, retains authority to remove appointed members, and receives the Commission's annual reports on activities and strategic plans.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a new ongoing state body—the Maryland Aerospace and Technology Commission—and authorizes the Commission to establish advisory committees as needed to support its mission.
The Office of Appointments within the Executive Department is tasked with vetting, recruiting, and coordinating the Governor's appointments of the four public and industry members to the Commission.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Governor to include an annual $5,000,000 appropriation in the budget bill for the Historical and Cultural Museum Assistance Program. Allocates the funding to the Maryland Historical Trust to provide grants to museums. Repeals the restriction barring grants to museums currently receiving operating support from the Maryland State Arts Council. Permits political subdivisions and nonprofit organizations to use grant funds for collections care, exhibits, research, and operating support. Takes effect July 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Historical Trust
qa_results.stakeholders: Political subdivisions, nonprofit organizations, and museums throughout Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures and special fund revenues and expenditures increase by an assumed $5.0 million annually beginning in fiscal 2026. Local government revenues and expenditures increase annually beginning in fiscal 2026 from the receipt and expenditure of grant funds.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Historical Trust (MHT) is a unit within the Department of Planning. The bill directly impacts MHT by authorizing a $5 million annual appropriation for grants under the Historical and Cultural Museum Assistance Program, removing certain grant prohibitions, and necessitating administrative staffing at MHT to manage the program.

The bill explicitly authorizes the Governor to include an appropriation of $5.0 million in the annual budget bill for the Maryland Historical Trust to fund grants under the program starting in fiscal year 2025 and each year thereafter.

As the agency responsible for developing the Governor's annual state budget and overseeing general fund expenditures and state personnel additions, DBM is impacted by the potential $5.0 million general fund appropriation and new positions associated with the program.

The bill references statutory responsibilities of the State Archivist, requiring the Museum Assistance Review Panel to seek advice and recommendations from the State Archivist on grant applications relating to the care, preservation, or access to archival material.

The bill repeals the prohibition barring museums that receive operating support from the Maryland State Arts Council (housed within Commerce's Division of Tourism, Film and the Arts) from receiving grants from the Maryland Historical Trust.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters membership requirements for the Adult Protective Services Review Board in Charles County. Authorizes appointing a physician's assistant or nurse practitioner in psychiatry instead of a psychiatrist. Maintains the requirement for one physician's assistant, nurse practitioner, or physician who is not a psychiatrist. Applies these modified board qualifications specifically to Charles County appointments. Takes effect October 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Charles County Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Adult Protective Services Review Board members in Charles County; psychiatrists, physician's assistants, and nurse practitioners in the field of psychiatry in Charles County; vulnerable adults under public guardianship in Charles County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or Charles County government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Human Services (DHS) oversees Adult Protective Services and the local departments of social services, which initiate adult public guardianships reviewed by county Adult Protective Services Review Boards under Title 14 of the Family Law Article.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Office of Tenant and Landlord Affairs within the Department of Housing and Community Development. Limits residential lease security deposits to one month's rent, except under specified utility assistance conditions. Grants eligible tenants an exclusive negotiation period and right of first refusal to purchase certain rental properties. Increases civil case filing surcharges in the District Court and circuit courts to fund rental and legal assistance. Extends the minimum timeline from repossession judgment to restitution warrant issuance from four to seven days. Requires district administrative judges to stay eviction warrant executions during extreme weather conditions or declared emergencies.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development; Office of Tenant and Landlord Affairs; Maryland Judiciary
qa_results.stakeholders: Residential tenants; residential landlords and rental property owners; civil litigants in the District Court and circuit courts; legal services providers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues increase by up to $13.3 million in FY 2025 and up to $17.7 million annually thereafter from increased civil filing surcharges. State general fund expenditures increase by $379,300 in FY 2025 ($344,500 for DHCD personnel and $34,800 for Judiciary computer programming), increasing to $466,500 by FY 2029. Local fee revenues, particularly in Baltimore City, potentially decrease minimally if ejectment filings decline.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DHCD is the primary implementing agency for this legislation. The bill establishes the Office of Tenant and Landlord Affairs within DHCD, directs the department to publish a Tenants' Bill of Rights, receive and monitor notices regarding tenants' rights of first refusal and exclusive negotiations, gather and publish statewide eviction and property transfer data dashboards, and allocate surcharge funds to the Statewide Rental Assistance Voucher Program.

The bill directly impacts the Maryland Judiciary by increasing civil and summary ejectment court surcharges, altering how surcharges are assessed and prohibited from being passed to tenants, requiring mandatory stays of warrants of restitution during extreme weather or emergencies, extending eviction timelines, and expanding monthly eviction data collection and reporting requirements to DHCD.

The bill creates an exception allowing landlords to collect up to two months' security deposit if the tenant qualifies for utility assistance through the Department of Human Services and pays utilities directly to the landlord. In addition, surcharge revenues are directed to statutory funds codified under the Human Services Article.

The newly established Office of Tenant and Landlord Affairs will identify non-compliant landlords, conduct fair housing testing, and facilitate referrals of unlawful housing practices and statutory violations to law enforcement agencies and civil enforcement bodies such as the Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division.

The bill empowers the new Office of Tenant and Landlord Affairs to conduct fair housing testing, monitor unfair housing practices, and notify or refer complaints of unlawful housing discrimination to relevant enforcement authorities like the Commission on Civil Rights.

The bill is an Administration priority sponsored on behalf of the Governor's legislative agenda, requires DHCD to submit an annual comprehensive eviction data report to the Governor, and ties stay-of-eviction procedures to states of emergency declared by the Governor.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires commercial real estate sales contracts submitted by real estate licensees to state in bold type that buyers may select their own providers. Specifies the buyer's right to choose a title insurance company, settlement company, escrow company, or title lawyer. Requires the disclosure to state that sellers are not prohibited from offering owner financing as a condition of settlement. Prohibits real estate licensees and lawyers acting as brokers from conditioning commercial real estate settlements on using specific settlement providers. Defines commercial real estate to include multifamily and nonresidential properties while excluding agricultural land and single-family units conveyed individually.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Real Estate Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: commercial real estate buyers and sellers, licensed real estate brokers and salespersons, lawyers acting as real estate brokers, title insurance companies, settlement companies, escrow companies, and title lawyers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Does not materially affect Maryland Real Estate Commission finances or operations, and is not anticipated to materially affect local finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor houses the Maryland Real Estate Commission, which regulates and licenses real estate brokers, associate brokers, and salespersons under Title 17 of the Business Occupations and Professions Article amended by this bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Defines returning election judges eligible for extra daily compensation as judges who served during the immediately preceding statewide election. Requires the State Board of Elections to develop and implement an election judge recruitment marketing campaign. Entitles county employees serving as election judges during scheduled work hours to administrative leave and election judge compensation. Requires the State Board of Elections to adopt regulations standardizing and minimizing election judge documentation. Prohibits local election boards and county governments from requiring additional forms beyond State Board regulations.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Elections; local boards of elections
qa_results.stakeholders: Election judges, prospective election judges, county employees serving as election judges, and county governments
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Local expenditures increase by $25,000 in FY 2025 for one-time system programming. State and local expenditures decrease annually beginning in FY 2026 due to fewer judges qualifying for extra compensation, though the exact decrease cannot be reliably determined (illustratively estimated at $190,100 annually for the State and $190,100 collectively for local governments).

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Elections (SBE) is the primary implementing agency for the bill. SBE is required to develop and implement a statewide marketing campaign for recruiting election judges, adopt regulations standardizing and minimizing election judge documentation, and manage reimbursements to local election boards for returning election judge compensation.

qa_results.bill_summary: Exempts certain minor league baseball players from the Maryland Wage and Hour Law. Applies to an individual under contract to play baseball at the minor league level. Requires the individual to be compensated under a collective bargaining agreement. Mandates that the agreement expressly state employee wages and working conditions. Takes effect October 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor
qa_results.stakeholders: Minor league baseball players and minor league baseball teams operating in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No substantive impact on State operations or finances, and no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor administers and enforces the Maryland Wage and Hour Law. This bill creates a specific statutory exemption from that law for certain minor league baseball players compensated under a collective bargaining agreement.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes a licensed real estate broker to designate themselves as the manager of a branch office. Applies existing qualification standards only when the broker designates another individual as branch office manager. Retains requirements for obtaining and renewing branch office certificates and paying the five-dollar fee. Directs the designated manager to supervise real estate brokerage services provided from that branch office. Takes effect October 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Real Estate Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: licensed real estate brokers, associate real estate brokers, and licensed real estate salespersons in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Real Estate Commission can implement the bill with existing resources. State revenues and local finances are not affected. May reduce operating costs for small real estate brokerage businesses.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Real Estate Commission is housed within the Maryland Department of Labor's Division of Occupational and Professional Licensing. The bill alters requirements for branch office certificates and manager designations regulated by the Commission.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Household Goods Movers Registration Fund as a special, nonlapsing fund in the Maryland Department of Labor. Requires the Comptroller to distribute all fees collected from household goods movers into the fund. Directs the Secretary of Labor to annually calculate the department's direct and indirect regulatory costs. Authorizes the department to set reasonable fees by regulation based on the Secretary's calculations. Prohibits the department from increasing any fee by more than 12.5% annually. Credits any investment earnings of the fund to the General Fund of the State.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor
qa_results.stakeholders: Household goods movers and applicants for registration to provide household goods moving services in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No net effect on State finances. General fund revenues and expenditures for regulating household goods movers are replaced by special fund revenues and expenditures from registration fees. There is no local government fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Household Goods Movers Registration Fund within the Maryland Department of Labor to cover the costs of regulating household goods movers, and authorizes the Secretary of Labor to calculate costs and set registration fees.
The bill requires the Department of Labor to pay all fees collected under Title 8.5 to the Comptroller, who is responsible for distributing the fees into the newly created special fund.
The bill specifically mandates that the Legislative Auditor audit the accounts and transactions of the Household Goods Movers Registration Fund.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Department of Natural Resources to issue lifetime complimentary fishing and hunting licenses to certain unemployable American veterans. Covers Maryland residents and qualified out-of-state veterans whom the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs determines are unemployable. Requires out-of-state veterans' home states to offer reciprocal privileges to Maryland veterans. Applies to lifetime angler's licenses, Chesapeake Bay and coastal sport fishing licenses, and hunting licenses. Exempts holders of these lifetime angler's licenses from obtaining a trout stamp.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
qa_results.stakeholders: American veterans determined to be unemployable by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues likely decrease annually beginning in fiscal 2025 from foregone license and stamp fee revenue, but the exact amount cannot be reliably estimated. Expenditures are not affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Natural Resources is the primary implementing agency responsible for issuing lifetime complimentary angler's, sport fishing, and hunting licenses and providing trout stamp exemptions to qualifying unemployable veterans, which will also result in a decrease in the department's special fund revenues.

The department advocates for and assists Maryland veterans with securing state benefits and services, provided data regarding veterans determined to be unemployable, and connects eligible veterans with state benefits like complimentary licensing.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires every deputy clerk or deputy sheriff in Carroll County to take and sign the constitutional oath of office. Specifies the oath prescribed by Article I, Section 9 of the Maryland Constitution replaces the standard statutory oath. Aligns Carroll County with Montgomery County and Washington County deputy oath requirements. Takes effect immediately as an emergency measure upon enactment on April 25, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Clerk of the Circuit Court for Carroll County; Carroll County Sheriff's Office
qa_results.stakeholders: Deputy clerks and deputy sheriffs in Carroll County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state fiscal effect. Carroll County operations and finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters the required oath of office for deputy clerks in Carroll County, who are personnel within the Maryland Judicial Branch supported administratively by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Attorney General to seek injunctive relief on behalf of the State to prevent irreparable harm to residents. Applies to imminent or ongoing violations of specified resident rights in health care facilities and assisted living programs. Prohibits the Attorney General from duplicating corrective actions imposed by the Maryland Department of Health for the same violation. Requires the Department's resident bill of rights for assisted living programs to include eight specified minimum rights. Takes effect July 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General; Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: residents and operators of health care facilities and assisted living programs
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures and revenues are not affected, as the Office of the Attorney General and the Maryland Department of Health can handle the requirements with existing budgeted resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly expands the authority of the Office of the Attorney General, authorizing it to seek injunctive relief in circuit court on behalf of the State to prevent irreparable harm to residents of health care facilities and assisted living programs.

The Maryland Department of Health licenses and regulates assisted living programs and comprehensive care facilities, establishes the assisted living resident bill of rights updated by the bill, and takes corrective enforcement actions that the Attorney General is prohibited from duplicating.
The Administrative Office of the Courts supports the circuit courts, which will adjudicate the petitions for injunctive relief and potential civil penalty actions authorized under the bill.
The Department of Aging oversees long-term care advocacy and older adult protections, and shares statutory authority with MDH to approve regulations governing assisted living programs.

The Department of Human Services maintains adult protective and social service responsibilities and possesses statutory approval authority alongside the Department of Aging over assisted living program regulations implemented by MDH.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange to submit a federal State Innovation Waiver application amendment by July 1, 2025. Requires the Exchange to establish and implement the Qualified Resident Enrollment Program contingent on federal approval. Allows qualified Maryland residents, regardless of immigration status, to purchase qualified health plans on the individual exchange. Authorizes the Maryland Insurance Commissioner to waive certain carrier requirements in calendar year 2025. Requires the Exchange to submit an implementation plan to the General Assembly and adopt regulations by January 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Health Benefit Exchange; Maryland Insurance Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland residents ineligible for federal coverage options due to immigration status, health insurance carriers, and the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Health Benefit Exchange can apply for the waiver and absorb initial start-up costs using existing budgeted resources. If the General Assembly authorizes funding to subsidize premiums under the program in future years, State expenditures will increase by an indeterminate amount.
