Federal pass-through funding is not anticipated. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MHBE is the primary implementing agency required to apply for the federal Section 1332 State Innovation Waiver, establish and administer the Qualified Resident Enrollment Program, adopt regulations, and report to the General Assembly.

The Maryland Insurance Administration and the Insurance Commissioner must be consulted regarding the waiver application and program implementation, and the Commissioner is authorized to waive carrier notification or other requirements under the Insurance Article.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals a restriction preventing Baltimore City ordinances or municipal officers from conflicting or interfering with the Police Commissioner's powers. Conditions this change on voter approval of a Baltimore City Charter amendment at the 2024 general election. Requires the charter amendment to establish the appointment, terms, and duties of the Police Commissioner and department. Takes substantive effect on January 1, 2025, if city voters ratify the charter amendment. Renders the repeal null and void if voters do not pass and ratify the amendment.
qa_results.responsible_party: Mayor and City Council of Baltimore
qa_results.stakeholders: Mayor and City Council of Baltimore, Baltimore City municipal officers, Baltimore City Police Commissioner, Baltimore City Police Department, and Baltimore City voters
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state fiscal effect. Baltimore City finances are not anticipated to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill's primary provisions are contingent upon the submission and ratification of a Baltimore City Charter amendment by voters at the 2024 general election, which is administered and supervised under the authority of the State Board of Elections and the local board.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the state's coordinating body for public safety and criminal justice policy, GOCPP monitors governance and structural policy changes regarding Maryland's law enforcement agencies, including the transition of local control over the Baltimore Police Department.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters alcoholic beverages licensing fees, supplementary fees, and renewal application fees in Baltimore City. Increases the license renewal application fee from $50 to $78. Raises statutory annual license fees for multiple license classes, including Class A, B, C, and D licenses. Requires the Board of License Commissioners to set fees for specified festival, sampling, tasting, and per diem licenses. Increases supplementary fees from $75 to $120 for permitted Sunday sales.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore City; Baltimore City Director of Finance
qa_results.stakeholders: holders of and applicants for alcoholic beverages licenses in Baltimore City, including restaurants, bars, breweries, package stores, and event organizers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Baltimore City revenues increase by approximately $823,200 annually beginning in FY 2025 due to higher license fees. Baltimore City expenditures and State finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland regulates the state's alcoholic beverage industry. Although this legislation specifically alters local alcoholic beverage licensing fees administered by the Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners and has no state fiscal impact, it relates to the regulation and licensing structure of the alcoholic beverage industry in Maryland.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands the requirement for drivers traveling slower than the general speed of traffic to use the right-hand lane. Applies this rule to all roadways, removing the restriction to rural interstate highways. Conditions the requirement on whether the driver determines it is practicable to do so. Prohibits issuing a citation for a violation of this provision. Requires the Motor Vehicle Administration to include the rule in the driver education curriculum. Authorizes the State Highway Administration to inform drivers using highway signs and dynamic message signs.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Highway Administration; Motor Vehicle Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: motorists traveling on Maryland roadways; student drivers enrolled in driver education
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Transportation Trust Fund expenditures increase by at least $250,000 and up to $750,000 in FY 2025 only for the State Highway Administration to install highway signs. Revenues are unaffected because citations may not be issued, and local governments experience no material fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates that the State Highway Administration inform drivers of the slow-moving vehicle requirements by placing signs on state highways and utilizing the dynamic message sign system, resulting in an estimated $250,000 to $750,000 in fiscal 2025 expenditures.
The bill requires the Administration (MVA) to incorporate the expanded slow-moving vehicle right-hand lane requirement into the State's driver education curriculum.
MDOT is the parent agency of the State Highway Administration and Motor Vehicle Administration, and the bill's implementation costs will directly affect the Transportation Trust Fund.

As the primary statewide highway patrol and traffic safety enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police is affected by changes to rules of the road, although the bill explicitly provides that no citation may be issued for a violation.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases the minimum general liability insurance requirement for home improvement contractors and license applicants. Requires an applicant for a contractor license to maintain at least $500,000 in general liability insurance. Requires a licensed contractor to maintain at least $500,000 in general liability insurance. Raises the statutory minimum insurance threshold from the prior requirement of $50,000.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Home Improvement Commission; Maryland Department of Labor
qa_results.stakeholders: applicants for a home improvement contractor license, licensed home improvement contractors, and Maryland homeowners
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on Maryland Home Improvement Commission finances or operations; no local government fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor houses the Maryland Home Improvement Commission (MHIC), which is the primary regulatory body responsible for licensing home improvement contractors and enforcing statutory licensing requirements, including the mandatory liability insurance minimums amended by this bill.

The Maryland Insurance Administration regulates commercial liability insurance policies and insurers operating in Maryland, making statutory changes to mandatory contractor liability coverage limits relevant to its oversight of market products and policy compliance.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Stadium Authority to study the feasibility of establishing a sports tourism facility at Reisterstown Regional Park. Directs the Authority to identify available and potential federal, State, and local funding sources. Requires assessing infrastructure needs, capital costs, and operating expenses for site construction and recreational amenities. Mandates evaluating local economic impacts, including employment opportunities, tax revenues, and property values. Requires consultation with specified State agencies and Baltimore County entities during the study. Directs the Authority to submit a final report to legislative committees by December 31, 2025.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Stadium Authority
qa_results.stakeholders: Residents, sports participants, and local businesses in northwest Baltimore County and the Reisterstown area
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $300,000 in FY 2025 and $100,000 in FY 2026 for the Maryland Stadium Authority to conduct the feasibility study. Other consulting State agencies and Baltimore County can carry out consultations with existing budgeted resources. State and local revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly requires the Maryland Stadium Authority to conduct a feasibility study and submit a report on developing and operating a sports tourism facility in northwest Baltimore County, resulting in an estimated expenditure increase of $400,000 across FY 2025 and FY 2026.
The bill explicitly mandates that the Maryland Stadium Authority consult with the Maryland Transit Administration during the feasibility study regarding transit and infrastructure needs.
The bill explicitly requires the Maryland Stadium Authority to consult with the Maryland Department of Commerce on the economic impact and feasibility of the sports tourism facility.
The Maryland Department of Transportation is the parent department of the Maryland Transit Administration, which is statutorily required to be consulted for the study.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the holder of a stadium alcoholic beverages license in Frederick County to sell liquor for on-premises consumption. Permits sales of liquor in plastic or paper containers to individuals present at stadium events. Applies to stadiums where a professional baseball team franchise plays its home games. Increases the annual stadium license fee from $2,000 to $2,500. Takes effect June 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Frederick County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Professional baseball team franchise owners holding a stadium license in Frederick County and attendees at stadium events
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Frederick County revenues increase by $500 annually beginning as early as fiscal 2024 due to the increased license fee. Any additional county enforcement activities can be handled using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland regulates the state's alcohol industry and administers state excise and sales taxes on alcoholic beverages. While this bill specifically amends local Frederick County licensing provisions regarding stadium sales of liquor with no direct state fiscal impact, it relates to the broader statutory framework governing alcoholic beverages in Maryland.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the promoter's permit in Frederick County to be a promoter's (on-sale) beer, wine, and liquor permit. Authorizes the Board of License Commissioners for Frederick County to issue the permit to certain for-profit organizations. Authorizes a permit holder to sell beer, wine, and liquor at an event. Prohibits the permit holder from holding an alcoholic beverages license under the article. Takes effect July 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Frederick County
qa_results.stakeholders: for-profit event promoters and organizations in Frederick County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state fiscal effect. Frederick County finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends provisions of the Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article regarding event permits and alcohol sales in Frederick County. While administered locally by the Frederick County Board of License Commissioners with no direct state fiscal impact, the Comptroller is responsible for overall state regulation and taxation of the alcohol industry.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes Maryland corporations and real estate investment trusts to adopt emergency bylaws in advance of catastrophic events. Permits boards of directors during emergencies to provide modified meeting notice and postpone or hold remote stockholder meetings. Protects directors, officers, employees, and agents from liability for corporate actions taken in good faith during an emergency. Establishes that redeemed or repurchased stock ceases to be outstanding once notice is given and funds are set aside. Alters definitions of principal office and resident agent to include limited partnerships and other Maryland business entities.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland corporations, real estate investment trusts, limited liability companies, limited liability partnerships, limited partnerships, and corporate directors, officers, and stockholders
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State operations or finances and does not directly affect local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters corporate governance standards and limits the liability of corporate directors, officers, and employees for actions taken in good faith during catastrophic emergencies, which directly affects standards applied in civil litigation heard within the Maryland court system.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Technology Development Corporation to include an option for investment applicants to provide specified demographic information. Mandates a statement advising that providing demographic information is voluntary but encouraged. Prohibits the Corporation from taking adverse action against any applicant who declines to provide the information. Requires the Corporation to submit an annual report on investment applications and funding starting October 1, 2024. Requires the report to include de-identified and disaggregated demographic data on applicants and founders if available.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Technology Development Corporation
qa_results.stakeholders: Technology-based businesses and entrepreneurs applying for investment financing from the Maryland Technology Development Corporation
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $50,000 to $75,000 in FY 2025 for one-time information technology costs. Program finances and operational costs are not otherwise affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 753 directly applies to TEDCO, requiring the corporation to modify its investment application to include voluntary demographic disclosures and to submit an annual report detailing applicant demographics and investment activities.

The bill mandates that TEDCO submit an annual report detailing application and investment activity, including disaggregated demographic data, directly to the Governor on or before October 1 each year.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the membership composition of the State Board of Social Work Examiners. Authorizes a licensed master social worker approved for independent practice to satisfy board membership requirements. Requires immediate appointment of any qualified licensee if a category vacancy exceeds three months. Repeals obsolete statutory references concerning certified social worker licenses for out-of-state applicants. Removes references to certified social worker licenses for license reissuance.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Social Work Examiners
qa_results.stakeholders: Licensed social workers in Maryland, applicants for social work licensure, and members of the State Board of Social Work Examiners
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on State or local governmental finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Social Work Examiners is a health occupation regulatory board operating under the Maryland Department of Health, and appointments are made with the advice of the Secretary of Health.
The statute specifies that the membership of the State Board of Social Work Examiners must include one licensed social worker employed by the Department of Human Services.
The Governor is responsible for formally appointing the members of the State Board of Social Work Examiners subject to the qualifications altered by this bill.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and managing appointments to state boards, including the State Board of Social Work Examiners.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Secretary of State, on request, to furnish a State flag to drape the casket of an eligible decedent. Directs the Secretary of State to adopt regulations establishing procedures to submit requests and verify decedent eligibility. Limits provision to one State flag per eligible decedent. Provides that after burial, the flag must be given to the decedent's next of kin, close friend, or associate. Prohibits procuring flags unless wholly produced in the United States, unless the Secretary of State reasonably waives the requirement.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Secretary of State
qa_results.stakeholders: Surviving next of kin, close friends, or associates of deceased Maryland public employees, constitutional officers, legislators, governors, and judges
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by at least $14,000 in FY 2025 to purchase an initial inventory of 100 cotton flags, followed by ongoing minimal annual expenses for inventory replenishment and postage. No effect on local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the Secretary of State with implementing and administering the program, including adopting regulations for request and verification processes, procuring U.S.-made State flags, and furnishing them to drape the caskets of eligible decedents. The fiscal note directly impacts the Secretary of State's budget.
The bill grants the Governor statutory authority to designate additional individuals as eligible decedents to receive a State flag through executive order.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes a supervised medical graduate to perform delegated duties under the direct supervision of a licensed physician. Limits an individual from practicing as a supervised medical graduate to a maximum period of 2 years. Requires the graduate to hold an accredited medical degree and pass parts 1 and 2 of the licensing examination. Specifies the delegating physician must be in the same medical office and immediately available to provide assistance. Repeals the September 30, 2024, termination date for delegating duties to registered cardiovascular invasive specialists.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Physicians
qa_results.stakeholders: supervised medical graduates, licensed delegating physicians, registered cardiovascular invasive specialists, and hospitals operating cardiac catheterization laboratories
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The State Board of Physicians can adopt required regulations using existing budgeted resources, with no effect on state revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Board of Physicians, which is a regulatory board housed within the Maryland Department of Health, is directly responsible for implementing the bill, including adopting regulations governing the delegated duties of supervised medical graduates and overseeing delegation to cardiovascular invasive specialists.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires advanced practice registered nurses practicing in the State to notify patients in writing if they lack professional liability insurance. Applies the notification requirement if the nurse's professional liability coverage lapsed and was not renewed. Directs nurses to provide notice at the first patient visit and within informed consent documents. Excludes visits solely to receive incidental medical care rendered free of charge. Mandates that nurses without coverage post this information conspicuously at their place of practice. Directs the State Board of Nursing to develop the notification language.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Nursing
qa_results.stakeholders: Advanced practice registered nurses practicing in Maryland and their patients
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact; the State Board of Nursing can develop required notification language using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the Maryland Department of Health because its constituent board, the State Board of Nursing, is specifically tasked with developing the required notification language for advanced practice registered nurses regarding professional liability insurance coverage.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires each local school system to submit a report on corrective actions to the Joint Audit and Evaluation Committee. Specifies that the report must address repeat findings and recommendations from the most recent legislative audit. Requires submission on or before November 1 of the third year of a six-year audit cycle. Mandates that each local school system publish the report on its website. Requires redaction of cybersecurity findings prior to publication consistent with auditing best practices.
qa_results.responsible_party: Joint Audit and Evaluation Committee; local school systems
qa_results.stakeholders: local school systems in Maryland and their financial management staff
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State effect. Local expenditures may increase by a minimal, indeterminate amount for local school systems to address repeat audit findings, while cybersecurity redactions can be handled with existing resources. Local revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends statutory provisions governing the Office of Legislative Audits' six-year audit cycle of local school systems, requiring local school systems to report to the Joint Audit and Evaluation Committee on the status of corrective actions addressing repeat findings and recommendations identified by OLA.

MSDE oversees Maryland's 24 local school systems and administers policies regarding annual school system financial audits under Section 5-109 of the Education Article, which is amended to require that audits address repeat audit findings.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits locating a school bus stop on any highway with five or more undivided traffic lanes in Montgomery County. Permits such stops only if a school crossing guard is posted or a specified traffic control device is placed. Requires the crossing guard to assist students in crossing the highway. Requires the traffic control device to maintain a red signal while students board or exit. Establishes a compliance deadline of December 31, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Montgomery County Board of Education; Montgomery County
qa_results.stakeholders: Montgomery County public school students, school bus drivers, school crossing guards, and motorists traveling on undivided highways in Montgomery County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on State finances. Indeterminate impact on Montgomery County expenditures beginning in fiscal 2026 to hire additional crossing guards, procure traffic control devices, or relocate bus stops. Potential decrease in county revenues from school bus monitoring cameras if bus stops are relocated. Specific figures are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill enacts § 7–801.1 of the Education Article governing the placement of school bus stops, crossing guards, and traffic control devices for Montgomery County Public Schools, falling under MSDE's purview over statewide public education and student transportation standards.

The bill regulates school bus stop conditions and traffic control devices on highways with five or more undivided lanes in Montgomery County, which may involve state-maintained highways governed by MDOT.

As the modal agency responsible for state highways in Montgomery County, SHA oversees roadway design, permits, and traffic control devices on state roads where school bus stops on multi-lane undivided highways may be located or modified.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes Class B beer, wine, and liquor license holders in Montgomery County to sell beer and wine for off-premises consumption. Permits off-premises sales only in manufacturer-sealed containers to customers who purchase prepared food. Prohibits displaying or providing shelving for off-sale alcohol in areas accessible to the public. Restricts off-premises sales to times when the licensed premises is open for business as a hotel or restaurant. Authorizes the Board of License Commissioners for Montgomery County to adopt regulations, including transaction quantity limits.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Montgomery County
qa_results.stakeholders: Class B beer, wine, and liquor license holders (restaurant and hotel owners and operators) in Montgomery County and their patrons
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State effect. Montgomery County operations and finances are not anticipated to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Although the bill directly pertains to local retail alcoholic beverage licensing administered by the Montgomery County Board of License Commissioners, the Comptroller of Maryland oversees state alcohol regulation and collects state sales and excise taxes on alcohol.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the membership structure of the Commission on Hate Crime Response and Prevention. Adds 15 members appointed by the Attorney General with the advice and consent of the Senate. Requires these 15 members to represent or advocate for individuals in protected classes under State hate crime laws. Adds one representative of the Office of the Public Defender while removing several designated organizational representatives. Terminates the terms of existing appointed Commission members on June 1, 2024. Sunsets the Commission and its adopted regulations and policies after June 30, 2027.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General; Commission on Hate Crime Response and Prevention
qa_results.stakeholders: members of protected classes under Maryland hate crime laws, civil rights and advocacy organizations, appointees to the Commission on Hate Crime Response and Prevention, and the Office of the Public Defender
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Commission on Hate Crime Response and Prevention is housed within, chaired by, and staffed by the Office of the Attorney General, and the Attorney General is responsible for appointing the commission's members.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters the commission's statutory membership by specifically adding a representative of the Office of the Public Defender as a member.
The Maryland Commission on Civil Rights holds a designated statutory seat on the Commission on Hate Crime Response and Prevention.
The Maryland Center for School Safety maintains a designated statutory seat on the Commission on Hate Crime Response and Prevention.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly restructures the membership, appointment qualifications, and sunset date of an executive branch advisory commission.
The commission is required by statute to report annual policy recommendations to the State Department of Education regarding hate crimes occurring in schools.

qa_results.bill_summary: Mandates an annual distribution of $27,000,000 from the State Lottery Fund to the Bus Rapid Transit Fund. Decouples these transit grants from Maryland Stadium Authority debt service payments. Requires an annual transfer of $27,000,000 to the Prince George’s County Blue Line Corridor Facility Fund. Directs the Maryland Stadium Authority to pay all approved expenses relating to Blue Line Corridor facilities. Requires the Authority to submit a corridor development report to legislative committees by December 15, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland; Maryland Department of Transportation; Maryland Stadium Authority
qa_results.stakeholders: Montgomery County and other local governments operating bus rapid transit systems, transit riders, Prince George's County, and communities along the Blue Line Corridor
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: General fund revenues decrease by $8.8 million in fiscal 2025 due to an accelerated lottery revenue transfer to the Prince George’s County Blue Line Corridor Facility Fund. Nonbudgeted revenues and expenditures for the Prince George’s County Blue Line Corridor Facility Fund increase by $8.8 million in fiscal 2025.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 764 directly affects the Maryland Stadium Authority by expanding the authorized uses of the Prince George's County Blue Line Corridor Facility Fund to pay any expenses incurred or approved by MSA, altering funding allocations, and requiring MSA to submit a comprehensive 30-year development report on the corridor by December 15, 2024.

MDOT administers the Bus Rapid Transit Fund and is responsible for awarding and distributing $27 million in annual bus rapid transit system grants to eligible local grantees under the revised statutory criteria. MDOT is also statutorily required to consult with MSA on the Blue Line Corridor report.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill modifies the required statutory distributions from the State Lottery Fund, establishing fixed annual allocations to the Bus Rapid Transit Fund and adjusting the timing and amounts directed to the Blue Line Corridor Facility Fund.

The Comptroller is responsible for accounting for the Prince George's County Blue Line Corridor Facility Fund and executing monthly distributions from the State Lottery Fund according to the updated statutory schedule.

The bill requires MSA to consult and meaningfully engage with the Department of Housing and Community Development in preparing the report on public and private development activities in the Prince George's County Blue Line Corridor.
The State Treasurer is statutorily directed to hold the Prince George's County Blue Line Corridor Facility Fund separately and invest its moneys in the same manner as other State funds.
DBM monitors state budget execution and fiscal planning; the bill accelerates lottery fund transfers, resulting in an estimated $8.8 million decrease in general fund revenues in FY 2025.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes Baltimore City, counties, and municipal corporations to grant property tax credits for hotel or residential development projects. Requires eligible projects to be newly constructed or involve substantial rehabilitation or revitalization of existing structures. Requires qualifying hotel projects to substantially increase the assessed value of the property. Requires qualifying residential projects to include at least 20 residential units. Mandates that at least 15% of units be affordable to households earning under 80% of area median income. Repeals a previous separate property tax credit authorization specifically for Wicomico County.
qa_results.responsible_party: Mayor and City Council of Baltimore City; governing bodies of Maryland counties; governing bodies of Maryland municipal corporations
qa_results.stakeholders: Commercial and residential real estate developers, hotel owners, low- and moderate-income tenants, Baltimore City, and county and municipal governments
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on state finances. County and municipal property tax revenues decrease beginning in FY 2025 to the extent local jurisdictions grant the credit; specific revenue losses are indeterminate because they depend on local enactment, credit amounts, and the number and assessed value of eligible properties.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill authorizes local jurisdictions to establish a property tax credit for qualifying hotel and residential development projects. The Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board is responsible for hearing appeals regarding property valuations and disputes over property tax credits.
The Maryland Tax Court hears appeals from final decisions of local taxing authorities and Property Tax Assessment Appeals Boards regarding property assessments and property tax credit disputes.

The bill relates to the department's mission of promoting affordable housing and community revitalization by incentivizing residential developments that designate at least 15% of units as affordable to households earning under 80% of area median income.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits a person from standing in a roadway, median divider, or intersection to solicit donations in Calvert County. Applies the ban to soliciting money or donations of any kind from vehicle occupants. Adds Calvert County to identical prohibitions already governing Carroll, Charles, Harford, and Washington counties. Takes effect October 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Calvert County Sheriff's Office; Maryland State Police
qa_results.stakeholders: individuals seeking money or roadside donations in Calvert County; motorists and vehicle occupants in Calvert County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State or Calvert County finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 766 amends the Maryland Transportation Article regarding the prohibition of roadside solicitations in roadways, median dividers, and intersections within Calvert County.
MDOT SHA plans, maintains, and regulates state non-toll highways and roadway safety, which encompasses roadway and median safety rules across Calvert County.
MSP is responsible for traffic enforcement and preserving public safety on state highways and roadways, including enforcing pedestrian and roadside solicitation prohibitions in Calvert County.
AOC provides operational and administrative support for the District Court, which processes traffic and pedestrian citations resulting from violations of the Transportation Article.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes a line-of-duty special death benefit for members of the Judges' Retirement System killed in service. Provides the member's accumulated contributions and an allowance equal to two-thirds of the current position salary. Authorizes surviving spouses, minor or disabled children, and dependent parents to receive the death benefit. Allows eligible survivors to enroll in the State health plan with the maximum allowable retiree subsidy. Permits surviving spouses of members killed before June 1, 2024, to apply retroactively by December 31, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System; Department of Budget and Management
qa_results.stakeholders: Members of the Judges' Retirement System and their surviving spouses, minor or disabled children, and dependent parents
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No discernible effect on State pension liabilities, contribution rates, or State health care costs due to the limited number of applicable cases. No effect on State revenues or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Retirement Agency administers the State Retirement and Pension System, which includes the Judges' Retirement System (JRS). The agency's Board of Trustees is directly tasked with administering, calculating, and disbursing the new line-of-duty special death benefits and retroactive payments established by the bill.

The Department of Budget and Management manages state employee health benefits and the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program. The bill directly alters program eligibility and subsidies, allowing surviving dependents of JRS members killed in the line of duty to enroll and receive the maximum allowable State retiree health insurance subsidy.

The Administrative Office of the Courts is the administrative and operational support arm of Maryland's Judicial Branch. The members of the Judges' Retirement System impacted by this legislation serve within the State judiciary supported by the agency.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Individuals With Disabilities and Service-Disabled Veterans Boating Fund administered by the Maryland Department of Disabilities. Supports sailing, boating, kayaking, canoeing, paddleboarding, and surfing for individuals with disabilities and service-disabled veterans. Authorizes the department to award annual grants of up to $40,000 to qualifying nonprofit organizations. Requires eligible nonprofits to be 501(c)(3) entities with at least three years of qualifying water-activity operations. Authorizes the Governor to appropriate $500,000 annually to the fund beginning in fiscal year 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Disabilities
qa_results.stakeholders: individuals with disabilities, service-disabled veterans, and qualifying 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations providing adaptive water sports
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by at least $47,000 in FY 2025 to cover administrative costs for a part-time grants coordinator, with special fund revenues and expenditures matching. State grant expenditures will increase by an additional indeterminate amount depending on appropriations and grant awards. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates the Department of Disabilities to administer the newly established Individuals with Disabilities and Service-Disabled Veterans Boating Fund, manage grant distribution to eligible nonprofit organizations, and oversee associated administrative responsibilities.

The fund specifically targets service-disabled veterans to provide adaptive boating, paddleboarding, and surfing opportunities, aligning directly with the department's mission to support disabled veterans.
The statute explicitly mandates that the State Treasurer shall hold the Individuals with Disabilities and Service-Disabled Veterans Boating Fund separately as a special, nonlapsing fund.
The statute explicitly requires the Comptroller of Maryland to account for the newly established special fund.
The legislation authorizes an ongoing annual general fund appropriation of up to $500,000 starting in fiscal year 2026, which falls under DBM's budget development and fiscal planning purview.
The bill authorizes the Governor to include a discretionary appropriation of up to $500,000 in the annual budget bill starting in fiscal year 2026.
The bill regulates water-based activities (boating, kayaking, canoeing, surfing) on State waters and DNR provided subject-matter information during the legislative fiscal review.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Maryland Technology Development Corporation, subject to a written agreement, to provide administrative support and services to certain entities. Applies to entities that the corporation creates, owns, controls, or joins, whether operated for profit or nonprofit. Authorizes the corporation to receive compensation for providing the administrative support and services. Takes effect October 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Technology Development Corporation
qa_results.stakeholders: Business entities created, owned, controlled, or joined by the Maryland Technology Development Corporation
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No direct effect on State revenues or expenditures, as the provisions are generally clarifying in nature. Local government finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 776 directly amends the statutory powers of the Maryland Technology Development Corporation (TEDCO) by authorizing it, subject to a written agreement, to provide administrative support and services to entities it creates, owns, controls, or is a member of, and to receive compensation for providing those services.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes competitive sealed proposals as the preferred procurement method for security services valued over $1,000,000. Requires procurement officers using this method to issue a request for proposals. Authorizes procurement units to conduct discussions and seek best and final offers from eligible offerors. Requires contract awards to go to the responsible offeror submitting the most advantageous proposal. Takes effect July 1, 2025.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of General Services; Board of Public Works
qa_results.stakeholders: Security service contractors bidding on State contracts valued over $1,000,000; State procurement officers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to have a material effect on State operations or finances; local governments are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the State's central procurement agency and manager of state facility operations and security contracts, DGS is directly responsible for executing solicitations for security services exceeding $1,000,000 using competitive sealed proposals.
The Board of Public Works oversees and approves significant State procurement contracts, including large-scale security service awards exceeding $1,000,000, and sets related procurement regulations.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel on State procurement matters and must approve in writing any correction or withdrawal of proposals or best and final offers submitted during the competitive sealed proposal process.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes certain volunteer fire company officers to equip privately owned vehicles with red or red and white lights. Limits this authorization to no more than five designated officers per volunteer fire company. Permits displaying these lights only en route to or at an emergency scene. Allows volunteer fire police to equip privately owned vehicles with red, red and green, or red and white lights. Restricts fire police lighting use to the scene of an accident, flood, or emergency response.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Motor Vehicle Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Volunteer fire company officers (fire chiefs, assistant or deputy chiefs, and emergency medical services commanders) and volunteer fire company fire police
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State finances or operations and does not directly affect local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Motor Vehicle Administration is responsible for administering the Maryland Vehicle Law and vehicle equipment standards, including authorized emergency lighting and signal devices.

The Maryland Department of Transportation oversees the state's transportation network and includes the Motor Vehicle Administration, which regulates vehicle equipment and lighting under Title 22 of the Transportation Article.
The Maryland State Police enforces state traffic and motor vehicle equipment laws, including compliance with statutory regulations governing emergency vehicle lighting and signal devices.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MIEMSS coordinates statewide emergency medical services and is referenced in the statute and fiscal note regarding authorized lighting devices for emergency response personnel and vehicles.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes State standards for school library media programs and State-funded public libraries. Prohibits excluding or removing library materials due to creator background or partisan, ideological, or religious disapproval. Requires local school systems to establish uniform objection procedures and keep challenged materials accessible during review. Protects school and public library staff from retaliation for performing their duties consistent with State standards. Makes State funding contingent on adopting written policies that comply with the standards. Requires the Comptroller to withhold State funds from libraries certified as noncompliant.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Library Board; Maryland State Library Agency; Comptroller of Maryland; county boards of education
qa_results.stakeholders: Public school students, parents, and school personnel; public school librarians, media specialists, and library staff; public library employees; State and regional resource centers; county public library systems
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material fiscal impact. The Maryland State Library Agency, local school systems, and local public libraries can implement the bill's requirements using existing resources. State and local revenues are not expected to be affected unless a library fails to adopt compliant policies and has State funding withheld.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Library Agency and State Library Board are the primary entities tasked with developing policies, ensuring libraries meet the State standards for libraries, certifying compliance, and authorizing the withholding of State funds.

The bill statutorily requires the Comptroller to withhold State funds from regional resource centers, metropolitan cooperative service programs, and county library systems that fail to adopt policies consistent with the State standards for libraries.

The bill establishes statewide standards and policies governing local school library media programs, restricts disciplinary actions against school library media staff, and references professional certification duties overseen by the State Superintendent.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Correctional facility libraries, which are operated within DPSCS correctional institutions, are explicitly included under the definition of libraries subject to the State standards for libraries.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the State Board of Dental Examiners to waive specified education requirements for applicants providing adult dental services. Expands limited dentistry license waivers beyond pediatric dentistry to include practitioners providing adult dental care. Allows applicants to complete fellowships at any dental school recognized by the Board. Authorizes health center dental directors or public health officers to request waivers justifying granting circumstances. Establishes a pathway to general licensure for qualifying limited licensees who complete a two-year service obligation.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Dental Examiners
qa_results.stakeholders: Foreign-trained dentists seeking Maryland licensure, public health dental clinics, federally qualified health centers, Maryland qualified health centers, and Medicaid, uninsured, or indigent dental patients
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State Board of Dental Examiners operations can be handled with existing budgeted resources, with no likely effect on revenues. Local health department impacts can be absorbed within existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly governs the licensing requirements administered by the State Board of Dental Examiners, a regulatory health occupations board housed within the Maryland Department of Health.

The bill alters requirements involving the University of Maryland School of Dentistry (an institution within USM), specifically addressing fellowship completion at the school and eliminating the requirement that the Dean of the dental school jointly submit waiver requests to the Board of Dental Examiners.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Allegany Regional Recreational Economic Development Authority in Allegany County. Requires the Authority to support developing regional recreation facilities, including athletic fields and indoor athletic facilities. Authorizes the Authority to manage appropriated funds from the State, Allegany County, Cumberland, and Frostburg. Permits the Authority to receive donated professional services and manage staff and consultants. Requires the Authority to report annually by October 31 to the Governor and designated legislative committees.
qa_results.responsible_party: Allegany Regional Recreational Economic Development Authority
qa_results.stakeholders: Residents and recreational visitors of Allegany County, Allegany County government, the City of Cumberland, the City of Frostburg, Frostburg State University, and Allegany College
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No direct State fiscal impact; expense reimbursements and staffing can likely be absorbed with existing resources. Local expenditures may increase minimally if existing staff resources are insufficient. The bill authorizes but does not require State or local funding appropriations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Frostburg State University is an institution within the University System of Maryland, and its President (or designee) is designated as a statutory member of the Authority. Additionally, the university noted that the Authority may manage remaining planning and design funds for its regional sports complex.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates the Allegany Regional Recreational Economic Development Authority as an independent entity consisting of public officials and appointed members, which operates for a five-year term before abrogating.
The newly established Authority is required to report its activities annually by October 31 to the Governor.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the County Commissioners of Carroll County to borrow up to $29,800,000 through general obligation bonds. Permits bond proceeds to finance the construction, improvement, or development of public facilities, including water and sewer projects. Authorizes loans to volunteer fire departments in Carroll County for fire and emergency-related equipment and facilities. Allows the county to issue installment purchase obligations to acquire agricultural land and woodland preservation easements. Requires the county to levy annual ad valorem property taxes sufficient to pay bond debt service. Caps the maturity term for any issued bonds at 30 years from the date of issue.
qa_results.responsible_party: County Commissioners of Carroll County
qa_results.stakeholders: Carroll County property taxpayers, public schools, and volunteer fire departments in Carroll County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Carroll County revenues increase by up to $29.8 million from bond proceeds. County debt service expenditures increase by an estimated $2.1 million annually over a 20-year period. There is no state fiscal effect.

qa_results.bill_summary: Applies Maryland Rules governing discovery in circuit court civil matters to administrative release proceedings for committed persons. Requires courts and the Maryland Department of Health to promptly notify a committed person's counsel regarding alleged release violations. Requires courts to hold a hearing on request by any party after an application for changed conditional release. Establishes that the applicant must prove any issue raised by a preponderance of the evidence. Mandates that the Maryland Department of Health provide evaluations and reports upon written request by specified parties. Authorizes courts to shorten, terminate, or extend conditional release by an additional term up to five years.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Judiciary
qa_results.stakeholders: individuals committed to the Maryland Department of Health after being found not criminally responsible; defense attorneys; State's Attorneys
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures for the Maryland Department of Health increase by up to $377,041 in FY 2025 and between $439,700 and $500,600 annually thereafter to hire six staff members for discovery and hearing workloads. No impact on State revenues. Local State's Attorneys' offices may experience operational efficiencies from expedited record access.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly governs the release, conditional release, and violation notification procedures for persons committed to the Department of Health (MDH) following a finding of not criminally responsible. MDH is required to provide comprehensive evaluations and reports upon request and incurs significant fiscal impacts for additional staffing.

OAH conducts the administrative hearings regarding eligibility for conditional release and discharge. The bill applies circuit court civil discovery rules to these administrative proceedings, requiring OAH administrative law judges to manage discovery timelines and disputes.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: OPD represents indigent defendants committed under not criminally responsible findings. The bill directly impacts their representation by ensuring counsel receives prompt notice of release violations, access to MDH records, and the ability to utilize civil discovery rules in administrative hearings.

The bill alters court procedures regarding committed persons, mandating notification to counsel upon receiving violation reports, requiring courts to hold hearings on request regarding changes to conditional release, and authorizing courts to shorten or terminate conditional release.

The OAG acts as legal counsel for MDH and state psychiatric facilities. Applying civil discovery rules to administrative release proceedings affects OAG attorneys handling cases and discovery on behalf of the Department.

qa_results.bill_summary: Restricts local zoning authority over licensed cannabis dispensaries and outdoor cannabis growers. Adds pre-existing places of worship to the 500-foot buffer requirement for licensed dispensaries. Permits political subdivisions to increase the distance between dispensaries to up to one-half mile. Requires political subdivisions to grant zoning waivers to dispensaries operating before April 1, 2024. Authorizes nearby residents and commercial tenants to file sworn protests against cannabis license renewals. Requires the Maryland Cannabis Administration to hold hearings on valid protests before approving renewals.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Cannabis Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Licensed cannabis dispensaries, licensed outdoor cannabis growers, commercial tenants and residents within 1,000 feet of cannabis premises, and local governments
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Potential minimal increase in special fund expenditures and revenues for the Maryland Cannabis Administration between FY 2028 and FY 2030 for renewal protest hearings. Potential minimal decrease in local revenues and general fund distributions if agency administrative expenses increase. Local planning and zoning agencies can implement provisions using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Cannabis Administration is the primary regulatory agency responsible for implementing the bill. It is tasked with receiving and adjudicating protests filed against cannabis license renewals, holding hearings, establishing implementing regulations, and overseeing licensee compliance with statutory zoning and location standards.

The Office of Administrative Hearings (OAH) is impacted because the Maryland Cannabis Administration currently delegates contested case hearings to OAH. An increase in protests against license renewals under the bill may result in an operational workload impact on OAH administrative law judges.

qa_results.bill_summary: Replaces supervision delegation agreements with collaboration agreements between physician assistants and patient care team physicians. Expands the scope of practice and clarifies prescriptive authority for licensed physician assistants. Permits physician assistants employed by the federal government to practice during declared disasters in Maryland. Increases the number of physician assistants a physician may collaborate with from four to eight. Requires the State Board of Physicians to review and update the list of advanced duties by January 1, 2025.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Physicians
qa_results.stakeholders: physician assistants, patient care team physicians, health care facilities, and patients in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State Board of Physicians special fund revenues and expenditures are not materially affected. The Board can implement the changes using existing budgeted resources, as potential loss of delegation agreement submission fees is offset by reduced workload and potential fees for advanced duty approvals. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Board of Physicians, which is housed within the Department of Health, is the primary regulatory body responsible for licensing physician assistants, approving advanced duties, managing collaboration agreements, and handling disciplinary actions as enacted under the bill.

The bill explicitly grants the Office of Controlled Substances Administration the authority to enter and inspect the offices of physician assistants who personally prepare and dispense prescription drugs at all reasonable hours.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Health Care Alternative Dispute Resolution Office
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends Courts and Judicial Proceedings Article § 3-2A-01 to explicitly include physician assistants in the definition of 'health care provider' for the purposes of medical malpractice claims administered by HCADRO.

The bill amends the Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article to update the criteria for physician assistants acting as certifying providers for medical cannabis by requiring an active collaboration agreement rather than a delegation agreement.
The bill amends the Education Article to allow physician assistants with an active collaboration agreement to conduct mandatory student physical examinations.

The bill amends the Transportation Article to update the definition of a licensed physician assistant authorized to certify disabilities for special registration plates and placards issued by the MVA.

qa_results.bill_summary: Renames aerial surveys for submerged aquatic vegetation to SAV surveys. Expands the definition to include surveys covering the Chesapeake Bay, the Atlantic Coastal Bays, or both. Requires qualifying alternative surveys to use methodologies approved by the Chesapeake Bay Program and the Department of Natural Resources. Updates the criteria for delineating and reopening SAV protection zones to include observed vegetation. Mandates that the Department of Natural Resources study alternative delineation methods. Directs the department to submit its report to the General Assembly by December 1, 2025.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
qa_results.stakeholders: commercial clammers and dredgers, shellfish aquaculture leaseholders and applicants, and marine conservation organizations
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Department of Natural Resources can complete the required study with existing budgeted resources. State general fund expenditures could increase by an indeterminate amount if the department chooses to implement additional survey methods in the future. Local finances and operations are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the Natural Resources Article governing Submerged Aquatic Vegetation (SAV) protection zones and Aquaculture Enterprise Zones administered by the Department of Natural Resources (DNR). It authorizes DNR to approve alternative SAV surveys and requires DNR to conduct a feasibility study and submit a report to the General Assembly by December 1, 2025.

MDE collaborates on Chesapeake Bay restoration and contributes funding to the Bay-wide VIMS submerged aquatic vegetation survey referenced in the bill and fiscal note, though it is not assigned direct administrative duties by the bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes a local delivery service permit authorizing holders to deliver alcoholic beverages from authorized retail license holders to purchasers. Applies only in jurisdictions where the local licensing board adopts regulations authorizing third-party delivery. Sets an annual permit fee of $1,000 collected by the local licensing board. Requires delivery personnel and alcohol recipients to be at least 21 years old with valid identification. Prohibits delivery service permit holders from directly selling or storing alcoholic beverages. Authorizes the Executive Director of the Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission to adopt enforcement regulations.
qa_results.responsible_party: local licensing boards; Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: licensed alcoholic beverage retailers, third-party delivery services, independent delivery drivers, and retail purchasers of alcoholic beverages
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not materially affected. Local government revenues increase by $1,000 for each permit issued beginning in fiscal 2025, alongside potential fine revenues, while local monitoring and enforcement are absorbed within existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill regulates the retail delivery of alcoholic beverages and ensures retail license holders retain control over sales and payments. The Comptroller serves as the state's chief tax collector overseeing alcoholic beverage sales taxes and has historical and administrative ties to alcohol industry regulation and revenue monitoring in Maryland.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the individual or entity that appointed a member to remove or suspend that member. Applies to members of any board, committee, commission, task force, or workgroup appointed for a fixed term. Permits removal or suspension for misconduct, incompetence, neglect of duties, or other good cause, except as otherwise provided by law. Requires consultation with the body's chair unless the member being removed or suspended is the chair. Requires providing the member notice and an opportunity to be heard regarding the reasons before removal or suspension. Excludes General Assembly standing committees and other committees established under Title 2 of the State Government Article.
qa_results.responsible_party: Appointing authorities of State boards, committees, commissions, task forces, or workgroups
qa_results.stakeholders: Members appointed for fixed terms to Maryland boards, committees, commissions, task forces, or workgroups created by State law; individuals and entities authorized to appoint those members
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local finances are not materially affected. The bill may have a minimal operational effect on affected State entities if the removal of a member disrupts their work.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and managing appointments to more than 600 state boards, commissions, task forces, and advisory councils, making statutory standards and procedures for removing or suspending members directly relevant to its core operations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly governs the removal and suspension of members appointed to boards, committees, commissions, task forces, and workgroups established by State law.

The Governor serves as the primary appointing authority for hundreds of statutory boards, commissions, and task forces across the executive branch and is empowered under this bill to suspend or remove appointees for cause under the established procedures.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Governor and state appointing authorities, advising on the required procedural due process (notice and opportunity to be heard) before removing or suspending appointed board and commission members.
The MDTA is specifically identified in the fiscal note as an affected entity that currently lacks statutory provisions for the removal of appointed members, which this bill directly remedies.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the statutory term "rapid fire trigger activator" to "rapid fire activator". Expands the definition of rapid fire activator to include a switch/auto-sear. Prohibits transporting, manufacturing, possessing, selling, transferring, purchasing, or receiving a switch/auto-sear. Exempts authorized law enforcement personnel and individuals holding parts for a registered machine gun. Imposes mandatory minimum prison sentences for using a switch/auto-sear in a felony or violent crime.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of State Police; Judiciary
qa_results.stakeholders: individuals possessing firearms or rapid-fire conversion devices, licensed firearms dealers, and law enforcement personnel
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Potential minimal increase in State and local general fund revenues and expenditures due to the expanded application of existing criminal penalty provisions; specific figures are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly references machine gun registration maintained by the Secretary of State Police as an exception to the prohibition on switch/auto-sears, and the Maryland State Police is the primary state law enforcement agency enforcing firearms regulations and criminal statutes.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill expands criminal prohibitions and applies mandatory minimum sentences and parole restrictions for offenses involving switch/auto-sears, directly impacting state correctional facilities and community supervision.
The Judiciary and court system will process, adjudicate, and sentence cases involving violations of the updated rapid-fire activator and switch/auto-sear criminal provisions.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The agency will be responsible for representing indigent defendants charged under the expanded criminal provisions and enhanced mandatory minimum sentencing requirements.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Financial Well–Being Pilot Program at the University of Maryland, College Park Campus and Morgan State University. Requires each participating institution to hire one full-time financial well-being coach by August 1, 2024. Directs each institution to create a system identifying students who may benefit from financial coaching services. Requires coaches to provide financial guidance, carry caseloads comparable to academic advisors, and survey participating students. Mandates interim and final reports on program effectiveness to the Maryland Higher Education Commission, Governor, and General Assembly. Terminates the pilot program on July 31, 2027.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Higher Education Commission; University of Maryland, College Park Campus; Morgan State University
qa_results.stakeholders: Students at the University of Maryland, College Park Campus and Morgan State University who experience financial burdens, loan debt, financial anxiety, or lack financial literacy
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State higher education expenditures increase by an estimated $315,500 in FY 2025 for two contractual financial coaches and student identification systems at participating institutions. Costs decrease to between $208,900 and $218,000 in FY 2026 and FY 2027, with $18,200 in FY 2028 before terminating. Local governments and revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MHEC is statutorily designated to jointly administer the Financial Well-Being Pilot Program alongside the participating institutions and is required to submit interim and final reports to Maryland institutions of higher education, the Governor, and the General Assembly.

MHEC is statutorily designated to jointly administer the Financial Well-Being Pilot Program alongside the participating institutions and is required to submit interim and final reports to Maryland institutions of higher education, the Governor, and the General Assembly.

Morgan State University is specifically designated as one of the two participating institutions required to jointly administer the pilot program, hire a full-time financial well-being coach, create an identification system, and submit interim and final status reports.

The University of Maryland, College Park (a USM constituent institution) is designated as a participating institution required to jointly administer the pilot program, hire a full-time financial well-being coach, create an identification system, and report on program status, resulting in notable fiscal impacts on USM.
The Governor's Office is a designated recipient of the interim and final reports on the operation and results of the Financial Well-Being Pilot Program submitted by MHEC.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases the required annual State budget appropriation to the Tri-County Council for Southern Maryland from $900,000 to $1,000,000. Repeals the June 30, 2025 termination date, making the annual Cigarette Restitution Fund appropriation permanent. Authorizes the Governor to appropriate up to 5% of the State's Master Settlement Agreement allocation to the Council. Requires the Council to use the appropriated funds to finance Southern Maryland Agricultural Development Commission activities. Mandates that these funds supplement and not supplant any other funding appropriated to the Council.
qa_results.responsible_party: Tri-County Council for Southern Maryland; Office of the Governor
qa_results.stakeholders: Southern Maryland farmers and agricultural businesses in Calvert, Charles, and St. Mary's counties
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund expenditures increase by up to $1.0 million annually beginning in fiscal 2026 due to the extension and enhancement of the mandate. General fund expenditures may increase by as much as $1.0 million annually beginning in fiscal 2026 to backfill other programs supported by the Cigarette Restitution Fund. Revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Cigarette Restitution Fund dollars dedicated to the Tri-County Council for the Southern Maryland Agricultural Development Commission are appropriated annually through the Maryland Department of Agriculture, which issues the grants to the Council.

DBM is responsible for state budget preparation and long-term fiscal planning, and this bill establishes an ongoing, increased statutory mandated appropriation of at least $1,000,000 annually from the Cigarette Restitution Fund.

The bill places a permanent statutory requirement on the Governor to include an annual appropriation of $1,000,000 (and authorizes up to 5% of Master Settlement Agreement payments) in the annual state budget bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands juvenile court jurisdiction over children aged 10 through 12 for specified firearm, animal cruelty, and sexual offenses. Requires law enforcement officers to submit a complaint or diversion report upon taking a child into custody. Mandates referral of complaints to the State's Attorney when intake officers deny petitions for certain firearm or felony allegations. Extends the maximum allowable probation durations for juveniles adjudicated delinquent for misdemeanors and felonies. Prohibits registered juvenile sex offenders from entering elementary or secondary school grounds and child care facilities. Codifies the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy, the Governor's Office for Children, and the Children's Cabinet.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Juvenile Services; Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy; Governor's Office for Children; Office of the Public Defender
qa_results.stakeholders: juveniles in the juvenile justice system, juvenile sex offender registrants, crime victims, law enforcement officers, State's Attorneys, and juvenile defense attorneys
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by at least $6.6 million in FY 2025 across the Department of Juvenile Services, Office of the Public Defender, and Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy, rising to $10.0 million by FY 2029. Local State's Attorneys' offices may incur indeterminate operational costs. State and local revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill comprehensively reforms juvenile justice administration and procedures, altering intake inquiry deadlines, detention eligibility, probation limits, electronic monitoring violation notifications, and treatment service plans, while adding new program and reporting requirements for DJS.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill formally codifies GOCPP in statute, assigns it to provide staffing and administrative support for the Commission on Juvenile Justice Reform and Emerging and Best Practices, mandates annual reporting on juvenile arrests, and incurs notable personnel expenditures.
The bill codifies the Governor's Office for Children and the Children's Cabinet in the Human Services Article as separate units within the Executive Department.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill significantly impacts OPD operations and budget (up to $1.9 million for additional attorney and support positions) due to expanded juvenile court jurisdiction, extended probation periods, and increased juvenile court proceedings.

The bill expands juvenile court jurisdiction over specific offenses committed by children ages 10 to 12, adjusts juvenile detention review schedules, alters maximum probation periods, and mandates judicial review procedures.

The bill formally establishes the Governor's Office for Children and the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy as units within the Executive Department and authorizes the Governor to define their duties and structures by executive order.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill substantially alters the membership, duties, and reporting timelines of the Commission on Juvenile Justice Reform and Emerging and Best Practices and repeals the State Advisory Board for Juvenile Services.

The State Board of Education must develop guidelines and a model policy for local school boards regarding the education of juvenile sex offender registrants, and MSDE is represented on the Commission on Juvenile Justice Reform.
The bill alters procedures for law enforcement officers who take children into custody, requiring specific written complaints and diversion reports to be submitted to DJS.

The bill amends the statutory reporting duties of the Juvenile Justice Monitoring Unit (JJMU), directing its reports to the Commission on Juvenile Justice Reform instead of the repealed advisory board.

The Secretary of Human Services serves on the Commission on Juvenile Justice Reform, the bill removes DHS from its previous co-staffing role for the commission, and law enforcement is directed to report suspected trafficking victims to local child welfare agencies.
MDH holds a designated seat on the Commission on Juvenile Justice Reform, serves as an entity to which courts may commit juveniles, and consults with DJS regarding juvenile competency evaluations.
The Commission on Juvenile Justice Reform is required to coordinate with the Maryland Department of Labor to identify potential job and apprenticeship opportunities for youth under DJS supervision.
The Commission on Juvenile Justice Reform is specifically directed to review data on arrests, programming completion, and recidivism from the Maryland Longitudinal Data System Center.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Prince George’s County Board of License Commissioners to issue an alcoholic beverages license near certain institutions. Applies to establishments located within 500 feet of a place of worship or 1,000 feet of a school building. Requires the applicant to have previously held a license of the same class for the establishment. Requires that the prior license was in effect before the place of worship or school building was built. Takes effect July 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Prince George's County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Alcoholic beverages license applicants and holders in Prince George's County, places of worship, and schools
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Prince George's County revenues increase by approximately $2,305 annually beginning in fiscal 2025 from the issuance of one Class B beer, wine, and liquor license. Additional local enforcement activity can be absorbed using existing budgeted resources. There is no state fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller is responsible for regulating Maryland's alcohol industry and administering related laws; however, this bill specifically affects retail alcoholic beverages licensing administered at the local level by the Prince George's County Board of License Commissioners, resulting in minimal to no state-level impact.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands the purposes of the Catastrophic Event Account and the Federal Government Shutdown Employee Assistance Loan Fund. Authorizes financial assistance and no-interest loans for noncivilian federal employees during a full or partial federal government shutdown. Applies to federal employees required to report to a Maryland work site without pay due to lapsed appropriations. Requires the Maryland Department of Labor to establish loan eligibility criteria, application procedures, and repayment timelines. Takes effect October 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor; Department of Budget and Management
qa_results.stakeholders: Noncivilian federal employees required to report to a work site in Maryland who are unpaid during a federal government shutdown
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No net effect on State finances, as the bill alters the allowable uses of existing funds. The Department of Budget and Management and the Maryland Department of Labor can handle any administrative changes using existing resources. No local effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor administers the Federal Government Shutdown Employee Assistance Loan Fund and is responsible for establishing loan procedures, application criteria, and repayment terms, which are expanded under this bill to include noncivilian federal employees.
DBM administers the Catastrophic Event Account within the State Reserve Fund and oversees budget execution and amendments that transfer funding between state accounts.
Statute requires the State Treasurer to separately hold and invest the moneys of both the Catastrophic Event Account and the Federal Government Shutdown Employee Assistance Loan Fund.
Statute designates the Comptroller as the entity responsible for accounting for both the Catastrophic Event Account and the Federal Government Shutdown Employee Assistance Loan Fund.
