The Governor is authorized to appropriate funds to the Catastrophic Event Account in the state budget and transfer funds by budget amendment to the Loan Fund during a federal shutdown.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes a Student Support Specialist Network in each public high school in Prince George's County. Requires the Prince George's County Board of Education to develop and disseminate an action plan template by December 31, 2024. Requires each network to develop and implement a Student Support Success Action Plan using the template. Requires each network to submit its plan to the county board for approval before implementation. Requires each network to report implementation results to the county board annually beginning July 1, 2025.
qa_results.responsible_party: Prince George's County Board of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: Prince George's County public high school students, teachers, administrators, school counselors, psychologists, nurses, social workers, and school security personnel
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal effect. Prince George's County expenditures increase by up to $3.7 million annually beginning in fiscal 2025 for additional staffing across 27 county public high schools. Local revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MSDE oversees Maryland's public education system, sets student discipline standards, and administers community school initiatives. While HB 821 places direct mandates on the Prince George's County Board of Education rather than state government, the policies regarding student support networks, restorative practices, and community school coordinators fall within MSDE's broader regulatory and educational domain.
The bill explicitly requires the template for the Student Support Success Action Plan to measure and improve metrics regarding student referrals to the Department of Juvenile Services.

MCSS coordinates school safety strategies, supports positive school climates, and oversees standards for School Resource Officers and school security personnel, who are designated members of the school-level support networks established by the bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Health to provide Medicaid services under the Employed Individuals with Disabilities Program. Prohibits the department from limiting eligibility based on income, spousal assets, retirement accounts, or independence accounts. Requires the department to provide services to qualified applicants who are at least 16 years old. Requires the department to meet twice annually with a State-based coalition of disability advocates. Requires the department to apply to federal authorities for necessary plan amendments or waivers. Directs the department to report by December 1, 2024, on serving individuals age 65 and older.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: employed individuals with disabilities in Maryland applying for or enrolled in the Employed Individuals with Disabilities Program
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material impact on State revenues or expenditures because the bill largely codifies existing Maryland Department of Health policies. The department can submit the required report using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health is the primary agency responsible for administering the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid), including the Employed Individuals with Disabilities (EID) Program. The bill establishes requirements and restrictions on eligibility criteria, requires federal approval/waiver submissions to CMS, and mandates a reporting requirement by December 1, 2024.

The Department of Disabilities coordinates statewide policies and programs supporting individuals with disabilities, particularly regarding employment opportunities, community living, and youth transitioning to adulthood. Revisions to Medicaid eligibility and asset limits for working individuals with disabilities align closely with the agency's policy purview.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes fire safety and notification requirements for residential rental high-rise buildings. Requires smoke detector installation in interior public corridors by July 31, 2025. Mandates emergency escape lighting along common egress routes and specific sprinkler warning notices on unequipped buildings. Prohibits landlords from charging deaf, deafblind, or hard of hearing tenants for required notification appliances. Authorizes local governments to grant property tax credits for buildings making fire safety improvements. Creates a workgroup to develop fire safety best practices for pre-1974 high-rise apartment buildings.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development; State Fire Marshal; Maryland Department of Emergency Management; Department of State Police
qa_results.stakeholders: owners and tenants of residential rental high-rise buildings, deafblind and deaf or hard of hearing tenants, condominium associations, cooperative housing corporations, and local governments
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $35,600 in fiscal 2025 for Department of State Police workgroup staffing. Higher education expenditures increase, likely significantly, in fiscal 2025 to upgrade university residential high-rise buildings. Local property tax revenues may decrease, potentially significantly, beginning in fiscal 2025 to the extent local governments grant authorized tax credits.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Fire Marshal is an entity within the Department of State Police and is tasked with chairing the new Workgroup to Develop Fire Safety Best Practices for Pre-1974 High-Rise Apartment Buildings, coordinating with DHCD on funding sources, and enforcing fire safety standards. DSP is also specifically designated to provide staff support for the workgroup, resulting in a general fund expenditure increase.

DHCD is statutorily required under the bill to coordinate with the State Fire Marshal and MDEM to identify available funding sources to assist building owners and condominium/cooperative boards with installing sprinkler systems, and must publish this information on its website.

USM incurs significant fiscal impacts (estimated at over $1.2 million in FY 2025 for UMD College Park alone, plus costs at Frostburg State) to inspect and upgrade university-owned residential rental high-rise dormitories to comply with the corridor smoke detector and emergency lighting mandates.

MDEM is specifically mandated under Section 9-403(E) to coordinate with the Department of Housing and Community Development and the State Fire Marshal to identify funding sources for residential high-rise sprinkler retrofits.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Section 2 of the bill establishes a temporary advisory body, the Workgroup to Develop Fire Safety Best Practices for Pre-1974 High-Rise Apartment Buildings, to conduct studies and submit recommendations by December 31, 2024.

The Governor is responsible for appointing seven stakeholder members to the Workgroup to Develop Fire Safety Best Practices for Pre-1974 High-Rise Apartment Buildings and will receive the workgroup's final report.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends public safety laws governing smoke alarms and notification appliances for deaf, hard of hearing, and deafblind tenants, directly aligning with ODHH's advocacy and policy focus on accessibility for deaf and hard of hearing residents.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases the maximum authorized number of public members on governing boards for regional resource centers. Allows up to two members of the public from each area served by participating library systems. Retains existing representation of one library trustee from each participating library system. Preserves the Washington County Free Library board of trustees as the Western Maryland governing board. Takes effect July 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Library Agency; Regional Resource Center Governing Boards
qa_results.stakeholders: Members of the public in areas served by regional library resource centers and regional resource center governing boards.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal effect, as altering board appointments does not affect governmental finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This was a departmental bill requested by the Maryland State Library Agency (MSLA), which oversees strategic leadership and coordination for the State Library Network and public libraries. The bill alters the governing board composition for regional library resource centers.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Insurance Administration to study professional employer organizations in the State. Directs the Administration to review regulations, industry history, health plans, and business participation requirements. Requires examination of regulatory structures allowing small employer co-employees to join large group plans. Directs the Administration to assess impacts of proposed health coverage statutory changes on the small group market. Requires the Administration to report its findings to designated legislative committees on or before December 31, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: professional employer organizations, small employers, co-employed workers, and health insurance carriers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are unaffected because the Maryland Insurance Administration can complete the study using existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local finances are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 827 specifically mandates the Maryland Insurance Administration to conduct a study on professional employer organizations (PEOs), their health plan structures, and their potential impacts on the small group market, and submit a report of its findings by December 31, 2024.

qa_results.bill_summary: Defines "damages" or "losses" in statutory causes of action created by the Maryland Code to protect civil rights or consumer rights. Specifies that the terms mean money claimed by or ordered paid to a person as compensation for loss or injury. Requires that the loss or injury results from a violation of the person's rights or protections. Includes reasonable nominal damages within the scope of these terms. Takes effect October 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary
qa_results.stakeholders: Plaintiffs and defendants involved in statutory civil rights and consumer protection legal actions in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Attorney General enforces state consumer protection laws through its Consumer Protection Division and represents the State in legal matters involving civil rights and statutory consumer claims.

The Commission on Civil Rights investigates and enforces Maryland's anti-discrimination statutes; the bill defines recoverable damages and losses, specifically including nominal damages, in statutory civil rights causes of action.
The Administrative Office of the Courts supports the state judicial branch, where civil claims and lawsuits seeking damages under statutory civil rights and consumer protection laws are adjudicated.

The State Treasurer's Office manages state liability and the State Insurance Trust Fund, which could be minimally impacted by changes to recoverable damages in actions involving the State or its personnel.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes a presumption that placement with a child's parent is in the child's best interest during certain treatment. The rule applies when a parent receives residential substance use disorder treatment with beds or services for children. Presumes the child receives proper care and attention while present with the parent for the treatment's duration. Requires a local department of social services to file a report explaining why a nonplacement occurred. Authorizes the Behavioral Health Administration to require treatment facilities to provide beds and services for patients' children.
qa_results.responsible_party: Behavioral Health Administration; Maryland Department of Health; Department of Human Services
qa_results.stakeholders: parents receiving residential substance use disorder treatment, children subject to child in need of assistance (CINA) proceedings, residential substance use disorder treatment facilities, and local departments of social services
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Indeterminate potential increase in State expenditures related to substance use disorder treatment programs and child out-of-home placements, along with potential matching federal Medicaid revenues. Local government operations and finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 833 directly authorizes the Behavioral Health Administration (BHA) within the Maryland Department of Health to require substance use disorder treatment facilities to provide beds and services for patients' children and allow them to remain together. The fiscal note highlights potential significant impacts on MDH expenditures and Medicaid matching funds.

The bill directly impacts child welfare operations administered by DHS and local departments of social services, requiring local departments to file specific explanatory reports with the court when children are not placed with parents undergoing residential treatment and altering shelter care placement standards.

The bill alters statutory standards and creates legal presumptions governing Child in Need of Assistance (CINA) and shelter care proceedings in circuit courts, and requires local departments to file specific reports with the courts.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires Calvert County to adopt conflict of interest provisions equivalent to or exceeding State judicial relief requirements. Requires county ethics provisions to mandate that the Calvert County Ethics Commission make public any recommendation to expel a Commissioner. Requires the Calvert County governing body to enact a law authorizing it to remove county elected officials for conflict violations. Takes effect immediately as an emergency measure upon approval on April 25, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governing Body of Calvert County; Calvert County Ethics Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Calvert County elected officials and County Commissioners
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on State operations or finances, and not expected to affect Calvert County government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Ethics Commission oversees the administration of Maryland Public Ethics Law, which includes reviewing and approving local government ethics laws to ensure they comply with State statutory requirements and minimum standards. HB 834 mandates specific conflict of interest and expulsion provisions for Calvert County's ethics laws.

The bill requires Calvert County to incorporate provisions equivalent to § 5-902 of the General Provisions Article regarding judicial relief, authorizing the circuit court to issue cease-and-desist orders, grant injunctive relief, impose fines, or void official acts.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the County Commissioners of Calvert County to enact an ordinance establishing a local percentage preference for certain procurement contracts. Allows resident businesses exceeding the lowest nonresident bid by not more than a specified percentage to receive contract awards. Defines a resident business as a business with its principal office located in Calvert County. Defines a nonresident business as a business whose principal office is outside the county. Requires the County Commissioners to comply with statutory notice and public hearing procedures when enacting the ordinance.
qa_results.responsible_party: County Commissioners of Calvert County
qa_results.stakeholders: resident businesses in Calvert County and nonresident businesses competing for Calvert County procurement contracts
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on State finances. Calvert County procurement expenditures may increase if the county enacts an ordinance and awards contracts to higher-bidding resident businesses, but specific figures are unavailable.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Prince George's County Family Child Care Home Expansion Grant Program within the county public school system. Requires the local school system to award grants to eligible nonprofit organizations in Prince George's County. Requires recipient nonprofits to train and assist prospective registered family child care providers in low-income communities. Restricts program eligibility to prospective providers whose household income does not exceed 50% of the statewide median income. Authorizes grant funds for multilingual outreach, background checks, licensing navigation, inspection costs, and quality benchmarks. Requires the Governor to include an annual appropriation of $500,000 for the program beginning in fiscal year 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Prince George's County Public School System
qa_results.stakeholders: Nonprofit organizations offering child care support services, prospective and registered family child care providers, and low-income families and children in Prince George's County.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not directly affected according to the Fiscal Note. Prince George's County Public Schools expenditures may increase significantly due to administrative start-up costs and grant funding, with preliminary illustrative estimates suggesting local expenditures could increase by up to $1.6 million in fiscal 2025.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Prince George's County Family Child Care Home Expansion Grant Program within the local public school system. The program's purpose is to help individuals navigate the Maryland State Department of Education's (MSDE) process for becoming registered family child care providers, which falls under MSDE's Division of Early Childhood.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases the threshold from $25,000 to $50,000 for Carroll County public work contracts and equipment purchases made by commissioner order. Requires the Procurement Officer to provide public notice for at least one week when costs exceed $50,000. Exempts emergency procurements and sole source purchases from the public bidding and notice requirements. Updates statutory references from the Chief of the Bureau of Purchasing to the Procurement Officer. Authorizes the County Commissioners to permit the Procurement Officer to engage in cooperative or piggyback purchasing.
qa_results.responsible_party: County Commissioners of Carroll County; Procurement Officer for the County Commissioners of Carroll County
qa_results.stakeholders: Vendors and contractors bidding on Carroll County public works or equipment contracts; Carroll County government departments
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No direct effect on Carroll County finances or revenues, though the county likely experiences administrative efficiencies in conducting small procurements. No state fiscal effect.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes dealers franchised to sell Class M motor homes or Class G trailers to participate in more than two annual shows. Extends this authorization to licensed vehicle salesmen employed by those dealers. Repeals the requirement that these vehicle shows be limited to Class M motor homes or Class G trailers. Aligns participation rules for motor and trailer home dealers with rules for motorcycle dealers. Takes effect October 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Transportation; Motor Vehicle Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: New vehicle dealers franchised to sell Class M motor homes or Class G trailers and licensed vehicle salesmen employed by them
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Motor Vehicle Administration licenses and regulates motor vehicle dealers and salespersons under Title 15 of the Maryland Transportation Article, directly overseeing the rules governing dealer participation in annual vehicle shows.
The Maryland Department of Transportation is the parent department of the Motor Vehicle Administration and oversees the implementation and enforcement of Maryland's Transportation Article.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Comptroller to implement and administer an individual income tax credit eligibility awareness campaign. Directs the campaign to identify underserved individuals eligible for personal income tax credits and encourage them to apply. Authorizes the Comptroller to enter into data sharing agreements with other State agencies to identify eligible individuals. Mandates an annual budget appropriation of $300,000 for the campaign in fiscal years 2026 through 2030. Requires biennial reporting to the General Assembly starting December 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Underserved Maryland taxpayers eligible for individual income tax credits
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $300,000 annually in FY 2026 through FY 2030 due to a mandated appropriation. General fund and local revenues may decrease beginning in FY 2026 if awareness efforts lead to increased credit claims. Montgomery County expenditures may also increase due to its local earned income credit supplement.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Comptroller to implement, administer, and report on the Individual Income Tax Credit Eligibility Awareness Campaign, including identifying underserved individuals, contacting them, and entering into data-sharing agreements.
The bill mandates that the Governor include an appropriation of $300,000 for the awareness campaign in the annual budget bill for each of fiscal years 2026 through 2030.

DBM is responsible for formulating the state budget and supervising budget execution, which directly involves implementing the statutory mandated appropriation of $300,000 annually from FY 2026 through FY 2030.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals statutory restrictions specifying allowable asset classes for investing State unexpended or surplus funds. Requires the State Treasurer to adopt regulations specifying authorized asset classes and maximum investment thresholds by December 1, 2024. Requires the Treasurer to consult with governmental entities before adopting regulations altering allowable local public investments. Authorizes the Treasurer and local governmental entities to continue current investments until new regulations take effect. Requires the Treasurer to notify local governing bodies in writing after adopting amended investment guidelines.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Treasurer
qa_results.stakeholders: local governmental entities, county boards of education, county boards of library trustees, and minority business enterprises providing brokerage and investment management services
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on State or local finances or operations. The State Treasurer's Office can adopt regulations and notify local governments using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Treasurer's Office is the primary implementing agency for this bill, which grants the Treasurer authority to establish allowable asset classes and investment thresholds via regulation, consult with governmental entities on local investment guidelines, and manage state investment portfolio policies.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill maintains statutory requirements that the Treasurer develop guidelines in conjunction with the Governor's Office of Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs to evaluate minority business enterprises for brokerage and investment management services, and submit an annual reporting update to this office.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands the Small Business Preference Program to all Executive Branch units and agencies. Repeals mandatory program participation for the University System of Maryland and Morgan State University. Designates the Board of Public Works as the regulatory authority for the program. Requires each procurement unit, subject to Board approval, to establish percentage price preferences. Caps preferences at 8 percent, including additional preferences for veteran-owned and disabled veteran-owned businesses. Authorizes units to designate procurements for the program with unit head approval.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of Public Works; Department of Commerce
qa_results.stakeholders: small businesses, veteran-owned small businesses, disabled veteran-owned small businesses, and Executive Branch procurement units
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State procurement expenditures across all funds may experience a minimal increase if agencies award contracts to small businesses that do not submit the lowest bid. No effect on State revenues or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates the Board of Public Works as the primary regulatory and oversight authority for the Small Business Preference Program, requiring it to adopt regulations setting small business qualification criteria and program operational procedures.

The bill explicitly mandates the Department of Commerce to assist the Board of Public Works in compiling and maintaining a bidder's list of small businesses and locating potential minority and small business sources.

As the state's central procurement agency, DGS is significantly impacted by the expansion of the Small Business Preference Program across executive agencies and the transfer of regulatory criteria authority to the Board of Public Works.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The agency oversees state socioeconomic procurement programs, including the Small Business Reserve (SBR) Program; the bill allows agencies to count Small Business Preference awards and non-designated contracts toward their overall SBR achievement goals.
MDOT is a major state procurement agency previously tasked with establishing its own Small Business Preference regulations, which will now be standardized under the Board of Public Works.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill maintains specific requirements for DPSCS to apply DGS-established percentage price preferences and procedures for procurements related to state correctional facility construction.
The bill explicitly repeals the University System of Maryland's mandatory participation in the Small Business Preference Program and removes its regulatory authority under the subtitle.
The bill explicitly removes Morgan State University from mandatory participation in the Small Business Preference Program and repeals its independent regulatory authority under the program.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals the statutory prohibition against harvesting shellfish on aquaculture leases between sunset and sunrise. Prohibits aquaculture leaseholders from harvesting shellfish outside hours established in regulation. Requires the Department of Natural Resources to establish harvest hours within leased areas by regulation. Directs the Department to consult with the Aquaculture Coordinating Council before establishing the harvest hours. Takes effect June 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources; Aquaculture Coordinating Council
qa_results.stakeholders: shellfish aquaculture leaseholders
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No direct effect on State or local finances; the Department of Natural Resources can adopt the required regulations using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 857 directly impacts the Department of Natural Resources by requiring it to adopt regulations establishing shellfish harvest hours within leased aquaculture areas, in consultation with the Aquaculture Coordinating Council, rather than adhering to the previous statutory sunrise-to-sunset restrictions.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates that the Department of Natural Resources consult with the Aquaculture Coordinating Council—a statutory advisory body—when developing and establishing regulations governing harvest hours for shellfish aquaculture leases.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires community action boards to meet federal tripartite board requirements under federal block grant law. Repeals existing state statutory provisions dictating the specific composition of community action boards. Eliminates the state requirement that community action boards consist of at least 15 members. Removes state term limits capping certain board members at five consecutive or ten total years. Takes effect October 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
qa_results.stakeholders: community action agencies, community action boards, and low-income individuals and families served by community action programs
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) administers the federal Community Services Block Grant (CSBG) program in Maryland and allocates funds to the community action agencies governed by the community action boards amended by this bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires electric companies, gas companies, and the Department of Housing and Community Development to implement greenhouse gas reduction plans. Directs the Public Service Commission to establish emissions reduction targets and oversee three-year program cycles beginning in 2027. Mandates full recovery of reasonably incurred program costs on a current basis through customer bill surcharges by 2028. Requires approved contractors for low-income programs to pay at least 150% of the State minimum wage and provide benefits. Prohibits utilities from requiring customers to authorize utility control over customer electricity or gas usage.
qa_results.responsible_party: Public Service Commission; Department of Housing and Community Development; Maryland Department of the Environment; Maryland Energy Administration; Governor's Office of Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs; Maryland Department of Transportation
qa_results.stakeholders: Electric companies; gas companies; electric cooperatives; municipal electric and gas utilities; utility ratepayers; low-income residential households; energy efficiency and weatherization contractors
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures for the Maryland Department of the Environment increase by $403,200 in FY 2025 and ongoing for staff and contractual analysis. Maryland Energy Administration special fund expenditures may increase by $50,000 in FY 2025. Department of Housing and Community Development special fund revenues and expenditures increase substantially beginning in FY 2027, potentially exceeding $12 million in FY 2027 and $24 million annually thereafter, funded through utility ratepayer surcharges.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Public Service Commission is the primary regulatory agency tasked with establishing greenhouse gas emissions reduction targets for electric and gas companies, reviewing and approving three-year energy efficiency and conservation plans, overseeing cost-recovery mechanisms, convening a moderate-income working group, and reporting annually to the General Assembly.

DHCD is directly tasked with developing and implementing plans to achieve specific greenhouse gas reduction targets through low-income energy efficiency, conservation, and electrification programs; establishing whole-home retrofit plans and budgets; and enforcing contractor labor standards, resulting in significant operational and special fund fiscal impacts.

MDE is required to provide baseline emissions calculations, project marginal greenhouse gas emissions rates, and conduct formal analyses for the PSC regarding the adequacy of utility and DHCD plans, requiring additional staff and contractual resources.

MEA participates in technical consultations on proposed utility and DHCD energy efficiency plans, provides written findings to the PSC, assists in applying for federal funds, and coordinates funding integration with the Strategic Energy Investment Fund.

OPC is statutorily required to be consulted on the design and adequacy of the utility and DHCD energy efficiency and greenhouse gas reduction plans and to submit written findings to the PSC on behalf of residential utility consumers.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOSBA is specifically tasked, alongside the state's MBE certification agency, with conducting and submitting a disparity study evaluating remedial measures for minority- and women-owned businesses in the energy efficiency and conservation services market by December 31, 2026.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates collaboration with the Green and Healthy Task Force on DHCD whole-home and low-income retrofit plans, and requires the PSC to establish a working group on the EmPOWER Maryland Program and moderate-income households.
As the designated MBE certification agency under state law, MDOT is tasked alongside GOSBA with conducting a disparity study regarding energy efficiency and conservation services used by DHCD.
OAG must be consulted during the disparity study conducted by the MBE certification agency and GOSBA to assess constitutional compliance with legal standards regarding minority business enterprises.
The Governor receives mandatory plans and reports, including DHCD's whole-home funding coordination plan and the PSC working group study on moderate-income households.
The Board of Public Works is referenced as the authority that designates the minority business enterprise certification agency participating in the required disparity study.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands mandated health insurance and Maryland Medical Assistance Program coverage to include prostheses and replacement prostheses. Requires carriers to cover prostheses deemed medically necessary for daily living, essential job activities, or physical activities. Prohibits carriers from imposing separate dollar maximums or higher cost-sharing than for similar medical benefits. Authorizes replacement coverage when physiological changes occur, irreparable damage happens, or repair costs exceed 60 percent. Mandates that insurers, health maintenance organizations, and Medicaid managed care organizations report claims data by June 2030. Directs the Maryland Health Care Commission and Maryland Department of Health to study orthoses coverage by December 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Maryland Insurance Administration; Maryland Health Care Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland Medical Assistance Program enrollees with limb loss; insured individuals requiring prostheses; health insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations; Medicaid managed care organizations; prosthetics providers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State Medicaid expenditures increase by an estimated $1.7 million in FY 2025 (split evenly between general funds and federal matching funds) and $3.5 million in FY 2026 to cover whole-body health prostheses, with federal revenues increasing concurrently. Maryland Insurance Administration special fund revenues increase minimally in FY 2025 from policy form filing fees. Local government health care expenditures may increase if commercial premiums rise.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDH administers the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid), which is mandated by the bill to cover prostheses and replacements beginning January 1, 2025, resulting in estimated expenditure increases of $1.7 million to $3.8 million annually. MDH is also tasked with conducting an 'L' code utilization review and submitting compliance reports jointly with MIA.

MIA regulates commercial health insurers, HMOs, and nonprofit health service plans subject to the new coverage requirements. It must review rate and form filings, consult on the orthoses cost evaluation study, and jointly prescribe reporting requirements and submit a compliance report to the General Assembly.

MHCC is explicitly mandated in Section 4 to review utilization data for 'L' codes within the All-Payer Claims Database, evaluate the cost impact of requiring coverage for orthoses, and submit a report of its findings to the General Assembly.

DBM administers the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program; while evaluated for the bill's insurance mandates, the fiscal impact was determined to be negligible as the program already provides prosthetic coverage.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires junk dealers, scrap metal processors, and automotive dismantlers and recyclers to record specific vehicle information when acquiring detached catalytic converters. Mandates recording the vehicle identification number of the vehicle from which a detached catalytic converter or part was obtained. Requires recording the registration plate number, make, and model of any vehicle from which the converter was obtained. Applies these record-keeping obligations to licensed automotive dismantlers, recyclers, and scrap metal processors acquiring detached catalytic converters from any person. Incorporates these requirements into vehicle acquisition records maintained under the Transportation Article.
qa_results.responsible_party: Motor Vehicle Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Licensed junk dealers, scrap metal processors, automotive dismantlers and recyclers, and individuals selling detached catalytic converters or parts
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State government operations or finances, and has no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor oversees the licensing and regulation of various commercial trades and businesses, including junk dealers and scrap metal processors regulated under Title 17 of the Business Regulation Article amended by this bill.

The MVA licenses and regulates automotive dismantlers, recyclers, and scrap processors under Title 15, Subtitle 5 of the Transportation Article, and sets standards for the required record keeping amended under Section 15-511.
MDOT is the parent department of the Motor Vehicle Administration and oversees the administration and enforcement of vehicle and automotive dismantler regulations across the state.

The Maryland State Police investigates vehicle-related property crimes, including catalytic converter theft rings, and enforces statutory compliance regarding required transaction logs and records maintained by scrap metal processors and automotive recyclers.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP tracks statewide public safety priorities, crime trends, and theft prevention strategies, including coordinated initiatives to curb catalytic converter theft.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands the Appraisal Gap From Historic Redlining Financial Assistance Program to include individual owner-occupant purchasers. Authorizes the Department of Housing and Community Development to provide financial assistance to qualifying buyers. Requires the individual to purchase a qualified property after a qualified project is completed. Mandates that the purchase occur at an affordable sales price determined by department regulations. Requires the department to accept applications from individuals proposing to purchase a qualified property.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals purchasing qualified residential properties as owner-occupants, affordable housing developers, and residents in historically redlined neighborhoods and designated sustainable communities
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on overall program finances. The Department of Housing and Community Development can administer the expansion using existing budgeted resources. Local government operations and finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the Appraisal Gap From Historic Redlining Financial Assistance Program (operated as UPLIFT), which is administered by the Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD), by expanding eligibility and requiring DHCD to accept and approve applications from owner-occupant purchasers.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the deadline to July 1, 2026, for individuals to obtain licensure before practicing as assisted living managers. Modifies required 80-hour manager training courses to allow in-person courses, virtual training methods, or a combination of both. Requires managers in assisted living programs with four or fewer beds to complete training requirements by June 30, 2026. Deems individuals employed in programs licensed for five or more beds as of June 30, 2024, qualified for licensure. Requires the State Board of Long-Term Care Administrators to report annually on licensure implementation through October 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Long-Term Care Administrators; Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Assisted living managers, assisted living program owners, and applicants for assisted living manager licensure
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The State Board of Long-Term Care Administrators can implement the bill and submit required reports using existing budgeted resources. There is no effect on State revenues and no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Long-Term Care Administrators is a health occupations licensing board within the Maryland Department of Health. Additionally, MDH approves the assisted living manager training programs and regulates assisted living facilities through the Office of Health Care Quality.

The Maryland Department of Aging oversees advocacy and services for older adults in long-term care facilities, and the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman—housed within the department—is a designated statutory member of the State Board of Long-Term Care Administrators.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Comptroller to develop and maintain a procurement transparency data dashboard on the Board of Public Works website. Establishes a governance committee representing the Governor, Comptroller, and Treasurer to review dashboard accuracy. Requires the dashboard to be public, interactive, searchable, and compatible with the Comptroller's payment processing portal. Mandates inclusion of Board of Public Works meeting materials, contract spending amounts, and procurement preference goals. Requires the Governor to appropriate annual funding for software and at least one full-time Comptroller position.
qa_results.responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland; Board of Public Works
qa_results.stakeholders: State procurement vendors, Minority Business Enterprises, Veteran-Owned Small Business Enterprises, and the general public
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $170,500 in FY 2025 to fund one full-time IT administrator and software costs, rising to $194,700 by FY 2029. Funding is discretionary in FY 2025 and mandated beginning in FY 2026. No impact on revenues or local governments.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Comptroller to develop and maintain the procurement transparency data dashboard, integrate it with the Comptroller's online payment portal, and designate a liaison to serve on the governance committee. The bill also provides for at least one full-time position in the Comptroller's Office.

The procurement transparency data dashboard must be hosted on the Board of Public Works' website, display BPW agendas, announcements, and contract spending data, and be reviewed by a governance committee composed of liaisons to the BPW.

A liaison to the Board of Public Works from the Governor's Office must serve on the governance committee reviewing the dashboard. Additionally, the Governor is required to include appropriations in the annual state budget for software and staffing to support the dashboard.
A liaison to the Board of Public Works from the State Treasurer's Office is mandated to serve on the governance committee tasked with reviewing the dashboard's contents for accuracy and completeness.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires each retail service station dealer to prominently display credit and debit prices for regular gasoline on premises signage. Authorizes the same pricing display options for whole measurement units of diesel and other motor fuel products. Repeals the signage exemption for dealers operating three or fewer dispensing units with six or fewer nozzles. Requires all numerals on the pricing sign to be uniform and the same size. Requires gasoline suppliers to provide any new or additional compliant signs and numerals without cost to dealers. Establishes that these motor fuel pricing signage provisions supersede inconsistent local law.
qa_results.responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: retail service station dealers, gasoline suppliers, and motorists in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal state and local fiscal impact. The Comptroller can enforce the signage requirements with existing budgeted resources, and existing penalty provisions are not expected to materially affect state or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller regulates the motor fuel industry in Maryland, sets fuel grade designation display requirements, and is responsible for enforcing retail service station compliance with the pricing signage requirements established by the bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Health to contract with an independent consultant to study four state entities. Directs the study to review the Health Services Cost Review Commission and Maryland Health Care Commission. Mandates review of the Maryland Community Health Resources Commission and Maryland Insurance Administration. Requires examination of overlapping statutory duties and alignment with state total cost of care models. Mandates that the consultant seek input from the department and all four studied entities. Requires the department to report study findings to the Governor and legislative committees by January 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland Department of Health, Health Services Cost Review Commission, Maryland Health Care Commission, Maryland Community Health Resources Commission, and Maryland Insurance Administration
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $50,000 total, with $30,000 in FY 2025 and $20,000 in FY 2026, for the Maryland Department of Health to contract with an independent consultant. State revenues are unaffected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDH is the primary agency responsible for implementing the bill; it is required to contract with an independent consultant to conduct the study, participate in consultations, absorb the fiscal cost ($50,000), and submit the final report.

HSCRC is one of the core health regulatory entities being evaluated by the study for statutory overlap, functional streamlining, and administrative alignment with models like AHEAD and TCOC, and must provide input to the consultant.
MHCC is directly subject to the study regarding its regulatory duties, potential streamlining, and organizational efficiency, and is required to provide input during the evaluation.

MIA is directly subject to the required study to evaluate overlap of statutory and regulatory duties and administrative structure with state health commissions, and must provide input to the independent contractor.
The Governor's Office is a designated recipient of the final report resulting from the study, due by January 1, 2026.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters statutory procedures for Maryland corporations to ratify defective corporate acts and putative stock issuances. Requires stockholder approval if required by corporate charter, bylaws, law, or company agreements. Sets specific voting standards when ratifying director elections. Authorizes state and federal courts sitting in Maryland to determine ratification validity and waive procedural requirements. Requires legal challenges by adversely affected parties to be brought within 120 days after ratification or notice.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland corporations, corporate boards of directors, corporate stockholders, and holders of putative stock
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters provisions governing court actions regarding the ratification of defective corporate acts, granting Maryland state courts jurisdiction to determine the validity of ratifications and modify or waive ratification procedures.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires counties to defend, settle, and pay tort claims arising from law enforcement or detention center functions of sheriffs. Designates the State as the proper defendant in these actions and prohibits naming counties as defendants. Caps tort claim liability at the statutory limits of the State's waiver of sovereign immunity. Relieves the State Treasurer of liability and transfers the State's tort duties and liabilities to the applicable county. Authorizes counties and Baltimore City to obtain insurance to provide coverage and defense under the Maryland Tort Claims Act.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General; Maryland State Treasurer
qa_results.stakeholders: County governments, Baltimore City, sheriffs, deputy sheriffs, and tort claimants
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State Insurance Trust Fund special fund expenditures decrease by at least $75,000 in FY 2025 and $100,000 annually thereafter. Local expenditures collectively increase by at least $75,000 in FY 2025 and $100,000 annually thereafter as liability costs shift to counties, though future local expenditures may decrease if covered through lower-cost insurance pools.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly relieves the State Treasurer from liability under § 9-107 of the State Finance and Procurement Article for tort claims arising out of sheriffs' law enforcement and detention center functions, transferring responsibility to counties. Consequently, special fund expenditures from the State Insurance Trust Fund (administered by the Treasurer's Office) decrease by an estimated $75,000 to $100,000 annually. The bill also directs the Treasurer to work cooperatively with county officials on allocation disputes.

As the chief legal counsel defending state personnel and agencies under the Maryland Tort Claims Act, OAG is directly impacted by changes in legal defense responsibilities for sheriff tort claims, resulting in reduced litigation workloads. Additionally, uncodified language expresses legislative intent for the OAG to work cooperatively with counties, MACo, and insurers to resolve disputes over claim responsibility allocations.

The bill maintains statutory provisions under § 9-108 of the State Finance and Procurement Article allowing the State to intercept and set off assessments and litigation expenses from a local subdivision's share of income tax collected by the State Comptroller if the county fails to obtain adequate insurance coverage.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands eligibility for the Charles W. Riley scholarship to individuals enrolled in any course at eligible higher education institutions. Alters maximum scholarship award amounts based on full-time resident tuition at certain public two-year or four-year institutions. Requires non-loan student financial aid to be credited toward tuition before calculating any scholarship award amount. Mandates that initial scholarship awards be provided to recipients on a first-come, first-served basis. Prioritizes students majoring in specified fire, rescue, and public safety fields for the first $400,000 distributed annually.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Higher Education Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Career and volunteer firefighters, ambulance and rescue squad members, and Maryland public and private nonprofit higher education institutions
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $10,000 in FY 2025 for Maryland Higher Education Commission system enhancements. Any impact on public higher education and local community college finances is assumed to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MHEC is the primary implementing agency responsible for administering the Charles W. Riley Firefighter and Ambulance and Rescue Squad Member Scholarship, updating award criteria in the Maryland College Aid Processing System ($10,000 IT expense in FY 2025), and managing the scholarship fund.

MHEC is the primary implementing agency responsible for administering the Charles W. Riley Firefighter and Ambulance and Rescue Squad Member Scholarship, managing the fund, and updating the eligibility criteria and award calculations.

USM institutions serve as eligible institutions where students may use the scholarship; additionally, the statutory maximum award calculation is directly indexed to the highest resident undergraduate tuition and mandatory fees within USM.
The Comptroller is statutorily designated under the bill to account for the Charles W. Riley Firefighter and Ambulance and Rescue Squad Member Scholarship Fund.
The State Treasurer is statutorily directed to hold the Charles W. Riley Firefighter and Ambulance and Rescue Squad Member Scholarship Fund separately as a nonlapsing fund.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Maryland Higher Education Commission to waive minimum course load requirements for certain scholarship applicants. An applicant for a part-time senatorial or delegate scholarship must have a documented disability to request the waiver. The waiver exempts eligible applicants from the requirement to take at least six semester hours each semester. Recipients remain subject to existing program limits, including maximum allowable years of part-time study. The Act takes effect July 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Higher Education Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: applicants and recipients of part-time senatorial or delegate scholarships who have documented disabilities
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on State revenues or overall scholarship spending. The Maryland Higher Education Commission can implement the waiver process using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the Maryland Higher Education Commission with administering and approving waivers of minimum semester-hour requirements for part-time senatorial and delegate scholarship applicants with documented disabilities.
The bill directly authorizes the Commission to grant course-load waivers for part-time senatorial and delegate scholarship recipients with documented disabilities.

The department coordinates state policies and programs to ensure inclusivity and accessibility for individuals with disabilities, aligning with the bill's accommodation for students with documented disabilities.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes a provider in the Ulysses Currie Head Start Program to receive full State prekindergarten funds even if receiving federal funds. Exempts program providers from statutory prekindergarten quality structural elements that conflict with federal Head Start requirements. Requires providers to follow federal requirements whenever a conflict arises with State structural standards. Maintains the existing annual State budget appropriation of at least $3,000,000 for the program.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: Ulysses Currie Head Start Program providers, early childhood educators, and low-income prekindergarten students and families
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures and revenues are not materially affected because the bill is largely clarifying, no clear conflicts exist between federal and State requirements, and the $3.0 million annual minimum appropriation remains unchanged. Local government finances are also not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) oversees early childhood development, publicly funded full-day prekindergarten, Maryland EXCELS, and the distribution of state funding to eligible prekindergarten and Head Start providers under the Education Article.

The Department of Budget and Management monitors and manages state budget appropriations, including statutory funding mandates and formula-based education allocations such as those for the Ulysses Currie Head Start Program and prekindergarten funding.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Access to Attorneys, Advocates, and Consultants for Special Education Program and a dedicated special fund. Designates the Maryland Volunteer Lawyers Service to administer the program and the State Department of Education to administer the fund. Directs legal, advocacy, and consultant resources to qualifying low-income students with disabilities facing special education disputes. Caps provider reimbursement at customary rates up to $200 per hour and lifetime assistance at $20,000 per student. Mandates an annual state budget appropriation of $1,000,000 to the fund beginning in fiscal year 2026. Requires public agencies to provide program information to parents before individualized education program meetings, mediation, and due process hearings.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Volunteer Lawyers Service; Maryland State Department of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: Students with disabilities from qualifying low-income households; parents and guardians of students with disabilities; special education attorneys, advocates, and consultants; local school systems and public educational agencies
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $1.0 million annually beginning in fiscal 2025, reflecting contingent budget funding in fiscal 2025 and a mandated $1.0 million appropriation starting in fiscal 2026. Special fund revenues and expenditures increase correspondingly by $1.0 million annually. Local school systems may incur indeterminate costs if due process filings increase.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MSDE is the primary implementing agency responsible for administering the Access to Attorneys, Advocates, and Consultants for Special Education Fund, compiling statewide data on dispute proceedings, developing informational materials and training in consultation with partners, and submitting an annual report to the General Assembly.

The bill explicitly defines the Maryland School for the Deaf as a public agency subject to the bill's requirements, including providing required notifications regarding the program at IEP and dispute resolution meetings and collecting dispute data annually.
The State Treasurer is statutorily directed to hold and invest the monies of the newly established Access to Attorneys, Advocates, and Consultants for Special Education Fund.
The Comptroller is statutorily required to account for the newly established Access to Attorneys, Advocates, and Consultants for Special Education Fund.
The bill establishes a statutory mandated appropriation requiring the Governor to include $1,000,000 in the annual budget bill for the Fund beginning in fiscal year 2026.
OAH conducts special education due process hearings, which are directly impacted by the bill's provision of funded legal counsel, advocates, and resolution procedures for eligible families.
The bill defines public agencies subject to the notification and annual dispute data collection requirements to include the Juvenile Services Education Program.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Garrett County Sheriff's salary at 80% of the salary of the State's Attorney of Garrett County. Repeals the requirement for the Garrett County Salary Study Commission to study the salary of the Sheriff. Applies the salary alteration beginning at the next term of office. Excludes individuals appointed or elected after the effective date to fill out an unexpired term. Takes effect October 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: County Commissioners of Garrett County; Garrett County Salary Study Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Sheriff of Garrett County and Garrett County government
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Garrett County expenditures increase by a minimum of $32,700 in FY 2027 and by at least $56,100 annually thereafter to fund the salary increase and fringe benefits. State finances and local revenues are not affected.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases the contract value threshold from $25,000 to $50,000 for mandatory newspaper bid advertising in Garrett County. Exempts contracts for professional services required to be licensed by the State of Maryland from newspaper advertising requirements. Authorizes Garrett County to solicit contracts for state-licensed professional services by written bids. Applies to contracts of sale or purchase entered into by the Garrett County Commissioners or county employees. Takes effect October 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of County Commissioners of Garrett County
qa_results.stakeholders: Garrett County government, county procurement officials, and vendors or contractors bidding on Garrett County contracts, including state-licensed professional service providers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The bill is procedural in nature and does not directly affect Garrett County government finances.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters application and award procedures under the Winery and Vineyard Economic Development Grant Program. Authorizes individuals and corporations to apply for grants for qualified capital expenses incurred during the immediately preceding calendar year. Repeals the statutory September 15 annual application deadline. Repeals the December 15 annual deadline for awarding grants to eligible applicants. Takes effect July 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Commerce
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals and corporations establishing new wineries or vineyards or making capital improvements to existing wineries or vineyards in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on State general fund expenditures or revenues, and no local fiscal impact. Commerce expects the grant program to operate at its statutory full capacity regardless of the procedural modifications.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Commerce is the administering agency for the Winery and Vineyard Economic Development Grant Program. The bill directly alters the program's application timing, eligible expense periods, and grant award schedule.

The Department of Agriculture supports Maryland's farming and agribusiness community, which includes vineyards and wineries, and served as an information source during the evaluation of this legislation.

qa_results.bill_summary: Removes the State Treasurer from the Board of Trustees for the Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation. Repeals the Treasurer's authority to approve foundation easement purchases, local preservation programs, and easement terminations. Removes the State Treasurer or designee from the Maryland Commission on Climate Change and the Coast Smart Council. Adds the Comptroller or designee to the Maryland Commission on Climate Change and the Coast Smart Council. Establishes an effective date of June 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Treasurer; Comptroller; Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation; Maryland Commission on Climate Change; Coast Smart Council
qa_results.stakeholders: State Treasurer, Comptroller of Maryland, and members and staff of the Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation, the Maryland Commission on Climate Change, and the Coast Smart Council
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no material impact on State operations or finances. The State Treasurer's Office may see administrative efficiencies from attending fewer meetings, and the Comptroller's Office can handle the duties with existing budgeted resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly removes the State Treasurer from membership on the Board of Trustees for the Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation (MALPF), the Maryland Commission on Climate Change, and the Coast Smart Council, eliminating associated statutory duties.
The bill adds the Comptroller or the Comptroller's designee as an ex officio member to the Maryland Commission on Climate Change and the Coast Smart Council.

MALPF is an entity within the Department of Agriculture; the bill alters the composition of the MALPF Board of Trustees and removes the requirement for the State Treasurer to review and approve agricultural land preservation easements and program actions.
The Maryland Commission on Climate Change is housed within the Department of the Environment, and the bill amends its statutory membership by replacing the State Treasurer with the Comptroller.
The Coast Smart Council is established within the Department of Natural Resources, and the bill alters its membership by substituting the Comptroller for the State Treasurer.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The legislation directly alters the statutory governance and membership composition of two state advisory bodies: the Maryland Commission on Climate Change and the Coast Smart Council.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the stadium beer and wine license in Washington County to a multi-use sports and events facility license. Authorizes the Washington County Board of License Commissioners to issue the license to professional baseball team franchise owners. Permits the license holder to sell beer, wine, and liquor for on-premises consumption at facility events. Requires all employees of the license holder to complete alcohol awareness and crowd control training programs. Increases the annual license fee to $2,500 while repealing the separate Sunday permit fee.
qa_results.responsible_party: Washington County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Professional baseball team franchise owners operating multi-use sports and events facilities in Washington County, facility employees, and event attendees
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Washington County license revenues increase by $250 annually per license beginning in fiscal 2025 due to an increased annual fee of $2,500 that replaces the prior $2,000 license fee and $250 Sunday permit. State operations and finances are not materially affected, and local enforcement will be conducted within existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters local alcoholic beverage licensing in Washington County by authorizing the sale of liquor in addition to beer and wine at a multi-use sports and events facility. The Comptroller of Maryland has general regulatory oversight of the state's alcoholic beverage industry and collection of alcoholic beverage taxes.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Labor to provide guidance on implementing and enforcing the Maryland Building Performance Standards. Mandates this guidance upon request by a local jurisdiction. Requires the Department to consult with the Office of the Attorney General when preparing the guidance. Directs that the guidance address the Standards in relation to any religious observance, practice, or belief. Takes effect October 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor; Office of the Attorney General
qa_results.stakeholders: Local jurisdictions, local building officials, and individuals or religious organizations seeking building permits or compliance accommodations
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are not materially affected because the Maryland Department of Labor and the Office of the Attorney General can implement the requirements with existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local government operations and finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires the Maryland Department of Labor to provide guidance, upon request by a local jurisdiction, regarding the implementation and enforcement of the Maryland Building Performance Standards in relation to religious observances, practices, or beliefs.

The bill statutorily requires the Maryland Department of Labor to consult with the Office of the Attorney General when developing and providing guidance on building standards related to religious observances, practices, or beliefs.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the County Commissioners of Washington County or a county employee to purchase vehicles without advertising for bids. Limits this authorization to vehicle purchase contracts that do not exceed $100,000. Creates an exception to the county requirement mandating advertised bids for contracts exceeding $50,000. Takes effect October 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: County Commissioners of Washington County
qa_results.stakeholders: Washington County government agencies and vehicle vendors
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on state finances. The bill likely has no direct effect on Washington County finances, though it may create administrative efficiencies for county vehicle purchases.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Secretary of Agriculture to implement a program using Bacillus thuringiensis israelensis to control or eliminate nuisance insects. Mandates program execution in accordance with the State budget and existing public notice requirements. Requires the Secretary to carry out a project if a county or municipality agrees to pay 50% of costs. Directs local matching payments to the Comptroller for deposit into the Nuisance Insects Fund. Takes effect July 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Agriculture; Secretary of Agriculture
qa_results.stakeholders: counties and municipalities affected by nuisance insects, private and local property owners, and residents and visitors in treated areas
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No direct effect on State or local finances. The Maryland Department of Agriculture can continue operating the existing nuisance insects program using budgeted funding ($687,500 in fiscal 2025). Local government matching fund contributions remain voluntary.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Secretary of Agriculture to implement the nuisance insects control program using Bti and to carry out specific projects when local cost-share requirements are met.
The bill explicitly directs that local cost-share payments received from counties or municipalities be remitted to the Comptroller for deposit into the Nuisance Insects Fund.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires health insurance carriers to establish an online prior authorization process linked to electronic health records by July 1, 2026. Mandates carriers honor prior authorizations granted by previous entities for the lesser of 90 days or the course of treatment. Prohibits adverse reauthorization decisions for certain continuous treatments, including qualifying mental disorder medications and human immune globulins. Establishes strict decision timelines for private review agents and deems requests approved if agents miss deadlines. Requires detailed written notices with specific clinical rationale and dedicated phone numbers for adverse decisions and grievance determinations. Directs the Maryland Health Care Commission and Maryland Insurance Administration to study practitioner-specific prior authorization reforms.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration; Maryland Health Care Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: health insurance carriers, private review agents, pharmacy benefits managers, health care providers, and insured patients
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures increase by $1.75 million in FY 2025 and $3.5 million annually thereafter if the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program complies with the requirements. Minimal increase in Maryland Insurance Administration special fund revenues from rate and form filing fees. Indeterminate increase in health care expenditures for local governments purchasing fully insured plans.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MIA is a primary regulator responsible for enforcing health insurance carrier and private review agent compliance with the bill's utilization review, prior authorization, reporting, and grievance requirements, as well as co-authoring a mandated study on prior authorization modification standards.

MHCC is statutorily mandated to establish regulations for health care provider waivers, jointly conduct a study on prior authorization standards with MIA, and monitor and report on the implementation of electronic prior authorization and real-time benefit requirements.

DBM administers the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program, which experiences a notable fiscal impact of $1.75 million in FY 2025 and $3.5 million annually thereafter to comply with the bill's prior authorization requirements.

The Health Education and Advocacy Unit (HEAU) within the OAG is specifically designated in the bill to receive carrier grievance processes, assist consumers with grievance and complaint filings, and publish an annual evaluation report.
MDH administratively houses the Maryland Health Care Commission and serves as a consultative body to the Insurance Commissioner regarding utilization review standards.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes a 25-cent monthly fee for switched local exchange access service, commercial mobile radio service, or other 9-8-8-accessible service. Exempts subscribers who are enrolled in the federal Lifeline program from paying the fee. Establishes a 25-cent prepaid wireless fee on retail transactions effective July 1, 2027. Requires telephone companies, service carriers, and sellers to collect and remit the fees to the Comptroller. Requires the Comptroller to deposit remitted fee revenues into the 9-8-8 Trust Fund after retaining administrative costs.
qa_results.responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland; Maryland Department of Health; Public Service Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Subscribers to telephone and commercial mobile radio services; consumers and retail sellers of prepaid wireless telecommunications services; telephone companies and commercial mobile radio service providers; individuals receiving behavioral health crisis response services
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: In FY 2025, special fund revenues for the 9-8-8 Trust Fund increase by $20.75 million, and general fund revenues increase by $1.32 million from retained fee revenue. General fund administrative expenditures for the Comptroller increase by $1.32 million in FY 2025 for staffing and system programming. State and local government expenditures increase minimally to pay fees on government communications accounts.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDH administers the 9-8-8 Trust Fund, utilizes the fund revenues to support the continuum of statewide behavioral health crisis response services, and is required to submit an annual report on fee collections and distributions.

The Comptroller is responsible for receiving and accounting for the remitted 9-8-8 monthly fees and prepaid wireless fees, adopting regulations and audit procedures, and managing an administrative cost account funded by a percentage of fee collections.

The bill explicitly mandates the Public Service Commission to direct telephone companies under its jurisdiction to assess and add the 9-8-8 fee to monthly customer bills for switched local exchange access service.
The State Treasurer is statutorily required to hold the 9-8-8 Trust Fund separately and invest its money in the same manner as other State funds.
The statute specifies that the 9-8-8 Trust Fund remains subject to periodic fiscal compliance audits conducted by the Office of Legislative Audits.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the circumstances under which individuals may perform X-ray duties without a license. Limits unlicensed X-ray procedures to the chest, spine, and lower and upper extremities under specified supervision. Requires unlicensed individuals to complete clinical experience, didactic coursework, clinical training, an examination, and board registration. Obligates employing physician offices to ensure all statutory requirements are satisfied for every performed examination. Authorizes the State Board of Physicians to assess civil penalties for unauthorized X-ray performance. Terminates the act on December 31, 2030, following a required board report by October 1, 2029.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Physicians
qa_results.stakeholders: unlicensed individuals performing X-ray duties, licensed physicians, certified radiologic technologists, and physician practices
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures and revenues are not materially affected, as the State Board of Physicians can implement the bill with existing budgeted resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the Maryland Board of Physicians, an entity operating within the Maryland Department of Health. The Board is responsible for adopting regulations governing unlicensed individuals performing X-ray duties, maintaining registrations, enforcing compliance through civil penalties, and submitting a report to the General Assembly on the implementation of these provisions.
