qa_results.bill_summary: Transfers deficiency reporting duties for contractor-operated State-owned nursing homes from the contractor to the oversight department. Requires the department to notify the Governor, specified legislators, and county governing bodies within 15 days of final survey findings. Requires the department to provide deficiency statements, correction plans or dispute results, and survey communications within 30 days. Triggers this 30-day submission upon plan acceptance or completion of informal dispute resolution. Expands monitoring agencies to include the Maryland Department of Labor and local health departments. Adds the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs and the federal Occupational Safety and Health Administration as monitoring agencies.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Veterans Affairs; Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Contractors operating State-owned nursing homes, residents and families of State-owned nursing home residents, and local governing bodies of counties containing State-owned nursing homes
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State requirements can be handled with existing budgeted resources. State revenues are not affected, and local finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Veterans and Military Families oversees the Charlotte Hall Veterans Home, which is the only State-owned nursing home operated by a contractor in Maryland. The bill directly places the legal duty on the department charged with oversight to issue notices and reports regarding deficiencies, enforcement actions, and plans of correction.

The Maryland Department of Health encompasses the Office of Health Care Quality, which surveys and monitors nursing homes, and the Department is statutorily required under the bill to compile and submit an annual report to the Governor and General Assembly on survey activities and enforcement actions.

The bill explicitly amends the law to include the Maryland Department of Labor as a designated 'monitoring agency,' meaning its findings, deficiencies, or enforcement actions regarding occupational safety directly trigger reporting mandates under the statute.
The Governor is a statutory recipient of the required notices of deficiencies, statements of findings, plans of correction, and the annual oversight report on State-owned nursing homes.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals the requirement that teacher preparation programs require passing a portfolio-based assessment for graduation beginning July 1, 2025. Alters initial teacher certification qualifications by creating alternative pathways through local teacher induction programs. Permits candidates to fulfill certification criteria with a 3.0 grade point average or three years of effective evaluations. Authorizes local school systems to establish comprehensive induction programs independently or collaboratively. Requires the State Superintendent of Schools to pursue reciprocal educator certification agreements with other states.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education; State Superintendent of Schools; State Board of Education; Accountability and Implementation Board
qa_results.stakeholders: Teacher candidates, public school teachers, out-of-state licensed teachers, teacher preparation programs, and local school systems
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on State higher education finances. The Maryland State Department of Education and the Accountability and Implementation Board can receive induction plans with existing resources, though reviewing plans may require additional personnel. Local school system expenditures likely increase to implement comprehensive teacher induction programs.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MSDE is the primary agency responsible for teacher certification and public school standards in Maryland. The bill directly alters initial teacher certification requirements, removes certain graduation testing mandates, tasks MSDE with developing/approving literacy and subject-specific examinations, requires receipt and review of local induction programs, and directs the State Superintendent to establish interstate reciprocity agreements.

USM institutions operate public teacher preparation programs that are directly impacted by the repeal of the portfolio-based assessment as a graduation requirement and the altered coursework and credentialing pathways for teacher candidates.
MHEC coordinates statewide postsecondary education policy and oversees teacher preparation academic programs in Maryland that must adjust their curriculum and graduation standards under the bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits firearm industry members from knowingly creating, maintaining, or contributing to public harm through unlawful or unreasonable conduct. Requires firearm industry members to establish and implement reasonable controls regarding firearm-related products. Establishes that a violation of these statutory requirements constitutes a public nuisance. Authorizes the Attorney General, county attorneys, and the Baltimore City Solicitor to bring civil enforcement actions. Allows authorized officials to seek injunctive relief, restitution, compensatory and punitive damages, and attorney's fees. Directs the Attorney General to study compelling licensed dealers to submit federal firearm trace records by June 30, 2025.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General; Department of State Police
qa_results.stakeholders: Firearm industry members, including manufacturers, distributors, importers, and retailers of firearm-related products; local governments; the public
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Potential increase in State general fund expenditures and local expenditures if civil actions are pursued against firearm industry members. Potential increase in State general fund revenues and local revenues to the extent damages, restitution, or legal fees are awarded. Specific figures are indeterminate.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly authorizes the Attorney General to initiate civil actions against firearm industry members for public nuisance, seek damages and injunctive relief, and requires the Attorney General to lead a study and submit recommendations to the General Assembly regarding firearm trace requests.

The Maryland State Police is the primary regulator of firearms and regulated firearms dealers in Maryland, and the bill explicitly requires the Attorney General to consult with the Department of State Police in conducting a study on requiring licensed dealers to report federal firearm trace requests.
The bill establishes a new statutory civil cause of action for public nuisance subject to adjudication, injunctive relief, and damages within the Maryland court system.

qa_results.bill_summary: Mandates an annual budget appropriation of at least $80,533,314 for the Locally Operated Transit System Grant Program. Requires the Governor to fund this appropriation through the Transportation Trust Fund. Applies the funding requirement starting in fiscal year 2026 and each fiscal year thereafter. Designates the mandated appropriation specifically for statewide program operations.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Transportation; Maryland Transit Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Locally operated transit systems, local governments in Maryland, and public transit passengers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on Transportation Trust Fund expenditures or local government finances is anticipated because funding for the Locally Operated Transit System Grant Program generally exceeds the mandated minimum appropriation level.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates funding for the Locally Operated Transit System (LOTS) Grant Program, which is directly administered by the Maryland Transit Administration to provide funding and technical assistance to local transit systems across Maryland.

The mandated appropriation is funded through the Transportation Trust Fund (TTF), directly impacting the Maryland Department of Transportation's budget flexibility and overall transportation funding allocations.
The bill places a statutory mandate on the Governor to include at least $80,533,314 from the Transportation Trust Fund in the annual budget bill beginning in fiscal year 2026.
DBM develops the annual state budget on behalf of the Governor and must incorporate this mandated annual appropriation into future executive budget plans.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the amount of funds the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange may designate under the State-Based Young Adult Health Insurance Subsidies Pilot Program. Authorizes the Exchange to designate up to $20,000,000 for subsidies in each of calendar years 2024 and 2025. Permits the Exchange to add unspent subsidy funds designated in previous calendar years to those annual amounts. Applies to subsidies provided to young adults who meet established eligibility and payment parameters.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Health Benefit Exchange
qa_results.stakeholders: Young adults between ages 18 and 40 purchasing health insurance through the Maryland Health Connection who qualify for pilot program premium subsidies
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund expenditures by the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange may increase in fiscal 2025 and 2026 as up to $12.9 million in unspent funds from calendar 2022 and 2023 are used for subsidies. There is no net increase in overall program expenditures beyond initial allocations, and state revenues are unaffected. Local governments experience no fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Health Benefit Exchange is the primary implementing agency of the State-Based Young Adult Health Insurance Subsidies Pilot Program. The bill directly alters the statutory cap on the amount of funding the Exchange may designate for annual young adult subsidies for calendar years 2024 and 2025 by allowing the rollover and use of unspent funds from prior years.

Under the underlying statute amended by the bill (Section 31-122 of the Insurance Article), the Exchange is required to establish subsidy eligibility and payment parameters for the pilot program in consultation with the Maryland Insurance Commissioner, who heads the Maryland Insurance Administration.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the continuing education renewal requirement for certified dialysis technicians. Requires certificate holders to complete three hours of Board-approved continuing education rather than a single three-hour course. Preserves requirements for active national certification and 16 practice hours in the preceding two-year period. Takes effect June 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Board of Nursing
qa_results.stakeholders: Certified dialysis technicians in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on State or local finances, as the change is technical in nature.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters the continuing education renewal requirements for certified dialysis technicians under the Maryland Board of Nursing (MBON), which operates under the Maryland Department of Health.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals provisions requiring a District Court judge to assign certain offenders to public road work in Frederick. Removes the mandate affecting vagrants and individuals who violate municipal laws or ordinances in the City of Frederick. Eliminates requirements that the Sheriff or local road supervisors oversee and guard offenders during road work. Takes effect October 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: District Court of Maryland; Frederick County Sheriff
qa_results.stakeholders: individuals convicted of vagrancy or municipal ordinance violations in the City of Frederick, the Frederick County Sheriff's Office, and the City of Frederick
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not have a material impact on State government operations or finances, nor on the operations or finances of the City of Frederick or Frederick County.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill repeals an archaic statutory provision requiring District Court judges trying municipal ordinance violations in the City of Frederick to assign offenders to work on local public roads.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill repeals a section under the Correctional Services Article concerning the assignment and guarding of committed offenders.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases the Small Business Reserve Program procurement goal from 15% to 20% for State procurement units. Authorizes units to count awards under designated and nondesignated contracts toward their overall achievement. Requires the certification agency and the Governor's Office of Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs to develop an outreach program. Focuses the outreach program on small businesses owned by economically disadvantaged individuals. Mandates annual reporting by the certification agency on outreach status and contract awards. Alters agency procurement reports to require data on contract awards instead of payments.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Transportation; Governor's Office of Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs
qa_results.stakeholders: Small businesses, certified minority business enterprises, and small businesses owned by economically disadvantaged individuals seeking Maryland State procurement contracts
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Potential minimal increase in State expenditures to the extent that expanded small business set-asides limit contract competition. The Maryland Department of Transportation can administer the outreach program and reporting requirements with existing resources. There is no effect on State revenues or local finances.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOSBA oversees the Small Business Reserve (SBR) Program, receives procurement reports from state units, consults with the certification agency to develop the new outreach program, and submits annual summary reports to the Board of Public Works and the General Assembly.

As the State's designated MBE/DBE certification agency, MDOT is required to develop an outreach program in consultation with GOSBA to increase participation of small businesses owned by economically disadvantaged individuals in the SBR program, and report annually on its status to BPW and the General Assembly.

The Board of Public Works receives annual statutory reports from both the certification agency regarding the outreach program and awards, and from GOSBA regarding statewide SBR procurement performance.
The Office of the Attorney General must be consulted every five years by the Special Secretary for GOSBA to establish standards and guidelines for participation in the SBR Program.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System to temporarily suspend allowances for certain retirees. Applies to Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System retirees elected as sheriff less than one year after retirement. Directs the Board to reinstate the allowance with accumulated cost-of-living adjustments when sheriff service ends. Protects survivorship benefits for eligible spouses, children, or designated beneficiaries if the retiree dies during sheriff service. Applies prospectively only to individuals who retire on or after July 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System; State Retirement Agency
qa_results.stakeholders: Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System retirees elected as sheriffs within one year of retirement and their surviving beneficiaries
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No discernible effect on State or local pension liabilities, contribution rates, or revenues due to the limited number of applicable cases.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 966 directly tasks the Board of Trustees of the State Retirement and Pension System and the Maryland State Retirement Agency with administering the suspension and reinstatement of retirement benefits for LEOPS retirees elected as sheriffs within one year of retirement, as well as managing employer reporting procedures.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits parking certain commercial and large vehicles on any street or highway in the Town of Keedysville. Applies the parking ban to specified trucks, tractors, trailers, school buses, and passenger buses. Exempts vehicles when parking is essential to their immediate use. Excludes passenger vehicles and qualifying light trucks from the parking restriction. Treats each day of violation as a separate offense and imposes separate fines for combination vehicles.
qa_results.responsible_party: Town of Keedysville
qa_results.stakeholders: Owners and operators of commercial trucks, tractors, trailers, school buses, and passenger buses in the Town of Keedysville
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on State or local government finances or operations. Local enforcement can be handled with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Maryland Transportation Article governing vehicle parking restrictions on streets and highways according to state vehicle registration classes.
Contested citations and penalties for violations of Maryland Vehicle Law parking provisions fall under the jurisdiction of the state court system administered by the AOC.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires medical examiners to notify prosecutors and law enforcement when a death certificate is amended to undetermined or homicide. Requires medical examiners to request a free amended certified death certificate for a person in interest. Directs law enforcement agencies to reopen or reinvestigate these deaths upon notification. Prohibits law enforcement agencies from closing a reopened investigation for at least 20 years. Requires an assistant State's Attorney to meet with a person in interest within 20 days of request.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Office of the Chief Medical Examiner; State's Attorneys' Offices; local law enforcement agencies
qa_results.stakeholders: Persons in interest of deceased individuals whose death certificate cause or manner is amended to undetermined or homicide, local law enforcement agencies, and State's Attorneys
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local expenditures can be absorbed with existing budgeted resources due to the small number of eligible death certificate amendments. Revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 969 directly impacts the Maryland Department of Health (MDH) and the Office of the Chief Medical Examiner (OCME). It requires the medical examiner to notify the State's Attorney and local law enforcement when a cause or manner of death is amended to undetermined or homicide, and requires the Secretary of Health to issue an amended certified death certificate to a person in interest at no cost.

As a principal statewide law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police is subject to the bill's requirement under Public Safety § 3-531 to reopen or reinvestigate death investigations if notified by a medical examiner of a reclassification to undetermined or homicide, and is prohibited from closing such a case for at least 20 years.

OAH conducts the contested case hearings when a person in interest appeals a medical examiner's denial to change findings on a death certificate under Health - General § 5-309(d). While the bill does not change OAH's hearing procedures, the administrative law judge's findings can lead directly to the reclassifications and subsequent notification mandates established by the bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Washington County Board of Education to waive enrollment eligibility requirements for high school interscholastic athletics. Applies when a student attends a non-zoned county public school that lacks an interscholastic athletics program. Requires students to satisfy all other county board and Maryland Public Secondary Schools Athletic Association eligibility standards. Permits participating students to compete in interscholastic athletics only at their zoned high school. Requires the local superintendent of schools to include authorized participating students in biennial member school enrollment classification reports.
qa_results.responsible_party: Washington County Board of Education; Washington County Superintendent of Schools
qa_results.stakeholders: Washington County public high school students attending non-zoned public schools without athletic programs; Washington County public high schools
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on State operations or finances. Local finances are not materially affected because the waiver authority is discretionary for the Washington County Board of Education.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill impacts State regulations (COMAR 13A.06.03) governing high school interscholastic athletics and classifications under the Maryland Public Secondary Schools Athletic Association (MPSSAA), which falls under the regulatory oversight of the Maryland State Department of Education.

qa_results.bill_summary: Excludes unsolicited positive community feedback regarding a police officer from the definition of personnel records under public information law. Requires the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission to develop a simple, uniform positive community feedback process. Directs each law enforcement agency to adopt the uniform process and post it online if the agency maintains a website. Mandates that law enforcement agencies maintain positive community feedback records for all officers in the agency. Establishes that these feedback records are subject to public inspection under the Maryland Public Information Act.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Law enforcement officers, state and local law enforcement agencies, and members of the public submitting or inspecting positive community feedback
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local finances are not materially affected. The Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission and law enforcement agencies can implement the uniform process, update websites, and manage public records requests using existing resources.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission (MPTSC) is housed within DPSCS and is the primary entity mandated by the bill to develop the uniform citizen positive community feedback process for all law enforcement agencies.

As the primary statewide law enforcement agency, MSP is directly required to adopt the uniform feedback process, post it on its website, maintain feedback records for all law enforcement officers, and manage public inspection under the Public Information Act.

DNR operates the Maryland Natural Resources Police, a statewide law enforcement entity required to implement the uniform feedback process, post it online, and maintain records of positive community feedback.
MDTA maintains a dedicated, accredited police force that must adopt the MPTSC uniform citizen feedback process, publish it online, and maintain accessible records for its officers.
MDOT oversees modal administrations with sworn law enforcement units (including MTA Police and MDTA Police) that must comply with the feedback posting and recordkeeping requirements.
DGS oversees the Maryland Capitol Police, a law enforcement force that is required to adopt the feedback process and maintain feedback records subject to public inspection.
OAG provides legal guidance on state statutory compliance, including the bill's amendments to the Maryland Public Information Act regarding the public inspection of police records.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the County Commissioners of Somerset County to enact local laws regulating fire, rescue, and emergency medical services. Authorizes the commissioners to create or authorize an entity to administer county emergency services while maintaining volunteer emergency services. Requires the commissioners to establish an Emergency Services Advisory Council if such an entity is authorized or created. Directs the council to provide recommendations regarding fire suppression, emergency medical, and hazardous materials services operations. Takes effect October 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: County Commissioners of Somerset County
qa_results.stakeholders: volunteer fire companies, rescue squads, emergency medical services personnel, and residents in Somerset County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state fiscal effect. The bill does not materially affect Somerset County operations or finances.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MIEMSS oversees and regulates the statewide emergency medical services (EMS) network. While this bill grants local governance and regulatory authority over EMS and rescue services specifically to the Somerset County Commissioners, it operates within the broader context of prehospital and emergency medical services regulated statewide by MIEMSS.

MDEM coordinates statewide emergency preparedness, response, and resilience efforts, and supports local emergency management jurisdictions. The restructuring and advisory bodies for emergency services in Somerset County relate to local emergency coordination, though the bill has no direct fiscal or operational mandates for MDEM.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases annual county appropriations to organized volunteer fire companies in Somerset County. Requires the County Commissioners of Somerset County to appropriate specified amounts for fiscal years 2025 through 2030. Provides annual appropriation increases for eight designated volunteer fire companies across the county. Maintains the required fiscal year 2030 appropriation levels for subsequent fiscal years unless altered by future enactment.
qa_results.responsible_party: County Commissioners of Somerset County
qa_results.stakeholders: organized volunteer fire companies in Somerset County and Somerset County taxpayers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Somerset County expenditures increase by $7,317 in fiscal 2025, rising annually to $46,154 in fiscal 2030 and subsequent years to fund eight volunteer fire companies. State finances and county revenues are unaffected.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the County Commissioners of Somerset County to sell county property located on Revells Neck Road. Identifies the real property as County Tax Map 32, Parcel 149. Permits the commissioners to execute the sale under terms they consider appropriate. Exempts the transaction from standard county surplus property public advertising and competitive bidding requirements.
qa_results.responsible_party: County Commissioners of Somerset County
qa_results.stakeholders: Somerset County government and prospective purchasers of county property on Revells Neck Road
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state fiscal effect. The bill will not materially affect the operations or finances of Somerset County.

qa_results.bill_summary: Replaces Maryland's two-tiered invasive plant regulatory framework with a single prohibited invasive plant classification and a watch list. Requires the Secretary of Agriculture to adopt assessment protocols and prohibited plant lists by October 1, 2024. Prohibits propagating, importing, transferring, selling, purchasing, transporting, or introducing any living part of a prohibited invasive plant without approval. Requires terrestrial plants previously classified as Tier 2 plants to be assessed by December 31, 2025. Authorizes the State Highway Administration to control or dispose of prohibited invasive plants along State highways without prior approval.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Agriculture; Invasive Plants Advisory Committee; Department of Natural Resources; State Highway Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Commercial and noncommercial plant growers, licensed nurseries, plant dealers, plant brokers, landscaping services, and State and local land management agencies
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Indeterminate expenditure increases across multiple state and local funds beginning in fiscal 2025 for plant removal, disposal, and alternative plantings on public lands. The State Highway Administration specifically estimates an expenditure increase of approximately $30,000 annually from the Transportation Trust Fund. The Maryland Department of Agriculture's operational workload is supported by $196,626 and three positions already included in the fiscal 2025 budget.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Agriculture is the primary implementing agency for the bill. The Secretary of Agriculture is tasked with establishing assessment protocols, adopting regulations, maintaining the Consolidated List of Maryland Invasive Plant Species and watch lists, overseeing the Invasive Plants Advisory Committee, and enforcing restrictions and plant destruction orders.

The bill requires the Secretary of Agriculture to consult with the Secretary of Natural Resources regarding assessment protocols and assessor qualifications. Additionally, DNR personnel may serve as expert assessors, and DNR is statutorily required to publish the Consolidated List and watch list on its website.

The bill grants the State Highway Administration statutory authorization to control and dispose of prohibited invasive plants along state highways without prior approval from the Secretary of Agriculture, subject to MDA regulations. The fiscal note also estimates an increase in Transportation Trust Fund expenditures of approximately $30,000 annually for SHA invasive plant removal operations.

MDOT is the parent department of the State Highway Administration and manages the Transportation Trust Fund, which will fund SHA's increased operational expenditures for invasive plant removal along state highway corridors.

The bill mandates that the University of Maryland Extension, an institution within the University System of Maryland, post a link to the Consolidated List of Maryland Invasive Plant Species and the watch list on its website.

The bill provides that when the Secretary of Agriculture destroys a prohibited invasive plant and incurs expenses, the statements of expense are submitted to the Attorney General, who is mandated to institute proceedings to collect those expenses.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Secretary of Health to present Opioid Restitution Fund allocation decisions to the Opioid Restitution Fund Advisory Council. Mandates that the Maryland Department of Health publish the Council's recommendations and fund allocation decisions online within one week. Expands permitted Fund uses to include supporting community-based nonprofit recovery organizations providing nonclinical substance use recovery support services. Updates Council membership and staffing to reflect the Special Secretary and Maryland's Office of Overdose Response. Directs the Department to report by December 1, 2024, on making public all opioid settlement expenditures.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Opioid Restitution Fund Advisory Council; Maryland's Office of Overdose Response
qa_results.stakeholders: community-based nonprofit recovery organizations providing nonclinical substance use recovery support services, individuals with substance use disorders, and local health departments
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State Opioid Restitution Fund revenues and expenditures are not materially affected, though permitted uses of the Fund are expanded. The Maryland Department of Health can implement the bill with existing budgeted resources. Local government revenues and expenditures may increase to the extent local health departments qualify as community-based recovery organizations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the Secretary of Health and the Maryland Department of Health with presenting allocation decisions from the Opioid Restitution Fund, posting findings and decisions to the department's website, and reporting on public transparency for opioid settlement expenditures.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill updates the composition and procedural responsibilities of the Opioid Restitution Fund Advisory Council, modifying its membership and requiring the Secretary of Health to formally present allocation decisions to the council.

The Opioid Restitution Fund Advisory Council is statutorily required to provide its annual findings and recommendations regarding fund allocations directly to the Governor to inform state budget decisions.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires each Executive Branch principal department to provide equal access to public services for individuals with limited English proficiency. Sets a full implementation deadline of July 1, 2025, for listed principal departments. Requires any principal department created on or after October 1, 2024, to comply within one year of creation. Mandates in-house oral language services when contact with limited English proficient individuals occurs weekly or more frequently. Requires translating vital documents into languages spoken by any eligible population constituting at least 3% of the served area.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Budget and Management; Maryland Department of Disabilities; Maryland Department of Emergency Management; Department of General Services; Department of Information Technology; Maryland Department of Planning; Department of Service and Civic Innovation
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals with limited English proficiency in Maryland; Maryland Executive Branch principal departments
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by approximately $100,000 in FY 2025 and $200,000 annually thereafter, primarily for expanded translation services in the Maryland Department of Emergency Management. Local finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As a principal department not previously included in the statutory LEP implementation schedule, MDEM must fully implement equal access requirements by July 1, 2025. It faces a direct fiscal impact of approximately $100,000 in FY 2025 and $200,000 annually thereafter to provide continuous 24/7 translation and interpretation services in languages such as Chinese and Korean.

The bill originally targeted the Department of Disabilities specifically and requires it, along with other unlisted principal departments, to achieve full compliance with LEP equal access mandates by July 1, 2025, necessitating expanded interpretation and document translation services.

As a principal department newly required to comply with the LEP implementation schedule by July 1, 2025, MDP must provide vital document translation and update public-facing materials and website content.
As a principal department established under § 8-201, DBM is directly required by the bill to fully implement the LEP equal access statutory requirements by July 1, 2025.

As an executive principal department not covered under the original statutory phase-in schedule, DGS is mandated to fully implement LEP equal access requirements for its public-facing services and facilities by July 1, 2025.

DoIT is a principal department required by the bill to achieve full compliance with LEP equal access provisions by July 1, 2025, potentially involving public digital services and IT-accessible translation resources.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Service and Civic Innovation
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Created in 2023 as a principal executive department, DSCI is required to comply with the statutory LEP access requirements by July 1, 2025, to ensure equal access to its civic engagement and service program offerings.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands pay rate requirements for Maryland Department of Health employees who have direct contact with patients. Adds Bargaining Unit G engineering, scientific, and administrative professionals classified as teachers or librarians. Applies the pay parity provisions to qualifying employees at the Regional Institutes for Children and Adolescents in Baltimore and Rockville. Requires eligible employee pay rates to equal two grades higher than specified rates at Clifton T. Perkins Hospital. Prohibits any provision from being construed to decrease the pay rate of any employee.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland Department of Health employees with direct patient contact in Bargaining Unit G classified as teachers or librarians, and employees at the Regional Institutes for Children and Adolescents in Baltimore and Rockville
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by at least $87,900 and reimbursable fund expenditures increase by at least $13,600 in FY 2025 to provide salary increases for nine eligible employees. Out-year expenditures reflect annual salary increases. Local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates pay rate adjustments for certain employees within the Maryland Department of Health who work at Clifton T. Perkins Hospital and other designated facilities, resulting in a direct fiscal expenditure increase.
As the State's central personnel and budget agency, DBM oversees state classification, salary scales, employee benefits, and budget execution required to implement the mandated pay grade increases.

The bill alters statutory compensation requirements that apply directly to state employees categorized by specific collective bargaining units (including Bargaining Units D, E, F, G, and H), falling within the scope of state labor relations and collective bargaining administration.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Health to study comprehensive obesity treatment coverage under the Maryland Medical Assistance Program. Defines comprehensive coverage to include intensive behavioral therapy, bariatric surgery, and FDA-approved antiobesity medication. Directs the Department to compare obesity coverage across medical assistance and other public health programs in other states. Requires the Department to examine and estimate potential savings resulting from requiring comprehensive coverage. Mandates reporting findings to specified legislative committees on or before December 31, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland Medical Assistance Program recipients with obesity
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures increase by $250,000 in FY 2025 (50% general funds and 50% federal funds) for actuarial analysis to support the required study. Federal fund revenues increase by $125,000 accordingly. There is no effect on local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health administers the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid) and is directly mandated to conduct the study on the impact of providing comprehensive coverage for the treatment of obesity, submit the final report to legislative committees, and expend $250,000 in FY 2025 for required actuarial analysis.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Montgomery County Planning Board or its designee to tentatively approve a subdivision plat subject to specified conditions. Prohibits entering the tentative approval on the plat or allowing the plat to be filed or recorded. Prohibits the board from endorsing a conditional subdivision plat before all specified conditions are completed. Removes the requirement for a postcompletion hearing before the board once all specified conditions are completed. Applies these provisions exclusively to subdivision plats in Montgomery County.
qa_results.responsible_party: Montgomery County Planning Board
qa_results.stakeholders: property owners and real estate developers seeking subdivision plat approvals in Montgomery County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No direct effect on State finances and no material effect on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Planning provides policy guidance and oversight on land use and growth planning across the state. While the bill specifically alters subdivision plat approval procedures for Montgomery County, it amends state land use statutes relevant to the department's area of policy focus.

Subdivision plats are ultimately submitted and recorded in county land records maintained by the Clerks of the Circuit Courts, which are supported and administered by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

qa_results.bill_summary: Excludes cement production from the statutory definition of manufacturing under the Greenhouse Gas Emissions Reduction Act. Requires the Department of the Environment to consider specified economic factors and consult stakeholders before regulating cement production. Limits certain greenhouse gas emissions protections exclusively to persons who engaged in manufacturing in 2023. Prohibits state regulations from requiring 2023 manufacturers to reduce emissions below their 2023 levels. Prohibits regulations from significantly increasing costs beyond 2023 levels for those covered manufacturers. Prohibits requiring manufacturers of renewable energy components or emissions reduction technology to reduce greenhouse gas emissions.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment
qa_results.stakeholders: Cement producers, manufacturing businesses operating in Maryland, manufacturers of renewable energy components or emissions reduction technologies, and state and local capital construction projects
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Department of the Environment can implement the bill using existing budgeted resources. State and local governments may experience increased costs for cement on capital construction projects, but total State capital budget spending is unaffected. Revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) is the primary regulatory and implementing agency for the Greenhouse Gas Emissions Reduction Act. The bill specifically tasks MDE with adopting regulations and policies concerning greenhouse gas emissions reductions for manufacturers, specifically excluding cement production from manufacturing definitions, consulting with cement industry stakeholders, and considering technical and financial feasibility factors for cement emissions regulations.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes a food processing residuals utilization permit program administered by the Maryland Department of Agriculture. Prohibits any person from utilizing food processing residuals in the State without obtaining a permit for each site. Requires agricultural operations utilizing residuals to maintain and comply with an approved nutrient management plan. Establishes the Food Processing Residuals Administration Fund supported by regulatory fees set to approximate departmental costs. Authorizes the Department to inspect sites, issue stop work orders, and impose administrative penalties up to $50,000. Authorizes the Department to administer a Commercial Hauler Certification Program for individuals hauling food processing residuals.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Agriculture
qa_results.stakeholders: owners and operators of agricultural operations, commercial brokers, commercial haulers, and food processing plants
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues and expenditures increase correspondingly by $481,700 in fiscal 2025 to administer the regulatory program, with future costs covered by fee collections. General fund revenues increase minimally from fund interest earnings and any administrative penalties assessed. Local government finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDA is the primary implementing agency tasked with establishing and administering the food processing residuals utilization permit program, enforcing compliance, conducting site inspections, setting and collecting fees, administering the new Food Processing Residuals Administration Fund, and optionally creating a Commercial Hauler Certification Program.

MDE is required to be consulted by MDA in the adoption of regulations governing food processing residuals utilization and commercial hauler certification, and permit eligibility is conditioned on compliance with MDE-administered discharge permits.
The bill statutorily requires MDA to pay all fees collected under the subtitle to the Comptroller, who must distribute them into the newly established Food Processing Residuals Administration Fund.
The OAG is impacted as MDA requires one Assistant Attorney General position to assist with legal review of permits, enforcement actions, and injunction proceedings under the subtitle.
The statute explicitly subjects the accounts and transactions of the newly created Food Processing Residuals Administration Fund to audit by OLA pursuant to § 2-1220 of the State Government Article.
The Treasurer is responsible for holding, managing, and investing the monies of the newly created special nonlapsing Food Processing Residuals Administration Fund.
Permit suspensions, revocations, and modifications must be conducted in accordance with the Administrative Procedure Act, which may result in contested case hearings before OAH.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires delegated local health departments and county governments to submit permit review schedules to the Department of the Environment. Sets a deadline of December 1, 2024, for submitting the review schedule for departmental approval. Covers permits for installing on-site sewage disposal systems and constructing wells. Mandates quarterly submission of well and septic permit data to the department for review. Begins data reporting three months after the department approves the review schedule.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment; local health departments; county governments
qa_results.stakeholders: Local health departments and county governments administering well and septic programs, as well as permit applicants for wells and on-site sewage disposal systems.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local governments can handle the reporting and review requirements with existing budgeted resources. There is no direct effect on state or local revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the Maryland Department of the Environment with reviewing and approving schedules of review times for well and septic program permits submitted by delegated authorities, as well as receiving and reviewing permit data on a quarterly basis.

The Maryland Department of Health oversees local health departments across the state, which frequently serve as the delegated authorities responsible for administering well and septic permits and complying with the bill's reporting and scheduling mandates.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes residency requirements for members of the Washington County Board of Education. Requires each member to reside in Maryland for at least 12 months immediately preceding taking office. Requires each member to reside in Washington County for at least 6 months immediately preceding taking office. Requires members to maintain a primary residence in Washington County throughout their term. Prohibits any member who fails to maintain a primary residence in the county from continuing to serve. Takes effect July 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Washington County Board of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: candidates for and members of the Washington County Board of Education
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal effect; the bill is procedural in nature and does not affect Washington County finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Education Article regarding the qualifications, residency, and tenure of Washington County Board of Education members. The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) and the State Board of Education oversee public school systems and retain statutory authority over the removal of local board members.

Members of the Washington County Board of Education are elected at-large in general elections, and the State Board of Elections oversees candidate qualification and election administration across Maryland jurisdictions.

qa_results.bill_summary: Renames the Consumer Council in the Division of Consumer Protection to the Consumer Protection Commission. Authorizes Commission members to receive per diem compensation in accordance with the State budget. Maintains member reimbursement for all expenses reasonably incurred. Requires the Division of Consumer Protection to obtain Commission advice before adopting consumer protection rules and standards. Takes effect October 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Division of Consumer Protection in the Office of the Attorney General
qa_results.stakeholders: Members of the Consumer Protection Commission (formerly the Consumer Council), consumer groups, business groups, and Maryland consumers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances and operations are not materially affected. There is no local government or small business impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the statutory provisions governing the Division of Consumer Protection within the Office of the Attorney General, renaming its advisory body from the Consumer Council to the Consumer Protection Commission.
The Governor is responsible for appointing the nine members of the Consumer Protection Commission across the three designated categories with the advice and consent of the Senate.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and processing gubernatorial appointments for members serving on state boards and commissions, including the Consumer Protection Commission.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill modifies the governing statute and formal name of the Consumer Protection Commission (formerly Consumer Council), which operates as an advisory board within the executive branch.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Labor to study unemployment insurance actively seeking work requirements in Maryland and other states. Directs the department to evaluate the effects of job applicant ghosting on actively seeking work requirements. Requires the study to assess whether the department can periodically verify claimant work search information using existing resources. Tasks the department with evaluating the BEACON system regarding employer reporting of job contacts and ghosting incidents. Requires the department to report its findings and recommendations to the General Assembly by December 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor
qa_results.stakeholders: claimants for unemployment insurance benefits and employers in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are unaffected as the Maryland Department of Labor can complete the required study using existing budgeted resources. Revenues and local government finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 998 directly mandates the Maryland Department of Labor to conduct a study on the unemployment insurance system's actively seeking work requirements, evaluate the BEACON system regarding reports of job applicant 'ghosting', and submit a final report to the General Assembly by December 1, 2024.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Workgroup on Establishing a Science and Technology Best Practices and Innovation Network. Requires the University of Maryland, Baltimore County to provide staff for the workgroup. Directs the workgroup to analyze options for creating an open access network or hub of citizen scientists and experts. Charges the workgroup with evaluating methods to establish a virtual referral network and make expertise available to the public. Requires the workgroup to report its findings and recommendations to the Governor and the General Assembly by December 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: University of Maryland, Baltimore County; Workgroup on Establishing a Science and Technology Best Practices and Innovation Network
qa_results.stakeholders: Citizen scientists, academic researchers, higher education institutions, technology industry professionals, and science advocacy nonprofits in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures can be handled using existing budgeted resources. State revenues are not affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Workgroup on Establishing a Science and Technology Best Practices and Innovation Network, a temporary study body tasked with making recommendations regarding an open-access science, technology, and innovation network.

The University of Maryland, Baltimore County (UMBC), a constituent institution of the University System of Maryland, has a designated seat on the Workgroup and is statutorily assigned to provide administrative and operational staffing for the Workgroup.
The Executive Director of the Maryland Technology Development Corporation (TEDCO), or the Executive Director's designee, is designated as a mandatory member of the Workgroup.

The Governor is responsible for appointing 10 members to the Workgroup (five representing community-based applications and five representing institutions of higher education) and will receive the Workgroup's final report and recommendations by December 1, 2024.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and processing the 10 gubernatorial appointments to the newly formed Workgroup.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Attorney General, a Deputy Attorney General, or a designated Assistant Attorney General to issue civil investigative subpoenas. Limits this subpoena authority to furthering ongoing health care fraud investigations under the Maryland False Health Claims Act or other civil authority. Allows subpoenas to require documentary material, written interrogatories answered under oath, sworn oral testimony, or any combination thereof. Authorizes the Attorney General to report failure to obey a subpoena to a circuit court. Permits the court to grant appropriate relief after a hearing where the person may appear with counsel. Prohibits construing these provisions to abrogate any legally recognized privilege or right.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General
qa_results.stakeholders: individuals and entities subject to health care fraud investigations under the Maryland False Health Claims Act or other civil authority
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No meaningful state or local fiscal impact, as the changes in investigative subpoena authority are procedural in nature.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 1002 directly expands the investigative powers of the Office of the Attorney General by authorizing the Attorney General, Deputy Attorney General, or designated Assistant Attorneys General to issue subpoenas, demand written interrogatories, and take sworn testimony to investigate health care fraud under the Maryland False Health Claims Act or other civil authority.
The bill allows the Attorney General to report failures to obey an investigative subpoena to the circuit courts, which must conduct hearings and may grant appropriate relief to compel compliance.

The investigative authority granted under the Maryland False Health Claims Act directly supports the detection, investigation, and recovery of funds involving fraudulent claims against Maryland Department of Health programs, including Medicaid.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes subdivision plats in Montgomery County to be drawn in an electronic version approved by the State Archivist. Allows plats in the county to alternatively follow standard physical archival specifications. Authorizes the Clerk of the Circuit Court for Montgomery County to record or maintain plats in electronic form. Requires electronic plat recordation and maintenance methods to be approved by the State Archivist. Takes effect October 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Clerk of the Circuit Court for Montgomery County; State Archivist
qa_results.stakeholders: Landowners, surveyors, and developers submitting plats in Montgomery County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material fiscal impact on State or local finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires the State Archivist to approve the manner in which subdivision plats in Montgomery County may be drawn, recorded, and maintained in electronic format.

The bill directly impacts the operations of the Clerk of the Circuit Court for Montgomery County by authorizing the clerk to record and maintain plats in electronic format, and the Administrative Office of the Courts oversees and supports Circuit Court operations and recordkeeping systems.

qa_results.bill_summary: Excludes certain compensation adjustments from being considered extraordinary salary increases when calculating average final compensation for pension members. Applies to adjustments addressing position classification inequities or aligning pay with market compensation. Requires retiring members who receive qualifying adjustments to submit an employer-certified form to the State Retirement Agency. Mandates submission of the certified form within 30 days of written notice from the agency. Takes effect July 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Retirement Agency
qa_results.stakeholders: Members of the State Retirement and Pension System receiving position classification pay adjustments near retirement, and participating State and local employers.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Likely no discernible effect on State or local pension liabilities, contribution rates, expenditures, or revenues due to the very small number of affected retirees.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters the calculation of average final compensation (AFC) for members of the State Retirement and Pension System (SRPS) by excluding certain classification and market-based compensation adjustments from being considered extraordinary salary increases. The State Retirement Agency is responsible for administering this policy, issuing written notices, and providing and processing employer certification forms.

As the State's central personnel agency, the Department of Budget and Management oversees statewide position classifications, salary adjustments, and compensation studies to address salary inequities or align with market rates. State employers operating under DBM must complete and certify the required documentation for retiring members receiving these adjustments.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands membership in the Correctional Officers’ Retirement System to include specified employees of two state departments. Adds correctional maintenance regional managers in the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services. Includes direct care staff, health personnel, and security attendants at seven Maryland Department of Health facilities. Requires the State Retirement and Pension System to transfer prior creditable service to the system. Authorizes affected employees with pre-July 1, 2008 service credit to opt out by June 1, 2025. Requires the Board of Trustees to calculate and grant the greater ordinary disability benefit.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System; State Retirement Agency
qa_results.stakeholders: Correctional maintenance regional managers in the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services, and direct care, healthcare, and security attendants at seven Maryland Department of Health facilities.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State pension liabilities increase by $13.7 million and normal costs rise by $2.5 million. State pension contributions increase by approximately $4.87 million in FY 2027, growing annually thereafter, split 60% general funds, 20% special funds, and 20% federal/other funds. No effect on state revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Retirement Agency administers the State Retirement and Pension System, which includes the Correctional Officers' Retirement System (CORS) and Employees' Pension System. The agency is directly responsible for administering the transfer of service credit, calculating normal and disability benefits, and processing opt-out elections for affected members under this bill.

The bill directly impacts the Maryland Department of Health by moving over 800 of its facility employees (including direct care assistants, security attendants, and psychiatric associates at state hospital centers) into the Correctional Officers' Retirement System as a condition of employment.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters membership in CORS to include specified positions within the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services, specifically correctional maintenance regional managers.

The Department of Budget and Management oversees the state budget and personnel policies. The bill increases state pension liabilities by approximately $13.7 million, increasing annual employer pension contributions starting in FY 2027.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the timeframe for the State to recover funds under the Federally Qualified Health Centers Grant Program. Prohibits State recovery more than 15 years after project completion if the property was leased by the center. Prohibits State recovery more than 30 years after project completion if the property was owned by the center. Triggers recovery if the property is transferred to an unapproved entity or ceases operating as a qualified center. Authorizes the State to recover proportional project costs, litigation expenses, and reasonable attorneys' fees.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Board of Public Works
qa_results.stakeholders: Federally qualified health centers, property owners leasing facilities to health centers, and counties, municipal corporations, and nonprofit organizations sponsoring health center projects
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Indeterminate increase in general fund revenues that may occur sooner than expected due to accelerated recovery timeframes for leased properties; state workload can be handled with existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health administers the Federally Qualified Health Centers Grant Program, processes project applications, and monitors center compliance and potential fund recovery.
The Board of Public Works approves grant awards under the program and is statutorily responsible for approving property transferees to prevent recovery proceedings.

The Department of Budget and Management assists in overseeing state fiscal planning, capital budget expenditures, and monitoring potential state revenue impacts resulting from accelerated fund recoveries.

The Office of the Attorney General represents the State of Maryland in recovery proceedings, enforcing state liens and recovering grant funds and associated legal fees when grant conditions are violated.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes specified State officers and employees required to hold surety bonds to be covered by insurance policies instead. Repeals the Maryland State Employees Surety Bond Committee and transfers its responsibilities to the State Treasurer. Requires the State Treasurer to determine the coverage type, amount, and term for required bonds or insurance policies. Directs the State Treasurer to maintain records of all procured insurance policies. Requires copies of required surety bonds to be sent to and recorded by the State Comptroller.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Treasurer; State Comptroller
qa_results.stakeholders: State officers and employees required or designated to maintain surety bonds or insurance coverage
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Likely generates operational efficiencies and potential State expenditure savings by permitting insurance policies instead of surety bonds. The State Treasurer's Office can implement the changes with existing resources, and State revenues are unaffected. Specific dollar savings figures are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill was requested by the State Treasurer and transfers all duties, powers, and responsibilities of the abolished Maryland State Employees Surety Bond Committee directly to the State Treasurer. The Treasurer is tasked with determining the type, amount, and term of surety bond or insurance coverage for required State officers and employees, and maintaining records of policies.

The Comptroller's membership on the State Employees Surety Bond Committee is abolished, but the office retains and receives the statutory mandate to record and keep copies of all required bonds purchased across State government.

The Governor, in consultation with the State Treasurer, is statutorily required to determine the type and coverage amount of insurance or surety bonds for the State Treasurer and may require bonds or insurance for the Commissioner of Correction.

The Secretary of Labor must be consulted by the State Treasurer regarding the insurance policy or bond covering the Treasurer as custodian of the Unemployment Insurance Fund, and administrative funds from the department pay the associated premiums.

The bill repeals the Maryland State Employees Surety Bond Committee, of which the Attorney General was a member, and removes former requirements for Attorney General approval of the form of state employee surety bonds under the repealed subtitle.

The bill repeals provisions under Title 9, Subtitle 17 of the State Government Article that previously required Board of Public Works prior approval before the Treasurer could purchase or cancel State employee surety bonds.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill formally repeals and abolishes the Maryland State Employees Surety Bond Committee, a permanent state committee tasked with setting bond requirements.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Correctional Services Article allowing the Commissioner and employees of the Division to be covered by an insurance policy rather than solely a surety bond, subject to the approval of the Governor and State Treasurer.
The bill alters statutory bonding requirements for the Maryland Insurance Commissioner and the Deputy Commissioner, allowing coverage via an insurance policy determined by the State Treasurer.

The bill amends the State Personnel and Pensions Article regarding coverage for fiduciaries of the State Retirement and Pension System, allowing coverage via bonds or insurance determined by the State Treasurer in consultation with the Board of Trustees.
The bill amends statutory requirements in the State Government Article governing the Legislative Auditor, authorizing coverage by an insurance policy in lieu of a surety bond.

The bill amends the Natural Resources Article to allow the Treasurer and Deputy Treasurer of the Maryland Environmental Service to be covered by an insurance policy as determined by the State Treasurer instead of a surety bond.
The bill amends the Transportation Article to authorize employees of the Administration to be covered by an insurance policy determined by the State Treasurer rather than solely bonded.
The bill amends provisions in the Transportation Article regarding employee bonding and insurance coverage under State Treasurer oversight.
The bill amends the Agriculture Article regarding bonding and insurance requirements for employees and officers of the State Soil Conservation Committee and district supervisors.
The bill amends the Education Article regarding the required coverage for each fiduciary of the trust, permitting insurance policies in lieu of surety bonds as determined by the State Treasurer.
The bill updates the Natural Resources Article regarding surety bond and insurance coverage determinations for designated officers and authorities.
The bill amends bonding and insurance policy requirements under the Economic Development Article for authority members and executive staff associated with the department's financing authorities.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes a licensed professional counselor – clinical to sign an original certificate of illness or disability for State employees. Applies to employees in the State Personnel Management System using sick leave for five or more consecutive workdays. Covers sick leave used for personal illness or disability or that of an immediate family member. Requires the professional counselor to be authorized to practice and performing within that scope of authority. Takes effect July 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Budget and Management
qa_results.stakeholders: State Personnel Management System employees and licensed clinical professional counselors
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact; the bill is procedural and codifies existing practice under State Personnel Management System sick leave policies.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DBM serves as the central personnel agency for the State of Maryland, administering the State Personnel Management System (SPMS) and employee leave policies governed by the State Personnel and Pensions Article amended by this bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Frederick County School Construction Master Plan Workgroup. Requires the Frederick County Board of Education to provide staff for the Workgroup. Directs the Workgroup to comprehensively evaluate all school facility needs in the Frederick County Public Schools portfolio. Requires the Workgroup to explore solutions and cost-sharing opportunities to fund new construction, maintenance, and renovations. Mandates that the Workgroup report findings and recommendations to specified state and local officials by December 31, 2024. Terminates the Workgroup on June 30, 2025.
qa_results.responsible_party: Frederick County School Construction Master Plan Workgroup; Frederick County Board of Education; Interagency Commission on School Construction
qa_results.stakeholders: Frederick County Public Schools, Frederick County students and educators, and Frederick County taxpayers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local expenditures are not materially affected; the Interagency Commission on School Construction and Frederick County Public Schools can implement the bill with existing resources. State and local revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates that one member of the Interagency Commission on School Construction serve on the newly formed Frederick County School Construction Master Plan Workgroup, and requires the workgroup to submit its final report of findings and recommendations to the Commission by December 31, 2024.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The legislation formally establishes a temporary advisory task force/workgroup (the Frederick County School Construction Master Plan Workgroup) tasked with evaluating school facility needs and providing recommendations on educational facilities and school construction priorities.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Frederick County Soil Conservation District with boundaries corresponding to Frederick County boundaries. Consolidates the Catoctin Soil Conservation District and the Frederick Soil Conservation District into the single countywide district. Reduces the total number of established county soil conservation districts in Maryland from 24 to 23. Maintains the mandated annual state budget appropriation across the remaining 23 soil conservation districts.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Agriculture; State Soil Conservation Committee
qa_results.stakeholders: Agricultural producers, landowners, and residents in Frederick County, as well as supervisors and personnel of the Catoctin and Frederick soil conservation districts.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State expenditures or revenues for the Maryland Department of Agriculture. Consolidating the two districts is not anticipated to materially affect Frederick County operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Agriculture oversees and provides financial, technical, and staffing assistance to the State's soil conservation districts and houses the State Soil Conservation Committee. This bill directly amends the Agriculture Article to consolidate the two soil conservation districts in Frederick County into one unified district.

The Department of Budget and Management oversees the development of the Governor's annual budget. The bill updates the statutory provision governing the annual mandated appropriation for soil conservation districts from 24 to 23 districts.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the County Commissioners of Washington County to borrow up to $50,000,000 through general obligation bonds. Finances the acquisition, construction, improvement, or development of public facilities, including water and sewer projects. Authorizes loans to volunteer fire departments in the County for fire or emergency-related equipment and facilities. Permits borrowing through installment purchase obligations to acquire agricultural land and woodland preservation easements. Directs the County to levy annual ad valorem taxes sufficient to pay bond principal and interest. Exempts the bonds, refunding bonds, and related income from Maryland state and local taxation.
qa_results.responsible_party: County Commissioners of Washington County
qa_results.stakeholders: Property owners, taxpayers, and volunteer fire departments in Washington County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Washington County bond revenues increase by up to $50,000,000. County debt service expenditures increase by an estimated $3.4 million annually over a 20-year period assuming a 3.37% interest rate. No effect on State finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly exempts the bonds, refunding bonds, interest, and any income or profit derived from them from all State taxation. As the State's principal tax collector and administrator of state income and revenue laws, the Comptroller oversees the administration and enforcement of state tax exemptions.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Secretary of Transportation’s designee to attend WMATA Board of Directors meetings whenever the Secretary is not available. Grants the designee the same powers as the Secretary when attending meetings on the Secretary's behalf. Authorizes the Washington Suburban Transit Commission to reappoint its gubernatorial appointee to the WMATA Board of Directors. Repeals county review and approval requirements for Washington Suburban Transit Commission contracts and agreements.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Transportation; Washington Suburban Transit Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: members of the Washington Suburban Transit Commission, the Secretary of Transportation and designated staff, the Washington Metropolitan Area Transit Authority Board of Directors, and transit users in Montgomery and Prince George's counties
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends provisions governing the Secretary of Transportation's representation on the Washington Metropolitan Area Transit Authority (WMATA) Board of Directors, authorizing the Secretary's designee (who must be a Department of Transportation employee) to attend when the Secretary is unavailable and to exercise full powers.
WMATA is a tri-jurisdictional interstate compact agency, and this legislation governs the representation and reappointment of Maryland's commissioners serving on the WMATA Board of Directors.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands the Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission Connection Pipe Emergency Replacement Loan Program to include sewer pipes and diagnostic actions. Increases the maximum loan amount for residential customers from $5,000 to $10,000. Raises the total cap on outstanding program loans from $1,000,000 to $2,000,000. Requires the Commission to budget $200,000 annually for the program through fiscal year 2034. Mandates that Commission-licensed plumbers perform all replacements and diagnostic actions under the program. Extends the program termination date to June 30, 2034.
qa_results.responsible_party: Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Residential customers of the Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission and Commission-licensed plumbers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission expenditures increase by $100,000 annually from fiscal 2025 through 2034 to provide additional program funding. Commission revenues increase upon loan repayments through customer water and sewer bills. Total outstanding loans may not exceed $2.0 million at any time.

qa_results.bill_summary: Adds the United States Space Force to Maryland statutes governing the armed forces. Authorizes military spouses to terminate, suspend, or reinstate specified consumer service contracts upon receiving qualifying relocation orders. Extends those contract termination rights to Maryland residents serving in another state's National Guard or reserve components. Expands the Purple Star Schools Program to include dependents of Space Force and out-of-state National Guard personnel. Authorizes the Governor to posthumously award organized militia commissions, appointments, or promotions.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governor; Maryland Military Department; Maryland State Department of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: Members of the U.S. Space Force, military spouses, Maryland residents serving in out-of-state National Guard units or armed forces reserves, military-connected students, and consumer service providers
