qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Public Safety Article regarding appointments, commissions, and promotions of officers in the organized militia and Maryland Defense Force made on the recommendation of the Adjutant General.

The bill amends the Education Article to expand the definition of 'military-connected student' to include the Space Force and National Guard members of other states within the Purple Star Schools Program administered by MSDE.

The bill directly updates provisions governing military service, uniform regulations, military justice, and contract termination protections that reference the Maryland National Guard and its website.
The bill grants the Governor express statutory authority to award commissions, appointments, or promotions in the organized militia posthumously.

The bill expands legal protections for active-duty military personnel and military spouses and recognizes the U.S. Space Force across Maryland law, directly relating to the agency's mission of supporting military families.
The bill amends Family Law provisions concerning court orders for child custody and visitation during military deployment to incorporate members of the Space Force.
The bill expands consumer contract cancellation protections for service members and spouses, which fall under the scope of laws enforced by the Consumer Protection Division.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Electric Vehicle Supply Equipment Workgroup to study and develop standards for electric vehicle charging stations. Directs the Workgroup to develop a reliability and reporting framework and examine government agency accountability. Requires the Workgroup to recommend regulations on payment options, uptime standards, customer support, and equipment certification. Requires the Public Service Commission to provide staff for the Workgroup. Mandates a report with recommendations to specified legislative committees by November 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Public Service Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: electric vehicle owners, electric vehicle service providers, electric vehicle charging station operators, and electric vehicle industry business partners
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on State revenues. The Public Service Commission can staff the workgroup using existing budgeted resources, and member travel reimbursements are minimal and absorbable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Public Service Commission is the primary implementing agency; its Chair designates the Workgroup chair, designates multiple members, and the Commission is required to provide staff support for the Electric Vehicle Supply Equipment Workgroup.
The Secretary of Agriculture is required to designate a representative of the Department of Agriculture to serve as a member of the Electric Vehicle Supply Equipment Workgroup.

The Comptroller is required to designate a representative of the Office of the Comptroller to serve on the Electric Vehicle Supply Equipment Workgroup to study regulatory and reporting standards for EV charging equipment.
The Secretary of Transportation is required to designate a representative of the Maryland Department of Transportation to serve as a member of the Workgroup.
The Director of the Maryland Energy Administration is required to designate an agency representative to serve on the Electric Vehicle Supply Equipment Workgroup.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a temporary state advisory body, the Electric Vehicle Supply Equipment Workgroup, to study, develop frameworks, and make policy recommendations regarding EV charging infrastructure.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Tourist Area and Corridor Signage Program to direct motorists to eligible attractions. Requires the State Highway Administration and the Department of Commerce to administer the program and establish eligibility criteria. Requires participating attractions to pay review and permit fees and cover all sign design, fabrication, and installation costs. Authorizes the Administration to charge an annual administrative fee and remove noncompliant signs. Authorizes the Administration to amend the program to avoid federal sanctions after notifying four legislative committees.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Highway Administration; Department of Commerce
qa_results.stakeholders: operators of Maryland tourist attractions, motorists, and travelers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: General fund expenditures for the Department of Commerce increase by $53,000 in FY 2025 and $14,700 in FY 2026 for contractual staff. Transportation Trust Fund expenditures for the State Highway Administration increase by $86,400 in FY 2025, which are fully offset by sign review and annual administrative fee revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the State Highway Administration (SHA) with administering the Tourist Area and Corridor Signage Program, reviewing signage plans, inspecting highway right-of-way space, issuing permits, and collecting administrative and sign review fees.

The bill requires the Department of Commerce to collaborate in administering the program, develop eligibility standards, review applications for initial approval, coordinate with attractions to prepare signage plans, and identify generic symbols.

As the parent agency of the State Highway Administration, the Department of Transportation oversees the Transportation Trust Fund (TTF), which will incur expenditures for staffing and realize corresponding fee revenues to administer the program.

Operating within the Department of Commerce, the Office of Tourism Development promotes attractions throughout the state and will be directly involved in the programmatic implementation and coordination with tourist destinations seeking signage.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases the required number of assistant sheriffs appointed by the Baltimore City Sheriff from one to three. Authorizes the Sheriff to appoint up to two social workers. Authorizes additional sworn or civilian personnel appointments if funding is provided in the Ordinance of Estimates or any other source. Subjects additional personnel appointments to existing statutory collective bargaining provisions. Takes effect October 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Baltimore City Sheriff
qa_results.stakeholders: Baltimore City Sheriff's Office personnel and Baltimore City
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on State or Baltimore City finances. Baltimore City indicates the bill provides staffing flexibility without directly altering the city budget or the municipal budget authorization process.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill references the authority and regulations of the Secretary of Budget and Management regarding personnel policies and collective bargaining conflicts (§ 2-316(i)(10)) for the Baltimore City Sheriff's Office. However, the bill makes no direct changes to DBM operations and has no material impact on state finances.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Task Force on the Creation of a Division of Returning Citizens and Expanded Reentry Services. Requires the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services to provide staff for the Task Force. Directs the Task Force to assess existing reentry services, identify gaps, and evaluate markers of successful reentry. Mandates developing plans to establish a Division of Returning Citizens and expand post-release services. Requires the Task Force to submit its findings and recommendations to the General Assembly by December 31, 2025.
qa_results.responsible_party: Task Force on the Creation of a Division of Returning Citizens and Expanded Reentry Services; Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Incarcerated individuals, formerly incarcerated individuals, families of incarcerated individuals, and reentry service providers in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are minimal and absorbable within existing budgeted resources for task force member expense reimbursements and DPSCS staffing. State revenues and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS is required to provide staff for the task force, has two designated members (the Secretary and a representative from the Division of Parole and Probation), and the task force is charged with creating a plan to establish a Division of Returning Citizens within DPSCS.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a new temporary entity, the Task Force on the Creation of a Division of Returning Citizens and Expanded Reentry Services, to study and make recommendations by December 31, 2025.
The Secretary of Housing and Community Development (or designee) is designated as a member of the task force, which will study and develop plans for expanded housing reentry services.
The Secretary of Health (or designee) is designated as a member of the task force, which will assess and plan health, mental health, dental, and substance abuse reentry services.
The Secretary of Human Services (or designee) serves as a member of the task force examining reentry support and social services.

The Secretary of Labor (or designee) is designated as a member of the task force, which will develop plans to expand employment, job training, and workforce development services for returning citizens.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Public Defender (or designee) is designated as a member of the task force to advise on legal needs and reentry services.
The Attorney General (or designee) is named as a member of the task force.
The Governor is responsible for appointing numerous members representing various stakeholders, community organizations, and impacted individuals to the task force.
The Office of Appointments will assist the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and processing the appointment of twelve specified members to the task force.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals the requirement to send selection plans and job announcements to the Secretary of Budget and Management before posting. Eliminates the one-week advance notice mandated before posting a job vacancy. Repeals the requirement that an appointing authority wait until a position announcement closes to review applications. Applies to recruitment for vacant skilled service and professional service positions in the State Personnel Management System. Takes effect July 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Budget and Management
qa_results.stakeholders: Appointing authorities in the State Personnel Management System, state job applicants, and state employees seeking skilled or professional service positions
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No direct effect on state or local finances, though the bill creates operational efficiencies by removing hiring delays for skilled service and professional service positions.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the State's central personnel agency overseeing the State Personnel Management System (SPMS), DBM is directly impacted. The bill repeals the requirement that appointing authorities submit selection plans and job announcements to the Secretary of Budget and Management at least one week prior to public posting, streamlining the State's recruitment process.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits selling or distributing self-administered sexual assault evidence collection kits not issued by the Maryland Department of Health. Classifies violations as unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices enforced exclusively by the Attorney General. Bars admitting information that evidence was collected using prohibited kits in proceedings involving sexually assaultive behavior. Voids liability waivers and warranty disclaimers regarding products or services used to collect sexual assault evidence. Establishes the Forensic Nurse Examiner Training Grant Program to fund nurse training through grants to nonprofit entities.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General; Governor's Office of Crime Prevention, Youth, and Victim Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Manufacturers and distributors of self-administered sexual assault evidence kits, victims of sexually assaultive behavior, forensic nurses, nonprofit victim-services entities, and higher education institutions.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by at least $50,000 annually beginning in FY 2025 to capitalize the new special fund, with corresponding special fund revenues and grant expenditures. Civil penalty revenues from kit violations are assumed to be negligible. General fund interest earnings increase minimally, while local community colleges may see minimal increases in grant revenues and expenditures.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly designates the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy (referred to in the statute as the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention, Youth, and Victim Services) to establish, administer, and manage the Forensic Nurse Examiner Training Grant Program and the associated special fund.

The bill establishes that selling or distributing prohibited kits is an unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practice enforceable solely by the Attorney General under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act, and requires the Attorney General to adopt statewide regulations regarding waiver and warranty prohibitions.
The bill statutorily requires the Comptroller to account for the newly established Forensic Nurse Examiner Training Grant Program Fund.
The bill requires the State Treasurer to hold the Forensic Nurse Examiner Training Grant Program Fund separately and invest the money of the fund.

The bill alters the Maryland Rules of Evidence by enacting § 10-925 of the Courts and Judicial Proceedings Article, establishing that certain physical evidence obtained using prohibited kits is inadmissible in criminal or civil court proceedings.
The bill creates an explicit statutory exception to the sales and distribution prohibition for self-administered sexual assault evidence collection kits issued by the Maryland Department of Health.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill enacts rules governing the admissibility of evidence obtained from self-administered sexual assault kits in criminal proceedings involving allegations of sexually assaultive behavior, directly affecting the defense of indigent clients.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the membership of the Behavioral Health Advisory Council and the Commission on Behavioral Health Care Treatment and Access. Increases the terms of gubernatorial appointees to the Council from three years to four years. Requires the Commission to meet jointly with the Council at least three times each year. Directs both entities to coordinate on annual reports to the Governor and the General Assembly. Requires recommendations regarding the continuation of the State's Medicaid behavioral health carve-out by July 1, 2025. Mandates recommendations on financing structures and quality oversight to integrate somatic and behavioral health services.
qa_results.responsible_party: Behavioral Health Advisory Council; Commission on Behavioral Health Care Treatment and Access; Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: individuals with mental health and substance use disorders, behavioral health care providers, and Maryland Medical Assistance Program enrollees
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State agency operations and reporting requirements can be absorbed within existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local government operations and finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDH is the primary implementing agency; the bill was departmental legislation requested by MDH. It alters MDH representation on the Council, directs study of Medicaid behavioral health carve-out and somatic integration, and expresses legislative intent for MDH to evaluate CMS's Innovation in Behavioral Health Model.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly restructures the membership, meeting frequencies, workgroups, and reporting responsibilities of the Behavioral Health Advisory Council and the Commission on Behavioral Health Care Treatment and Access, requiring them to meet jointly.
The bill explicitly amends statutory membership to add the Secretary of Aging (or designee) to the Commission on Behavioral Health Care Treatment and Access, alongside existing Council membership.
The bill explicitly adds the Secretary of Labor (or designee) as a statutory member of the Behavioral Health Advisory Council.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters the Council's membership by removing the Deputy Director of the Division of Children and Youth while retaining the Executive Director, who also serves on the Commission.

The Governor appoints several members whose term lengths are altered from three to four years, and receives joint annual reports and specific recommendations on the Medicaid carve-out by July 1, 2025.
The Maryland Insurance Commissioner serves on the Commission, which is tasked with making recommendations regarding compliance with the Mental Health Parity and Addiction Equity Act.

The Executive Director serves on the Commission on Behavioral Health Care Treatment and Access, which is studying health care financing structures and the integration of somatic and behavioral health care.
The Executive Director serves as a statutory member of the Commission on Behavioral Health Care Treatment and Access.
The Executive Director of the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange serves as an ex officio member of the Behavioral Health Advisory Council.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Public Defender is a statutory member of the Council and represented on the Commission, participating in workgroups related to criminal justice-involved behavioral health.
The Secretary of Disabilities is a member of both the Council and the Commission, which address behavioral health services for individuals with developmental disabilities and complex needs.
The Secretary of Juvenile Services is an ex officio member of both the Council and the Commission, which evaluate youth behavioral health services and juvenile justice populations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Secretary of Public Safety and Correctional Services is an ex officio member of both the Council and Commission, which study behavioral health for criminal justice-involved and forensic populations.
The Secretary of Human Services serves as an ex officio member of both the Council and the Commission.
The State Superintendent of Schools and the Assistant State Superintendent of the Division of Rehabilitation Services serve on the Behavioral Health Advisory Council.
The judiciary has appointed representatives on the Council, and the Commission makes recommendations on treatment access for court-ordered populations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Executive Director of ODHH is an ex officio member of the Behavioral Health Advisory Council.
The Secretary of Housing and Community Development is a statutory member of the Behavioral Health Advisory Council.
The Secretary of Budget and Management is an ex officio member of the Behavioral Health Advisory Council.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires Medicaid-reimbursed obstetric providers to complete prenatal risk assessment forms and submit them to local health departments. Mandates hospitals and freestanding birthing centers delivering newborns after high-risk pregnancies submit postpartum referral forms and provide complications resources. Requires these facilities to call high-risk birthing parents between 24 and 48 hours after discharge. Prohibits Medicaid reimbursement for high-risk deliveries unless the facility submits the postpartum referral form. Directs the Secretary of Health and the Maryland Health Care Commission to develop an annual birthing facility report card. Requires hospitals and freestanding birthing centers to participate in the Severe Maternal Morbidity Surveillance and Review Program.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Maryland Health Care Commission; Secretary of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Pregnant and postpartum patients, newborns, obstetric care providers, hospitals, freestanding birthing centers, and local health departments
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact; the Maryland Department of Health and local health departments can implement the bill's assessment, reporting, and surveillance requirements with existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health is the primary implementing agency tasked with developing standardized prenatal risk assessment forms, establishing an electronic submission process, receiving annual reporting from local health departments, overseeing Medical Assistance Program standards, and developing and publishing the Maryland Report Card for Birthing Facility Maternity Care.

The Maryland Health Care Commission is explicitly required to collaborate with the Secretary of Health to develop the Maryland Report Card for Birthing Facility Maternity Care and collect the necessary data to complete the annual report cards.
The bill mandates that the findings and recommendations regarding severe maternal morbidity surveillance and review be formally reported to the Governor by December 1, 2025.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners to issue up to 10 Class B–D–7 and two Class A–7 licenses. Establishes exceptions to the 300-foot distance restriction from schools or places of worship in two bounded areas. Authorizes the Board to waive a layout requirement for certain Class D restaurants seeking after-hours dining exemptions. Extends expiration deadlines for specified licenses to allow pending transfers and renewals through July 2024 or July 2025. Prohibits license transfers in ward 24, precinct 5 to recipients of legislative bond initiative funding.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore City
qa_results.stakeholders: Alcoholic beverages license holders, license applicants, and restaurant operators in the 46th alcoholic beverages district in Baltimore City, as well as neighborhood associations, schools, and places of worship in affected areas.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State effect. Baltimore City revenues may increase minimally beginning in FY 2025 from application, license, renewal, and transfer fees for newly authorized or converted licenses; specific aggregate figures are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is responsible for regulating the alcohol industry and collecting alcohol-related taxes at the state level. While HB 1052 specifically governs local alcoholic beverages licensing and geographic restrictions administered by the Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners with no state fiscal effect, it pertains to the state's broader alcoholic beverages statutory framework under the Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals the requirement that the executive director of the State Board of Nursing be a registered nurse. Removes the qualification requiring a master's degree in nursing or equivalent professional education and administrative experience. Retains the Board's authority to employ staff and define staff duties. Directs that a deputy director assume the duties and authority of the executive director during an absence. Takes effect July 1, 2025, upon the termination of specified 2023 enactments.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Nursing
qa_results.stakeholders: Candidates for executive director of the State Board of Nursing, State Board of Nursing staff and members, and licensed nurses in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact, as the change is technical in nature and does not directly affect governmental finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Nursing is a health occupations licensing board housed within and overseen by the Maryland Department of Health. The bill alters statutory qualification requirements for the board's executive director position.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits a 340B manufacturer from restricting, discriminating against, or limiting the acquisition or delivery of 340B drugs to contract pharmacies. Permits distribution limitations only when federally prohibited or required under federal risk evaluation and mitigation strategies. Classifies violations as unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices subject to civil fines of $5,000 per drug package. Authorizes the State Board of Pharmacy and the Office of the Attorney General to investigate violations. Requires the Maryland Prescription Drug Affordability Board to study the 340B Program and report by July 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Pharmacy; Office of the Attorney General, Consumer Protection Division; Maryland Prescription Drug Affordability Board; Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: 340B drug manufacturers; wholesale drug distributors and third-party logistics providers; contract pharmacies; 340B covered entities including federally qualified health centers, Ryan White HIV/AIDS grantees, and certain hospitals
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures increase by $47,100 in FY 2025, reflecting $39,600 in special fund expenditures for the State Board of Pharmacy to hire a part-time investigator and $7,500 in general fund expenditures for the Prescription Drug Affordability Board for contractual study costs. PDAB contractual costs continue at $7,500 in FY 2026, while pharmacy board special fund operating costs continue annually. Penalties are not expected to materially affect State or local revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the State Board of Pharmacy (housed within the Maryland Department of Health) with investigating violations committed by its licensees and permittees, with authority to impose disciplinary sanctions. The Maryland Department of Health is also required to consult with the Prescription Drug Affordability Board on a comprehensive study of the 340B Program.

The bill designates violations of the 340B drug distribution prohibition as unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act, tasking the Consumer Protection Division of the Office of the Attorney General with investigating violations and enforcing statutory penalties.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates that the Maryland Prescription Drug Affordability Board (an independent state board) conduct a study regarding the 340B Program in Maryland, gather required reporting from manufacturers and covered entities, and submit findings and recommendations to the General Assembly by July 1, 2026, incurring contractual expenditures.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases the annual salary of the Sheriff of Carroll County. Sets the Sheriff's annual salary at $191,078.10 beginning in 2026. Increases the annual salary to $212,309 beginning in 2027. Applies salary changes at the beginning of the next following term of office. Excludes from that limitation individuals appointed or elected after the effective date to fill an unexpired term.
qa_results.responsible_party: Carroll County
qa_results.stakeholders: Sheriff of Carroll County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Carroll County expenditures increase by approximately $47,000 in fiscal 2027 and by $84,100 annually thereafter to fund the salary increases and fringe benefits. State finances and county revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill references the Department of State Police pay plan in statutory provisions concerning the salary of the Carroll County Sheriff, though it has no fiscal or operational impact on the agency.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands the definition of underlying crime applicable to prohibitions against participation in a criminal organization. Includes firearm use in a crime, general contraband, bribery, false statements, and police impersonation. Adds felony fraud, felony insurance fraud, child pornography, and threats of mass violence. Incorporates vehicle identification number alteration and abuse or neglect of a vulnerable adult. Alters the definition of criminal organization to explicitly include informal associations.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services; Office of the Attorney General
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals prosecuted for participation in criminal organizations; victims of organized crime offenses; law enforcement officers and prosecutors
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Potential minimal increase in State general fund expenditures for the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services due to increased correctional commitments. Potential minimal increase in local fine revenues collected in circuit courts.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill expands the definition of 'underlying crime' for criminal organization offenses, potentially subjecting more individuals to felony convictions and sentences of up to 15 to 25 years in State correctional facilities, creating a potential increase in incarceration expenditures.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The expansion of underlying crimes that qualify for organized crime charges increases caseload complexity and litigation effort for public defenders representing indigent clients charged with these serious felony offenses.

Under Criminal Law § 9-804, the Attorney General has concurrent authority with State's Attorneys to aid in the investigation and prosecution of criminal organization violations, which are expanded under this bill.
State circuit courts will preside over new felony indictments, trials, and sentencings arising from the broadened application of criminal organization statutes.
As the primary statewide law enforcement agency, MSP investigates multi-jurisdictional organized crime and criminal enterprises that involve the specified underlying offenses.

qa_results.bill_summary: Allows a Maryland personal income tax subtraction modification for certain death benefits paid under a collective bargaining agreement. Covers payments from a county or municipality to surviving spouses or other beneficiaries of law enforcement officers or fire fighters. Requires the death to arise out of or in the course of employment. Applies retroactively to all taxable years beginning after December 31, 2021. Takes effect immediately as an emergency measure.
qa_results.responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Surviving spouses and other beneficiaries of deceased law enforcement officers and fire fighters; Maryland counties and municipalities
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues and local income tax revenues decrease, likely minimally, beginning in fiscal 2024 to the extent subtraction modifications are claimed. Specific figures are unavailable because the number of eligible recipients is unknown. Comptroller of Maryland can implement the bill using existing resources; local expenditures are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As Maryland's chief financial officer and tax administrator, the Comptroller of Maryland is responsible for administering the personal income tax, updating tax forms, and processing the new subtraction modification for death benefits paid to surviving beneficiaries of law enforcement officers and firefighters.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Maryland Entertainment District Security Grant Program and an associated special, nonlapsing fund. Assists community organizations, nonprofit entities, and local governments funding security operations in designated entertainment districts. Targets districts experiencing high pedestrian traffic, elevated police calls, and dense concentrations of alcohol, hookah, or live entertainment venues. Requires the Executive Director of the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention, Youth, and Victim Services to establish application and eligibility standards. Authorizes the Governor to appropriate up to $1,000,000 annually to the fund beginning in fiscal year 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention, Youth, and Victim Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Community organizations, nonprofit entities, and local governments located in or containing entertainment districts, as well as entertainment venue owners, patrons, and visitors
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $250,000 in FY 2025 from budgeted funds, and by an estimated $1.0 million annually beginning in FY 2026 to capitalize the fund. Special fund revenues and grant expenditures increase correspondingly by $1.0 million annually starting in FY 2026. Local government revenues and expenditures increase to the extent local jurisdictions apply for and receive grant awards.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly tasks the Executive Director of the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy (referenced in statute as the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention, Youth, and Victim Services) with establishing and administering the Maryland Entertainment District Security Grant Program and the associated fund.
The bill statutorily requires the State Treasurer to hold the Maryland Entertainment District Security Grant Program Fund separately and invest its moneys in the same manner as other State moneys.
The bill statutorily mandates that the Comptroller account for the newly established Maryland Entertainment District Security Grant Program Fund.

The Governor is authorized beginning in fiscal year 2026 to annually appropriate up to $1,000,000 to the fund, and the implementing agency (GOCPP) is an executive office within the Governor's administration.
DBM is responsible for state budget preparation and supervision of funds, including the discretionary annual general fund appropriations of up to $1.0 million to capitalize the grant fund.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Comptroller to offer electronic income tax return filers the opportunity to make an anatomical gift. Directs the Comptroller to provide access through a hyperlink to the State anatomical gift donor registry. Requires transmitting consenting individuals' names, birth dates, and identification numbers to the contracted organ procurement organization. Applies to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2023. Takes effect July 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals filing Maryland resident individual income tax returns electronically and the State's contracted organ procurement organization
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Comptroller's Office can implement the bill using existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly requires the Comptroller to implement procedures offering electronic individual income tax return filers the opportunity to register as organ donors via a hyperlink, and to transmit relevant donor registration information to the State's contracted organ procurement organization.

The Maryland Department of Health oversees and contracts with the qualified nonprofit entity operating the statewide anatomical gift donor registry under § 4-516 of the Estates and Trusts Article, to which the new tax filing procedures link and transmit information.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Workgroup for the Deaf, Deafblind, and Hard of Hearing to study and recommend services and programs. Requires the workgroup to examine case management, educational and employment opportunities, and communication access solutions. Directs the Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing to provide staff for the workgroup. Mandates a final report of findings and recommendations to the Governor and General Assembly by June 1, 2025. Terminates the workgroup and abrogates the act on June 30, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing; Workgroup for the Deaf, Deafblind, and Hard of Hearing
qa_results.stakeholders: individuals who are deaf, deafblind, or hard of hearing; nonprofit organizations serving deaf, deafblind, and hard of hearing individuals
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures for the Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing increase by $67,100 in FY 2025 only to fund consultant services, a part-time graduate assistant, and interpreter services. The FY 2025 budget includes a contingent $10,000 appropriation for interpretation services. No effect on state revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 1069 directly names the Director of the Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing as a member of the Workgroup, designates the office to provide staff and administrative support, and results in a direct fiscal expenditure increase of $67,100 in FY 2025.
The Governor is responsible for appointing 10 community representatives of nonprofit organizations to the Workgroup and will receive the final report and recommendations by June 1, 2025.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a new temporary statutory workgroup (the Workgroup for the Deaf, Deafblind, and Hard of Hearing) tasked with studying issues and making policy recommendations to the Governor and the General Assembly before sunsetting on June 30, 2026.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and managing the appointment of the 10 community representatives to the newly established Workgroup.

qa_results.bill_summary: Modifies compliance reporting requirements for health insurance carriers under the federal Mental Health Parity and Addiction Equity Act. Repeals the sunset date of existing parity reporting requirements, making the provisions permanent. Requires carriers to submit biennial reports on at least five nonquantitative treatment limitations selected by the Commissioner. Places the burden of persuasion on carriers to demonstrate compliance during reviews, complaint investigations, or market conduct actions. Authorizes the Maryland Insurance Commissioner to assess daily penalties and charge carriers expenses incurred to review additional reports.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Commissioner; Maryland Insurance Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Health insurance carriers, health maintenance organizations, nonprofit health service plans, and enrollees receiving mental health or substance use disorder benefits
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Maryland Insurance Administration special fund revenues increase by an indeterminate amount beginning in fiscal 2025 and biennially thereafter from penalties and charges assessed on noncompliant carriers. Special fund expenditures decrease by an indeterminate amount in fiscal 2024 and 2025 due to a reduced volume of treatment limitations reviewed, but increase every two years starting in fiscal 2027 to support ongoing biennial reviews.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Insurance Administration is the primary regulatory and enforcement agency for this legislation. The bill tasks the Insurance Commissioner with developing standardized data reporting templates, selecting nonquantitative treatment limitations (NQTLs) for carrier reviews, evaluating biennial Parity Act compliance reports, adjudicating violations, and levying administrative penalties and fees.

The Department of Budget and Management oversees the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program; while evaluated for potential effects related to mental health and substance use disorder benefits parity, the fiscal note confirmed no fiscal impact on the state employee plan.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires county boards of education to determine instructional materials for blind or visually impaired students by March 15 annually. Directs county boards to coordinate with the Instructional Resources Center to provide specialized materials by the first day of classes. Requires boards and families to agree on a remedy plan at least 45 days before classes if needed. Requires county boards to mandate that textbook publishers submit electronic files to the National Instructional Materials Access Center. Mandates annual reporting by the Instructional Resources Center and the Maryland State Department of Education on textbook equity.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education; Instructional Resources Center; county boards of education
qa_results.stakeholders: Blind and visually impaired elementary and secondary school students and their families; county boards of education; textbook publishers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $86,400 in FY 2025, increasing to $117,900 by FY 2029 to fund one staff specialist at the Maryland State Department of Education. Local school board expenditures may increase significantly to independently acquire specialized instructional materials if unavailable through the Instructional Resources Center. State and local revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) houses the Instructional Resources Center, provides support to ensure specialized format materials are available statewide, enters into MOUs with local school boards, posts accessibility reports online, and submits an annual report to the Governor and General Assembly. MSDE also incurs general fund expenditures to hire an education program specialist to administer the requirements.

The Governor's Office is mandated to receive an annual report from the Maryland State Department of Education on findings regarding the equity of textbooks and supplemental materials for blind and visually impaired students.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Medical Assistance Program to cover remote ultrasound procedures and remote fetal nonstress tests using Current Procedural Terminology codes. Applies when the patient is outside the provider's office and the provider follows on-site standards of care. Mandates reimbursement for remote fetal nonstress tests in the same manner as on-site tests. Requires providers to use secure, federally compliant, and Food and Drug Administration-approved digital technology. Requires remote monitoring solutions cleared for monitoring fetal heart rate, maternal heart rate, and uterine activity. Directs the Program to issue implementation guidance for providers.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: eligible pregnant women enrolled in the Maryland Medical Assistance Program and participating health care providers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Medicaid expenditures and matching federal fund revenues may increase by a minimal amount beginning in fiscal 2025 to the extent remote access reduces missed appointments and increases service utilization.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the Health - General Article governing the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid), which is administered by the Maryland Department of Health. The department is required to provide coverage and reimbursement for remote ultrasound procedures and remote fetal nonstress tests, as well as issue guidance to Medicaid providers.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes that captured automatic license plate reader historical data is the property of the law enforcement agency. Prohibits law enforcement agencies and contracted vendors from selling the data or selling subscriptions to access it. Prohibits vendors from accessing the data unless expressly authorized by the law enforcement agency. Authorizes uploading captured data to the Maryland Coordination and Analysis Center but prohibits uploads to other entities. Extends criminal penalties of up to one year imprisonment and a $10,000 fine to contracted vendors. Requires the Department of State Police and law enforcement agencies to adopt data breach and protection procedures.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of State Police; Maryland Coordination and Analysis Center
qa_results.stakeholders: Law enforcement agencies, contracted automatic license plate reader vendors, and motor vehicle owners whose license plate data is captured
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local government finances are not anticipated to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly names the Department of State Police, requiring it along with other law enforcement agencies using automatic license plate reader (ALPR) systems to adopt specific procedures regarding data protection, auditing, breach reporting, and coordination with the Maryland Coordination and Analysis Center (MCAC).

The bill governs the storage and uploading of ALPR data to the Maryland Coordination and Analysis Center (MCAC), which is the state's primary intelligence and fusion center closely tied to Maryland's homeland security operations.

MDOT was an information source for the bill's fiscal note, and its law enforcement divisions (such as the Maryland Transportation Authority Police and MTA Police) operate LPR systems subject to the bill's data handling and vendor restrictions.

MDTA operates a nationally accredited police force that uses LPR technology subject to the bill's regulations, and existing ALPR statutes specifically reference electronic toll collection systems operated by or with MDTA.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends indefinitely the requirement for county governing bodies and local school systems to jointly appoint an implementation coordinator. Requires each county board of education to provide $150,000 each fiscal year for the coordinator's salary and benefits. Mandates that the State and each county fund these costs in the same proportion as the foundation program. Takes effect July 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Accountability and Implementation Board
qa_results.stakeholders: Blueprint for Maryland's Future implementation coordinators, county boards of education, and county governments (including Baltimore City)
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures increase by approximately $1.8 million annually beginning in FY 2025 to support coordinator salaries, funded by the Blueprint for Maryland's Future Fund through FY 2027 and general funds thereafter. Local school systems receive $1.8 million annually in State aid, while local expenditures increase by $3.6 million annually starting in FY 2027 to maintain the positions beyond their previous statutory termination date.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the 24 local school systems overseen and funded by the Maryland State Department of Education, tying the state funding portion for local Blueprint implementation coordinators to the foundation program formula under Title 5 of the Education Article.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Accountability and Implementation Board (AIB), established to govern and oversee the Blueprint for Maryland's Future, is responsible for administering the required implementation coordinator salary grants with existing resources.

The Department of Budget and Management is responsible for state budget development and oversight; the bill establishes a mandated annual state appropriation of approximately $1.8 million beginning in fiscal 2026.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters cultivation and production requirements for Class 4 limited winery license holders. Replaces references to grapes or other fruit with Maryland-grown agricultural products. Defines Maryland-grown agricultural products as items cultivated on Maryland farms or vineyards, excluding cannabis and tetrahydrocannabinol products. Requires licensees lacking 20 cultivated acres to ensure at least 51% of annual ingredients are Maryland-grown. Authorizes licensees to purchase finished wine made entirely of Maryland-grown agricultural products fermented by a licensed manufacturer.
qa_results.responsible_party: Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission; Maryland Department of Agriculture
qa_results.stakeholders: Class 4 limited winery license holders, Maryland agricultural producers, and Maryland wine manufacturers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State revenues and expenditures and local government operations and finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill authorizes the Secretary of Agriculture to grant one-year exemptions from the Maryland-grown agricultural product percentage requirement for Class 4 limited winery licenses and mandates that the Secretary adopt regulations governing the exemption process.

The Comptroller regulates the alcohol industry in Maryland, and the bill specifies reporting and record-keeping requirements under the Comptroller's purview for license holders conducting off-premises winemaking and packaging activities.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires the Secretary of Agriculture to consult with the Advisory Commission on Maryland Alcohol Manufacturing prior to adopting regulations governing license exemption criteria.

The bill references food service authorizations by limited wineries and explicitly notes that licensees remain subject to food safety regulations and provisions under Title 21 of the Health - General Article administered by MDH.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands eligibility for erroneous conviction compensation to individuals convicted of conspiracy to commit a felony. Authorizes administrative law judges to grant compensation when an order vacating a conviction prohibits retrial. Lengthens the higher education tuition and fee assistance benefit from five years to eight years. Measures housing accommodations and healthcare benefits from the date an eligibility order is issued. Requires the State to provide 15 days' written notice before introducing evidence of concurrent lawful confinement.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of Public Works; Office of Administrative Hearings
qa_results.stakeholders: individuals erroneously convicted, sentenced, and confined for a felony or conspiracy to commit a felony in Maryland and their estates
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Indeterminate increase in general fund expenditures to compensate individuals erroneously convicted of conspiracy to commit a felony. Specific figures are unavailable because the exact amount of compensation cannot be reliably quantified. No material effect on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Board of Public Works is directly responsible for administering and paying the monetary compensation awarded by administrative law judges to erroneously convicted individuals, consulting on regulations, and submitting an annual report to the General Assembly.

The Office of Administrative Hearings receives the petitions, conducts the hearings, and its Administrative Law Judges issue the orders determining eligibility and awarding compensation and benefits under the altered standards.

The bill was requested by the Office of the Attorney General, which represents the State as a mandatory party in all erroneous conviction compensation proceedings and must comply with new 15-day advance written notice requirements regarding concurrent sentences.
The Governor's issuance of a full pardon stating a conviction was in error remains one of the primary statutory bases for an individual's eligibility for compensation under the bill.

The bill expands the period of enrollment during which eligible erroneously convicted individuals may receive tuition and fee waivers at public senior higher education institutions from five to eight years.
As a public senior higher education institution, Morgan State University is subject to the extension of the tuition and fee waiver benefit from five to eight years for eligible recipients.
MHEC is the state coordinating body for higher education policies and was consulted as an information source regarding the extension of postsecondary education and tuition benefits.

AOC provided information on the bill and court records are involved in documenting vacated convictions, orders not allowing retrial, and verifying reimbursement for court fines, fees, and restitution.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners to issue Class B licenses in Ward 4, Precincts 1 and 2. Requires restaurants to derive at least 51% of average daily receipts from food sales. Requires health department classification as a high priority or moderate priority food service facility. Mandates an executed memorandum of understanding with the Downtown Partnership of Baltimore. Prohibits off-premises alcoholic beverage sales, except under a refillable container permit, and prevents location transfers. Bars issuing new licenses after June 30, 2028, but permits renewing licenses issued on or before that date.
qa_results.responsible_party: Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Restaurants located in Ward 4, Precincts 1 and 2 of Baltimore City; Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners; Downtown Partnership of Baltimore
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Baltimore City revenues increase minimally beginning in fiscal 2025 from initial application fees, annual license fees, and renewal fees to the extent qualifying licenses are issued. No effect on State finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill pertains to alcoholic beverages licensing, which falls within the broader regulatory scope of the alcoholic beverage industry administered at the state level by the Comptroller, although local administration and enforcement for this specific Class B license is handled by the Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners with no state fiscal impact.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands the authorized purposes of the 9-1-1 Trust Fund. Allows the fund to cover the costs of telecommunications cardiopulmonary resuscitation training. Prohibits allocating these funds for public safety answering point personnel salaries or county personnel salaries. Bars using allocated funds for any purpose associated with the 9-8-8 suicide prevention hotline. Takes effect October 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland 9-1-1 Board; Maryland Department of Emergency Management
qa_results.stakeholders: Public safety answering point personnel, 9-1-1 specialists, and local governments operating emergency communications centers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on State special fund revenues or expenditures, as telecommunications CPR training is already an allowable fund expense. Local expenditures incurred by counties to provide telecommunications CPR training to public safety answering point personnel are reimbursable through the 9-1-1 Trust Fund.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Emergency Management (MDEM) oversees the Maryland 9-1-1 Board, which administers the 9-1-1 Trust Fund and oversees training standards and funding distributions for public safety answering points (PSAPs).

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MIEMSS coordinates and regulates Maryland's emergency medical services network and prehospital emergency care protocols, which intersect with standards and instruction for telecommunications cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR).

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Anne Arundel County Human Relations Commission to apply to a circuit court when a person disobeys a subpoena. Authorizes the court to compel witness testimony and production of books, papers, records, electronically stored information, documents, and tangible property. Requires notice to the subpoenaed person and a finding that requested testimony or materials are relevant or necessary. Requires a sheriff or deputy sheriff to serve the court order on the person. Authorizes the court to punish failure to obey the order as contempt of court.
qa_results.responsible_party: Anne Arundel County Human Relations Commission; Circuit Courts; Anne Arundel County Sheriff's Office
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals and entities subpoenaed by the Anne Arundel County Human Relations Commission; parties to discrimination complaints in Anne Arundel County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill allows the Anne Arundel County Human Relations Commission to petition the Circuit Courts to enforce subpoenas and initiate contempt proceedings, directly involving the judicial branch's caseload and court procedures managed and supported by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes veterinary assistants to perform specified tasks under the direct or immediate supervision of a veterinarian or veterinary technician. Authorizes veterinary technicians to perform designated medical procedures under the direct supervision of a licensed veterinary practitioner. Permits veterinary technicians to perform specified noninvasive tasks under indirect supervision if determined qualified by a supervising practitioner. Allows veterinary technicians to provide emergency life support before an initial examination and perform euthanasia under specified circumstances. Prohibits veterinary technicians from diagnosing, prescribing treatments or medications, or performing surgery.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Veterinary Medical Examiners
qa_results.stakeholders: Veterinary assistants, veterinary technicians, licensed veterinarians, animal emergency hospitals, and animal shelters
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues to the State Board of Veterinary Medical Examiners Fund increase by an estimated $2,700 annually in FY 2025 through FY 2027 and by $5,400 annually thereafter from additional veterinary technician registration and renewal fees. State expenditures are unaffected, and local finances experience no material impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Veterinary Medical Examiners is housed within the Maryland Department of Agriculture (under Title 2, Subtitle 3 of the Agriculture Article). The bill defines scopes of practice, supervision levels, and regulatory authority for veterinary technicians and veterinary assistants, generating special fund revenue for the board.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes legal standing for persons meeting federal standing requirements to enforce specified nontidal wetland and stream standards. Authorizes eligible persons to bring civil actions against any person or political subdivision alleged to violate those standards. Requires a plaintiff to provide 60 days' notice before commencing an enforcement action. Prohibits citizen actions if the Secretary of the Environment is diligently prosecuting a civil or criminal compliance action. Authorizes courts to grant equitable relief, award litigation costs, and impose statutory civil penalties. Authorizes persons meeting federal standing requirements to intervene in civil actions brought by the Secretary.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment; Office of the Attorney General
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals and nongovernmental organizations enforcing water quality standards; political subdivisions and entities regulated under Maryland nontidal wetland and water pollution control laws
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $86,400 in FY 2025 for the Maryland Department of the Environment to hire an assistant Attorney General, with future annualized costs. Special fund revenues may increase from civil penalties deposited into the Nontidal Wetland Compensation Fund or the Maryland Clean Water Fund. Local governments may incur increased legal and compliance costs if named as defendants.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes citizen suit standing and intervention rights for violations of standards under the Environment Article (specifically nontidal wetlands and water pollution control in ephemeral and intermittent streams). The Department of the Environment (MDE) must be served with 60-day violation notices and proposed consent judgments, and MDE incurs direct general fund expenditures to hire an Assistant Attorney General to handle notices, litigation, and enforcement reviews.

The Office of the Attorney General (OAG) must receive statutory 60-day advance notice of any citizen civil action as well as copies of any proposed consent judgments or settlement agreements at least 45 days prior to filing. OAG represents MDE in reviewing notices, initiating enforcement, and intervening in civil actions under the bill.

The bill confers jurisdiction to county circuit courts to hear citizen suits, award litigation costs, issue equitable relief, and approve settlement agreements with supplemental environmental projects. The Judiciary noted potential expenditures for training circuit court judges on providing equitable relief in these environmental actions.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Miriam Kelty Aging and Senior Social Connection Hub and Spoke Pilot Program in the Department of Aging. Directs the department to select the Montgomery County Village Consortium to implement the pilot program for three years. Requires the consortium to establish a three-year strategic plan and submit annual progress reports to the department. Requires the consortium to submit a final best-practices report to the department by September 1, 2027. Mandates an annual state appropriation of $80,000 in fiscal years 2026 through 2028 to support consortium operations. Terminates the pilot program on June 30, 2028.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Aging
qa_results.stakeholders: Montgomery County Village Consortium, local volunteer-led villages, and seniors aging in place in Montgomery County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $80,000 annually in fiscal years 2026 through 2028 to fund the mandated appropriation for the pilot program. State revenues and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 1103 establishes the Miriam Kelty Aging and Senior Social Connection Hub and Spoke Pilot Program within the Maryland Department of Aging (MDoA). MDoA is tasked with administering the program, selecting the Montgomery County Village Consortium, transferring $80,000 in mandated grant funds annually from FY 2026 through FY 2028, and receiving annual and final implementation reports.
HB 1103 includes a mandated general fund appropriation of $80,000 annually for fiscal years 2026 through 2028, which DBM must incorporate and supervise within the executive budget.
The bill statutorily requires the Governor to include an annual appropriation of $80,000 in the state budget bill for fiscal years 2026 through 2028 for the pilot program.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires an individual to be certified as an advanced practice registered nurse before practicing advanced practice registered nursing in the State. Exempts students enrolled in graduate-level accredited advanced practice registered nursing programs while practicing in those programs. Exempts individuals permitted to practice under rules and regulations adopted by the Maryland Board of Nursing. Takes effect July 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Board of Nursing
qa_results.stakeholders: advanced practice registered nurses, graduate nursing students in accredited advanced practice programs, and the Maryland Board of Nursing
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The Department of Legislative Services notes the change is technical in nature.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health houses and oversees the Maryland Board of Nursing, which regulates health occupations and administers certification, licensing, and regulatory exceptions for advanced practice registered nurses.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the City of Frederick to participate in the Maryland Intrastate Emergency Management Assistance Compact. Allows the city to request and provide emergency management mutual aid to other member jurisdictions. Requires the senior elected official of each jurisdiction to designate authorized representatives to request assistance. Mandates written confirmation within 10 calendar days following any verbal request for assistance. Requires party jurisdictions to consult frequently with the Maryland Department of Emergency Management.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Emergency Management; City of Frederick
qa_results.stakeholders: City of Frederick, emergency management personnel, and participating jurisdictions in the Maryland Intrastate Emergency Management Assistance Compact
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State operations and finances are not materially affected. Local government finances are not anticipated to be significantly affected, although member jurisdictions may benefit from the additional participant.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 1110 expands the Maryland Intrastate Emergency Management Assistance Compact (MIEMAC) to include the City of Frederick. Under the compact, participating jurisdictions coordinate with and report assistance requests to the Maryland Department of Emergency Management (MDEM), which facilitates mutual aid and consultation statewide.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the State Board of Education to adopt a uniform process for sharing county school board budget information with county governing bodies. Mandates that county boards include reserve funds, recent federal funds, and postemployment benefit obligations in their annual budgets. Directs county boards to post submitted and approved annual budgets in easily identifiable locations on their public-facing websites. Requires annual financial audit results to be submitted directly to the county council or county commissioners. Mandates online posting of requested biannual operational and fiscal status reports between county boards and county governing bodies.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Education; Maryland State Department of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: county boards of education, county commissioners, county councils, county executives, and public school taxpayers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. Local school system administrative expenditures may increase by a potentially minimal amount to comply with new reporting procedures and budget categories.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates that the State Board of Education establish and adopt a uniform process for county boards of education to timely share detailed budget information with county governing bodies, and requires county boards to report audit results and approved budgets to the State Superintendent of Schools.

qa_results.bill_summary: Limits the trader's license exemption for licensed restaurants doing business as traders or exhibitors in the State. Applies the exemption only to licensed restaurants that generate 10% or less of annual sales from nonfood items. Requires licensed restaurants exceeding that threshold to obtain a trader's license. Takes effect October 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Clerks of the Circuit Court
qa_results.stakeholders: Licensed restaurants in Maryland selling nonfood items and retail traders.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal effect on State finances and local revenues. Circuit courts can handle additional licensing activity within existing resources, and local governments may receive minor revenue increases from additional trader's license fees; specific figures are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: In Maryland, trader's and restaurant licenses under Title 17 of the Business Regulation Article are issued by the Clerks of the Circuit Court, which are supported administratively and operationally by the Administrative Office of the Courts. The bill modifies licensing exemptions and may increase the volume of trader's license applications processed by the circuit courts.

The Maryland Department of Labor oversees the regulation and licensing of various businesses and commercial activities across the state and was consulted as an information source on the statutory adjustments to business licensing requirements.

The Office of the Attorney General, specifically its Consumer Protection Division, monitors business compliance and enforces state consumer protection and business regulatory laws, serving as an information source on the legislation.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes an implied warranty of habitability for landlords offering residential dwelling units for rent. Expands the list of serious and dangerous defects requiring landlord repair to include hazardous mold. Authorizes multiple tenants to join as co-plaintiffs in rent escrow and habitability defect actions. Creates a rebuttable presumption entitling tenants to prospective rent abatement not exceeding 50% of rent. Permits courts to award actual damages, attorney's fees, litigation expenses, and tenant relocation costs.
qa_results.responsible_party: District Court of Maryland; Judiciary of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: residential tenants and residential landlords in Maryland, including property management companies
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government operations or finances, although small business landlords and property management companies may experience increased litigation complexity and potential liability for attorney's fees.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill significantly alters judicial procedures in landlord-tenant proceedings under the Real Property Article. It authorizes tenant joinder under Maryland Rules, establishes rebuttable presumptions regarding rent abatement and rent escrow, modifies how courts administer escrow accounts and hearings, and permits court-awarded attorney's fees, litigation expenses, and damages.

The Office of the Attorney General, through its Consumer Protection Division, enforces consumer protection laws relating to residential leases and landlord-tenant rights, and was consulted regarding the legal and consumer impact of the warranty of habitability remedies established by the bill.

The Department of Housing and Community Development is the state's principal housing agency tasked with ensuring safe, affordable, and quality housing across Maryland, making statutory habitability standards and landlord maintenance obligations closely aligned with its core mission.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters eligibility for a performing arts theater license in Harford County by permitting issuance to for-profit organizations instead of nonprofits. Excludes the showing of movies or films from the definition of a performing arts theater. Authorizes license holders to sell and serve liquor for on-premises consumption alongside beer and wine. Requires license holders to offer snacks for sale whenever selling alcoholic beverages. Increases the annual license fee from $500 to $1,500.
qa_results.responsible_party: Harford County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: For-profit performing arts theaters in Harford County and theater patrons
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Harford County license fee revenues increase by approximately $1,000 annually beginning in fiscal 2025 from the increased annual fee. State finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller regulates the alcohol industry and oversees state excise tax collections on alcoholic beverages, though this bill specifically affects local retail licensing administered by the Harford County Board of License Commissioners.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires a person to submit an acquisition request to the Maryland Health Care Commission before acquiring a nursing home. Mandates filing the request at least 60 days before the acquisition's closing date. Requires the prospective buyer to notify nursing home residents, resident representatives, and employees of the acquisition request. Directs the Executive Director to review completed requests within 45 days in consultation with the Secretary of Health. Mandates regulations requiring buyers to reduce resident rooms containing more than two beds or obtain a waiver. Requires purchasers to submit annual reports to the Commission for three years after the acquisition.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Health Care Commission; Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: nursing home owners, prospective nursing home purchasers, nursing home residents, resident representatives, and nursing home staff
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Maryland Health Care Commission special fund expenditures increase by $107,100 in FY 2025 to hire one program manager to review acquisitions, with ongoing costs reflecting annualization. Revenues are unaffected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MHCC is the primary implementing agency responsible for reviewing requests for nursing home acquisitions, adopting regulations, issuing determinations, and monitoring post-acquisition compliance reports.

MHCC is an independent commission within MDH. The Secretary of Health must be consulted on acquisition requests and, through the Office of Health Care Quality (OHCQ), receives final decisions, compliance reports, and incorporates acquisition approvals into nursing home licensure decisions.

The bill requires the Executive Director of MHCC to consult with the Office of the Attorney General to determine whether a proposed nursing home acquisition raises public interest concerns, and OAG receives copies of final decisions and annual reports.
The Secretary of Aging and the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman are statutorily required recipients of all final acquisition decisions and annual post-acquisition reports from MHCC.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters licensing requirements and designations for certified nursing assistants and geriatric nursing assistants in Maryland. Establishes new credentials designating fully qualified practitioners as certified nursing assistant-I and restricted practitioners as certified nursing assistant-II. Requires applicants for certified nursing assistant certification to complete an approved nursing assistant competency evaluation. Exempts individuals practicing as a certified nursing assistant-I for less than four months under federal regulations from State certification. Authorizes approved acute care nursing assistant training programs to request waivers of certain federal instructor experience requirements. Requires the State Board of Nursing to notify certificate holders and update regulations by June 1, 2025.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Nursing; Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: certified nursing assistants; geriatric nursing assistants; certified medicine aides; nursing homes and skilled nursing facilities; nursing assistant training programs
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State Board of Nursing special fund expenditures increase by $209,901 in FY 2025 for one staff position and one-time licensing software updates, followed by ongoing annual costs of $103,594 in FY 2026. Special fund revenues are not affected. Local governments experience no fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the State Board of Nursing and the Office of Health Care Quality, both housed within the Department of Health. It overhauls the credentialing, training, and examination standards for certified nursing assistants, requires regulatory updates, and requires software and administrative updates funded via special fund expenditures.

Under Section 8-6A-14 of the Health Occupations Article referenced in the bill, the Maryland Higher Education Commission works in conjunction with the State Board of Nursing to approve nursing assistant training programs and develop applicable program regulations.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes reimbursement by the Criminal Injuries Compensation Board for sexual assault forensic examinations conducted through peer-to-peer telehealth. Requires physicians, qualified health care providers, and hospitals to provide these telehealth examinations without charge to victims. Extends civil liability immunity to qualified providers conducting examinations on alleged child sexual abuse victims without parental consent. Directs the Maryland Sexual Assault Evidence Kit Policy and Funding Committee to study the feasibility of a statewide telehealth program. Requires the committee to report its findings and recommendations regarding a TeleSAFE Pilot Program by December 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Criminal Injuries Compensation Board; Maryland Sexual Assault Evidence Kit Policy and Funding Committee
qa_results.stakeholders: Victims of alleged rape, sexual offenses, or child sexual abuse; physicians; qualified health care providers; forensic nurse examiners; hospitals
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Potential increase in State general fund expenditures beginning in fiscal 2025 for additional reimbursement claims and administrative processing through the Criminal Injuries Compensation Board.
