A reliable estimate is unavailable because the volume of peer-to-peer telehealth claims cannot be predicted. State revenues and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Criminal Injuries Compensation Board (CICB) and its Sexual Assault Reimbursement Unit (SARU) operate within GOCPP. SARU is directly responsible for processing and reimbursing provider claims for sexual assault forensic examinations, which this bill expands to include peer-to-peer telehealth services, leading to potential increases in claims and staffing expenditures.

The Office of the Attorney General provides staff support and legal counsel to the Maryland Sexual Assault Evidence Kit Policy and Funding Committee, which is mandated by the bill to conduct a feasibility study and submit a report on the TeleSAFE Pilot Program by December 1, 2024.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Sexual Assault Evidence Kit Policy and Funding Committee is specifically mandated under Section 2 of the bill to study the feasibility of a telehealth program (TeleSAFE Pilot Program) for sexual assault forensic examinations and submit recommendations to the General Assembly.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Talent Innovation Program in the Maryland Department of Labor to expand access to high-quality job training. Requires the Division of Workforce Development and Adult Learning and the Governor's Workforce Development Board to jointly administer the program. Directs the program to launch an initial pilot program supporting cybersecurity training by expanding regional cyber ranges. Creates the Talent Innovation Fund as a special, nonlapsing fund to finance workforce grants and innovative talent financing mechanisms. Credits interest earnings directly to the fund rather than the General Fund.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor; Division of Workforce Development and Adult Learning; Governor's Workforce Development Board
qa_results.stakeholders: Job trainees and Maryland residents seeking workforce training, employers in targeted industry sectors including cybersecurity, health care, biotechnology, manufacturing, and artificial intelligence, institutions of higher education, registered apprenticeship sponsors, and local workforce development boards
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $2.0 million annually beginning in fiscal 2025 to capitalize the fund. Special fund revenues and expenditures increase correspondingly by $2.0 million annually to support program administration and grants. Local revenues and expenditures may increase beginning in fiscal 2025 to the extent local entities receive program funding or provide matching funds.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 1128 establishes the Talent Innovation Program and Talent Innovation Fund within the Maryland Department of Labor, whose Division of Workforce Development and Adult Learning will co-administer the program and manage fund expenditures.
The bill explicitly mandates that the Governor's Workforce Development Board jointly administer the Talent Innovation Program alongside the Division of Workforce Development and Adult Learning.
The bill designates the State Treasurer to hold the Talent Innovation Fund separately and invest fund monies in the same manner as other state funds.
The bill tasks the Comptroller with accounting for the newly established special fund and exempts fund interest from reverting to the General Fund.
The bill involves $2.0 million annually in state General Fund appropriations and budget oversight to capitalize and manage the new special fund.
The Department of Labor is required to submit an annual report on program activities and fund utilization to the Governor by January 1 each year.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands the statutory definition of accredited residential treatment center to include facilities accredited by two additional entities. Recognizes accreditation by the Commission on Accreditation of Rehabilitation Facilities or the Council on Accreditation. Alters the definition of nonaccredited residential treatment center to reflect these additional accrediting bodies. Subjects accredited centers to state inspection when these accrediting bodies identify serious or life-threatening patient care deficiencies. Takes effect October 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Residential treatment centers in Maryland and children and adolescents receiving residential psychiatric evaluation and treatment
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State operational changes can be absorbed within existing budget resources for the Maryland Department of Health. State revenues and local government operations and finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health (MDH) regulates, licenses, and oversees health care facilities and residential treatment centers, granting 'deemed status' based on accreditation and conducting inspections for compliance or deficiencies under Health - General § 19-301 and § 19-360.

qa_results.bill_summary: Permanently establishes the Growing Family Child Care Opportunities Program within the Maryland State Department of Education. Repeals the June 30, 2025, termination date of the original pilot program. Requires the Governor to include an annual appropriation of $450,000 for the program starting in fiscal year 2026. Authorizes the Governor to satisfy the funding mandate with federal funds to the extent allowed under federal law. Requires grant recipients to raise matching funds or in-kind resources at a one-to-one match. Directs the Department to partner with the Maryland Child Care Resource Network to administer the program.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: family child care providers, prospective registered family child care providers, county governing bodies, and child care resource centers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $450,000 annually beginning in fiscal 2025 to maintain program grant funding, reflecting a mandated appropriation of $450,000 in fiscal 2026 and discretionary appropriations thereafter; federal funds may offset general fund expenditures if available. Local grant revenues and required one-to-one local matching expenditures continue.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill permanently establishes the Growing Family Child Care Opportunities Program within the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE), requiring MSDE to administer the program, award grants, establish program guidelines and goals, and submit annual status reports to the General Assembly.

The bill establishes a mandated annual appropriation of $450,000 starting in fiscal year 2026, which impacts the Department of Budget and Management's responsibility for preparing and executing the annual state budget.
The bill places a statutory requirement on the Governor to include an annual appropriation of $450,000 in the state budget bill for fiscal year 2026 and each subsequent fiscal year.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Maryland Emergency Department Wait Time Reduction Commission to address factors contributing to increased emergency department wait times. Requires the Health Services Cost Review Commission to staff the commission and cochair it with the Secretary of Health. Authorizes the commission to request data from specified state agencies, hospitals, health care providers, and payors. Requires entities providing data with personally identifiable information to enter into data sharing and use agreements. Requires the commission to submit annual reports with findings and recommendations by November 1 beginning in 2025.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Emergency Department Wait Time Reduction Commission; Health Services Cost Review Commission; Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: hospital emergency departments, emergency care patients, health care providers, health care payors, and emergency medical services personnel
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Health Services Cost Review Commission special fund expenditures increase by $100,000 annually from FY 2025 through FY 2027 for contractual staffing and reporting. State revenues and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates that the Executive Director of HSCRC serves as co-chair of the new Maryland Emergency Department Wait Time Reduction Commission, requires HSCRC to provide staff support, enter into data sharing and use agreements, and incurs a fiscal impact of $100,000 annually from FY 2025 through FY 2027 for contractual staffing and reporting.

The Secretary of Health serves as co-chair of the Commission, appoints nine members representing various health care sectors, and MDH is subject to data requests from the Commission to analyze emergency department wait times.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Executive Director of MIEMSS (or a designee) is named as a statutory member of the Commission, and the agency is subject to data requests by the Commission.
The Executive Director of MHCC (or a designee) is designated as a statutory member of the Commission, and MHCC is subject to data requests to support wait time reduction initiatives.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a new temporary state commission—the Maryland Emergency Department Wait Time Reduction Commission—effective through June 30, 2027, with the authority to form advisory workgroups.
The Commission is statutorily required to submit an annual report detailing its activities, findings, and policy recommendations to the Governor by November 1 of each year.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits installing, supplying, selling, soliciting, or offering for sale playground surfacing materials containing excessive lead or intentionally added PFAS chemicals. Restricts lead content to no more than 90 parts per million beginning October 1, 2024. Requires manufacturers of playground surfacing materials to establish a certificate of compliance and submit it upon request. Prohibits local governments from enacting regulations on lead or PFAS chemicals in playground surfacing that are less stringent. Establishes civil and administrative penalties up to $2,500 per violation, capping administrative penalties at $100,000 total. Applies prospectively only to contracts awarded on or after October 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment
qa_results.stakeholders: Manufacturers, suppliers, sellers, and installers of playground surfacing materials; local governments and state agencies operating playgrounds; children using public playgrounds.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $118,900 in FY 2025 for MDE staff, testing, and equipment, decreasing to $68,700 by FY 2027. Local government and State agency expenditures may increase minimally if compliant playground surfacing materials cost more than noncompliant options. Revenues are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDE is the primary regulatory and enforcement agency under the bill, responsible for adopting regulations, receiving and verifying manufacturer certificates of compliance, sampling and testing playground surfacing materials, and taking enforcement actions.

DNR is specifically identified in the fiscal note as a state agency that constructs and renovates playgrounds across state parks and public lands, which must comply with the material restrictions on lead and PFAS when purchasing or installing new surfacing.
MSDE oversees public education and local school systems, which regularly purchase, install, and renovate playground surfacing materials that will be subject to the bill's lead and PFAS restrictions.

Pursuant to the enforcement provisions incorporated in the bill (Environment Article § 9-344), the Office of the Attorney General is tasked with representing the State and prosecuting violations or handling judicial actions arising from non-compliance.

qa_results.bill_summary: Exempts accounts established under the Maryland 529 Program from the Maryland Uniform Disposition of Abandoned Property Act. Excluded accounts include the Prepaid College Trust, College Investment Plan, and Maryland ABLE Program accounts. Applies the abandoned property provisions to any sum payable on a check drawn against an account established under Title 18. Protects higher education and disability savings accounts from premature escheatment to the State. Takes effect June 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Treasurer's Office; Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Holders and designated beneficiaries of Maryland 529 Program accounts, including the College Investment Plan, Prepaid College Trust, and ABLE accounts, and recipients of distribution checks
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on State operations or finances, as the bill codifies an existing legal interpretation regarding dormant accounts and uncashed checks. Local government finances and operations are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Treasurer's Office requested this legislation and administers the Maryland 529 Program, including the College Investment Plan, Prepaid College Trust, and Maryland ABLE accounts affected by this exemption.

The bill explicitly exempts accounts established under the Maryland 529 Program from the Maryland Uniform Disposition of Abandoned Property Act while subjecting uncashed distribution checks to the Act.

The Comptroller administers the Maryland Uniform Disposition of Abandoned Property Act (Unclaimed Property Division), which receives and processes abandoned uncashed checks drawn on Maryland 529 accounts.
The Office of the Attorney General issued the formal legal guidance interpreting the application of abandoned property laws to Maryland 529 accounts, which this legislation codifies into statute.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of the Environment to identify significant industrial users that currently and intentionally use PFAS chemicals. Requires the department to establish PFAS monitoring protocols, action levels, and discharge mitigation plans for pretreatment permits in 2025. Requires covered industrial users to measure and report PFAS levels in industrial wastewater by September 1, 2025. Requires covered users to implement measures reducing PFAS discharged to publicly owned treatment works by July 1, 2026. Prohibits significant industrial users from disposing of stored PFAS chemicals in solid waste landfills or by incineration. Requires the department to update its PFAS Action Plan regarding disposal methods by December 1, 2025.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment
qa_results.stakeholders: Significant industrial users holding pretreatment permits that use PFAS chemicals or operate on sites with known PFAS history; publicly owned treatment works
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material impact on State or local finances. The Maryland Department of the Environment and affected publicly owned treatment works can implement the bill using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDE is the primary regulatory and implementing agency tasked by the bill with identifying significant industrial users of PFAS, establishing monitoring protocols, setting action levels and mitigation plans for pretreatment permits, and updating the state's PFAS Action Plan.

The bill explicitly authorizes the Attorney General to request and review documentation of PFAS chemical storage or reuse from significant industrial users, and OAG enforces civil and criminal violations of state environmental laws.

MES operates water and wastewater treatment facilities across Maryland for public and private clients, which serve as publicly owned treatment works (POTWs) that receive industrial wastewater and must collaborate with MDE on pretreatment standards and PFAS mitigation.
AOC is affected to a minimal extent through potential civil and criminal judicial proceedings resulting from enforcement actions under Maryland's water pollution control laws.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires hospitals to establish and maintain protocols and capacity to treat opioid-related overdoses and emergency medical conditions. Requires hospitals to provide evidence-based harm-reduction interventions to patients before discharge. Requires hospitals to possess, dispense, administer, and prescribe specified medications for opioid use disorder. Requires hospitals to maintain capacity to administer medication if recommended by practitioners and voluntarily accepted by patients. Requires hospitals to refer diagnosed or treated patients to appropriate community providers for timely appointments before discharge. Requires hospitals to work with available peer support professionals to assist patients in accessing treatment services.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: hospitals, emergency department patients with opioid use disorder or opioid overdoses, and peer support professionals
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State or local fiscal impact, as the bill primarily regulates private-sector hospital activities.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Health - General Article to require hospitals to establish protocols and capacity to treat opioid-related overdoses and opioid use disorder. The Maryland Department of Health regulates hospitals and healthcare facilities, oversees public and behavioral health policy, and the bill explicitly requires hospital protocols to include any department requirements regarding prescribing opioid agonist treatments.

As a division of the Maryland Department of Health responsible for enforcing the Controlled Dangerous Substances (CDS) Act and regulating the prescribing and dispensing of controlled medications, OCSA's work relates to the requirements for hospitals to possess, dispense, and administer controlled opioid agonist and antagonist medications.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Grow Your Own Educators Grant Program administered by the Maryland State Department of Education. Awards grants to participating local school systems partnering with employee organizations and approved teacher preparation programs. Covers tuition, books, fees, mentor stipends, and administrative costs for support professionals and provisional teachers. Limits grant spending on provisional teacher candidates to at most one-quarter of total expenses. Requires candidates to complete at least a two-year service obligation in designated shortage areas. Authorizes the Governor to include an appropriation for the program in the annual budget bill.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education; Maryland Department of Labor
qa_results.stakeholders: Noncertified education support professionals, provisional teachers, mentor teachers, local school systems, public school employee organizations, and institutions of higher education with approved teacher preparation programs.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by approximately $1.5 million in FY 2025 and increase to at least $5.4 million annually by FY 2028 to fund program grants and two administrative staff positions at the Maryland State Department of Education. Public higher education revenues and expenditures increase as participants enroll in approved teacher preparation programs. Local school system expenditures for program administration and mentor stipends increase, partially or fully offset by grant funds.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MSDE is the primary implementing agency tasked with establishing, administering, and monitoring the Grow Your Own Educators Grant Program, awarding grants to local school systems, and publishing required annual program data.
The bill explicitly requires the Maryland Department of Labor to collaborate with MSDE, on request, to provide technical assistance to collaboratives in obtaining state, federal, or other funding.

USM institutions with approved teacher preparation programs are eligible higher education partners in collaboratives, leading to potential increases in student enrollment and tuition revenues covered by grant awards.

As a public institution of higher education with an approved teacher preparation program, Morgan State University may participate in program collaboratives, experiencing increased enrollment, revenues, and expenditures.

As an independent public institution offering teacher education, St. Mary's College of Maryland may participate in local school system collaboratives, impacting its course enrollments and tuition revenues.
The bill authorizes the Governor to include an appropriation in the annual budget bill beginning in FY 2026 to support the grant program.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters annual reporting and publication requirements for the Attorney General. Repeals the annual reporting mandate regarding legal actions challenging federal government action or inaction. Requires the Attorney General to submit the office's annual report to the General Assembly as well as the Governor. Removes the requirement that the annual report contain an itemized statement of receipts and disbursements. Mandates website publication of annual reports and official opinions instead of bound volume printing.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General
qa_results.stakeholders: Office of the Attorney General, the Governor, the General Assembly, and the public
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on State finances or operations, though the Office of the Attorney General may experience administrative efficiencies. No effect on local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly governs the Office of the Attorney General by altering its annual reporting requirements, eliminating the requirement to publish opinions and reports in bound volumes, and mandating electronic publication on the agency's website instead.

The bill alters statutory reporting requirements to the Governor, specifically repealing the requirement that the Attorney General submit a separate annual report to the Governor regarding actions taken under the Maryland Defense Act.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the 9–1–1 Specialist Recruitment and Retention Workgroup. Requires the Workgroup to examine recruitment and retention challenges affecting 9–1–1 specialists across the State. Directs the Workgroup to study salary ranges, benefits, training requirements, and workers' compensation claims. Requires recommendations on incentives and potential inclusion in the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System. Mandates submission of an interim report by December 1, 2024, and a final report by December 1, 2025.
qa_results.responsible_party: 9–1–1 Specialist Recruitment and Retention Workgroup; Department of Legislative Services; Maryland Department of Emergency Management
qa_results.stakeholders: 9–1–1 specialists, Public Safety Answering Point directors, local governments operating emergency dispatch centers, and emergency response personnel
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on State or local revenues. State expenditures are minimally impacted, as the Department of Legislative Services and the Maryland Department of Emergency Management can likely staff the Workgroup using existing budgeted resources, though contractual support may increase general fund costs if specialized expertise is needed. Local governments can supply requested data using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly names the Secretary of Emergency Management (or designee) as a member of the workgroup and tasks the Maryland Department of Emergency Management (MDEM), along with DLS, with providing staff support for the workgroup.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a temporary state entity, the 9–1–1 Specialist Recruitment and Retention Workgroup, to study challenges affecting 9-1-1 personnel and submit reports to the Governor and General Assembly.
The Secretary of State Police, or the Secretary's designee, is designated by statute as a voting member of the newly formed workgroup.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Executive Director of MIEMSS, or the Executive Director's designee, is designated by statute as a member of the workgroup.
The Governor is required to appoint eight members representing various emergency communications stakeholder groups to the workgroup and receives both an interim and final report from the workgroup.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting and coordinating the gubernatorial appointments of the eight designated members to the workgroup.

The workgroup is specifically charged with evaluating the feasibility of, and barriers to, incorporating 9-1-1 specialists into the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System (LEOPS), which is administered by the State Retirement and Pension System.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Governor to include an increased general fund appropriation for the Division of Rehabilitation Services in the annual budget bill. Permits this appropriation to ensure the State meets its required match amount under federal acts. Defines the State match amount as the State's share of funding required under federal acts. Takes effect July 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education; Office of the Governor
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals with disabilities receiving vocational rehabilitation or independent living services through the Division of Rehabilitation Services
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: General fund expenditures increase by $700,000 in fiscal 2025 due to contingent funding included in the state budget. The legislation is otherwise authorizing in nature and does not mandate future spending increases.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly relates to the Division of Rehabilitation Services (DORS), which is an operational division housed within the Maryland State Department of Education, providing authorization for increased general fund appropriations to satisfy federal match requirements.

The bill explicitly authorizes the Governor to include an increased general fund appropriation in the annual executive budget submission to meet the state match amount for federal rehabilitation funds.

As the agency responsible for preparing and supervising the execution of the Governor's annual state budget, DBM is responsible for calculating and incorporating general fund appropriations to fulfill federal match requirements.

The statutory section amended by the bill specifies the State Treasurer's ongoing duty to serve as the custodian and disbursing officer of all federal funds received under the federal rehabilitation acts.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Whole Watershed Restoration Partnership to accelerate restoration of the Chesapeake and Atlantic Coastal Bays and their watersheds. Requires the Secretary of Natural Resources to establish an interagency State management team to administer the partnership. Establishes the Whole Watershed Fund as a special, nonlapsing fund to support approved five-year restoration projects. Authorizes transfers from specified State environmental and agricultural funds into the Whole Watershed Fund. Requires stream and floodplain restoration applicants to provide public notice, hold community meetings, and submit detailed project plans. Authorizes the Department of the Environment to approve restoration projects and requires at least five years of post-project monitoring.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources; Maryland Department of the Environment
qa_results.stakeholders: local governments, stream and floodplain restoration project sponsors and contractors, property owners adjacent to restoration sites, and residents of affected watersheds
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures for the Department of Natural Resources increase by at least $200,000 in FY 2025 and $178,000 annually thereafter for staff. From FY 2026 through FY 2030, the bill mandates up to $100,000 annually from the 2010 Trust Fund for operations grants. Department of the Environment expenditures increase by an estimated $285,000 to $325,000 annually starting in FY 2026 for regulatory staff. State agencies and local governments undertaking stream restoration projects face potentially significant cost increases for enhanced public notice, review, and five-year monitoring requirements.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DNR is the primary implementing agency responsible for administering the Whole Watershed Restoration Partnership and the Whole Watershed Fund. The Secretary chairs the State Management Team, administers project grants, establishes the permit tracking dashboard, and oversees revenue transfers from the 2010 Trust Fund and Waterway Improvement Fund.

MDE is a primary regulatory and implementing agency. It designates a member to the State Management Team, oversees transfers from the Bay Restoration Fund and Clean Water Commerce Account to the Whole Watershed Fund, and assumes extensive new permitting, evaluation, and 5-year post-project monitoring mandates for stream and floodplain restoration projects.

MDA designates a representative to the State Management Team, and statutory provisions governing the Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Fund and the Maryland Agricultural Water Quality Cost-Share (MACS) Program are amended to authorize funding for the Whole Watershed Fund.
The Secretary of Planning designates a representative to serve on the State Management Team that administers the Whole Watershed Restoration Partnership and selects projects for funding.
The Chief Resilience Officer (housed within MDEM) or their designee is statutorily designated as a member of the State Management Team administering the Whole Watershed Restoration Partnership.

MDOT conducts stream restoration projects to satisfy environmental mitigation and MS4 stormwater permit requirements; as noted in the fiscal note, the department faces potentially significant cost increases and operational delays under the bill's new project application and monitoring mandates.

SHA holds an NPDES Phase I MS4 stormwater permit and frequently undertakes stream restoration projects to meet TMDL compliance targets, making it directly impacted by the bill's new public notice, application review, and post-project monitoring requirements.

MDTA conducts stream restoration projects for environmental and permit compliance, incurring potential operational and cost increases under the bill's rigorous new design, public meeting, and monitoring requirements.

The State Treasurer is required to hold and invest the moneys of the newly created Whole Watershed Fund, and interest earnings are exempted from accruing to the General Fund under the State Finance and Procurement Article.
The Comptroller is statutorily designated to account for the newly created special, nonlapsing Whole Watershed Fund.
The bill references DoIT's maintenance of the statewide digital watershed file used to establish eligible geographic boundaries for project proposals.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Secure Schools Emergency Response Grant Program administered by the Maryland Center for School Safety. Authorizes county boards of education to apply for grants in consultation with local law enforcement and public safety answering points. Requires grant recipients to use funds to improve emergency notification systems or enhance communications with public safety agencies. Permits notification systems to include mobile applications, automated proximity threat alerts, intercoms, and public address equipment. Requires the Center to ensure the program is operating and available to each county board by September 1, 2026. Authorizes the Governor to include an appropriation for the program in the annual budget bill.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Center for School Safety
qa_results.stakeholders: local school systems, public elementary and secondary school personnel, public safety answering points, local law enforcement agencies, and first responders
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $3.0 million annually beginning in fiscal 2025 to fund grants, while the Maryland Center for School Safety implements the program with existing resources. Local school system revenues and expenditures increase by up to $3.0 million annually beginning in fiscal 2025 to the extent local school boards apply for and receive grant awards.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the Maryland Center for School Safety (MCSS) with administering the newly established Secure Schools Emergency Response Grant Program and ensuring the program is operating and available to local school boards by September 1, 2026.

MCSS is an independent unit within the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE), and the grant program directly funds emergency notification and communication systems across Maryland's public elementary and secondary schools.

MDEM oversees the Maryland 9-1-1 Board and state emergency management response; the bill focuses heavily on integrating school notification systems with local Public Safety Answering Points (PSAPs) and first responders.
The bill explicitly authorizes the Governor to include an appropriation in the annual state budget bill to fund the Secure Schools Emergency Response Grant Program.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes a regulatory framework for reduction operators, reduction facilities, and crematories performing alkaline hydrolysis or natural organic reduction. Requires the Office of Cemetery Oversight and the State Board of Morticians and Funeral Directors to adopt identical regulations. Directs reduction facilities to implement mandatory contamination testing programs before releasing any soil remains. Prohibits using soil remains to grow food for human or livestock consumption, selling them, or creating commercial compost. Establishes disposition and notification procedures for unclaimed hydrolyzed remains and soil remains of veterans and eligible dependents.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of Cemetery Oversight; State Board of Morticians and Funeral Directors
qa_results.stakeholders: crematories, reduction facilities, registered reduction operators, morticians and funeral directors, cemeteries, and consumers seeking alternative disposition methods
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal increase in special fund fee revenues for the Office of Cemetery Oversight and the State Board of Morticians and Funeral Directors beginning in fiscal 2025. Workload can be handled using existing budgeted resources. Potential minimal operational monitoring by local health departments with no effect on local revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of Cemetery Oversight (OCO) is housed within the Maryland Department of Labor. The bill directly tasks the Director of OCO with registering and regulating natural organic reduction facilities and operators, developing joint regulations, establishing fees, and setting contamination testing and training standards.

The State Board of Morticians and Funeral Directors is an agency within MDH. The bill requires the Board, in conjunction with OCO, to establish regulatory frameworks and adopt identical regulations governing alkaline hydrolysis, natural organic reduction facilities, and reduction operators, in addition to amending the Health - General and Health Occupations Articles.

The bill establishes notification and disposition procedures for unclaimed hydrolyzed remains or soil remains of veterans and eligible dependents, requiring facilities to notify and transfer qualifying remains to the Department for appropriate disposition.

The Division of Consumer Protection within the Office of the Attorney General is statutorily required, in conjunction with OCO and the State Board of Morticians and Funeral Directors, to update and publish consumer information pamphlets describing consumer rights regarding natural organic reduction.

The bill incorporates environmental biosolids standards for testing soil remains, and MDE notes in the fiscal note that reduction and alkaline hydrolysis facilities may require air quality permits to construct and permits to address potential soil and wastewater discharge.

The bill explicitly prohibits using soil remains produced by natural organic reduction to grow food for consumption by humans or livestock and prohibits incorporating soil remains into commercial or agricultural compost.
The bill permits the disposition and transfer of certain soil remains to owners of woodlands protected under the Forest Conservation Act, a program administered under the purview of DNR.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits selling or offering for sale a natural membrane condom by vending machine or other automatic device. Excludes violations of this vending ban from criminal and civil penalties under the Maryland Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act. Repeals the criminal prohibition and fine against selling nonlatex condoms through a vending machine or automatic device. Requires the formulary committee to include all nonprescription contraceptive drugs and devices approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Authorizes registered nurses in local health departments to provide nonprescription drugs and devices without a prescription under specified circumstances.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Committee on Registered Nurses Personally Preparing and Dispensing Drugs and Devices in Local Health Departments
qa_results.stakeholders: registered nurses in local health departments; patients seeking communicable disease, reproductive health, family planning, or addiction services at local health departments; vending machine operators; consumers purchasing condoms
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material fiscal impact on State or local finances. The Committee on Registered Nurses Personally Preparing and Dispensing Drugs and Devices in Local Health Departments can update its formulary using existing budgeted resources. Local health departments can implement the provisions without affecting local finances, and repealing the criminal penalty has no material impact on State or local revenues or court operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDH is the primary state department responsible for public health and local health departments. The bill amends the Health - General and Health Occupations Articles to allow registered nurses in local health departments to provide nonprescription drugs and devices without a prescription, requires MDH-administered training and inventory procedures, places condom vending regulations under MDH's Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, and oversees the committee establishing the formulary.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates that the statutory Committee on Registered Nurses Personally Preparing and Dispensing Drugs and Devices in Local Health Departments expand and update its formulary to include all FDA-approved over-the-counter nonprescription contraceptive drugs and devices.

The bill repeals a criminal misdemeanor penalty previously under the Criminal Law Article and excludes the new prohibition under the Health - General Article from existing criminal and civil penalties, with minimal operational impact on District Court caseloads.

qa_results.bill_summary: Exempts certain applicants for a video lottery employee license from mandatory disqualification for nonviolent misdemeanor crimes of moral turpitude. Applies this exemption when the applicant will not be employed in gaming or security operations. Requires the video lottery operation licensee to request that the Commission issue the license. Defines the value of an authorized table game chip for theft crimes as its depicted face value. Establishes that chips lacking a depicted face value receive the Commission's designated value based on color.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Lottery and Gaming Control Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: applicants for video lottery employee licenses, video lottery operation licensees, and individuals prosecuted for theft of table game chips
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on State or local finances or operations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the Maryland State Lottery and Gaming Control Agency by altering the statutory criteria and exemptions under which the Commission may grant video lottery employee licenses, and by tasking the Commission with designating the value of table game chips based on color when no face value is depicted.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the State Department of Education and the Maryland Department of Health jointly to develop food allergy guidelines. Directs the State Department of Education to establish a model policy and identify free training resources. Requires registered large family child care homes and licensed child care centers with allergic children to adopt policies. Requires covered facilities to update policies based on State revisions and distribute copies annually to parents or guardians. Grants civil liability immunity to child care providers and staff responding in good faith to anaphylactic reactions.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education; Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: registered large family child care homes, licensed child care centers, child care staff, and enrolled children with anaphylactic food allergies and their families
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are not affected as the Maryland State Department of Education and the Maryland Department of Health can implement the bill with existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE), which regulates and licenses child care facilities, is tasked jointly with the Maryland Department of Health with developing guidelines on anaphylactic food allergens, creating a model policy for child care providers, and publishing the guidelines, model policy, and training resources on its website.

The Maryland Department of Health (MDH) is mandated to jointly develop guidelines with the Maryland State Department of Education to reduce the risk of exposure to anaphylactic major food allergens in child care settings and identify appropriate free training resources.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes a Class M–F alcoholic beverages license for a municipal bowling alley and skating rink in Baltimore City. Authorizes the Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore City to issue the license under specified agreements. Sets the annual license fee at $500 and establishes permitted hours of sale. Authorizes the board to issue a Class B restaurant license on West 29th Street under certain conditions. Extends the expiration of a Class A license on West Biddle Street until July 1, 2025.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore City
qa_results.stakeholders: Municipal bowling alley and skating rink operators, restaurant applicants, Class A license holders on West Biddle Street, and neighborhood community associations in Baltimore City's 40th alcoholic beverages district
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Baltimore City revenues increase by $3,300 in fiscal 2025 and $1,650 annually thereafter from Class M-F license fees, with potential additional revenues from Class B licenses. State finances are not affected, and the city can handle enforcement with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 1198 amends the Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article to establish and alter specific local alcoholic beverages licenses in Baltimore City. While primarily administered by the Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners, the Comptroller of Maryland is the state agency responsible for overseeing state alcohol regulation and collecting state alcoholic beverage taxes.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Transportation Institute at the University of Maryland to study methods to improve paratransit services. Mandates an analysis comparing Maryland Transit Administration ADA MobilityLink operations, service models, and workforce metrics nationwide. Directs the institute to consult with specified disability entities and solicit input from MobilityLink riders. Requires recommendations regarding service outside fixed route corridors and interjurisdictional restrictions for medical appointments. Mandates submission of a final report to the Governor and designated officials by July 1, 2025. Authorizes the Governor to include an appropriation of at least $150,000 in the fiscal 2026 budget.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Transportation Institute at the University of Maryland; Maryland Transit Administration; Maryland Commission on Disabilities; State Coordinating Committee for Human Services Transportation
qa_results.stakeholders: Riders of MTA's ADA MobilityLink paratransit service, paratransit service workers, and individuals with disabilities in the Baltimore metropolitan region
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Higher education expenditures for the University of Maryland increase by $449,000 in FY 2025 to conduct the study. State general fund expenditures and university revenues increase by $449,000 in FY 2026 to reimburse study costs. No direct effect on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly investigates and evaluates MTA's MobilityLink paratransit service, requiring MTA to provide operational data and consider recommendations for service, contract structure, and workforce improvements.

The Maryland Transportation Institute at the University of Maryland (a USM member institution) is mandated to conduct the extensive study, analyze performance and workforce metrics, solicit stakeholder input, and submit the final report.
MDOT is the parent department of the Maryland Transit Administration and is designated as a recipient of the study's final report and recommendations regarding paratransit service delivery.

The Maryland Commission on Disabilities, which serves as the advisory body to the Department of Disabilities, must be consulted by the researchers to solicit public and rider feedback on paratransit services.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill specifically requires consultation with the Maryland Commission on Disabilities and the State Coordinating Committee for Human Services Transportation to gather comments and public input.
The Governor receives the final study report and is authorized to include an appropriation of at least $150,000 in the fiscal year 2026 budget to fund the study.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Strategic Infrastructure Revolving Loan Program and Fund in the Maryland Economic Development Corporation. Authorizes the Corporation to make loans up to $20,000,000 for targeted infrastructure and real estate investments. Requires eligible projects to be located in a sustainable community, priority funding area, or transit-oriented development area. Limits loan terms to five years and caps loan fees at 1.5% of principal plus reasonable attorney's fees. Authorizes the Corporation, with local approval, to pledge alternative revenues generated from designated development projects.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Economic Development Corporation
qa_results.stakeholders: Real estate and infrastructure developers, local governments, and businesses operating in sustainable communities, priority funding areas, or transit-oriented development areas
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by an estimated $15.0 million in FY 2025 and $20.0 million annually from FY 2026 through FY 2029 under discretionary funding assumptions. Special fund revenues and expenditures increase correspondingly as MEDCO issues loans and receives repayments and fees. Local government revenues and expenditures may increase beginning in FY 2025 from pledged alternative revenues under tax increment financing.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 1203 directly establishes the Strategic Infrastructure Revolving Loan Program and Fund within MEDCO. MEDCO is the primary agency responsible for administering the fund, adopting regulations, establishing an advisory loan committee, reviewing and issuing loans, and exercising expanded tax increment financing authorities.
The bill explicitly directs the State Treasurer to hold the Strategic Infrastructure Revolving Loan Fund separately and invest the money in the fund in the same manner as other State funds.
The bill statutorily requires the Comptroller to account for the newly created Strategic Infrastructure Revolving Loan Fund.

The bill targets loans and alternative revenue pledges to 'sustainable communities' designated under the Housing and Community Development Article administered by DHCD, and DHCD provided subject-matter analysis for the bill.

The bill specifically focuses on enhancing transit-oriented development (TOD) as defined under the Transportation Article and allows projects and alternative revenue pledging in TOD areas, with MDOT providing input on the legislation.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes a Class BWLT beer, wine, and liquor tasting permit in Allegany County. Authorizes the Allegany County Board of License Commissioners to issue permits to beer, wine, and liquor license holders. Authorizes permit holders to allow on-premises consumption of beer, wine, and liquor for tasting. Requires permit holders to notify the board at least seven days before holding a tasting event. Sets an annual permit fee of $150 and an initial one-time issuing fee of $150. Requires the board to adopt regulations to carry out the section.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Allegany County
qa_results.stakeholders: beer, wine, and liquor license holders in Allegany County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Allegany County revenues increase by at least $1,200 in fiscal 2025 and at least $600 annually thereafter from permit fees and one-time issuing fees. County expenditures are not materially affected, as permit monitoring and regulation adoption can be handled with existing resources. No State fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill regulates alcoholic beverages by creating a tasting permit in Allegany County. Although administered locally by the Allegany County Board of License Commissioners with no direct state fiscal impact, the Comptroller of Maryland maintains broad state-level regulatory responsibilities regarding the alcohol industry.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Maryland–Ireland Trade Commission in the Department of Commerce to study and promote trade between Maryland and Ireland. Requires the Commission to evaluate bilateral trade, joint policy initiatives, business and academic exchanges, and infrastructure investment. Directs the Governor, Senate President, and House Speaker to appoint commission members representing government, business, academia, and the Irish-American community. Prohibits compensation for members but authorizes expense reimbursement under standard State travel regulations. Mandates that the Commission submit an annual report of its findings and recommendations beginning December 1, 2025. Terminates the Commission on September 30, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Commerce; Maryland–Ireland Trade Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland businesses engaged in international trade with Ireland, public institutions of higher education, and the Irish-American community in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Department of Commerce can support the commission with existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local government finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly establishes the Maryland-Ireland Trade Commission within the Department of Commerce, which will be responsible for housing, staffing, and supporting the commission's work and report preparation.
The Secretary of State (or designee) is designated as an ex officio statutory member of the newly formed commission.
The Governor is responsible for appointing several commission members with the advice and consent of the Senate, holds removal authority, and receives the commission's annual report.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a new executive commission tasked with studying trade relations, making recommendations, and reporting to state leadership.

As the division within the Secretary of State's office managing international engagement and the Maryland Sister States Program (which includes a sister-state relationship with Ireland), the work of this commission directly aligns with its core missions.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and managing the appointment process for the public members of the new commission.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals an obsolete exemption from reemployment earnings offsets for certain retirees whose positions were funded by non-State grants. Repeals related reporting and reimbursement requirements for participating State employers. Exempts certain Teachers' Pension System retirees from reemployment benefit offsets under specific joint employment agreements. Requires the retiree to be jointly employed with, and fully funded by, the Maryland Association of Boards of Education. Requires local employers to submit joint employment and salary funding documentation to the State Retirement Agency. Applies the joint employment exemption retroactively to January 1, 2021, and sunsets that provision on December 31, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Retirement Agency; Board of Trustees of the State Retirement and Pension System
qa_results.stakeholders: reemployed retirees of the Teachers' Pension System, retirees of the Employees' and Teachers' Retirement and Pension Systems, local school systems, and the Maryland Association of Boards of Education
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on State revenues and no discernible effect on State pension liabilities or contribution rates. No direct local fiscal effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Retirement Agency is the primary implementing agency responsible for administering the Employees' and Teachers' Retirement and Pension Systems. It is directly tasked with processing retirement allowances, applying or waiving earnings offset reductions, and receiving employer documentation verifying eligibility under the bill's exemption.

The bill impacts members of the Teachers' Pension System and local school systems regarding reemployment policies and offset exemptions for educators funded via the Maryland Association of Boards of Education.

As the central personnel and human resources agency for State government, DBM is interested in state employment rules, including the repeal of the obsolete non-State grant-funded reemployment offset exemption for state government units.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Executive Director of the State Retirement Agency to employ a Director of Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion. Directs the new director to identify and minimize barriers to ensure access and opportunities for underrepresented groups. Establishes a governance program within the agency's Investment Division according to policies of the Board of Trustees. Requires the Chief Investment Officer to employ an individual to assist in implementing the governance program. Permits the Executive Director to terminate either position only upon recommendation and majority vote of the Board of Trustees.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Retirement Agency; Board of Trustees of the State Retirement and Pension System
qa_results.stakeholders: underrepresented groups seeking access and employment opportunities; State Retirement Agency personnel; State Retirement and Pension System members and retirees; participating employers including State agencies and local governmental units
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special and reimbursable fund expenditures increase by $107,100 in FY 2025 to hire the new Director of Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion, offset by administrative fee revenues from participating employers. State agency expenditures across all funds increase by $42,800 in FY 2025 for their share of administrative fees. Local participating governmental units experience minimal cost increases to pay their prorated share of fees.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 1212 directly impacts the State Retirement Agency by requiring its Executive Director to employ a Director of Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion and codifying the governance program and personnel requirements within the agency's Investment Division.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the annual salary of the Sheriff of Baltimore County. Sets the salary at $90,000 for calendar years 2024 and 2025. Increases the salary to $138,000 for 2026, $143,000 for 2027, $150,000 for 2028, and $157,500 for 2029. Directs that the salary for subsequent calendar years be as provided by the Baltimore County Council in its annual budget. Applies the compensation increases at the beginning of the next term of office.
qa_results.responsible_party: County Council of Baltimore County; Sheriff of Baltimore County
qa_results.stakeholders: Sheriff of Baltimore County and Baltimore County government
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on State operations or finances. Baltimore County expenditures increase by $48,800 in fiscal 2027 and by at least $90,400 annually thereafter through fiscal 2030 due to salary and fringe benefit increases.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires each public middle school and high school to include a cardiac emergency response plan in athletic facility emergency plans. Requires each nonpublic middle school and high school that receives State funding to develop an athletic facility emergency action plan. Mandates that plans establish a cardiac emergency response team and integrate with local emergency medical services protocols. Requires designated school personnel, coaching staff, and response team members to complete cardiopulmonary resuscitation and automated external defibrillator training. Requires each covered middle school and high school to review and update its cardiac emergency response plan each year.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems; Maryland State Department of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: Public middle and high schools, nonpublic middle and high schools receiving State funding, student athletes, athletic coaches, school nurses, and athletic trainers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures for the Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems may increase beginning in fiscal 2025 to furnish automated external defibrillators to participating nonpublic schools, but the total amount cannot be reliably estimated. Local school systems may incur minimal administrative and training costs that can likely be absorbed with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Education Article to mandate that public and state-funded nonpublic middle and high schools include cardiac emergency response plans in their athletic venue-specific emergency action plans, directly falling under MSDE's oversight and administration of educational health and safety policies.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires nonpublic schools to comply with the Public Access Automated External Defibrillator (AED) Program overseen by MIEMSS pursuant to § 13-517 of the Education Article, which may result in an increase in MIEMSS expenditures to furnish AEDs and oversee compliance.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters property insurance requirements maintained by a condominium council of unit owners for certain detached units. Requires councils to insure units and common elements for detached units in condominiums not composed entirely of similar detached units. Restricts the mandate that detached unit owners carry homeowners insurance to condominiums composed entirely of similar detached units. Authorizes councils to carry homeowners insurance on all detached units within a condominium composed entirely of similar detached units. Requires councils of unit owners to give annual written notice of insurance obligations to residential detached unit owners. Mandates prompt updated notice if an owner's insurance obligation changes.
qa_results.responsible_party: Council of Unit Owners
qa_results.stakeholders: condominium councils of unit owners, residential detached condominium unit owners, and property and casualty insurers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends statutory requirements governing condominium property insurance and homeowners insurance obligations for detached units, which directly relates to property and casualty insurance policies and insurer practices regulated by the Maryland Insurance Administration.

The Office of the Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division oversees consumer protection and dispute concerns involving common ownership communities and condominiums, and served as an information source for the bill's fiscal and policy note.

The Administrative Office of the Courts oversees the court system where civil litigation and property disputes between condominium councils of unit owners and individual unit owners regarding insurance requirements and deductibles would be adjudicated.

qa_results.bill_summary: Exempts noncommercial telephone solicitations for public opinion research from certain automated dialing and recorded message prohibitions. Authorizes an aggrieved called party to bring an action to enjoin violations and recover damages. Sets recoverable damages up to $500 or actual damages, whichever is greater. Authorizes courts to award up to three times that amount for willful or knowing violations. Prohibits waiving statutory telephone solicitation requirements and remedies by agreement except within legal dispute settlements.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General (Consumer Protection Division)
qa_results.stakeholders: telephone solicitors, public opinion researchers, and called parties receiving telephone solicitations in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill regulates telephone solicitations, violations of which constitute unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act enforced by the Office of the Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division.

The bill establishes a private right of action permitting aggrieved called parties to bring civil lawsuits in state courts for injunctive relief, actual damages, or statutory damages up to $500 (or treble damages for willful violations).

The bill cross-references telephone solicitation definitions under the Public Utilities Article (§ 8-205) and clarifies the interaction with utility laws overseen and regulated by the Public Service Commission.

qa_results.bill_summary: Regulates the preparation, distribution, advertising, and sale of kratom products in Maryland. Requires retailers to disclose on kratom product labels the factual basis for the product representation. Prohibits distributing or selling kratom products to individuals under the age of 21 years. Bans adulterated, contaminated, synthetic, or unapproved kratom products and bars marketing them to minors. Establishes civil penalties up to $2,000 and criminal penalties up to $5,000 or 90 days imprisonment. Requires the Maryland Department of Health to adopt regulations and report on adverse health events.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Retailers, manufacturers, wholesalers, and distributors of kratom products; consumers of kratom products; individuals under the age of 21 years
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local finances are not materially affected. The Maryland Department of Health and local health departments can handle regulations, reporting, and enforcement within existing budgeted resources. Civil and criminal penalty provisions have no material fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates the Maryland Department of Health to adopt regulations implementing the Kratom Consumer Protection Act and requires the department to collaborate with the Maryland Hospital Association to submit a report to the General Assembly on adverse health events related to kratom and other opioid-like substances.

The bill creates civil causes of action, civil penalties, and new misdemeanor criminal penalties for unlawful distribution and marketing of kratom products, which falls under the purview and caseload of the Maryland court system.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits a retailer from distributing, selling, exposing for sale, or advertising for sale a tianeptine product. Restricts retailers from directly or indirectly advertising or marketing tianeptine products to minors. Establishes misdemeanor penalties with fines up to $5,000, imprisonment for up to 90 days, or both. Holds violating retailers liable for civil damages sustained by an individual resulting from the violation. Requires the Maryland Department of Health to adopt implementing regulations.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Retailers, manufacturers, wholesalers, and distributors of tianeptine products, and consumers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local finances and operations are not materially affected. The Maryland Department of Health and local health departments can implement regulations and enforcement using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill adds a new subtitle under the Health - General Article and specifically requires the Maryland Department of Health to adopt regulations to carry out and enforce the provisions regulating tianeptine products.

The bill establishes a misdemeanor penalty (subject to fines up to $5,000 and imprisonment up to 90 days) and civil liability for damages resulting from violations, which directly impacts court case filings and judicial proceedings.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals a restriction prohibiting the Department of Natural Resources from reducing or altering certain oyster sanctuary boundaries. Applies to oyster sanctuaries established in the September 2010 Chesapeake Bay sanctuary report. Requires the Department's oyster fishery management plan to end overfishing in all affected bay areas. Mandates that the plan achieve target mortality rates, increase oyster abundance and habitat, and sustain harvests. Maintains requirements for biennial oyster stock reviews and benchmark assessments every six years.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Natural Resources
qa_results.stakeholders: commercial oyster harvesters, public oyster fishery participants, seafood industry members, and environmental conservation organizations in the Chesapeake Bay region
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State or local fiscal effect; the bill does not directly affect State or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the Department of Natural Resources (DNR) by repealing a statutory prohibition that previously prevented the department from altering or reducing boundaries of certain Chesapeake Bay oyster sanctuaries until an updated fishery management plan was completed.

The bill directly references the University of Maryland Center for Environmental Science (UMCES), a USM member institution, as a required consultative and coordinating partner in developing the oyster stock management strategies and science-based modeling tools.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Oyster Advisory Commission is specifically tasked under the statute with collaborating with DNR and external specialists to develop consensus recommendations for oyster stock management.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the expiration dates of two Class B–D–7 alcoholic beverages licenses in Baltimore City until July 1, 2025. Authorizes transferring a license in the 5517 block of Harford Road to another owner at the same location. Requires the Harford Road applicant to execute a memorandum of understanding with the Hamilton Community Association. Authorizes renewing and transferring an East Fayette Street license to a different applicant at the same location. Requires the East Fayette Street applicant to sign an agreement with the C.A.R.E. Community Association. Limits that license to beer and wine for 12 months and prohibits transferring it to another location.
qa_results.responsible_party: Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: alcoholic beverages license applicants and holders in Baltimore City, the Hamilton Community Association, and the Cleaning, Active, Restoring, Efforts (C.A.R.E.) Community Association
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Baltimore City revenues may increase minimally in FY 2025 to the extent that license renewals and transfers occur under the bill. State finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is responsible for state-level regulation and taxation of the alcohol industry. Although this legislation specifically addresses local retail license extensions administered by the Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners and has no direct state fiscal impact, it relates to the regulation and operation of licensed alcoholic beverage establishments in the state.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters academic program approval processes and institutional mission statement reviews for Maryland institutions of higher education. Requires the Maryland Higher Education Commission, Department of Labor, and Department of Commerce to coordinate workforce data collection. Requires public senior higher education institutions and private nonprofit institutions to submit biannual letters of intent for graduate programs. Establishes the Proposed Programs Collaborative Grant Fund to support institutional collaboration on new graduate offerings. Grants four historically Black institutions and the University of Maryland, College Park Campus initial proposal priority for emerging workforce programs. Requires the Commission to conduct annual reviews of approved programs contested by historically Black colleges or universities.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Higher Education Commission; Maryland Department of Labor; Department of Commerce
qa_results.stakeholders: public senior higher education institutions, community colleges, private nonprofit and for-profit institutions of higher education, historically Black colleges and universities, and postsecondary students
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by at least $264,000 in FY 2025 for two agency analysts and one-time workforce data setup costs at the Maryland Longitudinal Data System Center, with ongoing personnel costs between $195,900 and $222,900 annually through FY 2029. Special fund revenues and expenditures may increase if the Proposed Programs Collaborative Grant Fund receives appropriations. Higher education institutions and local community colleges face indeterminate revenue and expenditure impacts from revised program approval timelines and grant funding.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MHEC is the primary implementing agency for the bill, tasked with reforming the academic program approval process, creating an administrative procedures guide, establishing the Program Review Process Advisory Council, administering the Proposed Programs Collaborative Grant Fund, and updating the State Plan for Higher Education.
As the alternate listing for MHEC, this agency is the primary regulator and administrator of the academic program approval and institutional mission statement reforms required by the bill.

The bill mandates that the Department of Labor have at least one full-time staff member dedicated to compiling workforce needs data and collaborating with MHEC and Commerce, resulting in direct operational and fiscal impacts.

The bill requires the Department of Commerce to compile state and regional workforce data and collaborate with MHEC and the Department of Labor to establish baseline workforce data informing postsecondary education policy.

Morgan State University is directly affected as an independent public university subject to revised program approval processes, mission statement review, and a specific priority lead-time provision for emerging workforce need graduate programs.

USM and its constituent institutions (including UMCP, Bowie State, Coppin State, and UMES) are directly governed by the new graduate program letter-of-intent requirements, emerging workforce need approval processes, and mission statement reviews.

MHEC must consult with the MLDS Center for workforce data, and the fiscal note indicates a fiscal impact of at least $100,000 for MLDS to incorporate workforce and labor market projection data into its system.
As a public senior higher education institution, SMCM is subject to the new program approval procedures, biannual letter of intent submissions, and mission statement review standards.

The bill requires MHEC to consult with the Office of the Attorney General in adopting regulations for standards to analyze program objections alleging unnecessary duplication in violation of equal educational opportunity laws.
The Treasurer is required to hold and invest the newly established Proposed Programs Collaborative Grant Fund.
The Comptroller is required to account for the newly established Proposed Programs Collaborative Grant Fund.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires each investor-owned electric company to file opt-in time-of-use tariffs with the Public Service Commission by July 1, 2025. Mandates that investor-owned electric companies propose reasonable enrollment targets to attempt to achieve by January 1, 2028. Directs the Commission to adopt regulations by May 1, 2025, establishing expedited interconnection processes for bidirectional electric vehicle systems. Requires the Commission to develop a program for electric companies to compensate distributed energy resources on a pay-for-performance basis. Authorizes the Commission to approve or require upfront customer incentives or rebates for renewable on-site generating systems. Authorizes investor-owned electric companies to recover reasonable costs incurred under these programs.
qa_results.responsible_party: Public Service Commission; Maryland Energy Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: investor-owned electric companies; municipal electric utilities; electric cooperatives; distributed energy resource owners and aggregators; electricity customers, including low- and moderate-income households; bidirectional electric vehicle owners
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund expenditures and matching assessment revenues for the Public Service Commission increase by $410,628 in FY 2025, including $250,000 annually for consultant costs through FY 2028. Expenditures and revenues for the Office of People's Counsel may also increase beginning in FY 2025.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Public Service Commission is the primary regulator and implementing agency for the bill. It is tasked with reviewing and approving time-of-use tariffs, adopting regulations for bidirectional EV grid interconnection, establishing pilot programs and tariffs for distributed energy resources, and submitting evaluative reports to the General Assembly.

As the advocate for residential utility customers before the PSC, OPC will participate in the complex rate design, tariff filings, and regulatory proceedings mandated by the bill, with potential fiscal impacts for staff and technical consultants.

The bill explicitly requires the Public Service Commission to consult with the Maryland Energy Administration when approving or requiring upfront incentives or rebates to align and supplement existing State and federal clean energy programs.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands health insurance coverage requirements for supplemental breast examinations to include image-guided breast biopsies without cost sharing. Requires insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations to cover recommended lung cancer screening and follow-up diagnostic imaging. Prohibits covered entities from subjecting required lung cancer screening or follow-up diagnostic imaging to prior authorization. Limits cost-sharing requirements for lung cancer screening or imaging to amounts charged for breast cancer screening or diagnosis. Applies to all applicable policies, contracts, and health benefit plans issued, delivered, or renewed on or after January 1, 2025.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Commercial health insurers, nonprofit health service plans, health maintenance organizations, and insured individuals seeking breast or lung cancer screenings and diagnostic imaging
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal increase in special fund revenues for the Maryland Insurance Administration in FY 2025 from $125 rate and form filing fees. Form reviews can be handled with existing budgeted resources. There is no impact on the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program, but there is a potential minimal expenditure increase for local governments purchasing fully insured health plans.
