agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Insurance Administration regulates private health insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations in the state. MIA is responsible for enforcing these new coverage and prior authorization requirements and reviewing policy rate and form filings, which will generate a minimal increase in special fund revenues.

DBM administers the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program. While the fiscal note indicates the program already complies with the bill's requirements and will experience no fiscal impact, DBM is responsible for monitoring state health benefit mandates.
MHBE oversees individual and small group qualified health plans offered on Maryland Health Connection, which must comply with state health insurance benefit mandates and coverage rules.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of the Environment to allow nonuniform payment schedules for certain Clean Water Commerce Account contracts. The requirement applies on request for projects involving construction, reconstruction, or rehabilitation. These payment schedules must vary the cost-per-pound of reduced nitrogen based on agreed performance milestones. Prohibits the first performance milestone from occurring before construction, reconstruction, or rehabilitation is complete. Authorizes the Department to require a minimum final payment to ensure agreed environmental outcomes. Authorizes additional financial protections, including performance bonds or letters of credit, for contract awards exceeding $500,000.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment
qa_results.stakeholders: Owners and contractors of environmental outcome projects, local governments, and small businesses participating in the Clean Water Commerce Account
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund administrative expenditures for the Maryland Department of the Environment increase by an unknown but likely modest amount beginning in fiscal 2025. Overall finances of the Clean Water Commerce Account are unaffected, though contract payment timing shifts from level to nonuniform schedules. Local governments and small businesses seeking project funding may experience significant financial effects.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 1266 directly governs the Maryland Department of the Environment's administration of the Clean Water Commerce Account. It mandates MDE to allow nonuniform payment schedules on request for certain projects and authorizes MDE to require minimum final payments and financial protections for large contracts, resulting in modest administrative expenditure impacts for the agency.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters notice requirements for alcoholic beverages license applications before the Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore County. Requires the Board to publish notice of an application twice in one local newspaper of general circulation. Authorizes the Board to fulfill the notice requirement by posting hearing notices online at least 14 days beforehand. Retains the requirement to post physical notice at the proposed location at least 10 days before the hearing. Takes effect July 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore County
qa_results.stakeholders: Alcoholic beverages license applicants in Baltimore County, local newspapers, and Baltimore County residents
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state fiscal effect. Baltimore County expenditures decrease by as much as approximately $40,000 annually beginning in fiscal 2025 from reduced newspaper publishing expenses. Local revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland regulates the state's alcoholic beverage industry; however, this bill strictly alters local hearing notice procedures for the Baltimore County Board of License Commissioners and has no state fiscal or operational impact.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits motor vehicle manufacturers, distributors, and factory branches from refusing delivery of vehicles upon receiving an electronic order. Applies delivery requirements to new motor vehicles, new two-stage vehicles, and truck component parts. Requires deliveries in reasonable quantities and within a reasonable time under existing franchise or contract agreements. Maintains existing exemptions for failures caused by labor strikes, government regulations, or other non-fault causes. Takes effect October 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Transportation
qa_results.stakeholders: licensed motor vehicle dealers, motor vehicle distributors, motor vehicle manufacturers, and factory branches
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on State or local finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Motor Vehicle Administration regulates motor vehicle dealers, manufacturers, and related automotive businesses under Title 15 of the Transportation Article, which this bill directly amends.
The Department of Transportation oversees the Motor Vehicle Administration and the enforcement of the Maryland Vehicle Law governing commercial vehicle transactions.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the governing body of a county or municipality and Baltimore City to designate tourism zones. Allows a designated tourism zone to also be designated as an arts and entertainment district. Authorizes local jurisdictions to exempt qualifying tourism enterprises from local admissions and amusement taxes. Authorizes local governing bodies to grant property tax credits on qualifying real and personal property. Requires establishing jurisdictions to notify the Comptroller regarding designated zones and participating qualifying enterprises.
qa_results.responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland; Mayor and City Council of Baltimore City; governing bodies of Maryland counties and municipalities
qa_results.stakeholders: For-profit and nonprofit qualifying tourism enterprises, commercial property owners in designated tourism zones, and Maryland local governments
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on State finances. Local property tax and admissions and amusement tax revenues may decrease beginning in fiscal 2025 if local jurisdictions designate tourism zones and grant property tax credits and tax exemptions. Indeterminate statewide impact; Baltimore City estimates an annual revenue decrease of up to $6.4 million.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires local jurisdictions establishing a tourism zone to notify the Comptroller prior to the effective date and provide details regarding qualifying tourism enterprises receiving local admissions and amusement tax exemptions.

The Department of Commerce oversees statewide economic development and administers the Arts and Entertainment District program, which the bill specifically clarifies can co-exist alongside newly created local tourism zones.

As the agency tasked with stimulating Maryland's tourism economy, the establishment of local tourism zones and local tax incentives directly aligns with and touches upon its core mission of fostering travel and tourism development.

qa_results.bill_summary: Consolidates two separate public school leadership training programs into a single unified training program. Requires the State Superintendent, county superintendents, and board chairs and vice chairs to complete the program. Encourages senior instructional staff, other school board members, and principals to complete the training when practicable. Establishes a 12-month program duration provided through both in-person and virtual sessions. Expands program curriculum to include research on attracting and retaining diverse teachers and an inclusive workforce.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education; Accountability and Implementation Board
qa_results.stakeholders: State Superintendent of Schools, county superintendents of schools, chairs, vice chairs, and members of the State Board of Education, local boards of education, and the Accountability and Implementation Board, senior instruction-related staff, and public school principals
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local expenditures experience minimal net impacts. Shorter program duration and virtual options may yield minor savings, while training attendance requirements for Accountability and Implementation Board leadership create minimal new costs. Exact figures are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE), in collaboration with the Accountability and Implementation Board, to establish and implement a unified school leadership training program, establishes curriculum requirements, and mandates completion by the State Superintendent of Schools and other key educational leaders.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the Accountability and Implementation Board (AIB) with co-developing the school leadership training program alongside MSDE and mandates that the chair and vice chair of the AIB complete the training program, resulting in operational and fiscal impacts noted in the fiscal note.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Health to develop and implement an education campaign on prostate, lung, and breast cancer prevention. Directs the campaign to target communities disproportionately impacted by prostate, lung, and breast cancer. Requires the department to collaborate with health care providers, hospitals, and specialized health care associations. Requires the campaign to promote cancer screenings, clinical trials, and legislation reducing cost barriers to prevention services. Sets deadlines of December 1, 2026, for campaign development and January 1, 2027, for campaign implementation. Mandates that the Governor appropriate not more than $750,000 total from the Cigarette Restitution Fund through fiscal 2030.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Communities disproportionately impacted by prostate, lung, and breast cancer, as well as health care providers, hospitals, and health care associations.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund expenditures from the Cigarette Restitution Fund shift up to $750,000 across fiscal 2026 through 2030 from existing programs to MDH for the campaign. Revenues and overall expenditures are not materially affected, though general fund expenditures may increase by up to $750,000 to backfill special funds diverted from Medicaid.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Maryland Department of Health to develop, implement, and establish measurable goals for a three-year public education campaign on prostate, lung, and breast cancer prevention, as well as report on its progress annually.

The bill includes a statutory mandate requiring the Governor to include an appropriation for the public education campaign in the annual budget bill from the Cigarette Restitution Fund for fiscal years 2026 through 2030.

As the agency responsible for preparing the state budget and managing fiscal allocations, DBM is impacted by the mandated appropriation from the Cigarette Restitution Fund and was consulted for the fiscal analysis.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Public Service Commission to evaluate revised schedules, sizes, or pricing for previously approved Round 2 offshore wind projects. Authorizes Round 1 offshore wind projects to seek approval to increase offshore wind renewable energy credits and modify project schedules. Directs the Commission to develop a plan to achieve 8,500 megawatts of offshore wind energy capacity by 2031. Alters Department of General Services procurement requirements by removing the annual procurement cap and mandating a second solicitation. Mandates specific procurement contract terms to facilitate low-cost financing, including waiving automatic termination for nonappropriation.
qa_results.responsible_party: Public Service Commission; Department of General Services; Maryland Energy Administration; Department of Natural Resources; Maryland Department of the Environment
qa_results.stakeholders: offshore wind energy developers, electric utility ratepayers, and State agencies procuring electricity
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $400,000 across FY 2025 and FY 2026 for Department of General Services consultant costs, while Department of Natural Resources expenditures may increase by up to $350,000 in FY 2025. PSC and MEA can largely absorb costs with existing resources. The net long-term impact on State electricity expenditures from altered offshore wind power purchase agreements is unknown but potentially significant. No direct local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Public Service Commission is the primary implementing agency tasked with opening a revised Round 2 offshore wind project proceeding, evaluating revised applications, amending Round 1 offshore wind project orders, and developing a comprehensive plan and report to achieve 8,500 megawatts of offshore wind energy by 2031.

The Department of General Services is directed to execute competitive solicitations and procurements for offshore wind energy power purchase agreements, manage contract terms and labor peace agreements, and assist the Public Service Commission with the offshore wind capacity plan, incurring an estimated $400,000 in consultant costs.

The Maryland Energy Administration is granted statutory access to confidential information submitted during revised Round 2 proceedings and is specifically required to assist the Public Service Commission in developing the offshore wind capacity plan.

The Department of Natural Resources is explicitly tasked with assisting the Public Service Commission in developing the state's offshore wind capacity plan and may incur up to $350,000 in consultant costs in FY 2025 to participate.

The Department of the Environment is explicitly named in the legislation to assist the Public Service Commission in the development of the plan to reach 8,500 megawatts of offshore wind energy capacity by 2031.

As the independent representative of residential utility consumers in Public Service Commission proceedings, the Office of the People's Counsel is impacted by regulatory reviews and determinations regarding offshore wind renewable energy credit pricing and ratepayer protections.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the definition of providing esthetic services under the Maryland Cosmetologists Act. Adds cosmetic microneedling, exfoliating, and toning of the skin or scalp to authorized esthetic services. Includes eyelash extensions, superficial epidermal exfoliation, nonablative skin rejuvenation, and relaxation or beautification treatments. Authorizes removing superfluous hair by electrical, mechanical, or other means except laser light-based devices. Excludes the diagnosis of illness, disease, or injury and performing ablation of the dermis or hypodermis. Takes effect October 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Cosmetologists
qa_results.stakeholders: Licensed cosmetologists, senior cosmetologists, estheticians, and cosmetology small businesses in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on State Board of Cosmetologists finances or operations; implementation requires existing resources only. No local fiscal impact. Small businesses may experience a meaningful positive effect by offering and charging for expanded esthetic services.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor houses the State Board of Cosmetologists, which licenses and regulates cosmetologists and estheticians. The bill directly alters the scope of practice and statutory definition of 'provide esthetic services' enforced by the Board.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Health to develop a process for providing information about the State's earned income tax credit. Applies this requirement when providing information to enrollees and potential enrollees of specified health programs. Covers the Maryland Medical Assistance Program, Maryland Children's Health Program, and Qualified State Long-Term Care Insurance Partnership. Extends the process to individuals receiving services under the Senior Prescription Drug Assistance Program and Prescription Drug Repository Program. Requires the Department of Aging to provide periodic training on the credit to the Maryland Access Point network.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Maryland Department of Aging
qa_results.stakeholders: Enrollees and potential enrollees in the Maryland Medical Assistance Program, Maryland Children's Health Program, and Qualified State Long-Term Care Insurance Partnership; individuals receiving services under the Senior Prescription Drug Assistance Program or the Prescription Drug Repository Program; and staff and clients of the Maryland Access Point network.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Agency operational requirements can be handled with existing budgeted resources. To the extent the bill increases uptake of State and local earned income and poverty level tax credits, State general fund revenues and local revenues may decrease beginning in fiscal 2025. Montgomery County expenditures for its earned income tax credit supplement program may also increase; specific figures cannot be reliably estimated.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 1304 directly mandates the Maryland Department of Health to develop a process for providing information regarding the availability of the State's earned income tax credit to enrollees and recipients of several MDH-administered programs, including Medicaid, the Maryland Children's Health Program, and prescription drug assistance programs.

HB 1304 directly mandates the Department of Aging to provide periodic training to the Maryland Access Point network to raise awareness regarding the availability of the State's earned income tax credit.

The Comptroller of Maryland administers the state's tax system and the Earned Income Tax Credit. Increased awareness and uptake of the credit resulting from this bill will impact state income tax collections and tax credit claims.

The fiscal note highlights that the Qualified State Long-Term Care Insurance Partnership is jointly administered by the Maryland Department of Health and the Maryland Insurance Administration, which may require MIA's assistance in distributing EITC information to current or prospective policyholders.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits a person from recording a deed or other instrument known to contain false information. Establishes that a violator is guilty of a misdemeanor subject to a fine not exceeding $500. Requires prosecution for a violation to be instituted within three years after the offense occurred. Authorizes a court in a quiet title action to award costs and reasonable attorney's fees to either party. Applies fee awards when a claim or defense relates to recording an instrument with false information.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary
qa_results.stakeholders: property owners, individuals recording deeds and land instruments, and litigants in quiet title actions
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Potential minimal increase in State general fund revenues from District Court fines. State and local government operations and finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a new misdemeanor offense for recording property instruments with known false information, establishes a three-year statute of limitations, and authorizes courts to award costs and reasonable attorney's fees in actions to quiet title related to such violations. This directly affects District and Circuit Court operations and judicial case processing.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes code counties in the Southern Maryland class to adopt specific subdivision regulations for recreational purposes. Permits these counties to require the dedication of real property for recreation. Authorizes counties to allow a fee payment in lieu of dedication. Requires counties to use fee revenue to purchase, develop, and improve real property for recreational facilities. Takes effect October 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Southern Maryland code county governing bodies; Charles County Board of County Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Land developers, subdividers, and residents in Southern Maryland code counties (currently Charles County)
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not materially affected. Charles County revenues and expenditures may increase to the extent the county establishes and collects fees in lieu of property dedication to purchase, develop, and improve recreational facilities.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Land Use Article regarding local subdivision regulations and property dedication for recreational purposes in Southern Maryland code counties. The Department of Planning is the state's principal agency for land use planning and advisory assistance to local jurisdictions on planning and zoning matters.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes individuals under private home detention monitoring as a condition of probation to earn compliance credits. Expands the definition of abatement to include an end to active home detention. Requires the court or Maryland Parole Commission to adjust home detention periods based on accrued credits. Requires private home detention monitoring agencies to report compliance upon request by the Division of Parole and Probation. Mandates that compliance reports include court conditions, all infractions, and relevant information.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services; Division of Parole and Probation
qa_results.stakeholders: individuals on probation monitored by private home detention monitoring agencies; licensed private home detention monitoring agencies
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Potential minimal increase in Judiciary expenditures to process adjustments to home detention periods, with no material impact on State or local finances. State revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS oversees the Division of Parole and Probation (DPP), which is the primary implementing agency tasked with tracking and awarding earned compliance credits, requesting compliance reports from private home detention monitoring agencies, placing individuals on abatement, and regulating private home detention monitoring agencies.

The Judiciary and state courts are responsible for ordering private home detention monitoring as a condition of probation and adjusting the terms or duration of home detention upon recommendation from the Division of Parole and Probation.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the minimum age of an individual who may be employed by an alcoholic beverages license holder in Allegany County. Authorizes an Allegany County license holder to employ individuals between the ages of 16 and 21 years. Requires an individual to be at least 18 years old to sell or serve beer, light wine, and liquor. Takes effect July 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Allegany County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Alcoholic beverages license holders in Allegany County and individuals ages 16 and 17 seeking employment at licensed establishments
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state fiscal effect. The bill does not materially affect Allegany County operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland regulates the alcoholic beverage industry in the state. While this legislation applies specifically to local retail license holders in Allegany County, it relates to the broader regulatory framework governing alcoholic beverage establishments.

The Maryland Department of Labor oversees and enforces state labor and employment standards, including youth employment regulations, which intersects with altering the minimum allowable employment age for individuals working at licensed establishments.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Commission on Health Equity to develop and monitor a statewide health equity plan. Designates the Secretary of Health and the Executive Director of the Health Services Cost Review Commission as cochairs. Reconstitutes the Commission's membership by removing twelve State agency heads and adding diverse health sector representatives. Directs the Commission to coordinate with specified health entities to establish an advisory committee on health equity data. Extends the final reporting deadline and termination date of the Commission on Public Health to June 30, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Commission on Health Equity; Maryland Department of Health; Health Services Cost Review Commission; Commission on Public Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland residents experiencing health disparities, hospitals, federally qualified health centers, commercial health insurers, managed care organizations, community-based organizations, healthcare clinicians, and patients from underserved communities
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures and revenues are not materially affected. Additional agency workloads, advisory committee coordination, member expense reimbursements, and the one-year extension of the Commission on Public Health can be absorbed within existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDH provides primary staff support to the Maryland Commission on Health Equity (MCHE), the Secretary of Health co-chairs MCHE and appoints several new members, and the bill extends reporting and operations for the Commission on Public Health which studies MDH capabilities.

The Executive Director of HSCRC is designated to co-chair MCHE, advise on member appointments, collaborate on an advisory committee for health equity data, and integrate the statewide health equity plan required under CMMI/Total Cost of Care models.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly restructures the purpose, membership, and duties of the Maryland Commission on Health Equity and alters reporting timelines and the termination date of the Commission on Public Health.

The Executive Director of the Maryland Health Care Commission is added as a statutory member of MCHE, and health care payers reporting to MHCC are designated data sources for the commission's health equity data set.

The bill receives interim and final reports from the Commission on Public Health and removes the Governor's duty to designate the chair of the Maryland Commission on Health Equity in favor of statutory co-chairs.
The Maryland Insurance Commissioner (or designee) is retained as an active statutory member of the Maryland Commission on Health Equity.
The Secretary of Aging (or designee) is retained as a statutory member of the Maryland Commission on Health Equity.
The Secretary of Budget and Management (or designee) is retained as a statutory member of the Maryland Commission on Health Equity.
The Secretary of Disabilities (or designee) is retained as a statutory member of the Maryland Commission on Health Equity.
The State Superintendent of Schools (or designee) is retained as a statutory member of the Maryland Commission on Health Equity.
The Secretary of Housing and Community Development (or designee) is retained as a statutory member of the Maryland Commission on Health Equity.
The Secretary of Human Services (or designee) is retained as a statutory member of the Maryland Commission on Health Equity.
The Secretary of Planning (or designee) is retained as a statutory member of the Maryland Commission on Health Equity.
The bill removes the Secretary of Agriculture from statutory membership on the Maryland Commission on Health Equity.
The bill removes the Secretary of Commerce from statutory membership on the Maryland Commission on Health Equity.
The bill removes the Secretary of General Services from statutory membership on the Maryland Commission on Health Equity.
The bill removes the Secretary of Information Technology from statutory membership on the Maryland Commission on Health Equity.
The bill removes the Secretary of Juvenile Services from statutory membership on the Maryland Commission on Health Equity.
The bill removes the Secretary of Labor from statutory membership on the Maryland Commission on Health Equity.
The bill removes the Secretary of Natural Resources from statutory membership on the Maryland Commission on Health Equity.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill removes the Commissioner of Correction from statutory membership on the Maryland Commission on Health Equity.
The bill removes the Secretary of Transportation from statutory membership on the Maryland Commission on Health Equity.
The bill removes the Secretary of Veterans Affairs from statutory membership on the Maryland Commission on Health Equity.
The bill removes the Secretary of the Environment from statutory membership on the Maryland Commission on Health Equity.
The bill removes the Secretary of State Police from statutory membership on the Maryland Commission on Health Equity.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals the termination date of the Continuing the CORE Partnership Fund, extending the fund indefinitely. Requires the Governor to include a $50,000,000 appropriation to the Fund annually beginning in fiscal year 2026. Continues the Fund's mission to assist in expeditiously removing blighted property within Baltimore City. Directs the Department of Housing and Community Development to partner with the Maryland Stadium Authority and Baltimore City. Authorizes fund expenditures for property removal and related administrative expenses.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development
qa_results.stakeholders: Baltimore City government, residents and property owners in Baltimore City neighborhoods with blighted properties, and the Maryland Stadium Authority
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State PAYGO general fund expenditures increase by $50.0 million annually beginning in FY 2026 due to the mandated budget appropriation. Local effect on Baltimore City depends on whether the mandated funds supplement or replace planned general obligation bond funding for Project CORE.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DHCD is the primary administering agency of the Continuing the CORE Partnership Fund, responsible for overseeing the removal of blighted property under Project CORE in Baltimore City and utilizing the fund's appropriations.
MSA is explicitly named in the statute as DHCD's partner entity working in conjunction with Baltimore City to demolish and remove blighted property supported by the fund.
The bill mandates that the Governor include an annual appropriation of $50,000,000 to the Continuing the CORE Partnership Fund in the state budget bill beginning in FY 2026.
DBM is responsible for drafting and managing the state budget, which will be fiscally impacted by incorporating the mandatory $50,000,000 annual PAYGO general fund appropriation starting in FY 2026.
The statute specifically designates the State Treasurer to hold the Continuing the CORE Partnership Fund separately and invest its funds in the same manner as other state moneys.
The statute explicitly mandates that the Comptroller account for the Continuing the CORE Partnership Fund.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands quarterly reporting requirements for health insurance carriers submitting appeals and grievances data to the Maryland Insurance Commissioner. Requires each carrier to report the number of members entitled to health care benefits under Maryland policies, plans, or certificates. Requires each carrier to report the number of clean claims for reimbursement processed. Directs the Commissioner to include this information in an annual summary report to the Governor and General Assembly.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Commissioner
qa_results.stakeholders: Health insurance carriers operating in Maryland and individuals enrolled in health benefit plans in the State
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not substantively change State activities or operations and has no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires health insurance carriers to submit additional data on covered members and clean claims processed to the Maryland Insurance Commissioner quarterly. The Maryland Insurance Administration is responsible for collecting this data and incorporating it into its annual summary report on health care appeals and grievances.
The Maryland Insurance Commissioner is required to submit a copy of the annual summary report on appeals, grievances, and claims data to the Governor.
The annual summary report compiled by the Insurance Commissioner incorporates information provided by the Secretary of Health regarding health maintenance organizations.

qa_results.bill_summary: Reduces the term of office for Howard County agricultural preservation advisory board members from five years to three years. Authorizes members serving on October 1, 2024, to complete the remainder of their five-year terms. Requires each subsequent member appointed after October 1, 2024, to serve a three-year term. Maintains the restriction prohibiting members from serving more than two consecutive full terms.
qa_results.responsible_party: Howard County Agricultural Preservation Advisory Board; Howard County Government
qa_results.stakeholders: members and prospective appointees of the Howard County Agricultural Preservation Advisory Board and commercial farm owner-operators in Howard County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal effect. The bill does not materially affect Howard County operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Agriculture Article concerning county agricultural preservation advisory boards, which advise the Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation (MALPF) housed within the Maryland Department of Agriculture.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations to cover hearing aids for adults. Mandates coverage for medically appropriate hearing aids prescribed, fitted, and dispensed by a licensed audiologist. Authorizes carriers to limit coverage to $1,400 per hearing aid for each ear every 36 months. Allows insured individuals to choose higher-priced hearing aids by paying the difference without penalty to the provider. Applies to health insurance policies issued, delivered, or renewed on or after January 1, 2025.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: adult health insurance policyholders, health insurers, nonprofit health service plans, health maintenance organizations, and licensed audiologists
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal special fund revenue increase for the Maryland Insurance Administration in FY 2025 from $125 rate and form filing fees, which can be reviewed with existing resources. No effect on the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program and no material effect on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MIA is the primary regulator enforcing health insurance mandates in Maryland. It will be responsible for reviewing policy and contract form filings from carriers to ensure compliance with the adult hearing aid mandate and will receive minimal special fund revenue from filing fees.

DBM administers the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program, which must be monitored for compliance with state health benefit mandates (though it currently already complies with the bill's requirements).

MHBE administers qualified health plans and the individual/small group marketplace, where federal Essential Health Benefits (EHB) and State benchmark plan rules interact with state-mandated hearing aid benefits.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: ODHH promotes the welfare and accessibility needs of deaf and hard of hearing Marylanders, making mandated insurance coverage for adult hearing aids directly relevant to its policy and advocacy focus.

MDH oversees health care policy and health professional licensing boards (including licensed audiologists who must prescribe, fit, and dispense the mandated hearing aids) and served as an information source for the legislation.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals the wholesale monopoly of the Liquor Control Board for Wicomico County over wine and liquor sales. Authorizes holders of Class A, Class B, Class C, and Class D licenses to purchase alcoholic beverages from wholesalers. Repeals the restriction prohibiting licensed wholesalers from delivering liquor directly to retail licensees in Wicomico County. Repeals the authority of the Liquor Control Board to conduct wine tasting promotional events in dispensaries. Takes effect July 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Liquor Control Board for Wicomico County
qa_results.stakeholders: Class A, Class B, Class C, and Class D alcoholic beverages license holders in Wicomico County, licensed alcohol wholesalers, and Wicomico County dispensaries
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Wicomico County revenues decrease to the extent retail licensees purchase wine and liquor from private wholesalers rather than county dispensaries, though specific figures cannot be estimated at this time. Local enforcement activities can be handled with existing resources, and State finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland regulates the alcohol industry and issues state wholesaler's licenses. The bill alters distribution and sales rules for state-licensed Class 1 and Class 2 wholesalers in Wicomico County by repealing the county dispensary monopoly.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes Class B beer, wine, and liquor license holders in Wicomico County to purchase liquor from licensed wholesalers. Permits these license holders to continue purchasing liquor for retail sale from a county dispensary. Prohibits a county dispensary from charging more than 15% above wholesale operating cost. Allows Class B restaurant license holders holding Class 9 limited distillery licenses to sell manufactured products. Permits those sales for on-premises and off-premises consumption at the Class B licensed location.
qa_results.responsible_party: Wicomico County Board of License Commissioners; Wicomico County Liquor Control Board
qa_results.stakeholders: Class B beer, wine, and liquor license holders in Wicomico County, licensed alcoholic beverage wholesalers, and the Wicomico County dispensary
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal impact. Wicomico County revenues decrease to the extent that Class B license holders choose to purchase liquor from licensed wholesalers rather than through the county dispensary; specific figures are unavailable. County enforcement can be handled with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters local alcoholic beverage purchasing rules and retail privileges for certain license holders in Wicomico County. While the bill has no state fiscal impact, it has minor relevance to the Comptroller's broad oversight and administration of the state's alcohol industry and related excise taxes.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the governing body of Howard County and real property owners to enter into payment in lieu of taxes agreements. Exempts qualifying real property from county property taxes when owners agree to pay a negotiated amount. Requires owners to maintain moderate income housing units exceeding the minimum number required by local zoning laws. Requires the Howard County Executive to publish the payment calculation methodology online and reevaluate it every five years. Prohibits entering an agreement unless the negotiated payment is determined in accordance with the most recently published methodology.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governing body of Howard County; County Executive of Howard County
qa_results.stakeholders: Owners and developers of moderate income housing in Howard County, moderate income households seeking housing in Howard County, and Howard County government
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Howard County property tax revenues may decrease beginning in fiscal 2025 due to property tax exemptions for qualifying moderate income housing developments. Revenue losses will be mitigated by negotiated PILOT payments, with the net impact depending on the number and assessed value of participating properties. There is no state fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Although the bill directly authorizes and applies only to Howard County to establish payment in lieu of taxes (PILOT) agreements for moderate-income housing, it relates to broader state housing affordability goals and moderate-income housing policies within the scope of the Department of Housing and Community Development.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Department of Natural Resources and Baltimore City to convene focus group meetings on establishing Gwynns Falls State Park. Directs both entities to develop a list of priority needs and associated cost assessments for park operations and improvements. Requires the Department and Baltimore City to establish a stakeholder advisory committee on park scope and management. Requires the Department to report to the General Assembly by December 1, 2025, regarding suitable properties and needed funding.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources; Baltimore City
qa_results.stakeholders: Baltimore City residents, local park visitors, and community, environmental, and historic preservation organizations near the proposed park site
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general and special fund expenditures increase by as much as $70,000 in FY 2025 and $30,000 in FY 2026 if a consultant is needed. Baltimore City can implement the bill using existing budgeted resources. State and local revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DNR is the primary implementing agency responsible for collaborating with Baltimore City to convene focus groups, establish a stakeholder advisory committee, assess priority park operational and capital improvement needs, and submit a report to the General Assembly.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill statutorily creates a stakeholder advisory committee composed of community, environmental, and historical preservation representatives to advise DNR and Baltimore City on the scope and management of Gwynns Falls State Park.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the membership composition of the seven-member State Board of Cosmetologists. Requires one board member to be a licensed esthetician. Reduces the number of consumer members serving on the board from two to one. Maintains requirements for four licensed cosmetologists and one private cosmetology school affiliate. Takes effect October 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Cosmetologists; Maryland Department of Labor; Governor
qa_results.stakeholders: licensed estheticians, consumer representatives, licensed cosmetologists, and private cosmetology schools
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on State operations or finances, and no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Cosmetologists is an occupational licensing board housed within the Maryland Department of Labor, directly impacting its board composition and governance.

The Office of Appointments vets and manages candidate recommendations for gubernatorial appointments to state boards, including the newly designated licensed esthetician position and altered consumer seat on the State Board of Cosmetologists.
The Governor is statutory authority responsible for appointing the members of the State Board of Cosmetologists with the advice of the Secretary of Labor.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes a Class DBR brewery license and a Class DDS distillery permit in Frederick County. Authorizes the Frederick County Board of License Commissioners to issue a Class DBR license to a Class 5 brewery licensee. Allows Class DBR licensees to sell food, nonalcoholic beverages, and brewed beer for on- and off-premises consumption. Authorizes the board to issue a Class DDS permit to a Class 1 distillery licensee. Allows Class DDS permit holders to sell food, nonalcoholic beverages, and designated distilled spirits for on- and off-premises consumption. Requires the board to adopt regulations and set annual fees for the license and permit.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Frederick County
qa_results.stakeholders: Class 5 brewery licensees and Class 1 distillery licensees in Frederick County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Frederick County revenues may increase from new license and permit fees set by the board. Frederick County can handle any additional enforcement activity using existing budgeted resources. There is no state fiscal effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland regulates the state's alcoholic beverage industry and oversees state manufacturer's licenses (including Class 1 distillery and Class 5 brewery licenses), upon which the local Frederick County Class DBR license and Class DDS permit are based.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland State Department of Education to develop guidelines for an antibias training program for school employees. Mandates consultation with the Professional Standards and Teacher Education Board to create and periodically update the guidelines. Requires each county board of education to develop or update antibias training based on the guidelines. Requires county boards every other year to train public school employees who frequently interact with students. Mandates that training be job-embedded, paid professional development provided during nonteaching time. Authorizes nonpublic schools participating in State-funded education programs to develop and provide similar antibias training.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education; Professional Standards and Teacher Education Board
qa_results.stakeholders: public school employees with frequent student interaction, public school teachers and students, county boards of education, and nonpublic schools participating in State-funded education programs
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $100,000 in FY 2025 for the Maryland State Department of Education to contract with a consultant to develop the training guidelines. Local school system expenditures increase, likely minimally, to develop training programs and provide paid professional development to specified staff every other year.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 1386 requires the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) to develop and periodically update comprehensive guidelines for an antibias training program for public school employees, resulting in an estimated general fund expenditure of approximately $100,000 to contract for program development.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires MSDE to develop the antibias training guidelines in consultation with the Professional Standards and Teacher Education Board (PSTEB).

qa_results.bill_summary: Voids noncompete and conflict of interest provisions for licensed veterinary practitioners and veterinary technicians. Voids noncompete clauses for licensed health care professionals providing direct patient care who earn $350,000 or less annually. Restricts noncompete clauses for higher-earning direct patient care health professionals to one year and 10 miles. Requires employers of higher-earning direct patient care health professionals to notify patients upon request of new practice locations. Directs the Maryland Health Care Commission to study private equity and hospital consolidation impacts on the health care market. Applies the health care noncompete restrictions to employment contracts executed on or after July 1, 2025.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Health Care Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: licensed veterinary practitioners, licensed veterinary technicians, licensed health care professionals providing direct patient care, employers of veterinary and health care professionals, and patients
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures increase by approximately $150,000 in fiscal 2025 for the Maryland Health Care Commission to hire a private consultant to study the health care market. Revenues are not affected, and local governments experience no material fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates the Maryland Health Care Commission to contract with a private consultant to conduct a comprehensive study on the health care market (including private equity impacts and hospital consolidations) and submit a report by January 1, 2025, resulting in a direct special fund expenditure of $150,000 in FY 2025.

The bill amends Title 3 of the Labor and Employment Article regarding noncompete and conflict of interest provisions in employment contracts, which relates directly to the Department of Labor's administration and enforcement of state labor and employment standards.

The bill extends noncompete restrictions to veterinary practitioners and veterinary technicians licensed under Title 2, Subtitle 3 of the Agriculture Article, which is overseen by the Department of Agriculture.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals the scheduled termination of the School Safety Grant Program to maintain its funding. Reduces the mandated annual appropriation to the Nancy K. Kopp Public School Facilities Priority Fund to $70,000,000 beginning in fiscal year 2027. Establishes a 100% State share of eligible costs for qualifying public high school major renovation projects. Alters distribution timelines and governance requirements for Prince George's County public-private partnership school construction agreements. Establishes the Workgroup on the Assessment and Funding of School Facilities.
qa_results.responsible_party: Interagency Commission on School Construction; Maryland Stadium Authority; Department of Legislative Services
qa_results.stakeholders: public school students and staff; local school systems; Prince George's County Board of Education; public school systems in counties qualifying for 100% State construction cost share
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures increase by $54.0 million in FY 2025 due to an accelerated distribution to Prince George's County for its public-private partnership agreement. Beginning in FY 2027, Priority Fund special fund revenues and expenditures decrease by $10.0 million annually, offset by continuing $10.0 million in general fund expenditures for the School Safety Grant Program (resulting in no net general fund impact). Prince George's County local revenues increase by $54.0 million in FY 2025.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: IAC is the primary state entity responsible for administering the public school construction programs affected by the bill, including the School Safety Grant Program, the Nancy K. The State Superintendent of Schools (or designee) is designated as a statutory member of the Workgroup on the Assessment and Funding of School Facilities, and the bill directly shapes public school capital improvements statewide.

The State Treasurer (or designee) is a member of the Workgroup on the Assessment and Funding of School Facilities, and the Treasurer is statutorily required to hold and invest the Nancy K. Kopp Public School Facilities Priority Fund.

The Secretary of Budget and Management (or designee) serves on the Workgroup on the Assessment and Funding of School Facilities, and the bill alters mandated appropriations and budget distributions for school construction funds.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates the Workgroup on the Assessment and Funding of School Facilities to evaluate school facility condition indices and provide recommendations on funding decisions to the Governor and General Assembly.
The Secretary of General Services (or designee) is named as a member of the Workgroup on the Assessment and Funding of School Facilities.
The Comptroller is statutorily designated to account for the Nancy K. Kopp Public School Facilities Priority Fund.

The bill adjusts mandated annual budget appropriations required to be provided by the Governor for school construction programs and requires the Workgroup to report its findings and recommendations to the Governor.

qa_results.bill_summary: Broadens the scope of State electric system planning goals and reporting beyond distribution to the entire electric system. Requires electric companies to report at least quarterly on federal funding applications to state regulators. Directs the Public Service Commission to require electric companies to pursue federal funds and use least-cost debt. Extends the deadline to December 31, 2025, for the Commission to adopt electric system planning regulations. Mandates consideration of demand-side reliability methods, including virtual power plants, and differences among utility types. Expands prevailing wage and labor standards to electric infrastructure projects funded under the federal Inflation Reduction Act.
qa_results.responsible_party: Public Service Commission; Maryland Energy Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Investor-owned electric companies, electric cooperatives, municipal electric utilities, gas and electric companies, utility construction contractors and subcontractors, and electric utility customers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local finances and operations are not materially affected. The Public Service Commission and the Maryland Energy Administration can implement the bill's requirements using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Public Service Commission is the primary regulatory and implementing agency under the bill, responsible for adopting regulations and orders regarding electric system planning, requiring utilities to pursue federal funds and use least-cost debt, receiving quarterly utility reports, and submitting annual progress reports to the General Assembly.

The Maryland Energy Administration is specifically tasked under the bill to identify federal and other funding sources (including under the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act and the Inflation Reduction Act), assist electric companies in obtaining funds, and receive quarterly reports from electric companies.

The bill amends the Labor and Employment Article to expand the application of prevailing wage, apprenticeship participation, and workforce standards to electric system planning and infrastructure projects funded by federal programs.

The Office of the People's Counsel represents residential utility consumers before the Public Service Commission in regulatory proceedings and rulemakings, which will include the new electric system planning policies, demand-side requirements, and least-cost financing rules established by the bill.

The bill aligns electric system planning with state greenhouse gas reduction goals established under the Climate Solutions Now Act, for which the Department of the Environment is the lead agency and a coordinating partner with PSC and MEA on grid-related federal funding.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands statutory protections against discrimination across multiple articles of the Maryland Annotated Code. Adds sexual orientation, gender identity, race, religious beliefs, marital status, and disability to specified antidiscrimination provisions. Prohibits wage discrimination and unequal employment opportunities based on race, religious beliefs, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, and disability. Bars using the discovery or perception of religious beliefs or disability as provocation for manslaughter or an assault defense. Withdraws and repeals Chapter 244 of the Acts of the 2023 General Assembly.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor; Maryland Commission on Civil Rights
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland employers and employees, lenders and loan applicants, health care entities and patients, and State contractors and vendors
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Potential minimal increase in State general fund expenditures for the Maryland Department of Labor to process additional complaints, conduct investigator training, and provide educational materials. No material impact on local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the State's Equal Pay for Equal Work law within the Labor and Employment Article, expanding protected classes. As noted in the fiscal note, the Maryland Department of Labor may see an increased volume of complaints, requiring additional staff time and educational resources.

The Commission on Civil Rights is the primary state agency enforcing anti-discrimination statutes in employment, housing, public accommodations, and state contracting, areas directly expanded and harmonized across Maryland law under this bill.

The OAG represents the state in civil rights enforcement actions, brings actions against employers for wage discrimination violations upon referral from the Commissioner of Labor, and provides counsel on the enforcement of amended criminal and civil statutes.

The bill amends the Health - General and Health Occupations articles to prohibit discrimination based on protected characteristics by home health agencies, health maintenance organizations, and regulated health professionals.
The bill amends the Insurance Article by adding protected classes to non-discrimination mandates applicable to carrier provider panels and health network services, which the MIA regulates.
The bill updates non-discrimination provisions in the Education Article governing public school employee discrimination and student access to advanced coursework.

The bill amends the Public Utilities Article to prohibit electricity suppliers regulated by the Public Service Commission from discriminating against customers based on gender identity, disability, or sexual orientation.

As the state's central procurement authority, DGS must ensure state contracts and solicitation clauses incorporate the updated protected classes required by the amendments to the State Finance and Procurement Article.
The Board of Public Works oversees state procurements and approvals, which must adhere to the expanded commercial nondiscrimination policy and revised mandatory procurement clauses.
The bill updates the Human Services Article regarding provider contract requirements and the Residents' Bill of Rights to include gender identity among protected characteristics.
The bill amends the Housing and Community Development Article regarding non-discrimination pledges in employee organization constitutions and bylaws.

The bill amends the Courts and Judicial Proceedings Article to prohibit exclusion from jury service based on sexual orientation and gender identity, and updates the statute of limitations for wage discrimination actions.
OAH adjudicates contested administrative hearings resulting from state agency enforcement actions, including potential increases in complaints referred under non-discrimination laws.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill limits defenses and legal provocation standards in criminal assault and murder prosecutions based on religious beliefs or disability, directly impacting criminal defense litigation handled by OPD.
The bill amends the Criminal Law Article relating to hate crimes and false reports to law enforcement, updating the protected categories under which hate crimes are investigated and charged.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes collective bargaining rights for nonprobationary employees of the Montgomery County State's Attorney's Office, including nonsupervisory assistant State's Attorneys. Subjects covered employees to county merit system law and personnel regulations unless excluded through collective bargaining. Designates the County Executive as the employer for bargaining over compensation, active employee pensions, fringe benefits, and hours. Designates the State's Attorney as the employer for bargaining over all other terms and conditions of employment. Mandates a single collective bargaining agreement covering both county government and State's Attorney's Office employees. Subjects required funding for negotiated agreements to the budget and fiscal policies of the county.
qa_results.responsible_party: Montgomery County Executive; Montgomery County State's Attorney; Montgomery County Labor Relations Administrator
qa_results.stakeholders: Nonprobationary employees and nonsupervisory assistant State's Attorneys of the Montgomery County State's Attorney's Office, and Montgomery County government
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State effect. Montgomery County expenditures increase to facilitate collective bargaining and may increase, potentially significantly, from higher personnel costs under negotiated agreements, though the exact magnitude cannot be reliably predicted in advance.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the definition of public school employee in Dorchester County for collective bargaining purposes. Includes supervisory noncertificated employees within that definition. Covers any individual who responsibly directs the work of other employees. Allows supervisory noncertificated personnel to bargain collectively with certificated school employees. Takes effect July 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Dorchester County Board of Education; Public Employee Relations Board
qa_results.stakeholders: Supervisory noncertificated public school employees in Dorchester County and the Dorchester County Board of Education
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal effect. The bill does not materially affect Dorchester County local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Public Employee Relations Board (PERB) is responsible for administering collective bargaining, union representation, and dispute resolution for public school employees in Maryland. The bill alters the definition of public school employees eligible for collective bargaining units in Dorchester County.

qa_results.bill_summary: Modifies implementation timelines, funding mechanisms, and administrative responsibilities under the Blueprint for Maryland’s Future. Authorizes the State Department of Education to fund planning and development for Judy Centers and Patty Centers. Transfers authority to approve career ladder teaching time phase-in plans to the State Board of Education. qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education; Maryland State Board of Education; Accountability and Implementation Board; Career and Technical Education Committee; local school systems
qa_results.stakeholders: Nonclassroom educators including principals, assistant principals, and instructional specialists; public school students eligible for dual enrollment or prekindergarten; parents of young children; local school systems; Judy Centers and Patty Centers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures increase by an indeterminate amount (estimated under $300,000 annually) beginning as early as FY 2024 to cover certification fees for eligible nonclassroom teachers. Extending the Prekindergarten Expansion Grant Program through FY 2029 will produce indeterminate secondary shifts between State funding formulas and local share obligations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MSDE is the primary implementing agency for the bill's provisions, including awarding planning and development funding for Judy Centers and Family Support Centers, approving educator career ladder specifications, managing the Prekindergarten Expansion Grant Program, administering National Board Certification funding for nonclassroom teachers, and overseeing kindergarten assessments.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the Accountability and Implementation Board (AIB) by reassigning certain career ladder approval responsibilities to the State Board of Education, while jointly authorizing AIB and SBE to limit dual enrollment courses. It also directly alters reporting requirements and goal-setting deadlines for the Career and Technical Education (CTE) Committee.

Local departments of social services under DHS are required to notify eligible parents of publicly funded prekindergarten opportunities and share parental contact details with local school systems, resulting in operational duties and notification costs.

Local health departments under MDH are statutory entities required by the bill to notify parents about publicly funded prekindergarten programs and transmit contact information to local school systems.

The bill references registered apprenticeship programs approved by the Division of Workforce Development and Adult Learning within the Maryland Department of Labor for achieving statewide CTE completion goals.
The bill touches upon post-college and career readiness pathways and dual enrollment courses at Maryland institutions of higher education, which fall under MHEC's coordinating purview.

The Career and Technical Education (CTE) Committee, whose goal deadlines and annual progress reporting dates are extended by the bill, operates under the purview of the Governor's Workforce Development Board.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases the annual motor vehicle registration emergency medical services surcharge from $17.00 to $40.00. Allocates surcharge revenues among the Maryland Trauma Physician Services Fund, Shock Trauma, and emergency medical operations. Expands Trauma Physician Services Fund eligibility to trauma health care practitioners and increases provider reimbursement rates. Increases maximum fines for specified impaired driving violations, directing at least 20% of collections to trauma services. Requires an annual appropriation of at least $16,500,000 for the Amoss Fund beginning in fiscal year 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Health Care Commission; Health Services Cost Review Commission; Motor Vehicle Administration; Comptroller of Maryland; Maryland Department of Emergency Management
qa_results.stakeholders: Motor vehicle owners; trauma centers, trauma physicians, and trauma health care practitioners; R Adams Cowley Shock Trauma Center; pediatric trauma centers; drivers convicted of impaired driving; local fire, rescue, and ambulance departments
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues increase by approximately $104.8 million annually beginning in FY 2025 from the increased vehicle registration surcharge. Special fund expenditures increase by $3.4 million in FY 2025 and $4.9 million annually thereafter for credit card fees, mandated trauma grants, and Amoss Fund distributions. General fund fine revenues decrease minimally due to revenue diverted to the Maryland Trauma Physician Services Fund, while local jurisdictions receive increased funding through the Amoss Fund.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Motor Vehicle Administration is directly responsible for collecting the increased motor vehicle registration surcharge (raised from $17 to $40 per vehicle) across approximately 4.6 million vehicles and distributing the proceeds.

MHCC co-administers the Maryland Trauma Physician Services Fund with HSCRC, establishes reimbursement methodologies and parameters for trauma physicians and centers, awards annual trauma grants, and produces required annual reports.

HSCRC co-administers the Maryland Trauma Physician Services Fund with MHCC, helps set reimbursement methodologies, and tracks hospital trauma standby, staffing, equipment, and education costs accounted for in hospital global budgets.

The Comptroller statutorily administers the Maryland Emergency Medical System Operations Fund (MEMSOF), handling all accounting transactions and year-end reconciliations for the fund which receives millions in increased surcharge revenue.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MIEMSS receives funding from MEMSOF, designates trauma centers, maintains the State trauma registry, establishes on-call staffing criteria, and consults on the trauma center grant award process.
MDEM administers the Senator William H. Amoss Fire, Rescue, and Ambulance Fund, which receives a mandated annual budget appropriation of at least $16.5 million starting in fiscal year 2026.

MDOT oversees the Motor Vehicle Administration and the Transportation Trust Fund, which will experience approximately $2.2 million annually in credit card processing expenditures due to the higher registration surcharge.

The Judiciary adjudicates the impaired driving violations with increased maximum fines, diverts at least 20% of collected fine revenue to the Maryland Trauma Physician Services Fund, and incurs one-time IT programming costs.

The bill mandates the Governor to allocate at least $9.00 of the vehicle surcharge to the R Adams Cowley Shock Trauma Center and to mandate an annual budget appropriation of at least $16.5 million for the Amoss Fund beginning in FY 2026.
DBM is responsible for state budget preparation and execution, incorporating the mandated allocations and statutory appropriations required by the bill for MEMSOF and the Amoss Fund.
MDH receives transfers from the Maryland Trauma Physician Services Fund to cover the State's share of costs for undercompensated trauma care provided to Medicaid enrollees.
The Maryland State Police Aviation Division's medically oriented functions have historically been supported by MEMSOF, which is modified under the emergency services funding framework.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Howard County Board of Education to report differences between its approved capital budget and the Superintendent's proposal. Directs the Board to publish the differences and detailed rationales on the school system's website within 30 days. Requires the Superintendent to report differences between a proposed capital improvement program and the prior year's approved program. Directs the Superintendent to publish these differences and detailed rationales on the website within 30 days. Mandates that both the Board and the Superintendent submit their respective reports to the General Assembly.
qa_results.responsible_party: Howard County Board of Education; Howard County Superintendent of Schools
qa_results.stakeholders: Howard County Board of Education, Howard County Superintendent of Schools, and Howard County Public Schools community members
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal effect. The Howard County Board of Education and the Howard County Superintendent of Schools can publish and submit the required reports using existing local resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Interagency Commission on School Construction (IAC) manages state review, capital improvement plans (CIP), and allocations for local public school construction projects. While the bill specifically imposes reporting mandates on the Howard County Board of Education and Superintendent regarding capital budget differences, it directly relates to school capital improvement planning overseen at the state level by the IAC.

The Maryland State Department of Education provides regulatory oversight and leadership over the state's 24 local public school systems, including Howard County Public Schools, although the bill's reporting requirements are carried out entirely by local school officials.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters staff qualifications and operational requirements for publicly funded prekindergarten programs in the State. Requires the Maryland State Department of Education to establish a three-level early childhood educator career ladder for eligible private providers. Directs the Department to establish prekindergarten provider hubs and develop a model memorandum of understanding for county boards. Authorizes county boards of education to lease county space and seek State capital improvement funding for facility renovations. Establishes a service repayment requirement and prioritization criteria for the Child Care Career and Professional Development Fund. Extends mandated funding and consolidation timelines for the Prekindergarten Expansion Grant Program through fiscal 2030.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education; Office of Child Care
qa_results.stakeholders: Public and eligible private prekindergarten providers, early childhood educators and teaching assistants, county boards of education, and prekindergarten students and families
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $1.0 million in FY 2025 to develop the career ladder and train staff on classroom assessments. Special fund expenditures increase by $5.7 million in FY 2026 to satisfy the mandated appropriation for the Child Care Credential Program. Extending Prekindergarten Expansion Grants through FY 2029 has an indeterminate net effect on State education aid and local school funding shares.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MSDE is the primary implementing agency for the bill. It is tasked with establishing the early childhood educator career ladder, developing a model memorandum of understanding for local school systems, establishing prekindergarten provider hubs, administering technical assistance and aid programs, and managing the Prekindergarten Expansion Grant Program, Child Care Credential Program, and the Child Care Career and Professional Development Fund.

The bill directly addresses the Public School Construction Program and the Capital Improvement Program (CIP) administered by the IAC, authorizing local boards of education to apply for CIP funding for renovations to public facilities leased as prekindergarten classrooms.

The bill creates and extends statutory mandated appropriations across multiple fiscal years for early childhood education grant programs and alters funding formulas under the Blueprint for Maryland's Future, directly affecting DBM's budget development and fiscal planning duties.

The bill statutorily requires the Governor to include specific mandated appropriations in the annual state budget for the Maryland Child Care Credential Program and Prekindergarten Expansion Grant Program for fiscal years 2026 through 2030.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Howard County Task Force to Study Revenue Options for School Capital Needs. Directs the task force to identify Howard County Public Schools capital needs and funding gaps through 2035. Requires the task force to evaluate revenue options, including transfer tax reallocations and a commercial excise tax. Mandates a final report to county officials and the Howard County Delegation by October 31, 2024. Requires the County Council to request legislative authority by resolution if it lacks power to enact recommendations.
qa_results.responsible_party: Howard County Task Force to Study Revenue Options for School Capital Needs; Howard County Executive; Howard County Council
qa_results.stakeholders: Howard County Public Schools students and personnel, Howard County taxpayers, commercial property owners, and Howard County residents
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal effect. Indeterminate increase in Howard County expenditures to staff the task force and complete the final report by October 31, 2024, potentially requiring temporary contractual support; local revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a statutory task force, the Howard County Task Force to Study Revenue Options for School Capital Needs, charged with studying school capital funding gaps and recommending revenue options.

The Interagency Commission on School Construction oversees public school construction and capital improvement funding statewide; while the bill focuses on Howard County's local revenue options, it directly relates to school capital needs and local matching capacity for school construction programs.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Arts Incubator Workgroup to study how arts and cultural institutions can support local artists. Requires the Maryland State Arts Council to provide staff for the Workgroup. Entitles Workgroup members to reimbursement for standard travel expenses without compensation. Requires the Workgroup to submit a preliminary findings report by January 1, 2025. Mandates a final recommendations report to the Governor and General Assembly by October 1, 2025. Terminates the Workgroup on December 31, 2025.
qa_results.responsible_party: Arts Incubator Workgroup; Maryland State Arts Council
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland local artists, arts educators, local arts councils, arts organizations, and arts and entertainment districts
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Workgroup travel reimbursements are minimal and absorbable within existing budgeted resources. The Maryland State Arts Council can provide staffing using existing resources. There is no material local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Arts Council (MSAC), which is housed within the Department of Commerce, is required to staff the Arts Incubator Workgroup and accommodate any operational and member travel reimbursement costs within existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates the Arts Incubator Workgroup as a temporary advisory body to study support for local artists and submit preliminary and final reports.
The Governor is responsible for appointing eleven members to the Workgroup, selecting the Workgroup Chair, and receiving both the preliminary and final reports.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting and processing gubernatorial appointments to state boards, commissions, and task forces, including the members of the newly created Workgroup.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes a soil conservation district to recommend a fee system to cover the cost of reviewing small pond plans.
