Requires the district to determine annually the reasonable costs of reviewing small pond plans for the succeeding year. Requires the district to submit the proposed fee system to the local governing body. Allows the local governing body 90 days to enact the fee system, adopt an alternative, or provide funding. Enacts the district's fee system automatically on the 91st day if the local governing body takes no action. Specifies that collected fees must supplement county and State funds and not exceed plan review costs.
qa_results.responsible_party: Soil Conservation Districts; local governing bodies; Maryland Department of the Environment
qa_results.stakeholders: Landowners, agricultural operators, and developers constructing or modifying small ponds; soil conservation districts; local governments
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Soil conservation district revenues may increase beginning in FY 2025 to the extent districts recommend and implement small pond plan review fee systems; exact amounts depend on local fee rates and application volumes. State special fund revenues to the Wetlands and Waterways Program Fund may decrease minimally if reviews shift from the Maryland Department of the Environment to local districts. State expenditures are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 1465 amends Title 8 of the Agriculture Article regarding the powers and duties of soil conservation districts, authorizing them to recommend fee systems for reviewing small pond plans, which falls under the regulatory purview and soil conservation programs overseen by the Maryland Department of Agriculture.

The bill amends § 5-503 of the Environment Article concerning small pond permit exemptions and plan reviews. MDE currently reviews small pond plans where districts do not, and the bill could affect MDE's workload and special fund revenues deposited into the Wetlands and Waterways Program Fund.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals the annual $100,000 mandated appropriation for the Professional and Volunteer Firefighter Innovative Cancer Screening Technologies Program. Authorizes the Governor to include at least $500,000 in the annual State budget for the program starting in fiscal year 2025. Supports grants to local fire departments and volunteer fire companies to procure innovative cancer screening tests. Subjects all program appropriations, expenditures, and distributed funds to audit by the Office of Legislative Audits.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Office of Legislative Audits
qa_results.stakeholders: professional and volunteer firefighters, local fire departments, and volunteer fire companies and departments
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $400,000 annually beginning in fiscal 2025, assuming discretionary funding of at least $500,000 is provided to replace the repealed $100,000 mandate. Local fire department revenues and expenditures increase to the extent departments apply for and receive grant funding.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health (MDH) is the primary implementing agency responsible for administering the Professional and Volunteer Firefighter Innovative Cancer Screening Technologies Program and distributing grants funded through this appropriation.

The bill directly authorizes the Governor to include at least $500,000 in discretionary funding for the program in the annual state budget starting in fiscal year 2025, replacing a previously mandated appropriation.

The Department of Budget and Management develops the annual state budget on behalf of the Governor and oversees budget execution and fiscal planning impacted by the alteration of this funding authorization.
The bill explicitly references the Office of Legislative Audits as having statutory authority to audit the appropriations, expenditures, and grant funds disbursed under the program.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Governor to appoint audiologist members to the State Board of Examiners from Maryland Academy of Audiology nominations. Applies to the State Board of Examiners for Audiologists, Hearing Aid Dispensers, Speech–Language Pathologists, and Music Therapists. Replaces the requirement that the board itself submit the list of nominees to the Secretary and Governor. Requires the nomination list to contain at least three times the number of board vacancies. Requires the board to notify all licensed Maryland audiologists of vacancies to solicit nominations. Takes effect October 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governor; Maryland Department of Health; State Board of Examiners for Audiologists, Hearing Aid Dispensers, Speech–Language Pathologists, and Music Therapists
qa_results.stakeholders: Licensed audiologists in Maryland, the Maryland Academy of Audiology, and members of the State Board of Examiners for Audiologists, Hearing Aid Dispensers, Speech–Language Pathologists, and Music Therapists
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The bill is procedural in nature and does not affect finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Examiners for Audiologists, Hearing Aid Dispensers, Speech-Language Pathologists, and Music Therapists is a health occupations licensing board housed within the Maryland Department of Health, and the Secretary of Health provides advice to the Governor on these board appointments.
The bill directly governs the statutory appointment authority of the Governor regarding licensed audiologist members to the State Board.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in managing the recruitment, vetting, and appointment process for members serving on state boards and commissions.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases penalties for motor vehicle security lapses to $200 for the first 30 days and $10 per day thereafter. Raises the maximum annual uninsured driving penalty from $2,500 to $3,500. Establishes the Driver Education in Public High Schools Grant Program and Fund in the Maryland State Department of Education. Establishes the State-Aided Institutions Field Trip Grant Program and Fund to assist public schools with field trip transportation. Reallocates penalty revenues by distributing $2,000,000 to driver education, $600,000 to field trips, and an additional $3,000,000 to MAIF.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education; Motor Vehicle Administration; Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund
qa_results.stakeholders: uninsured motor vehicle owners, Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund, public high schools, public school students, and nonprofit driver education providers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Uninsured motorist penalty revenues increase by an estimated $3.0 million annually starting in FY 2025, with $900,000 retained by the Transportation Trust Fund. Mandated annual allocations from penalty distributions require $2.0 million for driver education grants, $600,000 for field trip grants, and an additional $3.0 million to MAIF's Uninsured Division, decreasing general fund revenues by $3.5 million in FY 2025. Special fund expenditures increase by $2.6 million annually for grants and administrative staffing at MSDE, while local school systems benefit from new grant revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MVA assesses and collects the uninsured motorist penalties, adjusts fee structures under the bill, enforces vehicle registration suspensions for lapsed insurance, and retains 30% of the penalty revenues.

MSDE is charged with creating, administering, and adopting regulations for two new programs and special funds: the Driver Education in Public High Schools Grant Program and the State-Aided Institutions Field Trip Grant Program.

MAIF receives a significant statutory increase in dedicated funding ($3 million in FY 2025 plus inflation adjustments in future years) specifically dedicated to the operations of its Uninsured Division.

As the parent agency of the Motor Vehicle Administration, MDOT's Transportation Trust Fund receives the 30% allocation of collected uninsured driving penalties, resulting in an estimated revenue increase of $900,000 annually.
The State Treasurer is statutorily required to hold the Driver Education in Public High Schools Fund and the State-Aided Institutions Field Trip Fund separately and invest their moneys.
The Comptroller is statutorily required to account for both the Driver Education in Public High Schools Fund and the State-Aided Institutions Field Trip Fund.

qa_results.bill_summary: Codifies the Maryland Entertainment Industry Council within the Department of Commerce as the permanent successor to the Maryland Entertainment Council. Expands the council's voting membership to include agency secretaries and 19 members appointed by the Governor. Directs the council to study Maryland's film, television, and entertainment assets and develop strategic industry recommendations. Authorizes the council to adopt regulations, enter into contracts, and accept gifts and federal grants. Requires an initial report by December 1, 2024, and annual reports beginning January 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Commerce; Maryland Entertainment Industry Council
qa_results.stakeholders: film, television, and entertainment businesses, independent creators, industry labor organizations, and workforce development partners in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal operational impact on the State. The Department of Commerce can staff the council and absorb travel reimbursements within existing budgeted resources. Expenditures may increase if the council exercises its authority to hire outside consultants. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Entertainment Industry Council is established within the Department of Commerce. The Secretary of Commerce is a statutory member of the Council, and Commerce is designated as the primary agency responsible for staffing the Council.

The Governor's Senior Advisor on Film, Television, and Entertainment chairs the Council. The Governor appoints the majority of the Council's members (including honorary co-chairs), may designate additional agencies to staff the Council, and receives the Council's reports.
The Secretary of Labor (or designee) is a designated statutory member of the Council, and the department may potentially be called upon to support staffing or workforce pipeline recommendations.
The Secretary of Housing and Community Development (or designee) is a designated statutory member of the Council.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill codifies, restructures, and makes permanent a state advisory body—the Maryland Entertainment Industry Council—tasked with assessing state assets and advising on strategic policies for the film and entertainment sector.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and processing gubernatorial appointments, which includes the 19 appointed members and up to 3 honorary co-chairs established by the bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires public schools administering the Armed Services Vocational Aptitude Battery to notify participating students and parents of score-withholding options. Mandates this notification occur two weeks before test administration. Allows students and parents to select Option 8 to prohibit releasing scores and personal information to military recruiters. Repeals the requirement that schools automatically choose Option 8 and notify test representatives. Authorizes individuals choosing Option 8 to later release information to military recruiters, apprenticeship programs, or registered employers. Preserves the authority of county boards of education to choose Option 8 for all schools within their jurisdiction.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland public schools; county boards of education
qa_results.stakeholders: Public school students taking the Armed Services Vocational Aptitude Battery (ASVAB), parents and guardians of participating students, military recruiters, and local school systems
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state fiscal impact. Local school systems can provide the required notifications two weeks prior to test administration using existing resources. Local revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Education Article concerning policies and notification requirements for public schools administering the Armed Services Vocational Aptitude Battery (ASVAB). As the state agency overseeing public schools and setting educational policies and standards across local school systems, the Maryland State Department of Education is directly concerned with the bill's implementation.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands the definition of practicing massage therapy to include instrument-assisted soft tissue manipulation techniques, specifically muscle scraping and vibration therapy. Subjects these techniques to additional education and training requirements determined by the Board in regulations. Requires applicants for license or registration reinstatement to submit evidence of a completed criminal history records check. Requires the Board to mandate a health care examination if objective evidence indicates a practitioner may cause harm. Deems refusal to submit to the examination prima facie evidence of incompetence unless beyond the individual's control. Directs the Board to pay the costs of designated examinations.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners
qa_results.stakeholders: licensed massage therapists, registered massage practitioners, and applicants for massage therapy licensure or registration
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not materially affected; the State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners can implement the bill and absorb examination costs with existing resources. No local effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners operates under the Maryland Department of Health. The bill directly impacts the Board's regulatory operations by modifying the scope of practice for massage therapy, establishing criminal history record check requirements for license reinstatements, and authorizing the Board to require and pay for independent health care examinations of licensees and applicants under investigation.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits a person from aiding or abetting the unauthorized practice of massage therapy in the State. Establishes that a violator is guilty of a felony. Subjects first-time violators to a fine up to $5,000 or imprisonment up to one year. Subjects repeat violators to a fine up to $20,000 per day or imprisonment up to five years. Requires convicted violators to reimburse the Board for direct prosecution costs. Authorizes the Board to assess a civil fine of up to $10,000 against violators.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners
qa_results.stakeholders: individuals and businesses aiding or abetting the unauthorized practice of massage therapy, unlicensed massage therapy practitioners, and licensed massage therapists
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The civil and criminal penalty provisions do not have a material impact on State or local finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners operates within the Maryland Department of Health. The bill establishes civil penalties assessed by the board, requires violators to reimburse the board's prosecution costs, and directs penalties into the State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners Fund.
The bill creates a new felony offense and establishes criminal penalties, fines, and restitution for prosecution costs, which are adjudicated within the Maryland court system.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a new felony offense carrying penalties of up to 5 years of imprisonment, potentially requiring public defender representation for indigent individuals charged under the statute.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes felony penalties including imprisonment of up to 1 year for a first offense and up to 5 years for subsequent offenses, which may result in individuals being committed to State correctional facilities or community supervision.

The Office of the Attorney General serves as legal counsel to the health occupation licensing boards, including the State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners, and supports enforcement and litigation matters.

qa_results.bill_summary: Reduces the frequency of certain performance audits conducted by the Office of Legislative Audits. Requires audits of the Board of Liquor License Commissioners for Baltimore City every six years instead of four. Requires audits of the Board of License Commissioners for Prince George's County every six years instead of three. Focuses these audits on liquor inspections, licensing, disciplinary procedures, and management oversight.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of Legislative Audits
qa_results.stakeholders: Board of Liquor License Commissioners for Baltimore City; Board of License Commissioners for Prince George's County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local government finances or operations, though the Office of Legislative Audits may realize administrative efficiencies.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 1501 directly modifies the statutory duties of the Office of Legislative Audits (OLA) by altering the required frequency of performance audits that OLA must conduct on the Board of Liquor License Commissioners for Baltimore City and the Prince George's County Board of License Commissioners to once every six years.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits the State Treasurer and persons acting on the Treasurer's behalf from participating in specified campaign finance activities during General Assembly regular sessions. Bars receiving, soliciting, or using contributions and conducting fundraising events for federal, State, or local candidates during session. Permits depositing electronic contributions made before the start of the legislative session. Excludes campaign activities solely related to an official's candidacy for an elective federal or local office. Subjects violating campaign finance entities to civil penalties distributed to the Fair Campaign Financing Fund.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Elections; State Treasurer
qa_results.stakeholders: State Treasurer, campaign finance entities of the State Treasurer, and political contributors
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances and operations are not anticipated to be materially affected. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly applies to the State Treasurer and persons acting on behalf of the State Treasurer, prohibiting them from engaging in certain campaign finance activities during the General Assembly's regular session.
The State Board of Elections regulates state campaign finance activities, enforces compliance with the restrictions, and assesses civil penalties for violations under the Election Law Article.
The Office of the State Prosecutor investigates and prosecutes violations of state election laws involving public officials.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands the information the Maryland Transit Administration must publish on its website before holding a hearing on major service changes. Requires publication of data on affected riders, service areas, schools, businesses, monthly ridership, and paratransit commute impacts. Mandates a visible primary website page link, a summary of related public records, and an explanation of the proposed change. Requires the Administration to distribute its post-hearing impact report to each legislator whose district is impacted.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Transit Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: transit riders, paratransit users, and communities affected by proposed transit service changes
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal increase in Transportation Trust Fund expenditures for the Maryland Transit Administration to modify consultant contracts for data collection and publication. State revenues are unaffected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies requirements placed on the Maryland Transit Administration, requiring it to publish expanded information regarding route demographics, schools, businesses, and paratransit impacts on its website before public hearings on major service changes, as well as distribute impact reports to affected General Assembly members.

MTA is a modal administration under MDOT, and the bill impacts Transportation Trust Fund expenditures to update consultant contracts and procedures for compiling and publishing the required transit equity information.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Baltimore Regional Water Governance Model Workgroup to study regional water and wastewater governance approaches in the Baltimore region. Directs the Mayor of Baltimore City and the Baltimore County Executive to jointly designate a chair and provide staff. Requires the Workgroup to review previous task force recommendations and analyze workforce, financial, equity, and operational transition issues. Mandates that the Workgroup hire independent consultants, including outside legal counsel and equity analysis experts. Prohibits the Workgroup from considering or making recommendations related to a privately operated regional water governance model. Requires the Workgroup to report its findings to state and local officials on or before June 30, 2027.
qa_results.responsible_party: Baltimore Regional Water Governance Model Workgroup; Office of the Mayor of Baltimore City; Office of the County Executive of Baltimore County
qa_results.stakeholders: water and wastewater ratepayers in Baltimore City, Baltimore County, and surrounding jurisdictions; Baltimore City and Baltimore County municipal water and wastewater employees; independent consultants and outside counsel
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $500,000 in fiscal 2026 due to a mandated appropriation to hire independent consultants. Baltimore City and Baltimore County revenues and expenditures increase correspondingly by a combined $500,000 in fiscal 2026 to contract the consultants.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires the Baltimore Regional Water Governance Model Workgroup to consult with the Department of the Environment (MDE) in developing its findings and final report regarding regional water and wastewater governance.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates the Baltimore Regional Water Governance Model Workgroup as an advisory/task force body tasked with studying and evaluating water governance models in the Baltimore region.
The Governor must appoint two members to the Workgroup, receive its final report, and include a mandated general fund appropriation of $500,000 in the fiscal year 2026 budget.
The Workgroup is statutorily required to consult with the Office of the Attorney General (OAG) during the development of its report, particularly on legal and governance issues.
DBM oversees the state budget and will be responsible for executing and monitoring the mandated $500,000 general fund appropriation required for fiscal year 2026.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting and processing the appointment of the two Workgroup members designated to be appointed by the Governor.

qa_results.bill_summary: Delays the effective date of extensive 2023 Forest Conservation Act revisions from July 1, 2024, to July 1, 2026. Modifies the definition of qualified conservation for forest mitigation banks by repealing the prior 2020 approval cutoff date. Authorizes qualified conservation to meet up to 50 percent, or conditionally 60 percent, of afforestation or reforestation mandates. Exempts solar photovoltaic facilities from Forest Conservation Act afforestation requirements. Expands priority retention areas and requires written findings and justification for clearing priority forest vegetation. Requires the Department of Natural Resources to update model ordinances by July 1, 2025, and adopt regulations by July 1, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
qa_results.stakeholders: Commercial and residential real estate developers, solar photovoltaic facility developers, local governments administering forest conservation programs, and forest mitigation bank sponsors
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Delays until fiscal 2027 at the earliest most of the state and local fiscal impacts associated with Chapters 541 and 542 of 2023, including potential increases in state and local capital construction costs and shifts in fee-in-lieu revenues. The Department of Natural Resources can implement required ordinance updates and regulations with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DNR is the primary state agency responsible for administering the Forest Conservation Act. HB 1511 requires DNR to update the State Forest Conservation Technical Manual, update the model local government ordinance by July 1, 2025, adopt implementing regulations by July 1, 2026, and approve local program justifications regarding forest mitigation bank credits.

The bill explicitly incorporates environmental designations established by MDE, specifically classifying forests located in Tier II or Tier III high-quality watersheds identified by MDE as priority retention and protection areas under the Forest Conservation Act.

The bill addresses exemptions and applicability provisions concerning solar photovoltaic facilities granted a Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity (CPCN) by the PSC under § 7-207 of the Public Utilities Article.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals the termination date governing specific uses of the Bay Restoration Fund's Septics Account. Permanently authorizes grants and loans to connect properties using on-site sewage disposal systems to municipal wastewater facilities. Applies to facilities under construction to achieve enhanced nutrient removal or biological nutrient removal level treatment. Authorizes payment of local government debt principal issued for eligible connection costs. Requires projects to meet designated environmental impact, cost-effectiveness, and local comprehensive planning conditions.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment; Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Owners of properties using on-site sewage disposal systems and local governments operating municipal wastewater facilities
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Overall finances of the Bay Restoration Fund Septics Account are not affected, as the bill permanently extends an existing authorized use. Local grant revenues and expenditures may shift between jurisdictions depending on which connection projects receive funding.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) administers the Bay Restoration Fund, including the Septics Account. The bill permanently authorizes MDE to use Septics Account funds for costs associated with connecting properties with septic systems to municipal wastewater facilities under construction for enhanced or biological nutrient removal.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the deadline to send real property reassessment notices for the 2024–2025 taxable year to May 1, 2024. Delays the statutory irrebuttable presumption that a property's prior value or classification has not changed. Applies to real property reassessments for the taxable year beginning after June 30, 2024, and before July 1, 2025. Maintains existing exceptions for property transfers, zoning changes, use changes, substantial improvements, calculation errors, and assessment decreases. Takes effect immediately as an emergency measure and sunsets on December 31, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland real property owners, particularly owners of 100,009 residential properties with delayed reassessment notices, as well as county and municipal governments
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Prevents an estimated State property tax revenue loss of $3,072,080 in FY 2025 ($18,432,477 over three years). Also prevents estimated local property tax revenue losses of $32.2 million in FY 2025 ($30,095,457 county and $2.1 million municipal) and $193.2 million over three years ($180,572,740 county and $12.6 million municipal).

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill extends the statutory deadline for sending real property reassessment notices for FY 2025 to May 1, 2024, preventing an irrebuttable presumption that property values did not change. Because these notices inform property owners of their new valuations and right to appeal, this change directly impacts the timing and volume of property assessment appeals filed with and heard by the 24 local Property Tax Assessment Appeals Boards.

The Maryland Tax Court serves as the highest administrative appellate body for property tax assessment disputes originating from the Property Tax Assessment Appeals Boards. By validating the FY 2025 reassessment notices, the bill maintains the standard assessment appeal pipeline that can culminate in cases before the Tax Court.

DBM oversees state revenue estimation, fiscal planning, and budget execution. The bill directly prevents a potential loss of $3.1 million in State property tax revenues in FY 2025 and $18.4 million over three years, directly impacting state fiscal forecasts and debt service funding.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals the requirement that the Maryland Children’s Health Program administer a separate premium plan. Eliminates mandatory family premium contributions for coverage under the Program. Expands non-premium coverage to individuals under 19 who do not qualify for Medicaid. Requires eligible individuals to have family income at or below 300 percent of federal poverty guidelines. Repeals outdated statutory provisions governing the former private option plan. Takes effect immediately as an emergency measure.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Children under age 19 in families with incomes up to 300 percent of the federal poverty guidelines enrolled in the Maryland Children's Health Program
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Net reduction in MCHP expenditures of approximately $100,000 annually ($35,000 general funds and $65,000 federal funds) beginning in FY 2025, with minimal impact in FY 2024. An annual loss of $866,167 in premium plan revenue is offset by $966,132 in administrative savings from eliminating premium collection systems. Federal fund revenues decrease correspondingly by about $65,000 annually. No local effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health is the primary agency responsible for administering the Maryland Children's Health Program (MCHP) and requested this departmental legislation to eliminate the MCHP premium plan, end monthly family contribution requirements, and restructure program administration.

The bill repeals and amends provisions within the Insurance Article concerning health benefit plan requirements, carrier obligations, and legacy coverage groups relating to the Maryland Children's Health Program, which falls under MIA's regulatory oversight.

MHBE operates the Maryland Health Connection marketplace and determines eligibility for state health coverage programs, including the Maryland Children's Health Program whose eligibility structures and premium rules are altered by the bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Transfers ownership and operational oversight of Maryland thoroughbred racing facilities to the Maryland Thoroughbred Racetrack Operating Authority. Increases the Maryland Stadium Authority bond debt limit for racing facility projects to $400,000,000. Authorizes transferring the Preakness Stakes to another State track during Pimlico Race Course reconstruction. Extends the required conveyance deadline for the Bowie Race Course Training Center to December 31, 2025. Mandates fiscal 2026 budget appropriations of $6,200,000 for Prince George's County and $4,500,000 for Rosecroft Raceway.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Thoroughbred Racetrack Operating Authority; Maryland Stadium Authority; State Racing Commission; Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland thoroughbred horse owners, breeders, trainers, and jockeys; Maryland Jockey Club; Laurel Racing Association; Prince George's County; Baltimore City; City of Bowie; Rosecroft Raceway; Ocean Downs Race Course
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State: Authorizes $400.0 million in Maryland Stadium Authority bond issuances in FY 2025, with estimated annual debt service of $24.0 million from FY 2026 through FY 2055. General fund expenditures increase by $10.7 million in FY 2026 for mandated appropriations ($6.2 million to Prince George's County and $4.5 million to the Racetrack Facility Renewal Account). General fund revenues decrease by $3.6 million annually beginning in FY 2025 due to statutory redistributions to special funds and local impact grants. Special fund revenues increase by $4.8 million in FY 2024, $13.6 million in FY 2025, and $8.1 million in FY 2026. Local: Prince George's County revenues increase by $3.0 million annually beginning in FY 2025 and $6.2 million in FY 2026; Baltimore City tax revenues decrease by an indeterminate amount.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 1524 directly authorizes the Maryland Stadium Authority to finance, plan, design, and construct horse racing facilities on behalf of the Maryland Thoroughbred Racetrack Operating Authority, while increasing its bond cap from $375 million to $400 million.

The Department of Labor houses the Maryland Racing Commission, which is tasked with licensing racing entities, allocating racing days, adopting regulations, and overseeing the Purse Dedication Account and Racetrack Facility Renewal Account under the bill.

The Comptroller is required to manage distributions from the State Lottery Fund, issue warrants from the Purse Dedication Account, administer sales and use tax exemptions, and redirect specific sales and use tax revenues into the Racing and Community Development Facilities Fund.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill impacts State Lottery Fund revenue allocations, waives sports wagering facility license fees for specified racing licensees, and expresses legislative intent regarding the frequency and operation of the Racetrax lottery game.

The bill requires a joint workforce housing and community development plan between MTROA and DHCD for the area surrounding Pimlico, and reallocates a $10 million capital grant to Park Heights Renaissance to be used in consultation with the department.

The Board of Public Works is responsible for approving bond issuances by the Maryland Stadium Authority and must approve key operating agreements and receive notices related to facility management and wind-down plans.

MEDCO's Chair or Executive Director serves as a statutory member of the Maryland Thoroughbred Racetrack Operating Authority, and MTROA is authorized to acquire property or contractual interests in coordination with MEDCO.

The Governor is tasked with appointing members to MTROA, including mandated funding of $10.7 million across two appropriations in the FY 2026 budget, and authorizing a fiscal 2025 budget transfer for racing working capital.

The authority acts as the local development council overseeing the allocation of video lottery local impact aid funds earmarked for capital projects and community development in neighborhoods surrounding Pimlico Race Course.

DBM is responsible for supervising state budget execution and preparing the Governor's budget bill, which must incorporate the mandated appropriations and fund transfers required by the bill for FY 2025 and FY 2026.

The Treasurer is statutorily designated to invest and reinvest monies in the Purse Dedication Account and serves as a member of the Board of Public Works that reviews racing bond issuances and facility agreements.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Camden Yards Football Sports Facility Capital Works Fund and the Emergency Repair Fund. Requires the Maryland Stadium Authority to administer both special, nonlapsing funds for stadium improvements and repairs. Mandates the transfer of $5,000,000 in Series 2023B bond proceeds into each fund. Prohibits using either fund for debt service, bond management charges, or pledging to authority borrowing. Exempts both funds from general fund interest accrual and fund reversion requirements.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Stadium Authority; State Treasurer; Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Baltimore Ravens; Maryland Stadium Authority; attendees and event organizers at the Camden Yards football sports facility
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: In FY 2025, Maryland Stadium Authority nonbudgeted expenditures and special fund revenues each increase by $10.0 million due to the mandated transfer of bond proceeds. Special fund revenues increase by $2.0 million annually from FY 2026 through FY 2030 ($1.0 million each from the authority and the Ravens) and by $1.0 million annually thereafter through at least FY 2038. Special fund expenditures increase to pay for capital improvements and emergency repairs. Local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Stadium Authority is the primary administering agency for the newly established Camden Yards Football Sports Facility Capital Works Fund and Camden Yards Football Sports Facility Emergency Repair Fund, which will fund capital improvements and emergency repairs at the facility pursuant to its lease agreement.

The State Treasurer is required to hold and invest the monies of both newly established funds separately and is specifically directed to transfer $10,000,000 in Series 2023B bond proceeds currently held by the Treasurer into the two funds.
The Comptroller is statutorily designated to account for the newly established special funds and manage the accounting of interest earnings.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes temporary relief programs for individuals and businesses impacted by reduced operations at the Port of Baltimore. Authorizes the Governor to transfer funds in increments up to $25,000,000 from the Revenue Stabilization Account. Creates the Fallen Transportation Workers Scholarship Program and Fund for surviving spouses and children of fallen transportation workers. Increases the Maryland Transportation Authority toll revenue bond cap from $3,000,000,000 to $4,000,000,000. Requires the Secretary of Labor to waive unemployment benefit charges against rating records of eligible affected employers. Directs the Attorney General to pursue legal actions to recover State economic damages from the bridge collapse.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor; Maryland Department of Commerce; Maryland Higher Education Commission; Maryland Transportation Authority; Office of the Attorney General
qa_results.stakeholders: Workers and businesses impacted by reduced operations at the Port of Baltimore; surviving spouses and children of fallen transportation workers; Maryland employers subject to unemployment insurance taxes; Maryland Transportation Authority bondholders
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures increase by at least $75.0 million in FY 2024 via transfers from the Rainy Day Fund and existing agency fund balances. MDTA nonbudgeted revenues and debt service expenditures increase significantly to the extent MDTA issues additional revenue bonds under its expanded $1.0 billion debt capacity. Nonbudgeted Unemployment Insurance Trust Fund revenues decrease from FY 2025 through FY 2029 due to employer benefit charge waivers. MHEC general fund expenditures increase beginning in FY 2025 for scholarship awards.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates the Department of Labor to establish and administer temporary relief grant programs for affected workers, small businesses, and labor unions, waives unemployment insurance benefit charges against employers' rating records, and authorizes work search requirement exemptions.

The bill mandates the Department of Commerce to establish and administer a temporary financial relief program for businesses whose operations or shipments rely on the Port of Baltimore and were hindered or diverted.

The bill directly amends the Transportation Article to increase MDTA's outstanding revenue bond cap from $3.0 billion to $4.0 billion to finance capital costs relating to transportation facilities such as the Francis Scott Key Bridge.
The bill creates the Fallen Transportation Workers Scholarship Program and establishes and charges MHEC with the administration of the Fallen Transportation Workers Scholarship Fund.

The bill specifically directs the Attorney General to pursue legal actions to recover economic damages arising from the closure of the Port of Baltimore and the collapse of the Francis Scott Key Bridge and submit monthly status reports to the General Assembly.

The Governor is authorized to transfer funds in increments of up to $25 million by budget amendment from the Rainy Day Fund or departmental fund balances to support the relief programs, and is mandated to provide regular reports and briefings to the Legislative Policy Committee.

The Comptroller is required to account for the new Fallen Transportation Workers Scholarship Fund, authorized to disclose confidential tax information to Labor and Commerce for program administration and fraud prevention, and responsible for administering the income tax subtraction modifications.
The State Treasurer is designated to hold and invest the monies of the newly created Fallen Transportation Workers Scholarship Fund separately as a special, nonlapsing fund.

MDOT is required to provide contact information for families of fallen transportation workers to MHEC for scholarship eligibility, and serves as the umbrella agency overseeing the affected port and bridge infrastructure.

As the modal administration responsible for the Port of Baltimore's public terminals and shipping operations, MPA is directly affected by the emergency response and relief measures resulting from the port's disruption.

Tuition and mandatory fee rates at USM institutions serve as the statutory benchmark cap for awards under the Fallen Transportation Workers Scholarship Program, and USM institutions determine eligibility and verify applicants.

qa_results.bill_summary: Regulates the retail marketing and sale of electricity and gas to protect residential consumers. Establishes licensing requirements and three-year terms for energy salespersons, energy vendors, electricity suppliers, and gas suppliers. Caps residential supply rates, restricts variable pricing, prohibits enrollment commissions for salespersons, and bans automatic renewals for green power. Requires residential energy retailers to provide specific disclosures and prohibits utilities from purchasing supplier accounts receivable. Authorizes the Public Service Commission to assess civil penalties up to $25,000 against suppliers and vendors for violations. Renames the Retail Choice Customer Education and Protection Fund and increases the annual Public Service Commission assessment cap.
qa_results.responsible_party: Public Service Commission; Office of People's Counsel
qa_results.stakeholders: residential electric and gas customers, electricity suppliers, gas suppliers, energy salespersons, energy vendors, and public service companies
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures and revenues for the Public Service Commission and the Office of People's Counsel increase by $1.7 million in FY 2025, rising to $2.1 million by FY 2029, funded through public service company assessments, a one-time $275,000 special assessment in FY 2025, and licensing fees. No material local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Public Service Commission is the primary implementing agency for the bill, tasked with licensing energy salespersons and vendors, enforcing consumer protections, reviewing green power pricing and marketing, administering the Education and Protection Fund, and conducting a co-located load configuration study.

The bill directly impacts the Office of the People's Counsel by expanding its authority in retail supply complaint, licensing, and rate proceedings, while the state budget enacts contingent funding and additional personnel for the agency funded through utility assessments.

The bill requires the Public Service Commission to consult with the Consumer Protection Division of the Office of the Attorney General before adopting customer protection regulations, authorizes the Attorney General to file complaints against suppliers and vendors, and preserves independent enforcement authority under consumer protection statutes.

The bill expresses the intent of the General Assembly for the Department of Budget and Management to create and include two additional Position Identification Numbers (PINs) in the Public Service Commission's fiscal year 2025 budget to support the new retail supply enforcement division.

The bill explicitly excludes the Department of General Services from the definitions and regulatory requirements governing energy salespersons, residential energy retailers, and green power marketing when selling energy under its statutory authority.
The bill specifies that the State Treasurer is responsible for holding separately and investing the moneys of the newly renamed Education and Protection Fund.
The bill designates the Comptroller to account for the Education and Protection Fund.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services to include specified system upgrades in certain vendor contracts. Applies to vendor contracts being negotiated when the act takes effect on October 1, 2024. Mandates system upgrades that allow for the automated expungement and partial expungement of charges. Does not alter existing statutory criteria or eligibility standards for expungement.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Information technology vendors negotiating contracts with the State, and individuals with criminal records potentially eligible for automated or partial expungement.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures for the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services increase by an estimated $26.0 million across five years, assumed to begin in FY 2026, to rebuild and upgrade information technology systems. Local governments experience no fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates that the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services (DPSCS) include system upgrades for automated and partial expungement in vendor contracts being negotiated when the Act takes effect. This requires rebuilding systems within the Criminal Justice Information System (CJIS) Central Repository at an estimated fiscal cost of $26.0 million over five years.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the District Court to shield failure to pay rent records within 60 days if no judgment of possession occurs. Authorizes the court, on tenant motion, to shield records resulting in a judgment of possession under specified conditions. Restricts unshielding of records solely to a tenant's written request or a court order for good cause shown. Requires the Maryland Judiciary to develop and publish a petition form for record shielding by October 1, 2024. Applies record shielding prospectively only to failure to pay rent actions initiated on or after October 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: District Court of Maryland; Maryland Judiciary
qa_results.stakeholders: Residential tenants and landlords in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $23,400 in FY 2025 only for one-time Judiciary computer programming, alongside potential minimal expenditure increases from an expanded District Court caseload. Local finances and State revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the Maryland Judiciary and the District Court by requiring the automatic or petition-based shielding of court records in failure to pay rent proceedings. The Judiciary is also mandated to develop and publish a standardized petition form on its website, incurring IT programming expenditures and operational workload impacts.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Governor to appoint and remove members of the Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners with Senate advice and consent. Transfers appointment, vacancy-filling, and removal authority from the Mayor and City Council President to the Governor. Subjects Board members and employees to State public ethics laws and State Ethics Commission financial disclosure requirements. Allows the executive secretary and deputy executive secretary to qualify through five years of prior Baltimore City government service. Sunsets the alternative city government service qualification for executive secretaries on June 30, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governor; State Ethics Commission; Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: members, candidates, and staff of the Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners; alcoholic beverage license holders and applicants in Baltimore City; Baltimore City government
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or Baltimore City operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill transfers the authority to appoint, fill vacancies for, and remove members of the Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners directly to the Governor.

The Office of Appointments vets, recruits, and processes gubernatorial appointments to state and local boards, which now includes the members and substitute member of the Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners.
The bill shifts ethics compliance and financial disclosure requirements for members and employees of the Board of License Commissioners from Baltimore City ethics laws to the State Ethics Commission.
The bill requires the Governor to file a statement of charges and findings with the Office of the Secretary of State whenever a member of the Board of License Commissioners is removed from office.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires each public high school to inform students of employment and skills training opportunities. Mandates this information be provided in the same manner as postsecondary educational options. Specifies opportunities through registered apprenticeship sponsors, registered employers, and training schools licensed by the Maryland Higher Education Commission. Requires high schools to highlight in-demand, high-skilled careers that do not require a college degree. Requires each county board of education to assist public high schools in meeting these requirements.
qa_results.responsible_party: County boards of education
qa_results.stakeholders: Public high school students, public high schools, county boards of education, registered apprenticeship sponsors, registered employers, and licensed career training schools
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal impact. The bill is not anticipated to have a material effect on local school board operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill places statutory requirements on public high schools and local county boards of education to provide information regarding career skills, apprenticeships, and non-degree training opportunities to students, which falls directly within MSDE's oversight and administration of public K-12 education.

The bill explicitly references apprenticeship programs registered with the Maryland Department of Labor's Division of Workforce Development and Adult Learning (DWDAL) and employers registered with the Department as key sources of skills training opportunities that high schools must inform students about.

The bill explicitly requires high schools to inform students of training, retraining, or employment skills enhancement opportunities available through vocational and technical schools licensed by MHEC.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Board of License Commissioners for Prince George's County to extend license renewal application filing deadlines. Considers unexpired until July 1, 2025, licenses and permits unrenewed between March 5, 2020, and December 31, 2023. Authorizes renewal of those licenses if the holder meets all other renewal requirements and pays all past due fees. Takes effect July 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Prince George's County
qa_results.stakeholders: Alcoholic beverages license and permit holders in Prince George's County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on State finances. Prince George's County finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is the primary state agency with regulatory and tax oversight of the alcoholic beverages industry. While this bill strictly affects local retail license renewal procedures and deadlines administered by the Prince George's County Board of License Commissioners with no state fiscal impact, it relates to the broader alcoholic beverages regulatory framework overseen at the state level by the Comptroller.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires hospitals to provide oral and written educational resources on safe sleep environments before discharging newborn infants. Mandates hospitals ask parents or legal guardians to describe home sleep setups and explain suffocation risks. Directs hospitals to establish processes by January 1, 2025, to distribute materials and maintain confirmation records. Requires the Maryland Department of Health to develop a county resource list by January 1, 2025. Mandates local health departments submit annual updated resource lists to the Department.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Hospitals, newborn infants, parents and legal guardians of newborns, and local health departments
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $19,400 in FY 2025 only for the Maryland Department of Health to hire contractual staff to create the county resource list. Local health departments can update resource lists using existing budgeted resources. State and local revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires the Maryland Department of Health (MDH), in consultation with local health officers, to develop and maintain a county-by-county list of resources for parents and legal guardians to obtain items needed for a safe infant sleep environment. The fiscal note also identifies a direct general fund expenditure impact on MDH of $19,400 in FY 2025 to hire contractual staff to compile this initial list.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands the definition of legally protected health care to include lawful gender-affirming treatment, medications, and supplies. Prohibits State and local government entities from using public resources to assist out-of-state investigations into protected care. Restricts Maryland health occupations boards from disciplining practitioners for providing or supporting lawful gender-affirming treatment. Bars State judges from compelling testimony, issuing foreign subpoenas, or enforcing foreign judgments concerning protected care. Prohibits the Governor from surrendering individuals demanded by other states for providing or receiving lawful gender-affirming treatment.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Health Occupations Boards; Maryland Judiciary; Office of the Governor
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals receiving gender-affirming treatment; licensed health care practitioners providing or supporting gender-affirming care; health occupations boards; state and local government agencies
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material fiscal effect on State or local government finances, as the changes are procedural in nature.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill impacts health occupations licensing boards housed within the Department of Health by prohibiting them from disciplining, revoking, suspending, or taking adverse licensing actions against health care practitioners for providing lawful gender-affirming care.

The bill directly restricts Maryland courts and clerks from issuing ex parte orders, compelling witness testimony or document production, issuing subpoenas, or enforcing foreign judgments in connection with out-of-state proceedings concerning legally protected gender-affirming health care.

The bill explicitly prohibits the Governor from surrendering an individual upon an interstate extradition demand from another state if the demanded act relates to providing or receiving legally protected gender-affirming health care.

The Secretary of State processes extraditions on behalf of the Governor, which are directly affected by the bill's prohibition on surrendering persons facing out-of-state charges for legally protected gender-affirming care.

By expanding the definition of legally protected health care to include gender-affirming care, the bill triggers statutory insurance protections regulated by the Administration that prohibit medical professional liability insurers from taking adverse actions against practitioners.

As the primary personnel agency overseeing the State Personnel and Pensions Article, DBM is implicated by amendments to Section 2-312 barring the use of state personnel and resources in out-of-state investigations against protected health care.

The Office of the Attorney General advises state agencies and officials regarding compliance with shield laws, interstate legal requests, subpoenas, and foreign legal challenges involving legally protected health care.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Office of the Correctional Ombudsman as an independent unit of State government. Authorizes the Office to investigate administrative acts and conduct independent reviews of health, mental health, and educational programs. Empowers the Office to inspect facilities, subpoena testimony and documents, and refer matters for criminal or disciplinary proceedings. Transfers the Juvenile Justice Monitoring Unit from the Office of the Attorney General into the new Office. Prohibits retaliatory personnel actions against state correctional or juvenile services employees who disclose information to the Office. Establishes a 12-member Correctional Ombudsman Advisory Board appointed by the Governor to provide assistance.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Correctional Ombudsman; Correctional Ombudsman Advisory Board; Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services; Department of Juvenile Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals confined by or under the supervision of the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services or the Department of Juvenile Services, and employees and contractors of both departments.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund expenditures increase by $1.0 million in FY 2025 from the Performance Incentive Grant Fund to establish the office. General fund expenditures increase by $836,800 in FY 2026 and rise to $914,000 by FY 2029 for ongoing staff and operational costs. Additionally, $603,067 in existing general funds and four positions transfer from the Office of the Attorney General to the new office. Potential indeterminate additional general fund expenditures for the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS is the primary target of oversight for the newly established Office of the Correctional Ombudsman, which is empowered to investigate administrative acts, inspect DPSCS facilities, review medical and mental health services, access records, and audit inmate programming.

The bill transfers the Juvenile Justice Monitoring Unit, along with its four authorized positions and $603,067 in funding, out of the Office of the Attorney General to the newly created independent Office of the Correctional Ombudsman.

DJS is directly overseen by the Juvenile Justice Monitoring Unit within the new office, which investigates facilities, monitors juvenile grievance processes, inspects conditions, and reviews complaints regarding youth under DJS jurisdiction.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill authorizes the Justice Reinvestment Oversight Board (staffed and housed within GOCPP) to recommend the distribution of savings from the Performance Incentive Grant Fund to fund the Office of the Correctional Ombudsman for fiscal year 2025.

The Governor appoints the Correctional Ombudsman with Senate advice and consent, appoints the members of the Correctional Ombudsman Advisory Board, and receives required annual and coordination reports.

The Judiciary's Mediation and Conflict Resolution Office is mandated to submit a report to the Ombudsman, Governor, and General Assembly on best practices for mediating grievances in the corrections system, and circuit courts are tasked with enforcing subpoenas issued by the office.

The Secretary of Budget and Management must cooperate with the Correctional Ombudsman to establish minimum salaries, qualifications, and standards of training and experience for positions within the office.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Correctional Ombudsman Advisory Board, a permanent advisory body charged with assisting the office in identifying matters to investigate and developing complaint processes.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting and processing appointments for the Correctional Ombudsman position and the 12 members of the Correctional Ombudsman Advisory Board.

The Juvenile Justice Monitoring Unit is directed to collaborate with DHS and local departments of social services on licensing, monitoring children's residential facilities, and child protective services investigations.
The Juvenile Justice Monitoring Unit is required to collaborate with MDH on matters related to the licensing and monitoring of children's residential facilities.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Workgroup to Study Funding for the Westernport Wastewater Treatment Facility. Requires the Department of the Environment to provide staff for the Workgroup. Directs the Workgroup to study existing and prospective federal, State, and local funding sources for the facility. Charges the Workgroup with examining whether increased funding could enhance facility operations. Requires the Workgroup to report its findings and recommendations to the Governor and General Assembly by December 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment; Workgroup to Study Funding for the Westernport Wastewater Treatment Facility; Upper Potomac River Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: residents and wastewater customers in Westernport and Luke, Maryland, and Piedmont, West Virginia; Allegany County; Upper Potomac River Commission
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expense reimbursements and staffing costs for the Maryland Department of the Environment are minimal and absorbable within existing budgeted resources. Local government finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of the Environment is the primary state agency responsible for staffing the Workgroup, and the Secretary of the Environment (or designee) serves as a designated member.
The Secretary of Budget and Management, or the Secretary's designee, serves as a statutory member of the Workgroup to study existing and potential funding sources.
The Secretary of Health, or the Secretary's designee, is designated as a member of the Workgroup.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a temporary advisory body, the Workgroup to Study Funding for the Westernport Wastewater Treatment Facility, tasked with evaluating operational funding and submitting recommendations.
The Workgroup is required to submit its report of findings and recommendations to the Governor by December 1, 2024.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes local school system superintendents and the Maryland School for the Deaf superintendent to rehire up to five retirees. Expands the reemployment offset exemption from school-based positions to any position within the school system. Applies to retirees of the Teachers' Retirement System and Teachers' Pension System. Establishes retroactive application for qualifying retirees reemployed by the Harford County Board of Education Payroll Department. Requires the Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System to refund offsets by December 31, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System; local school system superintendents; Superintendent of the Maryland School for the Deaf
qa_results.stakeholders: Retirees of the Teachers' Retirement System and Teachers' Pension System reemployed by local school systems or the Maryland School for the Deaf, including reemployed Harford County Board of Education payroll staff
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No discernible effect on State pension liabilities, contribution rates, or State revenues. No local fiscal effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the reemployment offset provisions for the Teachers' Retirement System and Teachers' Pension System, which are administered by the State Retirement Agency. Additionally, the bill mandates that the Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System issue a retroactive refund of any retirement benefit offset to a qualifying retiree.

The bill explicitly grants the Superintendent of the Maryland School for the Deaf the authority to rehire up to five retirees of the Teachers' Retirement and Pension Systems into any position at the agency (expanding beyond strictly school-based positions) without triggering a retirement benefit offset.

The Maryland State Department of Education oversees the state's 24 local school systems, whose superintendents are granted broadened authority under this bill to rehire retirees into non-school-based positions (such as central office roles) without a benefit offset.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Governor to include an annual $1,000,000 budget appropriation for fiscal years 2026 through 2028. Dedicates the funds solely as operating grants to qualifying nonprofit organizations for automotive repair training. Requires recipient organizations to train formerly incarcerated individuals and achieve at least a 50% job placement rate. Directs the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention, Youth, and Victim Services to administer the grant program. Requires grant recipients to submit annual expenditure proofs, participant counts, and outcome-based performance measures. Sunsets the program on June 30, 2028.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention, Youth, and Victim Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Qualifying nonprofit organizations providing reentry services, and incarcerated or formerly incarcerated individuals receiving automotive repair job training
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $529,700 in FY 2025, which includes a contingent $500,000 operating grant to Vehicles for Change Inc. and $29,661 for administrative staff. Future expenditures assume discretionary $1.0 million annual grant appropriations through FY 2028 plus ongoing administrative expenses through early FY 2029. Revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates that the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy (formerly Governor's Office of Crime Prevention, Youth, and Victim Services) administer the grant funds, collect reporting and outcome data from recipient nonprofits, and oversee the program, which also creates direct administrative expenditures and staffing needs.

The bill authorizes the Governor to include a discretionary appropriation of $1.0 million annually in the state budget bill for fiscal years 2026 through 2028 for the automotive repair reentry grant program.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes Prince George's County to grant a property tax credit on dwellings owned by qualifying public school employees. Limits eligibility to full-time school employees of at least two years who relocated to the county upon purchase. Caps the tax credit at the lesser of $2,500 or the property tax imposed on the dwelling. Requires a county report on credit recipients within five years after enacting the local credit law. Designates the Office of Integrity and Compliance as an independent unit within the local school system. Authorizes the Office of Integrity and Compliance to hire staff under the direction of the compliance officer.
qa_results.responsible_party: Prince George's County Council; Prince George's County Public School System; Office of Integrity and Compliance
qa_results.stakeholders: Full-time Prince George's County Public School System employees who relocate to the county, Prince George's County government, and the Prince George's County Public School System Office of Integrity and Compliance
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Prince George's County property tax revenues decrease beginning in fiscal 2025 to the extent the local credit is enacted and granted; the exact decrease is indeterminate. County expenditures and State finances are not directly affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Education Article regarding the internal governance, reporting, and operations of the Office of Integrity and Compliance within the Prince George's County Public School System, which operates under the overarching state public education regulatory framework overseen by MSDE.

The bill specifically directs the Integrity and Compliance Officer of the local school system to report allegations of serious violations of law to the State Ethics Commission, which oversees ethics standards for school boards and local educational authorities.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Pricing and Selection Committee for Preferred Providers to waive mandatory procurement from Maryland Correctional Enterprises. Permits waivers when prices are at least 10% above market rates or delivery times do not meet entity needs. Requires the Committee to review waiver requests submitted by a State or State-aided or controlled entity. Requires Maryland Correctional Enterprises to report annually on the length of time between each order and delivery. Requires the Department of General Services to adopt implementing regulations.
qa_results.responsible_party: Pricing and Selection Committee for Preferred Providers; Department of General Services; Maryland Correctional Enterprises
qa_results.stakeholders: State and State-aided or controlled entities, Maryland Correctional Enterprises, and commercial vendors including small businesses providing supplies and services to the State
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Potential significant decrease in Maryland Correctional Enterprises nonbudgeted sales revenues, potentially exceeding $1.0 million. Potential significant decrease in State expenditures across all funds if entities purchase lower-priced supplies and services under waivers. Reliable estimates are not feasible; no local impact.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Maryland Correctional Enterprises (MCE) is a division of DPSCS. The bill establishes new waiver criteria allowing state entities to bypass purchasing from MCE if prices are at least 10% above market rates or delivery timelines cannot be met, potentially resulting in a significant decrease in MCE's nonbudgeted sales revenues. The Secretary of Public Safety and Correctional Services also sits on the Pricing and Selection Committee for Preferred Providers, and MCE is required to submit new annual delivery reporting.

DGS is mandated by the bill to adopt regulations implementing the new preferred provider waiver provisions and receives annual compliance and delivery reports from MCE. Additionally, the Secretary of General Services serves on the Pricing and Selection Committee for Preferred Providers.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Pricing and Selection Committee for Preferred Providers is granted the explicit statutory authority under the bill to review waiver requests and grant waivers to State or State-aided or controlled entities.

The Secretary of Transportation or a designee is a statutory member of the Pricing and Selection Committee for Preferred Providers, which is responsible for reviewing and granting the procurement waivers authorized by the bill.

The Assistant Secretary for Vocational Rehabilitation within the Maryland State Department of Education serves as a designated statutory member of the Pricing and Selection Committee for Preferred Providers.
The Secretary of Labor or a designee is a designated statutory member of the Pricing and Selection Committee for Preferred Providers tasked with reviewing and granting waivers under the bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Caregiver Expense Grant Program within the Maryland Department of Aging. Authorizes the Department to award grants to caregivers for qualified expenses supporting qualified family members. Restricts eligibility to caregivers with federal adjusted gross income up to $75,000, or $150,000 for joint filers. Sets grant awards at 30% of qualified expenses exceeding $2,000, capped at $2,500 per fiscal year. Authorizes the Governor to include an appropriation of up to $5,000,000 annually in the state budget bill.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Aging
qa_results.stakeholders: Family and informal caregivers providing care to qualified elderly individuals or individuals with disabilities
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Assuming funding is provided at the authorized level, State general fund expenditures increase by $5.0 million annually beginning in fiscal 2026 for grants and administrative costs, including two new staff positions. Revenues are not affected. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: SB 202 establishes the Caregiver Expense Grant Program within the Maryland Department of Aging, making it the primary agency responsible for administering grant applications, awarding grants to eligible caregivers, and adopting implementing regulations.
The bill explicitly authorizes the Governor to include an appropriation of up to $5,000,000 in the annual budget bill for the Caregiver Expense Grant Program.

As the agency responsible for state budget preparation and personnel oversight, DBM would oversee the incorporation of the authorized $5,000,000 annual appropriation and evaluate new personnel positions needed to administer the grant program.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires appointing officials to ensure one University System of Maryland regent graduated from a system historically Black institution. Applies the requirement to appointments made by the Governor, the President of the Senate, and the Speaker of the House. Specifies that the member must have graduated from a historically Black college or university in the University System of Maryland. Applies this mandate prospectively after the next board vacancy occurring after July 1, 2024. Takes effect July 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governor; President of the Senate; Speaker of the House; Board of Regents of the University System of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Graduates of historically Black colleges and universities in the University System of Maryland (Bowie State University, Coppin State University, and the University of Maryland Eastern Shore) and members of the Board of Regents of the University System of Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the statutory membership criteria for the University System of Maryland's governing body, the Board of Regents, by requiring that at least one member be a graduate of an HBCU within the system.
The Governor is one of the primary appointing authorities tasked by the bill with ensuring that the Board of Regents includes a graduate of an HBCU within the University System of Maryland.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and recommending candidates for state boards and commissions, and will need to factor in this qualification requirement when vetting future nominees for the USM Board of Regents.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters membership requirements for the Maryland Economic Development Commission to include representatives from the life sciences and manufacturing industries. Requires the industries represented by Commission members to be diverse. Repeals requirements that the Commission incorporate the Port of Baltimore strategic plan or seek private-sector contributions. Removes mandates that the Commission review Department of Commerce budget requests and approve financing regulations before adoption. Repeals reporting requirements for the Office of International Trade and tourism plan submissions by the Maryland Tourism Development Board.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Economic Development Commission; Department of Commerce; Maryland Tourism Development Board
qa_results.stakeholders: members of the Maryland Economic Development Commission, life sciences industry businesses, manufacturing businesses, and Department of Commerce staff
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on State finances or operations. The changes align statutory responsibilities with current practice and do not affect Commission expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: SB 209 is a departmental bill requested by the Department of Commerce.
