It directly alters the statutory requirements, duties, and membership qualifications of the Maryland Economic Development Commission (which Commerce staffs), repeals the requirement for Commerce's Office of International Trade to report to the Commission, and eliminates Commission pre-approval/review for Commerce budget requests and financing regulations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the composition, mandates, and statutory duties of the Maryland Economic Development Commission, an executive commission established to guide state economic development policy.

The bill repeals the requirement that the Commission incorporate the Maryland Port Administration's strategic plan developed for the Helen Delich Bentley Port of Baltimore into the State's economic development strategic plan.
The bill repeals the requirement that the Maryland Tourism Development Board submit its five-year strategic plan and annual marketing plan to the Commission for review.

The Governor appoints up to 21 voting members of the Commission. The bill alters statutory appointment requirements by mandating representation from the life sciences and manufacturing industries while ensuring diverse industry representation.

The Office of Appointments vets and manages gubernatorial appointments to state boards and commissions, and will need to implement the new criteria requiring representation from the life sciences and manufacturing industries on the Commission.

The Executive Director of MEDCO serves as an ex officio member of the Commission, and MEDCO's economic development activities are reviewed by the Commission for compliance with the State strategic plan.

The CEO of TEDCO serves as an ex officio member of the Commission, and TEDCO's economic development activities remain subject to periodic review by the Commission for alignment with the State strategic plan.
MDOT is the parent department of the Maryland Port Administration, whose port strategic plan is no longer statutorily mandated to be incorporated into the State economic development strategic plan.
The Secretary of Labor (or designee) serves as an ex officio nonvoting member of the Maryland Economic Development Commission.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the authority of paramedics to administer influenza and COVID-19 immunizations until January 1, 2030. Authorizes paramedics to provide these immunizations as part of population health outreach efforts. Requires these efforts to be conducted by a local health department, hospital, or health system. Mandates a written agreement covering vaccine administration to individuals who are at least 18 years old. Requires medical director oversight, approval by the Institute, and documentation in the ImmuNet system.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems; Emergency Medical Services Board
qa_results.stakeholders: Paramedics, emergency medical services operational programs, ambulance services, local health departments, Maryland hospitals and health systems, and adult vaccine recipients
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No substantive impact on State activities or finances and no material effect on local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MIEMSS requested this departmental legislation and serves as the primary regulatory body overseeing emergency medical services and paramedics in Maryland, including the approval and authorization of paramedic immunization administration protocols.

The bill involves immunization outreach efforts coordinated with local health departments, which are overseen by MDH, and requires documentation in the state's immunization registry (ImmuNet) maintained by MDH.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the membership of the Maryland Military Installation Council to add state officials and community representatives. Adds the Secretary of Labor and the State Superintendent of Schools, or their designees, to the Council. Increases the number of Governor-appointed members from five to six. qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Military Installation Council; Maryland Department of Commerce
qa_results.stakeholders: Military service members and military spouses in Maryland, military base advocacy alliances, and state education and labor officials.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expense reimbursements for new council members are minimal and absorbable within existing budgeted resources. The bill does not affect local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This is a departmental bill requested by the Department of Commerce, which houses and supports the Maryland Military Installation Council under the Economic Development Article, and the Secretary of Commerce serves as a statutory member.
The bill amends the statute to add the Secretary of Labor (or their designee) as a new voting member of the Maryland Military Installation Council to coordinate on workforce matters.

The bill explicitly adds the State Superintendent of Schools (or their designee), the head of MSDE, as a new voting member of the Maryland Military Installation Council to address education and child care needs of military families.
The bill increases the number of council members appointed by the Governor from five to six and adds a requirement that at least one appointee must be the spouse of a service member.
The Secretary of the department serves as a statutory member of the Maryland Military Installation Council, which supports military bases, active-duty service members, and their families.
The Adjutant General of the Maryland National Guard serves as a statutory member of the Maryland Military Installation Council.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Military Installation Council is an executive advisory body whose statutory membership composition and naming conventions are directly altered by this legislation.
The Secretary of Transportation serves as an ongoing statutory member of the Maryland Military Installation Council.
The Secretary of the Environment serves as an ongoing statutory member of the Maryland Military Installation Council.

The Secretary of Planning serves as an ongoing statutory member of the Maryland Military Installation Council, which deals with land encroachment and community development around military installations.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting and vetting candidates for state boards and commissions, and will facilitate the appointment of the additional gubernatorial appointee (a service member spouse).

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters penalties assessed against employers who fail to secure required workers' compensation insurance for covered employees. Requires the Workers' Compensation Commission to order a noncompliant employer to pay a $25,000 penalty to the Uninsured Employers' Fund. Authorizes the Commission to order an additional $25,000 penalty if an employer disobeys an order to insure. Establishes that failure to pay an assessed penalty constitutes a default in payment of compensation. Takes effect July 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Workers' Compensation Commission; Uninsured Employers' Fund
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland employers required to maintain workers' compensation insurance, corporate officers and LLC members with general management responsibilities, covered employees, and the Uninsured Employers' Fund
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues for the Uninsured Employers' Fund increase, potentially by a couple hundred thousand dollars or more annually beginning in fiscal 2025. Specific figures are unavailable because annual penalty assessments and collections vary widely. State and local expenditures are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Workers' Compensation Commission is the primary regulatory and adjudicative agency responsible for holding show-cause hearings for noncompliant employers, issuing orders to secure insurance, and assessing the increased statutory penalties of up to $25,000 for failure to insure or failure to comply with commission orders.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the termination date of the Senior Prescription Drug Assistance Program from December 31, 2024, to December 31, 2030. Continues prescription drug benefit subsidies for eligible Medicare beneficiaries with household incomes at or below 300% of federal poverty guidelines. Requires the Maryland Department of Health to administer the program and maintain an eligibility waiting list. Authorizes the Department to determine annual enrollment numbers and subsidy amounts. Authorizes additional subsidies for individuals qualifying for a partial federal low-income subsidy. Takes effect October 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland Medicare Part D beneficiaries with household incomes at or below 300% of the federal poverty guidelines
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues and expenditures for the Senior Prescription Drug Assistance Program are maintained through the first half of fiscal 2031. The Governor's proposed fiscal 2025 budget includes $11.7 million for the program. No local fiscal effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health is statutorily responsible for administering the Senior Prescription Drug Assistance Program (SPDAP) and requested this departmental legislation to extend the program's sunset date through December 31, 2030.

The Maryland Health Insurance Plan (MHIP) board has historical and administrative ties to the operation of the Senior Prescription Drug Assistance Program as referenced in the bill's uncodified provisions and agency responsibilities.
SPDAP is funded by special fund revenues derived from the CareFirst premium tax exemption under § 14-106 of the Insurance Article, which is overseen by the Maryland Insurance Administration.

The Department of Aging serves Maryland's older adults and frequently coordinates healthcare and prescription assistance outreach, including Medicare Part D education and enrollment guidance for the population served by SPDAP.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes applicants for environmental health specialist licensure to complete a Board-approved apprenticeship instead of a specialist-in-training program. Defines an apprenticeship as supervised practical training required as part of an approved baccalaureate degree. Exempts individuals participating in an approved apprenticeship from environmental health specialist licensure requirements. Authorizes the State Board of Environmental Health Specialists to approve an external examination provider to administer licensure examinations. Requires the Board to adopt regulations governing approval standards and duration limits for apprenticeships. Clarifies that a quorum of the Board consists of a majority of appointed members.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Environmental Health Specialists
qa_results.stakeholders: Applicants for environmental health specialist licensure, students enrolled in environmental health baccalaureate degree programs, environmental health specialists-in-training, and licensed environmental health specialists
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Indeterminate minimal increase in special fund revenues beginning in fiscal 2025 if more environmental health specialist licenses are issued. Requirements, including adopting regulations, can be handled using existing budgeted resources. Local government operations and finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Environmental Health Specialists is a health occupations licensing board housed administratively within the Maryland Department of Health (MDH). MDH sponsored this departmental legislation, and the department will implement the statutory changes governing the Board's quorum, licensure exam administration, and apprenticeship approval regulations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Environmental Health Specialists is directly affected by the bill, which alters its quorum requirements to a majority of appointed members, authorizes the Board to approve third-party examination providers, and requires the Board to establish regulations for environmental health specialist apprenticeships.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the person in charge of a cemetery to record additional information on burial-transit permits. Alternatively, they must record the authorizing agent's contact details and relationship if the agent takes control of cremains. Morticians must complete this required information if no person is in charge of the cemetery.

qa_results.stakeholders: cemetery operators, crematory authorities, morticians, funeral directors, and authorizing agents receiving cremated remains

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill is a departmental bill requested by the Department of Labor, whose Office of Cemetery Oversight regulates cemeteries and independent crematories affected by the permit recording requirements.

Burial-transit permits are mandated under the Health - General Article and returned to the Secretary of Health; the Department of Health also oversees the State Board of Morticians and Funeral Directors and the Division of Vital Records.

qa_results.bill_summary: Continues the Occupational Safety and Health Advisory Board under the Maryland Program Evaluation Act. agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The legislation directly extends the statutory life and authorization of the Occupational Safety and Health Advisory Board through July 1, 2034.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Acupuncture Board is a health occupations licensing board housed within the Maryland Department of Health. qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the termination date for the State Board for Certification of Residential Child Care Program Professionals to July 1, 2030. qa_results.stakeholders: Residential child care program administrators, residential child and youth care practitioners, and licensed residential child care programs
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Maintains State general fund revenues and expenditures for the Board through fiscal 2030. No effect on local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board for Certification of Residential Child Care Program Professionals is housed within the Maryland Department of Health, which requested the legislation to extend the board's statutory termination date.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the termination date for the State Board of Dietetic Practice by five years to July 1, 2030. qa_results.stakeholders: licensed dietitian-nutritionists and license applicants in Maryland

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Dietetic Practice is an occupational licensing board housed within the Maryland Department of Health. This bill directly extends the Board's statutory authority and operations through July 1, 2030.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the termination date for the State Board of Occupational Therapy Practice to July 1, 2030. qa_results.stakeholders: licensed occupational therapists, licensed occupational therapy assistants, and recipients of occupational therapy services in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues and expenditures for the Board are maintained through fiscal 2030. There is no local fiscal impact.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the termination date for the State Board of Examiners in Optometry to July 1, 2030. Continues the board in accordance with the Maryland Program Evaluation Act. agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Examiners in Optometry is an occupational licensing and regulatory board housed within the Maryland Department of Health. qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the termination date for the State Board of Examiners of Psychologists to July 1, 2030. qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Examiners of Psychologists; Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: licensed psychologists, registered psychology associates, and mental health consumers in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Maintains special fund revenues and expenditures for the State Board of Examiners of Psychologists through fiscal 2030. Has no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Examiners of Psychologists is housed within the Maryland Department of Health (MDH) under the Health Occupations Article. qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the statutory and regulatory authority of the State Board of Social Work Examiners to July 1, 2030. qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the termination date for the Behavior Analyst Advisory Committee to July 1, 2026. qa_results.stakeholders: licensed behavior analysts in Maryland, applicants for behavior analyst licensure, and consumers of behavior analysis services
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Maintains special fund revenues and expenditures for the Behavior Analyst Advisory Committee and board regulatory duties through fiscal 2026. No local fiscal effect. Specific dollar figures are not provided.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Community Health Resources Commission (MCHRC) is an independent commission that operates within the Maryland Department of Health. qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits county public libraries from charging overdue fines or reserve fees to minors. Prohibits these fees for library materials intended for children or teens. Bars libraries from prohibiting borrowing for such overdue materials until 21 days or more after the due date. Prohibits charging replacement fees for these materials until 21 days after the due date. Requires libraries to cancel replacement fees if materials return undamaged, or refund them within six months of payment. Excludes designated special collections from these requirements.
qa_results.responsible_party: Boards of library trustees; county public libraries
qa_results.stakeholders: Minors, patrons borrowing library materials intended for children or teens, and county public library systems (notably Allegany, Garrett, and Washington counties)

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill was requested by the Maryland State Library Agency as a departmental bill and establishes statutory prohibitions and requirements concerning overdue fines, reserve fees, and replacement fees for public library materials across Maryland's 24 county public library systems, which the agency coordinates and supports.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the allowable uses of money in the 9-1-1 Trust Fund. Prohibits using State 9-1-1 fee revenue to pay salaries of public safety answering point or county personnel. Authorizes counties to use local 9-1-1 fee distributions to pay those personnel salaries. Retains the ban on using fund monies for purposes associated with the 9-8-8 suicide prevention hotline. Takes effect immediately as an emergency measure.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Emergency Management; Maryland 9-1-1 Board; Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: county governments, public safety answering point personnel, and county 9-1-1 personnel
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The bill is clarifying in nature and conforms statutory language to current practice.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDEM oversees the Maryland 9-1-1 Board and the administration of the 9-1-1 Trust Fund. This departmental legislation was requested by MDEM to clarify statutory restrictions regarding the use of State versus local 9-1-1 fee revenues for public safety answering point personnel salaries.

The Comptroller of Maryland receives remitted 9-1-1 fees, maintains the dedicated accounts within the 9-1-1 Trust Fund, allocates investment earnings, and disburses funds to counties and vendors as directed under the statute.
The 9-1-1 Trust Fund is administered subject to financial management and budgeting guidelines established by DBM, and disbursements must align with the State budget.

qa_results.bill_summary: Transfers administration of the Volunteer Company Assistance Fund from the Military Department to the Maryland Department of Emergency Management. Requires the Maryland State Firemen's Association to submit annual grant and loan reports to the department. Directs the Maryland Department of Emergency Management to review annual documentation of volunteer company expenditures. Requires the department to report review findings annually to specified legislative committees. Takes effect October 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Emergency Management
qa_results.stakeholders: Volunteer ambulance, fire, and rescue companies in Maryland and qualifying out-of-state companies
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact, as the bill codifies existing practice transferring fund management to the Maryland Department of Emergency Management.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill formally transfers the administration, review, and reporting responsibilities of the Volunteer Company Assistance Fund (VCAF) to the Maryland Department of Emergency Management.

The Adjutant General heads the Maryland Military Department, from which the statutory duties and oversight of the Volunteer Company Assistance Fund are being officially removed and transferred to MDEM.

The Board of Public Works is designated in the statute to receive the annual report on grants and loans from the Maryland State Firemen's Association and approves the requests funded through the VCAF.

The Legislative Auditor receives annual reports regarding VCAF grants and loans and is authorized to review documentation to verify that funds were spent in accordance with statutory requirements and approved requests.
The Comptroller is statutorily authorized under the subtitle to audit the financial affairs of the Maryland State Firemen's Association to ensure compliance with VCAF provisions.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the termination date of the State Board of Physical Therapy Examiners from July 1, 2025, to July 1, 2030. Continues the Board in accordance with the Maryland Program Evaluation Act. Maintains the statutory and regulatory authority of the Board over physical therapy practice in the State. Takes effect July 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Physical Therapy Examiners
qa_results.stakeholders: Licensed physical therapists, licensed physical therapist assistants, and consumers receiving physical therapy services in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Maintains special fund revenues and expenditures for the State Board of Physical Therapy Examiners through fiscal 2030. Has no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Physical Therapy Examiners is an occupational licensing board housed directly within the Maryland Department of Health. This departmental bill extends the board's termination date through July 1, 2030, maintaining its regulatory authority, special fund revenues, and operations.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases the State's target for reducing average energy consumption in State buildings to 20% by 2031 from fiscal 2018 levels. Requires the Maryland Green Building Council to update the High Performance Green Building Program by October 1, 2024. Directs the Department of General Services to identify State-owned facilities suitable for energy savings performance contracts. Mandates annual energy and greenhouse gas audits of at least 2,000,000 square feet of State-owned buildings. Requires each unit of State government to implement audit recommendations to the fullest extent practicable. Instructs the Department to maintain a utility database and report annually on agency compliance and progress.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of General Services; Maryland Green Building Council; Maryland Energy Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Units of State government; energy efficiency and construction contractors; commercial landlords leasing space to the State
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No direct state or local fiscal impact because the bill codifies existing Executive Order 01.01.2023.07; implementation costs and savings are attributable to the executive order.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DGS is the primary implementing agency responsible for setting energy performance indices, conducting annual energy and GHG emissions audits of at least 2 million square feet of State-owned buildings, managing the Comprehensive Utility Records Management Database, identifying candidates for energy savings performance contracts, and reporting annually on progress.
MEA is explicitly required to cooperate with DGS to assist State agencies in reducing the average energy consumption in State buildings by 20% from the fiscal year 2018 baseline by 2031.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Green Building Council is specifically mandated to update the High Performance Green Building Program by October 1, 2024, to align with the State's net-zero greenhouse gas emissions goal by 2045 and submit the updated program to the Governor and General Assembly.

The Governor's Office receives required statutory deliverables under the bill, including the Maryland Green Building Council's updated program report, annual reports from DGS on State unit utility data compliance, and annual progress reports on the 20% energy reduction goal.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the termination date of the State Board of Barbers to July 1, 2027. Continues the board's statutory and regulatory authority under the Maryland Program Evaluation Act. Requires the Maryland Department of Labor to submit a report to the Joint Audit and Evaluation Committee by July 1, 2025. Mandates that the report contain information regarding the State Board of Barbers as determined by the committee.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Barbers; Maryland Department of Labor
qa_results.stakeholders: Licensed barbers, barber-stylists, registered apprentices, and barber shop owners in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues and expenditures for the State Board of Barbers are maintained through fiscal 2027. The Maryland Department of Labor can prepare the required report with existing budgeted resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Barbers is housed within the Maryland Department of Labor. The bill extends the termination date of the Board to July 1, 2027, maintaining its licensing and regulatory operations and special fund finances, and requires the Department to submit a report to the Joint Audit and Evaluation Committee by July 1, 2025.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the termination date of the State Board of Cosmetologists to July 1, 2027. Continues the statutory and regulatory authority of the Board under the Maryland Program Evaluation Act. Requires the Maryland Department of Labor to submit a report to the Joint Audit and Evaluation Committee. Directs the Department to submit the report on or before July 1, 2025. Specifies that the Joint Audit and Evaluation Committee determines the information required in the report.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor; State Board of Cosmetologists
qa_results.stakeholders: Licensed cosmetologists, senior cosmetologists, hairstylists, blow-drying stylists, nail technicians, estheticians, registered apprentices, and beauty salons in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues and expenditures for the State Board of Cosmetologists are maintained through fiscal 2027. The Maryland Department of Labor can likely submit the required report with existing resources, resulting in no direct net fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Cosmetologists is housed within the Maryland Department of Labor (Division of Occupational and Professional Licensing). This departmental bill extends the board's statutory termination date to July 1, 2027, maintaining its licensing and regulatory operations, and explicitly requires the Department of Labor to submit a report on the board to the Joint Audit and Evaluation Committee.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters enforcement and after-the-fact application approval procedures under local Critical Area programs to apply to all Critical Area violations. Prohibits local jurisdictions from issuing permits, approvals, variances, or special exceptions until all violation penalties are fully paid. Prohibits local jurisdictions from accepting variance applications to legalize violations without first issuing a violation notice and penalty assessment. Repeals the 30-day waiting period before the Critical Area Commission Chair may refer enforcement matters to the Attorney General. Expands the Attorney General's authority to bring equitable actions for violations of orders, permits, plans, local programs, or regulations.
qa_results.responsible_party: Critical Area Commission for the Chesapeake and Atlantic Coastal Bays; Office of the Attorney General
qa_results.stakeholders: Property owners and developers in the Chesapeake and Atlantic Coastal Bays Critical Area; local governments with land in the Critical Area
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Does not materially affect State or local finances or operations, with only potential minimal increases in enforcement actions by the Office of the Attorney General.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Critical Area Commission for the Chesapeake and Atlantic Coastal Bays operates as an administrative unit within the Department of Natural Resources, and the bill amends the Natural Resources Article to alter enforcement and violation procedures administered under its oversight.

The bill directly broadens the authority of the Attorney General to initiate actions in equity to compel compliance or restrain noncompliance for critical area violations and repeals the 30-day waiting period required before the Chair of the Critical Area Commission can refer enforcement matters to the Attorney General.

The bill alters judicial enforcement provisions and remedies for critical area violations, which are subject to prosecution, civil suits, and equitable actions brought in the District Court and circuit courts.

qa_results.bill_summary: Reduces the membership of each adult public guardianship review board from 11 to 8 members. Requires local appointing authorities to recruit and appoint board members. Broadens medical qualification categories to include registered nurses, psychiatric nurse practitioners, and mental health medication specialists. Combines disability representation requirements into either a disabilities professional or a person with a disability. Repeals county-specific membership provisions for St. Mary's and Washington counties. Authorizes board members to serve another term upon appointment and repeals staggered term requirements.
qa_results.responsible_party: County Commissioners; Baltimore City Mayor; County Executives; Maryland Department of Human Services
qa_results.stakeholders: vulnerable adults under public guardianship, adult public guardianship review board members, local appointing authorities, and local departments of social services
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This is a departmental bill requested by the Department of Human Services (DHS). DHS oversees Adult Protective Services and the local departments of social services, whose representatives sit on the adult public guardianship review boards and often serve as public guardians.

The bill governs adult public guardianship review boards, which protect vulnerable and older adults. The statute specifically mandates that each review board include a representative from a local commission on aging.

The bill modifies review board membership criteria regarding representation from the disability community, requiring one member to be a professional in the field of disabilities or an individual with a disability.

qa_results.bill_summary: Modifies court reporting requirements to include only individuals convicted of a felony and sentenced to imprisonment with commitment papers. Requires public officials managing requested public buildings to make them available to local boards for early voting centers. Requires the State Board of Elections to adopt regulations establishing an appeals process for public officials contesting building availability. Requires final appeal decisions at least eight months before the primary election for the requested voting center. Authorizes an incumbent political party central committee member running for party office to serve as any responsible officer.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Elections; Maryland Judiciary; local boards of elections
qa_results.stakeholders: voters, individuals convicted of felonies sentenced to imprisonment, public officials managing public buildings, local boards of elections, and incumbent political party central committee members running for party office
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $170,000 in FY 2025 for one-time Judiciary programming costs to modify felony reporting. Local government expenditures decrease in certain counties beginning in FY 2026 due to reduced rental costs for early voting facilities.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill is a departmental initiative requested by the State Board of Elections (SBE). It modifies voter registration ineligibility reporting procedures received by the State Administrator of Elections, tasks SBE with adopting regulations establishing an appeals process for public building usage as early voting centers, and alters provisions related to campaign finance entities for political party central committee members.

The bill requires clerks of the circuit courts and administrative clerks of the District Court to alter monthly reporting regarding individuals convicted of felonies sentenced to imprisonment with commitment papers. The fiscal note identifies a direct fiscal impact of $170,000 in FY 2025 general fund expenditures for the Judiciary to implement necessary software and reporting modifications.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits intentionally operating an unmanned aircraft over a correctional facility to record images without specified authorization. Authorizes image recording only with permission from the facility's managing official or the Secretary of Public Safety and Correctional Services. Prohibits delivering any contraband to an individual detained or confined in a place of confinement using an unmanned aircraft. Establishes misdemeanor penalties of up to three years of imprisonment, a maximum $1,000 fine, or both for violations. Requires correctional facilities to post exterior warning signage in areas visible to the general public.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
qa_results.stakeholders: operators of unmanned aircraft, individuals detained or confined in places of confinement, and correctional facility administrators and staff
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Potential minimal increase in State and local general fund revenues and expenditures due to the bill's incarceration and monetary penalty provisions; specific estimates are unavailable.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS requested this departmental legislation. The bill directly impacts the security of state correctional facilities under DPSCS oversight by prohibiting unauthorized drone imaging and the delivery of contraband via unmanned aircraft, requiring the posting of warning signage, and granting authorization authority to the Secretary of DPSCS.
The bill creates two new misdemeanor offenses punishable by up to three years of imprisonment and/or fines up to $1,000, which will be prosecuted and adjudicated in Maryland's court system.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates new criminal misdemeanor offenses carrying potential terms of incarceration of up to three years, requiring legal representation by OPD for eligible indigent defendants charged under these statutes.

As the primary statewide law enforcement agency, MSP is responsible for investigating criminal violations and enforcing laws concerning illegal drone operations and contraband delivery into secure facilities.
The prohibition on delivering contraband via unmanned aircraft applies broadly to any 'place of confinement,' which statutorily includes secure detention and commitment facilities operated by DJS.
The delivery of contraband using an unmanned aircraft applies to a 'place of confinement,' which statutorily includes certain inpatient psychiatric or forensic facilities operated by MDH.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals the requirement that a notary public sign and issue a protest only in the form prescribed by the Comptroller. Removes the statutory prohibition that made issuing a protest in any other format unlawful. Eliminates an obsolete requirement, as the Comptroller never created or used such a form. Takes effect July 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Secretary of State; Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland notaries public
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on State operations or finances, and no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Secretary of State oversees the appointment, commissioning, and regulation of notaries public in Maryland and requested this departmental bill to repeal an obsolete statutory requirement concerning notarial protest forms.

The bill repeals a statutory requirement under § 18-106 of the State Government Article that specifically prohibited notaries public from issuing protests except in the form prescribed by the Comptroller.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes applicants for the homeowners' property tax credit to attest to gross income under penalties of perjury. Permits this attestation in lieu of submitting an income tax return to substantiate an application. Applies only when an applicant was not required to and did not file an income tax return. Extends this attestation option to home purchasers and homeowners filing late applications. Takes effect June 1, 2024, for taxable years beginning after June 30, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation; Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland homeowners and home purchasers applying for the homeowners' property tax credit who were not required to and did not file an income tax return
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal effect. The State Department of Assessments and Taxation can implement the application changes with existing operational resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends provisions of the Homeowners' Property Tax Credit, which the Comptroller is statutory tasked with disbursing upon certification by the State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT). Additionally, the bill pertains to taxpayers who are not required to and do not file Maryland state income tax returns, which falls under the Comptroller's jurisdiction as the state's tax administration agency.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the termination date for the State Board of Individual Tax Preparers by one year to July 1, 2027. Continues the statutory and regulatory authority of the Board under the Maryland Program Evaluation Act. Requires the Maryland Department of Labor to submit a report to the Joint Audit and Evaluation Committee. Mandates submission of the report on or before July 1, 2025. Specifies that the report must include information about the Board as determined by the committee.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor; State Board of Individual Tax Preparers
qa_results.stakeholders: individual tax preparers and applicants in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues and expenditures for the State Board of Individual Tax Preparers are maintained through fiscal 2027. The Maryland Department of Labor can implement the reporting requirement with existing resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Individual Tax Preparers is housed within the Maryland Department of Labor. The bill extends the Board's termination date to July 1, 2027, continues its special fund operations, and requires the Department to submit a report to the Joint Audit and Evaluation Committee by July 1, 2025.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases the maximum share of administrative expenses for the Office of the Director payable from a designated special fund. Raises the allowable payment cap from 5% to 15% of the office's administrative expenses. Maintains the fund's use for reviewing documents and paying ground rent redemptions. Authorizes the State Department of Assessments and Taxation to reallocate existing special funds for administrative needs. Takes effect July 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation
qa_results.stakeholders: Office of the Director of the State Department of Assessments and Taxation
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No net effect on state or local finances. The bill authorizes the State Department of Assessments and Taxation to use additional monies from an existing special fund to cover up to 15% of administrative expenses for the Office of the Director without altering overall agency funding.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Under § 1-203.3 of the Corporations and Associations Article amended by the bill, the State Treasurer holds, invests, and reinvests the special fund utilized for the administrative expenses of the State Department of Assessments and Taxation.

Under § 1-203.3 of the Corporations and Associations Article amended by the bill, the State Comptroller is statutorily designated to account for the special fund used for the administrative expenses of the State Department of Assessments and Taxation.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters reporting deadlines for waivers requested and granted under the Certified Local Farm and Fish Program. Postpones the Office's annual waiver report deadline to the Board of Public Works from July 31 to October 31. Extends the Board of Public Works' reporting deadline to legislative committees from October 1 to December 31. Updates the statutory reference for the Senate Committee on Education, Energy, and the Environment.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office for the Certified Local Farm and Fish Program; Maryland Department of Agriculture; Board of Public Works
qa_results.stakeholders: State procurement units; certified local farms; certified Chesapeake invasive species providers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal effect; the bill is procedural in nature.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: SB 290 alters the annual reporting deadline for the Office for the Certified Local Farm and Fish Program, which is housed within the Maryland Department of Agriculture, shifting the submission deadline of its waiver report to the Board of Public Works from July 31 to October 31.

SB 290 alters the deadline by which the Board of Public Works must receive the annual waiver report from the Office for the Certified Local Farm and Fish Program and extends the deadline for the Board to submit this record to General Assembly committees from October 1 to December 31.

qa_results.bill_summary: Renames the statutory title of the Assistant Secretary of State to Deputy Secretary of State. Authorizes the Governor to appoint a Deputy Secretary of State. Permits the Deputy Secretary to carry out any statutory duty if the Secretary of State is absent or ill. Authorizes the Governor to delegate the power to suspend or terminate special police officer commissions to the Deputy Secretary. Allows the Governor to delegate authority to sanction notary public commissions to the Deputy Secretary. Takes effect June 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Secretary of State; Governor
qa_results.stakeholders: Deputy Secretary of State, notaries public, and special police officers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: None. The change is technical in nature and does not directly affect state or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This departmental bill was requested by the Secretary of State to conform statutory language to existing practice by officially changing the title of 'Assistant Secretary of State' to 'Deputy Secretary of State' and specifying duties and delegated authorities under this title.

The bill updates statutory provisions concerning the Governor's authority to appoint the Deputy Secretary of State and delegate specific executive powers, such as the suspension or termination of special police commissions and notary public sanctions.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals the requirement that the Maryland Department of Planning prepare and periodically revise specific inventory lists. Eliminates inventory lists of the natural resources of the State. Removes inventory lists of major public works and private facilities important to the development of the State as a whole. Repeals the requirement to provide copies of the lists to any State agency and the General Assembly upon request. Takes effect October 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Planning
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland Department of Planning, State agencies, and the General Assembly
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: SB 295 directly modifies the statutory responsibilities of the Maryland Department of Planning by repealing the requirement that it prepare and periodically revise inventory lists of the State's natural resources and major public works and private facilities.

The Department of Natural Resources served as an information source for the bill's fiscal note and is identified as the entity that maintains state natural resources data previously referenced in the repealed statute.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the statutory and regulatory termination date for the State Board for Professional Land Surveyors to July 1, 2027. Continues the board under the Maryland Program Evaluation Act. Requires the Maryland Department of Labor to submit a report by July 1, 2025. Directs the report to the Joint Audit and Evaluation Committee. Mandates that the report include board information determined by the committee.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board for Professional Land Surveyors; Maryland Department of Labor
qa_results.stakeholders: Licensed professional land surveyors, licensed property line surveyors, license applicants, and consumers of land surveying services in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues and expenditures for the board are maintained through fiscal 2027. The Maryland Department of Labor can likely complete the required report using existing resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board for Professional Land Surveyors is housed within the Maryland Department of Labor. This bill extends the board's termination date under the Maryland Program Evaluation Act to July 1, 2027, maintaining its licensing and regulatory operations, and mandates that the department submit an evaluation report to the Joint Audit and Evaluation Committee by July 1, 2025.

qa_results.bill_summary: Reduces the engineering practice requirement for engineer members of the State Board for Professional Engineers from 12 to 10 years. Maintains the requirement that engineer members must have held responsible charge of important engineering work for at least 5 years. Expands eligibility for earlier-career licensed professional engineers to serve on the regulatory board. Takes effect October 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board for Professional Engineers; Maryland Department of Labor
qa_results.stakeholders: licensed professional engineers seeking appointment to the State Board for Professional Engineers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board for Professional Engineers is housed within the Maryland Department of Labor's Division of Occupational and Professional Licensing. The bill was requested by the department and directly alters the statutory experience requirements for engineer members serving on this board.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting, recruiting, and processing appointments to state boards and commissions, including the State Board for Professional Engineers, and must apply the revised 10-year experience requirement when vetting candidates.
The Governor is responsible for appointing members to executive branch boards and commissions, and this legislation alters the statutory qualifications for prospective engineer appointees.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the State Board of Electricians to impose a civil penalty up to $5,000 for each violation. Permits the penalty instead of or in addition to reprimanding, suspending, or revoking a license. Requires the Board to consider violation seriousness, harm caused, licensee good faith, and previous violation history. Directs all civil penalties collected under the Act into the State General Fund. Requires the Board to report to designated legislative committees on complaint resolution practices by October 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Board of Electricians
qa_results.stakeholders: licensed electricians and electrical license applicants in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State General Fund revenues may increase minimally from civil penalties up to $5,000 per violation, though State finances are not materially affected. The State Board of Electricians can prepare the required report with existing resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Electricians is an occupational licensing board housed within the Maryland Department of Labor. This departmental legislation directly authorizes the Board to assess civil monetary penalties and requires the Board to prepare and submit a reporting requirement on complaint resolution and licensing backlogs.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands the duties of the Coast Smart Council regarding capital projects and coastal flood construction practices. Requires the Council to develop eligibility criteria, standards, and procedures for categorical exemptions. Applies these exemptions to proposed capital projects designed with adaptation and resiliency features to mitigate damage. Authorizes the Council to recommend regulations for adoption by the Secretary of Natural Resources. Takes effect October 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Coast Smart Council; Department of Natural Resources
qa_results.stakeholders: State and local government agencies managing or funding capital construction projects subject to Coast Smart requirements
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on State or local finances or operations. The codification of categorical exemptions provides a more streamlined and expedited review process for eligible capital projects.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Coast Smart Council is housed within DNR, and the bill expands the Council's statutory duties while authorizing it to recommend regulations for formal adoption by the Secretary of Natural Resources.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the statutory duties, authorities, and regulatory recommendation powers of the Coast Smart Council, an executive advisory and coordinating body.
MDOT constructs and maintains state highway facilities and capital transportation infrastructure that are subject to Coast Smart siting, design criteria, and categorical exemption processes.
DGS manages planning, design, and construction of state-owned facilities and capital projects that must comply with or seek categorical exemptions under the Coast Smart Program.
IAC oversees state-funded public school capital construction projects, some of which may be located in coastal flood hazard areas and potentially subject to Coast Smart criteria or exemptions.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Department of Natural Resources to permit specified archeological, salvage, excavation, stabilization, and restoration activities in Belt Woods Wildland. Requires prior approval from the Maryland Historical Trust and internal departmental review before authorizing these activities. Permits using mechanical or motorized equipment to stabilize or remove existing structures and debris. Restricts historic structure stabilization and restoration to structures existing as of December 1, 1985. Requires the Department to consult with the Maryland-National Capital Park and Planning Commission before working on the Seton Belt Barn.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources; Maryland Historical Trust; Maryland-National Capital Park and Planning Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: visitors to Belt Woods Wildland, historic preservationists, archeological researchers, and contractors bidding on restoration work
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State and local operations can implement the bill with existing budgeted resources. The Department of Natural Resources previously received a $1.2 million appropriation that remains available to fund the planned barn preservation project.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the Natural Resources Article to grant the Department of Natural Resources authority to conduct and authorize archeological research, salvage, excavation, and the stabilization and restoration of historic structures within the Belt Woods Wildland.

The bill mandates that any archeological research, excavation, stabilization, or restoration activities within Belt Woods Wildland receive prior approval from the Maryland Historical Trust, which is housed within and administered by the Department of Planning.

As the State's central procurement and facilities management authority, the Department of General Services will be involved in bidding out contracts for the restoration and stabilization work of the historic barns on eMaryland Marketplace.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends authorization for aquaculture leaseholders to place shellfish, bags, nets, and structures on submerged aquatic vegetation through June 30, 2027. Requires leaseholders to obtain prior written approval from the Department of Natural Resources before placement. Prohibits the Department from authorizing shellfish harvesting by dredge where submerged aquatic vegetation is present. Requires the Department to authorize harvest by diving on submerged land leases with submerged aquatic vegetation. Directs the Department to submit annual impact reports to the General Assembly and specified entities through June 2027.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
qa_results.stakeholders: aquaculture leaseholders in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly extends the Department of Natural Resources' statutory authority and process for reviewing and approving aquaculture leases on submerged aquatic vegetation (SAV), and requires DNR to submit annual reports on the impacts through 2027.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the definition of shellfish governing certain aquaculture provisions in Maryland. Defines shellfish to include live bivalves and bivalve shells. Repeals references to live oysters, seed oysters, oyster shells, live hard-shell clams, live soft-shell clams, and clam shells. Prohibits importing or possessing out-of-state shellfish for planting in State waters without approval. Requires approval from the Department of Natural Resources before planting in State waters.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
qa_results.stakeholders: aquaculture leaseholders and individuals importing or possessing out-of-state shellfish for planting in Maryland waters
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Natural Resources Article and was introduced as a departmental bill by the Department of Natural Resources (DNR). It expands DNR's regulatory authority over the importation and planting of shellfish by altering the definition to include live bivalves and bivalve shells, allowing the department to enforce health protocols on additional species such as scallops.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the termination date for the Board of Boiler Rules to July 1, 2029. Increases the Board's appointed membership from nine to 10 members. Adds a representative with at least 10 years of experience constructing, installing, and repairing boilers and pressure vessels. Requires the Maryland Department of Labor to submit a report to the Joint Audit and Evaluation Committee. Mandates submission of the report on or before July 1, 2025.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor; Board of Boiler Rules
qa_results.stakeholders: Owners and users of boilers and pressure vessels, manufacturers and repairers of boilers and pressure vessels, boiler inspectors, and engineering professionals
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues and expenditures for the Board of Boiler Rules are maintained through fiscal 2029. Adding a board member and completing the required report can be absorbed with existing budgeted resources. No local fiscal impact.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals the requirement that the Maryland Department of Planning serve as a repository and clearinghouse for financial and technical assistance. Eliminates the requirement for the Department to adopt regulations mandating State units to submit assistance information. Requires the Department to annually publish information concerning State financial and technical assistance on the Maryland InfoPortal. Takes effect October 1, 2024.

qa_results.stakeholders: units of State government and individuals or entities seeking State financial and technical assistance programs

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the statutory responsibilities of the Maryland Department of Planning by repealing the requirement that it serve as a repository and clearinghouse for federal and State assistance, removing related regulatory requirements, and modernizing the requirement to publish State assistance program information annually on the Maryland InfoPortal.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes Baltimore City, counties, and municipal corporations to grant property tax credits for qualifying hotel or residential development projects. Requires qualifying projects to be newly constructed or involve substantial rehabilitation or revitalization of existing structures. Requires qualifying hotel projects to substantially increase the assessed value of the property. Requires qualifying residential projects to include at least 20 units with 15% affordable at under 80% area median income. Authorizes local governing bodies to establish the amount, duration, eligibility criteria, and application procedures for the credit. Repeals separate Wicomico County credit provisions while preserving credits for projects initiated between July 2021 and June 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Mayor and City Council of Baltimore City; governing bodies of Maryland counties and municipal corporations
qa_results.stakeholders: Developers and owners of newly constructed or rehabilitated hotels and residential developments; households earning less than 80% of area median income; Maryland county and municipal governments
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state fiscal effect. County and municipal property tax revenues decrease beginning in fiscal 2025 to the extent jurisdictions enact the credit; specific amounts cannot be reliably estimated because revenue loss depends on local credit design, project values, and eligibility.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill authorizes local property tax credits for hotels and residential developments, subject to conditions including substantial increases in assessed property value. As the administrative review board for disputes concerning real property valuations and property tax credits, PTAAB may hear appeals arising from assessments or credit eligibility determinations.

The Maryland Tax Court hears appeals from final decisions of local taxing authorities and the Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board concerning real property assessments and tax credits, meaning contested decisions related to the valuation or application of this credit may ultimately be appealed to the court.

While the tax credit is authorized and administered at the county and municipal level, the bill directly intersects with DHCD's mission by establishing local tax incentives tied to affordable housing criteria (requiring at least 15% of units to be affordable to households earning less than 80% of area median income).

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands the duties of the Vision Zero coordinator within the Maryland Department of Transportation. Requires the coordinator to hold quarterly public meetings with designated state transportation officials on Vision Zero implementation. Directs meeting participants to address roadway safety issues, analyze infrastructure reviews, and vote on those reviews. Mandates live video streaming of quarterly meetings and website archiving of unedited recordings for at least five years. Requires the Department to submit an annual report detailing coordinator activities, recommendations, and quarterly meeting summaries.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Transportation
qa_results.stakeholders: motor vehicle drivers and passengers, bicyclists, and pedestrians; State and local transportation and law enforcement agencies
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State requirements can be handled using existing budgeted resources, with no effect on revenues. Local government finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDOT is the primary implementing department responsible for the Vision Zero program, housing the Vision Zero coordinator, holding quarterly public meetings, complying with enhanced Open Meetings Act requirements, and submitting annual progress reports.

The State Highway Administrator (or designee) is statutorily required to participate in quarterly public meetings to address Vision Zero implementation, make recommendations, and review and vote on SHA-completed fatal crash infrastructure reviews.

The Motor Vehicle Administrator (or designee) is statutorily required to attend and participate in the quarterly public meetings regarding Vision Zero, which aligns directly with MVA's oversight of the Maryland Highway Safety Office and driver safety initiatives.
The Executive Director of the MDTA (or designee) is required by the bill to attend and actively participate in the quarterly public meetings on Vision Zero implementation and infrastructure reviews.

The Vision Zero coordinator is tasked with advising the Governor on roadway safety policies and priorities, and MDOT is required to submit an annual report on the status of Vision Zero to the Governor.

qa_results.responsible_party: State Retirement Agency; State Retirement and Pension System
qa_results.stakeholders: Active and vested former members of the State Retirement and Pension System who served on active duty with the commissioned corps of the Public Health Service, the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, or the Coast and Geodetic Survey
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact until FY 2027; total costs cannot be reliably estimated but are likely minimal. In FY 2027, average state employer costs to provide five years of credit range from $5,100 to $11,400 per member, funded 60% general funds, 20% special funds, and 20% federal and other funds. Local pension systems experience similar per-member expenditure increases with no effect on revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Retirement Agency directly administers the State Retirement and Pension System (SRPS). The bill directly amends the definition of military service to expand eligibility for service credit to members who served in the commissioned corps of the Public Health Service, NOAA, or Coast and Geodetic Survey, requiring the agency to process and award these credits.

The Department of Budget and Management serves as the state's central personnel agency and oversees state employee benefit policies, state budget planning, and employer pension contributions, which may experience minor fiscal adjustments as members claim additional service credits.

The Department of Veterans and Military Families advocates for and assists service members, veterans, and their families in securing state and federal benefits, including state-level recognition and credits related to uniformed and military service.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires residential service agencies to submit annual wage reports for personal care aides to the Maryland Department of Labor. Mandates reporting by September 1 each year, beginning in 2025, detailing average, highest, and lowest aide wage rates. Excludes personal care services provided through the Developmental Disabilities Administration from these reporting requirements. Requires the Maryland Department of Health to report on the final federal Ensuring Access to Medicaid Services rule. Directs the Department to submit this report within 180 days after the federal rule's release.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor; Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Residential service agencies, personal care aides, and Medicaid home- and community-based services participants
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The Maryland Department of Labor and the Maryland Department of Health can implement the reporting requirements using existing budgeted resources. State revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: SB 371 relates directly to the Maryland Medical Assistance Program administered by MDH. The bill requires MDH to submit a report to the General Assembly regarding the federal Ensuring Access to Medicaid Services rule, including the process the department will use to review wage reports of personal care aides and how data will be used to review Medicaid reimbursement rates.
The bill mandates that residential service agencies submit annual wage reports for personal care aides directly to the Maryland Department of Labor in a form and manner determined by the department.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits State contracts from containing specified provisions, including unappropriated indemnification, binding arbitration, out-of-state venues, and automatic renewals. Voids any prohibited provision in a State contract while keeping the remaining contract terms enforceable. Requires contracts containing prohibited provisions to be governed by and construed under Maryland law. Exempts, contingent on separate legislation, contracts regarding the purchase, redevelopment, or operation of a racing facility or training facility site. Applies prospectively to State contracts executed on or after October 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General; Board of Public Works; Department of General Services
qa_results.stakeholders: vendors and contractors doing business with the State; State procurement officers and agencies
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal effect. The bill is procedural in nature and generally conforms statutory law to current procurement practice.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly prohibits State contracts from appointing legal counsel other than the Maryland Attorney General (unless otherwise authorized by law) and impacts the enforcement, defense, and interpretation of State contracts.

As the State's central procurement agency responsible for awarding and administering contracts across state government, DGS must ensure all standard terms, conditions, and contract agreements comply with these statutory prohibitions.

The Board of Public Works oversees and approves significant State procurement contracts and expenditures, making its contract review processes directly subject to these restrictions on prohibited provisions.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Board of Contract Appeals
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MSBCA adjudicates disputes and claims arising from State contracts, including matters where contract clauses may be deemed void ab initio under this law.

MDOT enters into extensive multi-million dollar procurement and construction contracts and must conform all agreements to the bill's restrictions regarding indemnification, arbitration, liability, and renewals.

The State Treasurer manages the State Insurance Trust Fund and protects state funds; the bill's provisions directly touch upon State indemnification, unfunded liabilities, and liability for property damage or bodily injury.
The bill contains an explicit carve-out under § 10-601 of the Economic Development Article (governing the Maryland Stadium Authority) regarding racing facility and training facility contracts.
The bill mandates that State contracts cannot require binding arbitration or designate dispute venues other than courts of proper jurisdiction within Maryland.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends indefinitely the required annual state budget appropriation of at least $5,000,000 for the University of Maryland School of Medicine. Requires these funds to support clinical care at the University of Maryland Capital Region Medical Center by specialized faculty. Mandates annual General Fund appropriations for the MPowering Joint Steering Council for the University of Maryland Institute for Health Computing. Phases in Council funding at $1,500,000 in fiscal 2026, increasing to $6,000,000 in fiscal 2029 and thereafter. Specifies that appropriated funds must supplement and not supplant other university funding.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Governor; University of Maryland School of Medicine; MPowering Joint Steering Council
qa_results.stakeholders: University of Maryland School of Medicine; University of Maryland Capital Region Medical Center; MPowering Joint Steering Council; University of Maryland Institute for Health Computing; patients receiving care at the Capital Region Medical Center
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $1.5 million in FY 2026, growing by $1.5 million annually to $6.0 million in FY 2029 and each subsequent year for the University of Maryland Institute for Health Computing. The bill also permanently extends an existing $5.0 million annual funding mandate for clinical care at the University of Maryland Capital Region Medical Center, which carries no additional net expenditure impact relative to baseline budget assumptions.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the University System of Maryland (USM) by establishing and extending mandated funding for USM entities, including the University of Maryland School of Medicine, the MPowering Joint Steering Council, and the University of Maryland Institute for Health Computing.
DBM is the principal agency responsible for preparing the state budget and must incorporate the bill's mandated general fund appropriations into the annual budget starting in FY 2026.

The bill statutorily requires the Governor to include specific annual General Fund appropriations in the state budget for the University of Maryland School of Medicine and the MPowering Joint Steering Council.

qa_results.bill_summary: Renames the Task Force to Study Crime Classification to be the Task Force to Study Crime Reclassification and Penalties. Expands the membership of the task force to include additional state agency heads and advocacy representatives. Requires the task force to review penalties in the Criminal Law, Criminal Procedure, and Public Safety articles. Requires recommendations on reclassifying offenses, altering disproportionate penalties, codifying common law offenses, and addressing missing mens rea provisions. Extends the task force reporting deadline to December 31, 2025, and terminates the act on June 30, 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Task Force to Study Crime Reclassification and Penalties; Office of the Attorney General
qa_results.stakeholders: individuals accused or convicted of criminal and civil violations, crime victims, criminal defense attorneys, prosecutors, and victims' rights advocates
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $177,300 in FY 2025 and $155,900 in FY 2026 for the Office of the Attorney General to hire 1.5 contractual staff to support the task force. Task force member expense reimbursements are minimal and absorbable within existing resources. No effect on local finances or state revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Attorney General (or designee) serves as a member of the task force, and the Office of the Attorney General is statutorily designated to staff the task force, incurring direct fiscal impacts to hire contractual legal personnel.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly renames, expands the membership of, modifies the responsibilities of, and extends the termination date for the Task Force to Study Crime Reclassification and Penalties.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Executive Director of the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy (formerly the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention, Youth, and Victim Services), or their designee, is added as a statutory member of the task force.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Public Defender, or the Public Defender's designee, is designated by statute as a member of the task force reviewing state criminal penalties and classifications.
The task force is required to submit its final report of findings and recommendations regarding crime reclassification and statutory penalties to the Governor by December 31, 2025.

qa_results.bill_summary: Allows recipients of catalytic revitalization project tax credits for phased projects to claim 100% of the credit in one year. Repeals the restriction limiting initial tax credit certificates to one project within a two-year period. Prohibits issuing tax credit certificates exceeding $15,000,000 in the aggregate within a two-year period. Authorizes the Secretary of Housing and Community Development to revoke noncompliant initial certificates and re-award them to other applicants. Prohibits revoking certificates awarded on or before July 1, 2024, unless the recipient ceases project rehabilitation. Requires regulations establishing procedures for approving project phases.
qa_results.responsible_party: Secretary of Housing and Community Development; Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development; Maryland Department of Commerce
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals, nonprofit organizations, and business entities undertaking catalytic revitalization projects
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues decrease by at least $2.7 million in FY 2025, $2.6 million in FY 2026, $1.1 million in FY 2027, and $100,000 in FY 2028 due to the accelerated claiming of phased project tax credits. To the extent credits are claimed against the corporate income tax, Higher Education Investment Fund and Transportation Trust Fund revenues and expenditures, as well as local highway user revenues, may also decrease.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DHCD is the primary administering agency of the Catalytic Revitalization Project Tax Credit, responsible for accepting applications, issuing initial and final credit certificates, revoking certificates, and adopting implementing regulations.
The Comptroller administers the State income tax against which this tax credit is claimed and oversees the collection of State revenues impacted by the acceleration of credit claims.

The bill explicitly requires the Secretary of Housing and Community Development to consult with the Department of Commerce when adopting regulations to carry out the provisions of the tax credit program.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the membership of the Correctional Training Commission by removing the representative of the Federal Bureau of Prisons. Increases the number of correctional officers or officials appointed by the Governor from four to five. Requires these five appointed members to be from local correctional facilities. Mandates that each appointee represent one of five defined geographic regions across the State. Repeals the requirement that one appointed member be an employee or official of the Department of Juvenile Services. Prohibits these five members from designating substitute representatives to act at Commission meetings.
qa_results.responsible_party: Correctional Training Commission; Governor
qa_results.stakeholders: local correctional facility officers and officials, the Correctional Training Commission, the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services, and the Department of Juvenile Services
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not materially affected. Any local expense reimbursements for additional members can be handled with existing resources, with no other local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Correctional Training Commission is established within the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services (DPSCS), and key department leadership—including the Secretary, a Deputy Secretary, and a designated department representative—serve as statutory members.
