The bill directly alters membership criteria concerning DJS by repealing the requirement that at least one of the Governor-appointed correctional officers or officials on the Commission be a DJS employee or official. The Secretary and an agency representative also serve as members of the Commission.

The bill expands and alters the Governor's appointment authority by requiring the Governor to appoint five correctional officers or officials from local facilities representing five newly defined geographic regions of the State.

The Office of Appointments is responsible for recruiting, vetting, and managing appointments to State commissions on behalf of the Governor, and it must implement the bill's new regional representation and facility requirements for the five appointed members.
The Attorney General is designated by statute as an ex officio member of the Correctional Training Commission.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the State Board of Elections to evaluate the performance of the State Administrator of Elections at least annually. Requires the State Administrator to evaluate local election directors annually and recommend any disciplinary actions to local boards. Requires each local board of elections to confer with the State Administrator when appointing an election director. Mandates that local boards maintain a warehouse and provide for early voting center equipment expenses. Converts specified discretionary powers of local election directors into mandatory statutory duties under State Board regulations. Requires election directors to report cybersecurity violations or facility damage to state and local officials within 24 hours.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Elections; State Administrator of Elections; local boards of elections
qa_results.stakeholders: Local election directors, local election boards, county governments, and Maryland voters
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly governs the administration, oversight duties, and personnel evaluations of the Maryland State Board of Elections (SBE) and the State Administrator of Elections, as well as establishing requirements for local boards of elections and local election directors under SBE's supervision.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands the purpose and eligible use of the Seed Community Development Anchor Institution Fund. Authorizes grants and loans to anchor institutions for community development projects in designated sustainable communities. Broadens the definition of anchor institutions to include their departments, foundations, and other entities. Repeals the requirement that matching funds provided by anchor institutions come from a private source.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland institutions of higher education, qualifying hospital institutions, their departments and foundations, and communities designated as sustainable communities or blighted areas
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Overall State finances for the fund are not affected. Shifting eligibility may alter funding distribution among State entities, but the Department of Housing and Community Development can administer changes with existing budgeted resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DHCD is the primary implementing agency responsible for administering the Seed Community Development Anchor Institution Fund and awarding grants and loans to eligible anchor institutions under the expanded criteria.

USM institutions and their foundations/departments qualify as anchor institutions eligible to receive grants and loans from the fund, and the bill broadens allowable locations and removes the private matching fund restriction.

Morgan State University qualifies as an anchor institution eligible for grants and loans from the fund and will benefit from the broadened project locations and the removal of the private match requirement.
MDH oversees and regulates hospital institutions that qualify as anchor institutions under the fund and served as an informational agency for the legislation.
As an institution of higher education in the State, Saint Mary's College of Maryland meets the statutory definition of an anchor institution eligible to apply for funding under the program.
The State Treasurer's Office is statutorily designated to hold and invest the monies of the Seed Community Development Anchor Institution Fund.
The Comptroller is statutorily designated to account for the Seed Community Development Anchor Institution Fund.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires county treasurers, tax collectors, or directors of finance to issue certificates enumerating property taxes, assessments, and charges. Bars unlisted charges or assessments against bona fide purchasers for value who lack prior notice. Mandates collecting agents endorse deeds presented within 45 days upon payment of stated charges and applicable taxes. Authorizes counties and municipalities to collect a fee of up to $55 for issuing a certificate. Requires circuit court clerks and the State Department of Assessments and Taxation to coordinate electronic recording procedures.
qa_results.responsible_party: County Treasurers, Tax Collectors, and Directors of Finance; Clerks of the Circuit Courts; State Department of Assessments and Taxation
qa_results.stakeholders: Real property buyers and sellers, bona fide purchasers, title companies, county and municipal tax authorities, and circuit court land records divisions
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State operations and finances are not materially affected. Local government revenues may increase from authorized certificate fees of up to $55, which are anticipated to cover any minimal administrative costs.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends procedures for the clerks of the circuit courts regarding the recording of deeds and requires them to coordinate on electronic satisfaction of recording prerequisites in compliance with standards established by the Administrative Office of the Courts (AOC), which provides technological and operational support to the courts.

The bill amends Section 3-703 of the Real Property Article, which governs electronic recording of land documents and references the transmission of recorded documents to the Maryland State Archives for archival preservation and online publication.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes Class B-resort beer, Class B-resort beer and wine, and beer, wine, and liquor festival licenses in Garrett County. Expands permitted Sunday sales hours to begin at 6 a.m. instead of 10 a.m. in specified election districts. Requires at least one applicant for an alcoholic beverages license to reside in Maryland for license validity. Prohibits bringing, consuming, or transferring alcoholic beverages in specified adult entertainment establishments under criminal penalty. Increases the maximum administrative fine for alcoholic beverages violations in Garrett County from $3,000 to $5,000.
qa_results.responsible_party: Garrett County Board of License Commissioners; Garrett County
qa_results.stakeholders: alcoholic beverages license holders and applicants, adult entertainment venue operators, event organizers, and consumers in Garrett County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Garrett County revenues may increase minimally from new festival license fees, resort license issuing fees, and higher fine collections. Local administrative expenditures can be absorbed with existing resources, and there is no state fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes new alcoholic beverages licenses, adjusts operational hours, and sets requirements for alcoholic beverages in Garrett County. The Comptroller of Maryland regulates the state's alcohol industry and oversees statutory application form requirements referenced in the law.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals uncodified statutory provisions governing the Protestant Episcopal Church, Diocese of Washington, commonly known as the Vestry Act. Codifies general corporate governance laws for parishes and separate congregations in union with the diocese. Requires each subject religious corporation to adopt bylaws approved by a majority of qualified voting members. Subjects these religious corporations to the constitution and canons of the diocese and the national church. Authorizes the State Department of Assessments and Taxation to record certificates of incorporation upon request. Recognizes the corporate legal existence of specified parishes across Montgomery, Prince George's, Charles, and St. Mary's counties.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation
qa_results.stakeholders: Parishes, separate congregations, and vestries in union with the Protestant Episcopal Church in the Diocese of Washington located in Charles, Montgomery, Prince George's, and St. Mary's counties
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues increase minimally to the extent parishes file certificates or articles of incorporation. The State Department of Assessments and Taxation can implement the bill with existing resources, and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly establishes that the courts of the State are estopped from denying the legal existence of specified parishes and congregations recognized as bodies corporate under the Act.

The Office of the Attorney General acts as legal counsel to the State and was consulted regarding legal, constitutional, and corporate governance matters related to religious corporations and historic church charters.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Community Health and Safety Works Grant Program and related special fund in the Department of Housing and Community Development. Requires the Governor to include a $10,000,000 annual budget appropriation to the fund for fiscal years 2025 through 2028. Authorizes grants to eligible nonprofit organizations, local governments, and higher education institutions for targeted crime prevention and safety projects. Sets grant amounts between $25,000 and $50,000 for facility improvements and between $75,000 and $150,000 for business district projects. Caps grants for community-centered crime and violence intervention and prevention projects at $250,000. Requires camera or license reader applicants to submit monitoring plans and evidence of law enforcement partnerships.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development
qa_results.stakeholders: tax-exempt nonprofit organizations, local governments, and institutions of higher education collaborating with local neighborhood associations
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $10.0 million annually beginning in fiscal 2025 to capitalize the special fund, with matching special fund revenues and expenditures for grant awards. Local government and higher education revenues and expenditures increase to the extent they apply for and receive grants.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DHCD is the primary administering agency responsible for establishing, implementing, and adopting regulations for the Community Health and Safety Works Grant Program and managing the associated Fund.

The bill statutorily requires the State Treasurer to hold and invest the moneys of the newly established Community Health and Safety Works Grant Program Fund separately and credit interest earnings directly to the Fund.
The bill mandates that the Comptroller account for the new special, nonlapsing Community Health and Safety Works Grant Program Fund.
The bill requires the Governor to include a mandated appropriation of $10,000,000 to the Fund in the annual budget bill for fiscal years 2025 through 2028.
DBM oversees executive budget development and execution, including implementing the required $10,000,000 annual budget mandate for the Fund from FY 2025 through FY 2028.
State institutions of higher education are explicitly eligible applicants for Business District and Neighborhood Security Project grants when collaborating with local neighborhood associations.

As an independent public institution of higher education, Morgan State University is an eligible applicant for grants under the Business District and Neighborhood Security Project category in partnership with local neighborhood associations.

As an independent public higher education institution, St. Mary's College of Maryland is eligible to apply for grant funding for Business District and Neighborhood Security Projects in collaboration with a local neighborhood association.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases the minimum per capita State aid provided to the State Library Resource Center. Sets the funding allocation at $2.07 per State resident beginning in fiscal year 2025. Requires the Center to use the allocations for operating and capital expenses. Continues the designation of the Enoch Pratt Free Library Central Library as the Center. Takes effect July 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Library Agency
qa_results.stakeholders: State Library Resource Center (Central Library of the Enoch Pratt Free Library System), Maryland public library systems, and Maryland library patrons
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $616,500 in fiscal 2025, rising to $632,837 by fiscal 2029 due to projected population growth. The fiscal 2025 State budget includes funding for the enhancement. State revenues and local finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Library Agency coordinates the State Library Network, which includes the State Library Resource Center (SLRC) and the Maryland State Library for the Blind and Print Disabled (LBPD). The bill directly alters the statutory per capita funding formula for SLRC.
The bill increases a statutory mandated appropriation of General Funds starting in fiscal year 2026, impacting state budget development and long-term fiscal planning overseen by DBM.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires victims of domestic violence programs to be certified by the federally recognized State domestic violence coalition. Establishes the Victims of Domestic Violence Program Grant Fund as a special, nonlapsing fund. Requires the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention, Youth, and Victim Services to administer the fund. Authorizes the Governor to include an annual appropriation of $5,000,000 in the State budget bill. Limits fund expenditures to grants for certified public or private nonprofit comprehensive domestic violence programs.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention, Youth, and Victim Services; State Treasurer; Comptroller
qa_results.stakeholders: victims of domestic violence and their children; certified public and private nonprofit comprehensive domestic violence programs
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: General fund expenditures increase by $2.9 million annually beginning in fiscal 2025, assuming the full authorized $5.0 million discretionary appropriation is provided and incorporates $2.1 million in existing program funding. Special fund revenues and expenditures both increase by $5.0 million annually to provide grants.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP is the primary administering agency responsible for supervising the domestic violence program, establishing procedures to award grants, adopting regulations, and administering the newly established Victims of Domestic Violence Program Grant Fund.
The State Treasurer is statutorily directed to hold and invest the money of the newly created Victims of Domestic Violence Program Grant Fund and credit interest earnings directly to the Fund.
The Comptroller is statutorily required to account for the Victims of Domestic Violence Program Grant Fund under the State Finance and Procurement Article and the Family Law Article.
The bill explicitly authorizes the Governor to include an annual discretionary appropriation of up to $5,000,000 in the State budget for the grant fund.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Commission to Study African American Civil War Soldiers in Maryland. Requires the Commission to study the history of African American Civil War soldiers who fought for the Union Army. Requires the Commission to recommend the funding, design, construction, and location of an appropriate memorial. Requires the State Archives to provide staff for the Commission. Requires the Commission to report its findings to the Governor and the General Assembly by December 1, 2024. Terminates all provisions of the Act on June 30, 2025.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Archives; Commission to Study African American Civil War Soldiers in Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Historians, preservation organizations, descendants of Union soldiers, and the Maryland public
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $63,800 in FY 2025 for contractual staffing support and operating expenses. Expense reimbursements for Commission members are minimal and absorbable within existing resources. The bill has no effect on revenues or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Maryland State Archives is the primary operational agency designated to staff the Commission to Study African American Civil War Soldiers in Maryland, conduct historical research, and prepare the required report, with an estimated fiscal impact of $63,813 in FY 2025 for a contractual archivist position.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a new temporary study commission and incorporates representatives from existing bodies, including the Governor's Commission on Maryland Military Monuments and the Commission on African American History and Culture.

The bill requires a representative from the Department of Planning to serve on the commission; additionally, the department oversees state historical and cultural preservation programs and administers the Governor's Commission on Maryland Military Monuments.
The Governor is responsible for appointing six members to the commission, designating the commission chair, and receiving the commission's final report on findings and recommendations.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and processing gubernatorial appointments to the newly formed commission.

qa_results.bill_summary: Declares void and unenforceable liability waivers and indemnification provisions in contracts for using recreational facilities. Applies to commercial recreational facilities, commercial athletic facilities, and amusement attractions, including gymnasiums and swimming pools. Covers liability for injury resulting from the negligence or wrongful act of the facility, agents, or on-duty employees. Excludes health club services agreements for services rendered to an adult. Excludes lodging establishments unless their recreational facilities are open to the general public. Excludes units of state or local government that lease land or facilities to a recreational facility.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary
qa_results.stakeholders: commercial recreational facilities, athletic facilities, amusement attractions, gymnasiums, swimming pools, and facility patrons
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Indeterminate potential increase in State and local expenditures from increased liability exposure and litigation costs, depending on judicial interpretation; revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Treasurer's Office administers the State Insurance Trust Fund (SITF), which handles tort claims and liability coverage for state agencies. The bill could increase SITF expenditures if state-owned facilities face increased tort liability.

DNR manages extensive state park, land, and water recreational facilities and enters into agreements and leases for recreational use, making its liability exposure and contract waiver provisions a point of specific analysis in the fiscal note.

AOC supports the state court system, which will be tasked with interpreting the statute and adjudicating tort claims and contract disputes regarding void liability waivers in recreational facility contracts.
The OAG represents the state in tort litigation and contract enforcement and houses the Consumer Protection Division, which monitors consumer contract terms and was consulted on the legislation.

MDA oversees entities like the Maryland Horse Industry Board and the Agricultural Fair Board, which involve recreational and athletic activities, though the fiscal impact on them was determined to be minimal.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires private home detention monitoring agencies to notify designated entities when monitored individuals violate release or probation conditions. Mandates notice within 24 hours for general violations and within one hour for equipment tampering or maintenance failures. Demands immediate notice when an individual enters an expressly prohibited area. Authorizes the Secretary of Public Safety and Correctional Services to impose civil penalties on noncompliant monitoring agencies. Clarifies that individuals are released rather than committed to private home detention monitoring under second-degree escape provisions.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services; Secretary of Public Safety and Correctional Services; Division of Parole and Probation
qa_results.stakeholders: private home detention monitoring agencies, criminal defendants on pretrial release, individuals subject to home detention monitoring as a condition of probation, and local law enforcement agencies
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures and local operations are not materially affected, as the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services and the Judiciary can implement the bill with existing budgeted resources. Potential civil penalty revenues are not expected to materially affect State revenues.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS is the primary implementing agency for this legislation. The Secretary of Public Safety and Correctional Services licenses private home detention monitoring agencies (PHDMAs) and is specifically authorized to impose civil penalties on agencies that fail to provide required notifications. Additionally, the Division of Parole and Probation (DPP), a division within DPSCS, is the designated recipient of mandatory violation notifications concerning probationers.

The bill directly impacts the Maryland court system by altering notification requirements and imposing expedited deadlines (immediate, 1 hour, or 24 hours) for PHDMAs to notify the court when a defendant violates conditions of pretrial home detention monitoring.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: OPD represents indigent clients who are subject to pretrial release, probation conditions, and monitoring by private home detention agencies, as well as individuals facing criminal penalties for violation of movement restrictions or escape in the second degree under § 9-405.

qa_results.bill_summary: Exempts certain emergency backup generating facilities at critical infrastructure sites from Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity requirements. Defines critical infrastructure to include hospitals, health care facilities, and qualified data centers. Requires owners or operators of exempted facilities to submit annual operational reports to the Department of the Environment. Directs the Maryland Energy Administration to report biennially to the General Assembly on backup generation technologies. Requires the Comptroller to distribute 15% of specified corporate income tax revenues from qualified data centers to the Strategic Energy Investment Fund.
qa_results.responsible_party: Public Service Commission; Maryland Department of the Environment; Maryland Energy Administration; Comptroller of Maryland; Maryland Department of Commerce
qa_results.stakeholders: Owners and operators of critical infrastructure facilities, including hospitals, health care facilities, and qualified data centers; electric companies; construction and maintenance contractors; local governments
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: General Fund revenues decrease and Strategic Energy Investment Fund revenues increase by an estimated $2.3 million in FY 2026, rising to $9.9 million by FY 2029 due to reallocated corporate income tax receipts. Maryland Department of the Environment special fund revenues may increase from air quality permit application fees. Local government expenditures may increase significantly if jurisdictions choose to study, regulate, or review unpermitted backup generation projects.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the jurisdiction of the Public Service Commission by exempting certain backup generating facilities for critical infrastructure from obtaining a Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity (CPCN) or related PSC construction approvals.

Generating units seeking the CPCN exemption must be subject to an air quality permit to construct issued by MDE, and MDE receives and evaluates annual operating reports from these facilities to determine whether public disclosure poses security risks.

The bill directs dedicated corporate income tax revenues into the Strategic Energy Investment Fund (SEIF) administered by MEA and requires MEA to submit biennial reports to the General Assembly regarding backup generation technologies.
The Comptroller is tasked with calculating and distributing 15% of remaining corporate income tax revenues attributable to qualified data centers to the Strategic Energy Investment Fund.

Commerce must consult with MEA and select industry representatives for the backup generation technology studies, and oversees the data center eligibility certifications linked to the corporate tax distributions.

DNR evaluates power generation projects through its Power Plant Research Program as part of the CPCN review process; exempting these backup generators reduces the number of CPCN applications DNR reviews.

OPC advocates for residential utility consumers in proceedings before the Public Service Commission and monitors regulatory policies and utility generation exemptions affecting electric system reliability and costs.
The bill was introduced as an Administration priority to streamline critical infrastructure and data center development in Maryland.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes employers to grant a preference in hiring and promotion to spouses of eligible service members. Specifies that granting this employment preference does not violate State or local equal employment opportunity law. Expands preference definitions for eligible veterans to include all branches of the U.S. uniformed services. Requires Executive Branch appointing authorities to apply a 10-point credit on selection tests for eligible military spouses. Excludes current State employees and eligible veterans convicted of certain post-discharge crimes from receiving the test credit.
qa_results.responsible_party: Appointing authorities in the State Personnel Management System
qa_results.stakeholders: Spouses of active duty service members, veterans of the U.S. uniformed services, private employers, and applicants for State employment
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State operational requirements can be handled with existing budgeted resources. The bill has no effect on State revenues and no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the State's central personnel agency overseeing the State Personnel Management System (SPMS), DBM is responsible for implementing the requirement that appointing authorities grant a 10-point credit on selection tests for eligible military spouses and veterans of all uniformed services.

The bill directly impacts the constituency served by the department by supporting active-duty military spouses and veterans through employment preferences, and the agency directly contributed to the analysis of the legislation.

The bill amends the Labor and Employment Article regarding employer hiring and promotion preferences for military spouses, which falls within the regulatory and informational scope of the Department of Labor.

The Commission enforces Maryland's equal employment opportunity and anti-discrimination laws in employment; the bill explicitly provides that granting hiring and promotion preferences to military spouses does not violate State or local equal employment opportunity law.
This was introduced as a priority Administration bill ('Families Serve Act of 2024') by request of the Governor to expand employment opportunities for military families across Maryland.

qa_results.bill_summary: Codifies the Governor’s Office for Children as an independent agency headed by a Special Secretary. Establishes the ENOUGH Grant Program and Fund to implement place-based strategies addressing concentrated child poverty. Requires the Governor to include a general fund appropriation of at least $15,000,000 in fiscal year 2026. Directs the Children’s Cabinet to meet at least four times annually and submit a three-year plan. Mandates that the Office develop a public centralized database of available youth and family resources by July 2025.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governor's Office for Children; Children's Cabinet; Accountability and Implementation Board
qa_results.stakeholders: Children and families in high-poverty neighborhoods, community schools, local management boards, local governments, and participating community-based partner organizations
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $20.3 million in FY 2025 (reflecting $20.2 million in contingent budget appropriations and $75,000 in contractual costs) and by at least $15.6 million in FY 2026 due to a $15.0 million mandated appropriation to the ENOUGH Grant Fund and ongoing personnel costs. Special fund revenues and expenditures increase accordingly. Local revenues and expenditures increase by $5.0 million in FY 2025 through formula allocations to local management boards, with additional indeterminate gains for local entities serving as lead partners.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill codifies the Governor's Office for Children (GOC) and the Special Secretary as its head, and establishes the ENOUGH Grant Program, the ENOUGH Grant Fund, a public centralized resource database, and reporting requirements administered directly by the GOC.

The bill requires MSDE to share data with GOC for the neighborhood indicators of poverty report, receives the resulting report, and directly impacts education statutory provisions related to the Compensatory Education Program and the Concentration of Poverty School Grant Program.
The bill explicitly mandates the Maryland Longitudinal Data System Center to share required data with GOC to support the completion of the report on neighborhood indicators of poverty.

DBM is statutorily required to be consulted by the Accountability and Implementation Board when developing the methodological recommendations on poverty indicators, and oversees the state budget execution and mandated FY 2026 appropriation of $15 million.
The bill establishes the ENOUGH Grant Fund as a special, nonlapsing fund and requires the State Treasurer to hold the fund separately and invest its moneys.
The bill requires the Comptroller of Maryland to account for the newly created ENOUGH Grant Fund.

This Administration initiative formally codifies GOC within the Executive Department, mandates an appropriation in the Governor's FY 2026 budget bill, and requires program evaluation reporting to the Governor.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters qualifications for awards from the Child Care Career and Professional Development Fund. Requires applicants to commit to working at least 20 hours per week in an approved child care setting. Prioritizes awards for applicants without college credits and applicants enrolled in native language or bilingual coursework programs. Requires recipients to repay award funds if they fail to complete the service obligation. Authorizes the Office of Child Care to waive or defer repayment for extenuating circumstances.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of Child Care; Maryland State Department of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: child care workers seeking college degrees or credentials; approved child care settings; accredited colleges and universities offering early childhood education coursework
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland State Department of Education can implement the changes using existing budgeted resources. State revenues are not materially affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) houses the Office of Child Care, which directly administers the Child Care Career and Professional Development Fund and is responsible for establishing the service obligation duration, prioritizing awards, and managing repayments or waivers.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters statutory terminology across Title 2 of the State Government Article to use gender-neutral language. Replaces references to chairman, cochairman, chairmen, cochairmen, and vice chairman with gender-neutral terms. Applies these changes to committee leadership positions throughout the Maryland General Assembly. Updates statutory references to specific committees, including the Senate Committee on Education, Energy, and the Environment. Takes effect June 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland General Assembly
qa_results.stakeholders: Members and committee leadership of the Maryland General Assembly
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. Requirements can be absorbed within existing budgeted resources, with no effect on revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill makes technical, gender-neutral terminology updates to Section 2-1224 of the State Government Article, which governs the duties of the Legislative Auditor regarding the transmittal of audit reports to legislative committee chairs.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the deadline for Cecil County to submit its annual financial report to the Department of Legislative Services. Authorizes the county to file the report on or before December 31 rather than October 31. Extends the county's deadline to submit its annual audit to the State Legislative Auditor to December 31. Requires the financial report to use the form established by the Department of Legislative Services. Requires the county chief executive officer to verify the report. Takes effect October 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Cecil County; Department of Legislative Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Cecil County government and finance officials
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. Altering the filing deadline for the county's annual financial report and audit report does not affect county finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: By statute, the deadline for a county to submit its annual audit report to the State Legislative Auditor (Office of Legislative Audits) is tied to the due date of its annual financial report, thereby shifting Cecil County's audit filing deadline to OLA from October 31 to December 31.

Under Section 16-304 of the Local Government Article, the Comptroller holds statutory enforcement authority to discontinue state aid, grants, and tax distributions to a county that fails to file its required annual financial report.

qa_results.bill_summary: Regulates ticket sales and resales by imposing disclosure, prohibition, and refund requirements on ticket issuers, resellers, and secondary ticket exchanges. Requires ticket listings and purchasing steps to itemize all charges and disclose the total price, seat number, and section. Prohibits resellers from selling or offering to sell speculative tickets. Prohibits secondary ticket exchanges from providing a marketplace for noncompliant ticket sales. Mandates full refunds when an event is canceled, tickets are counterfeit, or tickets fail to match their descriptions. Directs the Consumer Protection Division to study the event ticket market and report by December 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General
qa_results.stakeholders: Ticket purchasers, ticket issuers, ticket resellers, and secondary ticket exchanges
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by approximately $200,000 in FY 2025 for the Consumer Protection Division of the Office of the Attorney General to hire a study consultant, with potential additional minimal increases for ongoing enforcement. No material impact on State revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates that the Consumer Protection Division of the Office of the Attorney General conduct a comprehensive review of the event ticket market in the State, hire a consultant to assist with the study, and report its findings and recommendations by December 1, 2024. Additionally, violations of the bill are classified as unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act, which the Consumer Protection Division enforces.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes distinct statutory requirements for real estate brokerage agreements between brokers and sellers or lessors versus buyers or lessees. Requires seller or lessor agreements to specify shared compensation amounts as a percentage, dollar amount, or combination. Requires buyer or lessee agreements to state the compensation amount using the same pricing formats. Mandates disclosures regarding third-party compensation authorization and related client rights and obligations in buyer or lessee agreements. Requires both categories of agreements to contain provisions allowing cancellation by either party or by mutual agreement. Takes effect October 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Real Estate Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: licensed real estate brokers, real estate salespersons, and residential real estate buyers, sellers, lessors, and lessees
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State Real Estate Commission finances or operations, and has no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor oversees the State Real Estate Commission, which regulates and licenses real estate brokers, salespersons, and real estate brokerage agreements under Title 17 of the Business Occupations and Professions Article.

The Administrative Office of the Courts was consulted as an information source regarding potential contract litigation or disputes arising under real estate brokerage agreements, though operational and fiscal impacts are negligible.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes expenditures from the Construction Contingency Fund to supplement capital appropriations for projects with material price adjustments. Applies to State-owned capital projects that include price adjustments for material price fluctuations of identified eligible project-specific materials. Requires approval from the Governor before the Secretaries of Budget and Management and General Services request fund expenditures. Requires authorization from the Board of Public Works to release money from the fund.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Budget and Management; Department of General Services; Board of Public Works; Office of the Governor
qa_results.stakeholders: Contractors and small businesses working on State-owned capital construction projects
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on State finances or operations because qualifying reimbursements are absorbed by existing balances and routine appropriations to the Construction Contingency Fund. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Secretary of General Services is specifically authorized, jointly with the Secretary of Budget and Management and with the Governor's approval, to request the Board of Public Works to authorize expenditures from the Construction Contingency Fund for contracts that include price adjustments for material fluctuations.

The Secretary of Budget and Management is statutorily authorized to jointly request Board of Public Works approval to use the Construction Contingency Fund for contracts with material price adjustments, directly involving the agency in capital budget management and contingency allocations.

The Board of Public Works is the administrative body authorized to approve and release expenditures from the Construction Contingency Fund to supplement capital appropriations under the new criteria established by the bill.

Requests to the Board of Public Works for expenditures from the Construction Contingency Fund require the explicit approval of the Governor, and unspent capital proceeds are allocated to the Fund by the Governor.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires licenses for real estate brokers, associate real estate brokers, and real estate salespersons to expire on a staggered basis. Lengthens the advance notice requirement for license renewals from one month to 60 days. Mandates that licensees complete continuing education requirements at least 30 days before their license expires. Imposes a reinstatement fee set by the State Real Estate Commission on licensees who miss the 30-day deadline. Requires the Commission to adopt regulations governing continuing education courses conducted through virtual or remote means.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Real Estate Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Licensed real estate brokers, associate real estate brokers, real estate salespersons, and continuing education course providers in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The State Real Estate Commission can implement the changes with existing resources, with no material impact on state revenues and no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor oversees occupational and professional licensing boards, including the State Real Estate Commission, which directly administers real estate broker licensing, renewal schedules, and continuing education requirements altered by this bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland State Department of Education to report to the General Assembly by December 1, 2024. Mandates a cost estimate for providing free breakfast and lunch to all Maryland public school students. Requires the department to evaluate current free meal participation under Maryland Meals for Achievement and federal programs. Directs the department to review county-level meal data disaggregated by school level and meal type. Requires the compilation of research and findings from other states with universal meal programs. Terminates the reporting requirement on June 30, 2025.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland public school students, local school systems, and county boards of education
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The Maryland State Department of Education can complete the required study and report using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates that the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) study and report to the General Assembly on the cost of providing free breakfast and lunch to all public school students in the State, including evaluating participation data, staffing costs, and policies from other states.

qa_results.bill_summary: Exempts from the State sales and use tax sales made by specified nonprofit organizations. Applies to organizations exempt from federal taxation under Section 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code. Requires the organization to maintain a memorial situated on property owned by the State. Conditions the exemption on using all sale proceeds to maintain a memorial on State-owned property. Takes effect July 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations maintaining memorials on State-owned property, such as the Maryland Fire-Rescue Memorial Foundation, and their patrons
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund and Blueprint for Maryland's Future Fund revenues decrease by a minimal amount annually beginning in fiscal 2025. Expenditures and local government finances are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is the state's principal tax collection agency responsible for administering and enforcing sales and use tax laws, including processing exemptions for qualifying nonprofit organizations.
The Department of General Services manages and maintains state-owned property and facilities where memorials maintained by qualifying nonprofit organizations are located.

The Maryland State Archives, which oversees the Commission on Artistic Property and maintains historical records of state properties and memorials, served as an information source for the bill's fiscal analysis.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Interagency Commission on School Construction to set the State share of eligible costs at 100% for the Maryland School for the Blind. Applies this requirement when adopting the State and local cost-share formula under the Public School Construction Program. Eliminates the local matching requirement for eligible school construction projects at the Maryland School for the Blind. Takes effect July 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Interagency Commission on School Construction
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland School for the Blind and local school systems
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Overall State expenditures and revenues are unaffected because total Public School Construction Program funding is fixed through the annual capital budget. Additional funding awarded to the Maryland School for the Blind may decrease the amount of State matching funds available to local school systems for public school construction projects.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly requires the Interagency Commission on School Construction (IAC) to adjust its regulations and set the State cost-share at 100% for eligible school construction projects for the Maryland School for the Blind under the Public School Construction Program.

The Maryland State Department of Education coordinates closely with the IAC on public school policies, standards, and school construction administration, and was noted in the fiscal note as assisting in implementation using existing budgeted resources.

qa_results.bill_summary: Adds real property title insurance services, including commercial real property title insurance services, to procurement industry types. Requires State procurement units to report minority business enterprise participation data for these services. Prohibits the Special Secretary from waiving reporting requirements for real property title insurance services. Directs the Governor's Office of Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs to include the data in annual reports. Takes effect October 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governor's Office of Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs; State procurement units
qa_results.stakeholders: Certified minority business enterprises offering real property title insurance services, commercial title insurance providers, and State procurement units
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on State or local finances because the reporting change is procedural in nature.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOSBA is the primary implementing agency for the bill. It receives annual MBE procurement reports from all state units, is specifically prohibited by the bill from waiving the reporting requirement for real property title insurance services, and compiles the annual summary report submitted to the Board of Public Works and the General Assembly.

MDOT serves as the State's official MBE certification agency, jointly prescribing the reporting forms with GOSBA and receiving the annual MBE procurement reports from state units. Additionally, its modal administrations routinely acquire real property requiring title insurance services.

DGS houses the Office of State Procurement and manages real estate leasing, acquisitions, and capital projects for the State, making it one of the primary agencies that procures real property title insurance services subject to the bill's reporting requirements.

The Board of Public Works oversees significant state procurements and property transactions, approves the reporting forms prescribed by GOSBA and the certification agency, and receives the annual MBE summary report.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Governor to annually proclaim September 30 as Maryland Veterans Suicide Prevention Day. Mandates that the proclamation declare a day of reflection, recollection, and determination remembering veteran suicide. Directs the proclamation to include a pledge to destigmatize mental health support for veterans. Requires the proclamation to pledge to create opportunities for individuals to speak freely and obtain needed support. Mandates that the proclamation pledge to encourage veterans to reach out for help.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governor
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland veterans, service members, and their families
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: None. Commemorating Maryland Veterans Suicide Prevention Day does not affect State or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates that the Governor annually issue a proclamation declaring September 30 as Maryland Veterans Suicide Prevention Day.

The commemorative day directly pertains to veterans' mental health, suicide prevention, and community support, aligning with the department's mission to support and advocate for Maryland veterans and their families.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes self-service storage facility operators to advertise personal property lien sales by electronic mail or website without occupant authorization. Repeals the requirement that an occupant must initial the rental agreement before an operator may advertise online or by email. Alters the mandatory rental agreement disclosure to state that advertising method selection is at the operator's sole discretion. Maintains the requirement that operators advertise the time, place, and terms at least 3 days before conducting a sale. Takes effect June 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General (Consumer Protection Division)
qa_results.stakeholders: Self-service storage facility owners and operators, and occupants leasing self-service storage units in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division enforces statutory consumer protections under the Commercial Law Article, including required disclosures in consumer agreements such as self-service storage facility contracts.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Baltimore City Department of Housing and Community Development to publicly disseminate illegal dumping surveillance images during investigations. Alters Maryland Public Information Act provisions that govern the inspection of surveillance images of illegal dumping in Baltimore City. Requires image custodians to permit inspection by employees or agents of the Baltimore City Department of Housing and Community Development. Replaces inspection authority previously held by the Baltimore City Department of Public Works. Takes effect October 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Baltimore City Department of Housing and Community Development
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals investigated or cited for illegal dumping in Baltimore City, registered vehicle owners in Baltimore City, and Baltimore City municipal agencies
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances and operations are not materially affected. Baltimore City may experience a potential minimal increase in fine revenues if public dissemination leads to additional identifications and citations. City expenditures for litter removal may decrease to the extent illegal dumping is deterred or violators reimburse cleanup costs.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Attorney General oversees interpretation and enforcement compliance of the Maryland Public Information Act (PIA), which this bill directly amends regarding the inspection and dissemination of surveillance records.
The District Court of Maryland adjudicates contested citations and defenses related to illegal dumping violations captured by surveillance images under Criminal Law § 10-112.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Department of Juvenile Services to report annually on shootings involving youth under its supervision. Mandates reporting to the Commission on Juvenile Justice Reform and Emerging and Best Practices and the General Assembly. Covers supervised juveniles who were nonfatally shot, shot another individual, or were homicide victims in the preceding year. Requires details on departmental response actions, response timelines, and each juvenile's age and county of residence. Requires the initial report to describe any established process the Department uses following such incidents.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Juvenile Services
qa_results.stakeholders: juveniles under the supervision of the Department of Juvenile Services
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The Department of Juvenile Services can implement the reporting requirements using existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: SB 652 directly tasks the Department of Juvenile Services with compiling and submitting an annual report detailing shootings, homicides, department response actions, timelines, and demographic data regarding juveniles under its supervision.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates that the annual report be submitted to the Commission on Juvenile Justice Reform and Emerging and Best Practices to inform their oversight and policy recommendations.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Prince George’s Gateway Development Authority to meet at least four times per year. Directs staff of the Prince George’s County Redevelopment Authority to provide operational support for the authority. Mandates that this operational support occur in consultation with the Department of Housing and Community Development. Takes effect July 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Prince George’s Gateway Development Authority; Prince George’s County Redevelopment Authority; Department of Housing and Community Development
qa_results.stakeholders: Prince George’s Gateway Development Authority, Prince George’s County Redevelopment Authority, Department of Housing and Community Development, and residents and local officials of Mount Rainier, Brentwood, Cottage City, Bladensburg, Colmar Manor, and North Brentwood
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State Department of Housing and Community Development operations are unaffected, with consultations handled using existing budgeted resources. Local expenditures for the Prince George's County Redevelopment Authority increase by up to approximately $90,000 annually from fiscal 2025 through 2028, and by up to approximately $22,500 in fiscal 2029, to provide contractual operational support staff. Revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires staff of the Prince George's County Redevelopment Authority to provide operational support for the Gateway Development Authority in consultation with the Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD). In addition, the Secretary of DHCD (or designee) serves as a member of the Authority.

Under the Economic Development Article, the Secretary of Commerce (or designee) serves on the Prince George's Gateway Development Authority, which the bill mandates must meet at least four times per year.

qa_results.bill_summary: Reduces the written consent threshold to amend a condominium declaration from 80% to 66 2/3% of unit owners. Maintains the 80% written consent requirement if the developer owns any units in the condominium. Excludes corrective amendments and specified assessment suspension provisions from these threshold requirements. Provides that an amendment becomes effective upon recordation in the same manner as the declaration. Takes effect October 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary; Office of the Secretary of State
qa_results.stakeholders: condominium unit owners, condominium councils of unit owners, and condominium developers in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Secretary of State manages the registration and oversight of condominiums in Maryland and receives copies of court orders of reformation when registered condominiums amend or reform their declarations.
The Administrative Office of the Courts supports the circuit courts, which have jurisdiction over petitions filed by condominium councils of unit owners to reform or correct declarations.
The Office of the Attorney General (via the Consumer Protection Division) regulates and enforces consumer protection standards in common ownership communities, including condominiums.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters maximum monetary relief amounts the Maryland Commission on Civil Rights may seek for public accommodation and occupational licensing discrimination. Increases standard relief limits to $1,000 for a first offense, $2,000 for a second offense, and $3,000 for subsequent offenses. Directs all collected monetary relief to be paid directly to the complainant instead of the State General Fund. Authorizes relief up to $25,000 if an employee or agent commits the act and the respondent fails to mitigate harm. Prohibits monetary relief for first-time accessibility violations that the respondent promptly corrects upon service. Requires administrative law judges to evaluate five specific criteria, including respondent assets and public harm, when determining awards.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Commission on Civil Rights; Office of Administrative Hearings
qa_results.stakeholders: complainants alleging discrimination, places of public accommodation, and businesses and individuals licensed or regulated by the Maryland Department of Labor
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal decrease in State general fund revenues because penalties previously remitted to the State will now be paid directly to complainants as monetary relief. Workload and expenditures for the Maryland Commission on Civil Rights, the Office of Administrative Hearings, and the Judiciary are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly governs the Maryland Commission on Civil Rights (MCCR), authorizing it to seek increased monetary relief directly for complainants rather than civil penalties paid to the General Fund, establishing criteria for relief, and mandating an annual report to the Governor and General Assembly.

The bill explicitly establishes statutory criteria that Administrative Law Judges must evaluate when determining the amount of monetary relief to award in contested discrimination cases brought under these provisions.

The bill's monetary relief provisions directly apply to discriminatory acts committed by individuals and entities licensed or regulated by units within the Maryland Department of Labor under Section 20-402 of the State Government Article.
The bill requires the Maryland Commission on Civil Rights to submit an annual report directly to the Governor each year through 2029 on the effect of the legislation.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals the annual reporting requirement for actions taken by the Attorney General regarding federal government actions or inactions. Eliminates the requirement that the Attorney General's annual report include an itemized statement of receipts and disbursements. Requires the Attorney General to submit the annual report to the General Assembly in addition to the Governor. Requires the Attorney General to publish annual reports and issued opinions on the agency website instead of in bound volumes.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Office of the Attorney General
qa_results.stakeholders: Office of the Attorney General, Maryland General Assembly, the Governor, and members of the public seeking access to State legal opinions and annual reports
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on State finances or operations, though the Office of the Attorney General may experience administrative efficiencies from eliminating physical bound volumes. No local fiscal effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the statutory reporting and publication duties of the Office of the Attorney General, repealing the Maryland Defense Act reporting requirement, removing the requirement to publish reports and opinions in bound volumes in favor of website publication, and altering the contents of its annual report.

The bill repeals an annual reporting requirement previously made to the Governor regarding actions taken under the Maryland Defense Act and modifies the distribution requirements for the Attorney General's annual report.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Department of Natural Resources to distribute at least $250,000 annually from the Waterway Improvement Fund. Directs the recipient historic preservation nonprofit organization to operate a maritime heritage competitive grant program. Requires vessel owners applying for a certificate of number to provide emergency contact information. Establishes new notice requirements before and after the Department seizes or removes abandoned or sunken vessels. Authorizes the Department of Natural Resources to establish and administer a voluntary vessel turn-in program.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
qa_results.stakeholders: vessel owners in Maryland, statewide and local historic preservation nonprofit organizations, and state, county, and municipal instrumentalities engaged in maritime heritage preservation
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund expenditures increase by at least $125,000 in fiscal 2025 to establish a voluntary vessel turn-in program, and by at least $375,000 annually thereafter to include the $250,000 mandated grant distribution from the Waterway Improvement Fund. Local revenues and expenditures may increase minimally beginning in fiscal 2026 from maritime heritage competitive grants.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Natural Resources is the primary implementing agency for the bill, tasked with collecting emergency contact information for vessel certificates, following new notification protocols for abandoned or sunken vessels, establishing and administering a voluntary vessel turn-in program, and distributing at least $250,000 annually from the Waterway Improvement Fund.

The Maryland Historical Trust (MHT), a division of the Department of Planning, must be consulted by DNR when adopting regulations concerning abandoned or sunken vessels, and MHT is identified in the fiscal note as an eligible state entity to receive maritime heritage grant funding.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes liability and settlement procedures for State actions arising from the Francis Scott Key Bridge allision. Requires the judge or jury to determine total liability and assign comparative responsibility to each joined party. Authorizes the State to pursue non-settling responsible persons if complete relief is not obtained in settlement. Exempts governed actions from the Maryland Uniform Contribution Among Joint Tort-Feasors Act. Protects settling responsible persons from claims for noncontractual contribution or indemnity regarding resolved actions. Reduces remaining liability by the larger of the settling person's proportionate share or settlement amount.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General; Maryland Judiciary
qa_results.stakeholders: Parties named or alleged to be liable in legal actions arising from the Francis Scott Key Bridge collapse, including vessel owners and maritime operators, and the State of Maryland.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Potential significant increase in State general fund revenues and a potential reduction in litigation costs if the provisions facilitate higher recoveries and faster settlements. Local government finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill was introduced at the request of the Office of the Attorney General and directly governs litigation strategy, comparative fault determinations, and settlement terms in actions brought by the State regarding the Francis Scott Key Bridge collapse.

MDTA owns, finances, and operates Maryland's toll facilities, including the Francis Scott Key Bridge. Recoveries, settlements, and legal relief related to the bridge's infrastructure damage directly impact MDTA.
MDOT oversees the state's transportation infrastructure network and is heavily involved in the response, channel reopening coordination, and multi-billion-dollar bridge replacement efforts.

The bill establishes specific judicial statutory requirements, mandating that judges and juries make determinations of total liability and allocate comparative responsibility among parties in applicable actions.
The bill explicitly governs State actions related to alleged or threatened environmental injuries resulting from the Dali allision and bridge collapse.
The bill specifically applies to actions brought by the State for alleged or threatened injuries to the natural resources and waterways of the State resulting from the incident.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals specific statutory provisions governing bail bonds and licensing fees within the Seventh Judicial Circuit. Eliminates the requirement that approved bail bondsmen in the circuit pay a 1% license fee on gross bond values. Removes the Seventh Judicial Circuit's exemption from statewide laws governing property bondsmen. Subjects property bondsmen in the circuit to general state requirements regarding authorized agents and property documentation. Takes effect July 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary; Circuit Courts of the Seventh Judicial Circuit
qa_results.stakeholders: Bail bondsmen, property bondsmen, and criminal defendants in the Seventh Judicial Circuit (Calvert, Charles, Prince George's, and St. Mary's counties)
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material state or local fiscal impact because the legislation codifies operational changes and fee terminations already implemented by judicial administrative order in 2022.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill was requested by the Maryland Judicial Conference and directly impacts circuit court administration by repealing specific statutory fee and regulatory provisions for bail bonds in the Seventh Judicial Circuit to align statute with Maryland Rules and current court operations.

The Maryland Insurance Administration licenses and regulates insurance producers, including bail bondspersons writing surety bonds in the State, and was consulted on the removal of local Seventh Judicial Circuit licensing exceptions.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the reimbursement limit for grant awards to Maryland National Guard members under the Tricare Premium Reimbursement Program. Repeals the sixty-dollar monthly cap on grant awards for health and dental care premiums paid by eligible recipients. Authorizes reimbursement for up to the total amount of monthly premiums paid for individual or immediate family coverage. Prohibits total annual grant awards from exceeding the annual appropriation in the State budget for the program. Requires the Military Department to adopt regulations to implement and administer the program.
qa_results.responsible_party: Military Department
qa_results.stakeholders: Members of the Maryland National Guard eligible for Tricare Reserve Select and their immediate family members
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No net effect on state revenues or expenditures because total awards cannot exceed the program's annual state budget appropriation ($871,300 in fiscal 2025). The bill increases the likelihood that appropriated funds will be fully expended. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Adjutant General heads the Maryland Military Department, which directly administers the TRICARE Premium Reimbursement Program and is responsible for adopting regulations and issuing grant reimbursements to eligible recipients under the program.
Members of the Maryland National Guard are the eligible recipients whose monthly health and dental premium reimbursement caps are altered by the bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands the definition of kinship caregiver for children in need of out-of-home placement. Includes unrelated individuals who have a strong bond with the child or are identified by the parent. Requires local departments of social services to give placement preference to kinship caregivers absent good cause. Requires placing a child with a kinship caregiver located after foster placement if in the child's best interest. Lowers the minimum age requirement for an approved kinship caregiver from 21 to 18 years.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Human Services; Social Services Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: children in need of out-of-home placement, prospective and approved kinship caregivers, parents, and foster care providers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local government operations or finances, and State revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill is a departmental initiative for DHS, directly governing its Kinship Care Program, modifying out-of-home placement criteria and procedures for local departments of social services, and directing the Social Services Administration within DHS to adopt corresponding regulations and policies.

The bill amends the definition of 'relative' in Title 3, Subtitle 8 of the Courts and Judicial Proceedings Article, which directly impacts Child in Need of Assistance (CINA) proceedings adjudicated in the Maryland court system.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Maryland Pathway to Nursing Pilot Program in the Maryland Higher Education Commission to support practical nursing students. Establishes the Maryland Pathway to Nursing Advisory Committee to assist the Secretary of Higher Education with program implementation. Requires the Secretary of Higher Education to issue grants to at least two pilot sites in diverse areas by July 1, 2025. Directs the program to provide participants with financial assistance for educational supplies and wraparound support services. Requires annual implementation reports to the Governor and General Assembly each December 15 through 2029.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Higher Education Commission; Secretary of Higher Education; Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: students in licensed practical nursing and registered nursing programs, community colleges and public higher education institutions offering nursing credentials, and Maryland healthcare facilities
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $184,200 in FY 2025 for initial staffing and program development. Expenditures escalate in FY 2026 to roughly $829,500 under illustrative scenarios for ongoing staff, pilot site grants, and participant financial aid. Costs may be offset by braided funding from local workforce development boards, health care systems, and federal grants. No local revenue impact, though local health departments may benefit from reduced nursing vacancies.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MHEC is the primary implementing agency tasked with establishing, administering, and staffing the Maryland Pathway to Nursing Pilot Program and its Advisory Committee, issuing grants to pilot sites, and submitting annual implementation reports.
MHEC is the primary implementing agency tasked with administering the new pilot program and staffing the advisory committee.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a new statutory advisory board, the Maryland Pathway to Nursing Advisory Committee, to advise and assist in the implementation of the pilot program.
The Secretary of Health or designee serves on the Advisory Committee, and the Maryland Board of Nursing (housed within MDH) is also designated a seat.
A representative of the Maryland Department of Labor is designated to serve on the Advisory Committee, and the program requires coordination with local workforce development boards.
The bill mandates representation from the Department of Veterans Affairs on the Advisory Committee to support nursing education pathways.

Public higher education institutions offering 4-year degree nursing programs within the state system are represented on the Advisory Committee and eligible to participate in nursing education pathways.
The bill specifies representation on the Advisory Committee from a public historically Black college or university (HBCU) with a 4-year degree nursing program.
The Secretary of Higher Education is required to report annually through 2029 to the Governor on the implementation of the pilot program.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires employers of security guards at health care facilities to report emergency codes to the Secretary of State Police. Mandates reporting every seven days on code greens for combative persons and code purples for security-only responses. Exempts these health care facility security guard employers from standard 48-hour use of force reporting requirements. Prohibits any use of force report from containing information protected from disclosure under state or federal law. Delays the effective date of Chapter 763 of 2023 from June 1, 2024, to January 1, 2025.
qa_results.responsible_party: Secretary of State Police
qa_results.stakeholders: Employers of security guards at health care facilities, licensed security guard agencies, and security guards
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the Department of State Police and the Secretary of State Police, who oversee security guard licensing and receive required weekly reports on emergency code responses (Code Green and Code Purple) from security employers at health care facilities. The bill also delays the implementation date of use of force reporting and certification standards established under Chapter 763 of 2023.

The bill regulates security guard intervention reporting at health care facilities governed under Title 10 of the Code of Maryland Regulations and the Health - General Article, referencing emergency codes used by facilities licensed and regulated by the Maryland Department of Health.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters residency and appointment requirements for members of the Harford Community College Board of Trustees. Requires all nine members to be appointed from Harford County at large. Mandates that each trustee remain a Harford County resident for the duration of the member's term. Requires the Governor, to the extent practicable, to consider county geographic and ethnic representation when appointing members. Limits required semiannual joint meetings to the college president and county public schools superintendent, removing governing board members.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governor; Harford Community College; Harford County Public Schools
qa_results.stakeholders: Members and prospective members of the Harford Community College Board of Trustees, Harford County residents, the Harford Community College president, and the Harford County public schools superintendent
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact, as the bill is procedural in nature and does not affect finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes appointment criteria for the Governor, requiring the Governor to appoint members to the Harford Community College Board of Trustees from the county at large and to consider the geographic and ethnic representation of Harford County when making appointments.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and processing gubernatorial appointments for state and local boards and commissions, and will implement the revised residency and representation criteria for the Harford Community College Board of Trustees.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes courts to prohibit individuals convicted of operating a vessel under the influence from operating for up to two years. Extends the maximum prohibition to five years if the violation results in another person's death. Requires the Department of Natural Resources to establish an accessible prohibition database by October 1, 2025. Requires courts to electronically report prohibited individuals to the Department of Natural Resources. Prohibits operating or attempting to operate a vessel while subject to a court-ordered ban. Establishes misdemeanor penalties of escalating fines and imprisonment terms for violating an operating prohibition.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources; Natural Resources Police Force; Judiciary
qa_results.stakeholders: vessel operators on Maryland waters, individuals convicted of operating a vessel while under the influence of alcohol, and Natural Resources Police officers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $37,600 in FY 2025 for one-time Judiciary computer programming costs. General fund and local revenues and expenditures may increase minimally due to the bill's criminal penalty provisions. The Department of Natural Resources can implement the database with existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DNR and its Natural Resources Police Force are tasked with establishing, maintaining, and providing mobile patrol access to a statewide database of individuals prohibited from operating vessels due to boating under the influence convictions.
