The Judiciary and court system must track vessel operation prohibitions and electronically notify DNR of prohibited individuals, incurring $37,567 in FY 2025 programming costs to update case management systems.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates new and expanded misdemeanor offenses for operating a vessel while prohibited, carrying maximum penalties of up to 3 years imprisonment, which could minimally affect state correctional facilities and community supervision.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates new misdemeanor penalties carrying potential incarceration of up to three years for operating a vessel while prohibited, potentially requiring legal representation for indigent defendants.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits merchants from knowingly selling open-loop or closed-loop gift cards without meeting packaging and fraud notice requirements. Requires merchants displaying gift cards to train retail sales employees on identifying and responding to gift card fraud. Directs the Division of Consumer Protection to create model notices and fraud detection guidelines for merchants. Mandates that third-party gift card resellers record and maintain specified transaction information for at least three years. Classifies violations as unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act.
qa_results.responsible_party: Division of Consumer Protection in the Office of the Attorney General
qa_results.stakeholders: Merchants selling gift cards in Maryland, third-party gift card resellers, retail store employees, and consumers purchasing gift cards
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material impact on State or local finances or operations. The Office of the Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division can implement the bill with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the Consumer Protection Division within the Office of the Attorney General with creating and maintaining a model notice for merchants, issuing guidelines on gift card fraud detection and prevention, and enforcing violations under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act.

As the primary state law enforcement agency, Maryland State Police officers are authorized under the bill to inspect third-party gift card reseller records and request that gift card issuers preserve relevant evidence following theft reports exceeding $500.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals statutory amount and duration limits for property tax credits on improved real property in Frederick County historic districts. Authorizes the governing body of Frederick County to establish the amount and duration of the tax credit by law. Permits the county to establish additional eligibility criteria and application regulations. Authorizes the county to adopt procedures for uniform request processing and any other necessary provisions. Takes effect June 1, 2024, and applies to taxable years beginning after June 30, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governing Body of Frederick County
qa_results.stakeholders: Owners of improved real property in Frederick County historic districts, Emmitsburg Civic Association, Incorporated, and Frederick County government
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal effect. Frederick County property tax revenues decrease by a minimal indeterminate amount depending on the credit amount and eligibility criteria established by the county. County expenditures are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters the criteria, amount, and duration of a local property tax credit in Frederick County for improvements to properties in historic districts. While the fiscal impact is local, the Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board is responsible for hearing appeals concerning real property assessments and property tax credit determinations.

The Maryland Tax Court serves as the highest administrative body hearing appeals from decisions of state and local taxing authorities and Property Tax Assessment Appeals Boards regarding property assessments and tax disputes.

qa_results.bill_summary: Renames the Regional Additive Manufacturing Partnership of Maryland to be the Regional Advanced Manufacturing Partnership of Maryland. Renames the associated special fund to match the partnership's updated title. Broadens the partnership's statutory purposes and workforce initiatives from additive manufacturing to advanced manufacturing. Removes a representative of 3D Maryland from the voting membership of the Executive Board. Expands board representation to include emerging advanced manufacturing industries and collaborating organizations.
qa_results.responsible_party: Regional Advanced Manufacturing Partnership of Maryland; Maryland Department of Commerce
qa_results.stakeholders: Advanced manufacturing businesses, educational institutions, students, and workers in Cecil and Harford counties
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material effect on State or local government finances or operations. Any State or local funding for the partnership remains discretionary.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Secretary of Commerce (or designee) serves as a voting member on the Executive Board of RAMP MD, appoints industry representatives to the board, and the Department provides operational and administrative support to the partnership.
The bill explicitly requires the Executive Director of the Governor's Workforce Development Board to appoint a representative to serve on the Executive Board of the partnership.

Towson University, a member institution of the University System of Maryland, has its President designated as a voting member on the board and is statutorily tasked with participating in workforce training and degree programs under the partnership.

The bill updates the name of the Regional Advanced Manufacturing Partnership of Maryland Fund within State Finance and Procurement provisions governing fund interest allocation administered by the Treasurer.
The bill makes conforming name changes to the fund under State Finance and Procurement Article Section 6-226, which governs interest earnings accounted for by the Comptroller.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Public Service Commission to establish the Small Solar Energy Generating System Incentive Program. Extends the lifespan of renewable energy credits under the Renewable Energy Portfolio Standard to five years. Establishes the Customer-Sited Solar Program within the Maryland Energy Administration to award grants to low- to moderate-income households. Requires counties and municipalities to implement automated solar permitting software by August 1, 2025. Mandates prevailing wages for workers on solar energy generating systems larger than one megawatt. Exempts specified rooftop and canopy nonresidential solar energy systems from state and local property taxes.
qa_results.responsible_party: Public Service Commission; Maryland Energy Administration; Maryland Department of Labor; State Department of Assessments and Taxation
qa_results.stakeholders: Solar energy developers and contractors; residential solar and energy storage customers; low- to moderate-income households; investor-owned gas and electric companies; electricity suppliers; local governments
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Public Service Commission special fund expenditures and matching revenues increase by $515,900 in FY 2025 and at least $256,600 annually thereafter. Strategic Energy Investment Fund revenues and expenditures may decrease beginning in FY 2025 due to reduced compliance fees. Annuity Bond Fund revenues and local property tax revenues decrease beginning in FY 2025 due to new and expanded property tax exemptions.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates the Public Service Commission to establish and administer the Small Solar Energy Generating System Incentive Program, certify qualifying solar facilities, track certified SRECs with enhanced compliance value, collect certification fees, and implement revised net metering aggregation and RPS compliance review systems.

The bill creates the Customer-Sited Solar Program within MEA to provide grants funded by the Strategic Energy Investment Fund (SEIF), authorizes MEA to use alternative compliance fee revenues for administrative expenses, requires MEA to establish consumer protection policies, and tasks the agency with overseeing local implementation of solar permitting software.

The bill requires the Department of Labor to enforce prevailing wage requirements for underground utility infrastructure projects and applies prevailing wage standards to large solar installations. It also imposes wildlife barrier requirements under home improvement contracts, which are regulated by MD Labor's Maryland Home Improvement Commission.

As the advocate for residential utility customers before the Public Service Commission, OPC is impacted by the bill's regulatory changes to net energy metering tariffs, RPS compliance mechanisms, consumer protection policies, and potential impacts on electricity rates.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Health to provide health care services under the Employed Individuals with Disabilities Program. Requires the Department to serve qualified applicants and existing recipients who are at least 16 years old. Prohibits the Department from limiting program eligibility based on applicant or spousal income and specified assets. Prohibits requiring applicants with earnings above substantial gainful activity levels to apply for federal disability benefits. Requires the Department to meet biannually with a state coalition of disability advocates for program feedback. Directs the Department to report by December 1, 2024, on serving individuals aged 65 and older.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Employed individuals with disabilities in Maryland who are eligible for or enrolled in the Maryland Medical Assistance Program
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material impact on State Medicaid revenues or expenditures because the bill largely codifies requirements already implemented by the Maryland Department of Health. The Department can complete the required study and report using existing budgeted resources. No local effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health is the primary implementing agency responsible for administering the Medicaid Employed Individuals with Disabilities (EID) Program, adopting program regulations, seeking federal CMS approvals and waivers, and submitting a required report to legislative committees.

The Department of Disabilities is the principal state agency coordinating services and employment opportunities for Maryland residents with disabilities, making the restructuring and eligibility rules of the EID Program directly relevant to its core policy mission.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Agriculture to coordinate with specified state agencies, universities, electric companies, farmers, and industry. Directs this coordination to ensure anaerobic digestion technology projects are appropriately coordinated. Requires the Department to establish guidance for farmers developing and implementing anaerobic digestion technology. Mandates that the guidance provide information on obtaining required permits and electric interconnection. Requires the guidance to detail available tax incentives, energy rebates, and relevant regulations for waste systems.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Agriculture; Maryland Energy Administration; Maryland Department of the Environment; Department of Commerce
qa_results.stakeholders: Farmers, electric companies, agricultural businesses, and anaerobic digestion technology developers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by an estimated $40,000 to $100,000 in fiscal 2025 for one-time contractual services to assist in developing guidance. State revenues and local government finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDA is the primary implementing agency responsible for coordinating with state agencies and stakeholders and developing comprehensive guidance for farmers on anaerobic digestion technology, incurring an estimated general fund expenditure in FY 2025.
MDE is statutorily required to coordinate with MDA to align project processes and develop guidance for farmers concerning environmental permits and waste system regulations.
MEA is statutorily mandated to coordinate with MDA to ensure project alignment and assist in developing farmer guidance regarding energy rebates, tax incentives, and technology implementation.
The Department of Commerce is explicitly named in the statute to coordinate with MDA and partner agencies on project facilitation and establishing business and implementation guidance for farmers.

USM institutions (University of Maryland College of Agriculture and Natural Resources and University of Maryland Eastern Shore) are statutorily designated partners required to coordinate with MDA on anaerobic digestion technology projects.
PSC oversees electric utility interconnection and renewable energy generation approvals, which are key components of the guidance that must be provided to farmers under the bill.

qa_results.bill_summary: Transfers administration of the Cyber Maryland Fund from the Cyber Maryland Program to the Maryland Technology Development Corporation. Clarifies fund use for administrative expenses, including hiring staff, consultants, and other professionals. Repeals statutory mandates to employ and fund a dedicated executive director and administrator. Requires the Governor to appropriate $99,000 annually for talent pipeline management beginning in fiscal year 2025. Authorizes an additional annual budget appropriation of $250,000 for the fund. Directs the corporation to adopt standards for awarding cybersecurity program grants.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Technology Development Corporation
qa_results.stakeholders: cybersecurity employers, elementary and secondary schools, institutions of higher education, community colleges, for-profit corporations, nonprofit organizations, and cybersecurity job seekers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not materially affected. The bill eliminates an existing mandate to fund specific staff and establishes a new $99,000 annual mandated appropriation beginning in fiscal 2026 for talent pipeline management. Discretionary funding authorizations include up to $250,000 annually. Any impact on local governments and small business grant recipients is expected to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: TEDCO is the primary implementing agency responsible for housing the Cyber Maryland Program, administering the Cyber Maryland Fund, and adopting standards to award program grants.

DBM is responsible for state budget preparation and execution, which is directly impacted by the bill's alteration of statutory budget mandates, establishing a new $99,000 mandated appropriation beginning in FY 2026.

The bill mandates the Governor to include a specific appropriation of $99,000 for the Cyber Maryland Fund in the annual budget bill, authorizes additional appropriations, receives annual program reports, and appoints members to the Cyber Maryland Board.

The Cyber Maryland Program is statutorily tasked with supporting DoIT's efforts to improve the State government's cybersecurity posture, and the Secretary of Information Technology serves on the Cyber Maryland Board.
The Secretary of Labor serves on the Cyber Maryland Board, and the program coordinates with MD Labor on cybersecurity workforce development and talent pipeline strategies.

The Secretary of Commerce (or designee) serves on the Cyber Maryland Board, and the board coordinates with the Department on workforce and economic development initiatives in the cybersecurity sector.
The State Treasurer is designated to hold the Cyber Maryland Fund separately and invest fund monies, with interest earnings credited to the General Fund.
The Comptroller is statutorily required to account for the Cyber Maryland Fund as a special, nonlapsing fund.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires each unit of State government to conduct annual data inventories and regular inventories of high-risk artificial intelligence systems. Requires the Department of Information Technology, in consultation with the Governor's Artificial Intelligence Subcabinet, to adopt artificial intelligence governance policies. Prohibits State units from deploying new artificial intelligence systems that do not comply with departmental policies beginning July 1, 2025. Directs constitutional officers, Baltimore City Community College, and public senior higher education institutions to establish compatible artificial intelligence policies. Establishes the Governor's Artificial Intelligence Subcabinet and creates a competitive proof of concept procurement method.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Information Technology; Governor's Artificial Intelligence Subcabinet; Department of General Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Executive branch units of State government; public senior higher education institutions; Baltimore City Community College; constitutional officers; commercial vendors and contractors developing or deploying artificial intelligence technologies
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures increase by at least $1.8 million in FY 2025, including $1.7 million for the Department of Information Technology for staff and expert consultants and $96,089 for the Department of General Services. Higher education expenditures increase, likely by more than $1.0 million annually, to establish and manage policies. Other State agency expenditures may increase to conduct required inventories and impact assessments. State revenues and local governments are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DoIT is the primary implementing agency under the bill. It is responsible for developing statewide AI policies and procedures, establishing guidelines for data inventories, reviewing and maintaining AI inventories and impact assessments, approving proof-of-concept procurements, chairing and staffing the AI Subcabinet, and incurs direct fiscal impacts of over $1.7 million.

DGS is required to develop policies and procedures for competitive proof-of-concept procurements in consultation with DoIT, serves as a member of the Governor's AI Subcabinet, and receives a fiscal appropriation to hire procurement staff.

As public senior higher education institutions, USM constituent universities must adopt functionally compatible policies and procedures for high-risk AI by June 1, 2025, report annually on high-risk AI, and face estimated costs exceeding $1.0 million across campuses.

Identified as a public senior higher education institution required to establish functionally compatible policies and procedures for high-risk AI systems by June 1, 2025, and submit annual reports to DoIT on high-risk AI procured and deployed.

Identified as a public senior higher education institution required to establish functionally compatible policies and procedures for high-risk AI systems by June 1, 2025, and submit annual reports to DoIT on high-risk AI procured and deployed.

The bill codifies the Governor's AI Subcabinet within the Governor's Executive Council, authorizes up to $3 million in budget appropriations for subcabinet partnerships, and directs multiple reports and the AI roadmap to the Governor.

Although generally exempt from the subtitle, OAG is explicitly mandated to establish policies and procedures functionally compatible with DoIT's policies for the procurement, deployment, and ongoing assessment of high-risk AI by June 1, 2025.

Although generally exempt from the subtitle, the Comptroller is explicitly mandated to establish policies and procedures functionally compatible with DoIT's policies for the procurement, deployment, and ongoing assessment of high-risk AI by June 1, 2025.

Although generally exempt from the subtitle, the Treasurer is explicitly mandated to establish policies and procedures functionally compatible with DoIT's policies for the procurement, deployment, and ongoing assessment of high-risk AI by June 1, 2025.
The Secretary of Budget and Management is designated by statute as a member of the newly codified Governor's Artificial Intelligence Subcabinet.
The Secretary of Commerce is designated by statute as a member of the newly codified Governor's Artificial Intelligence Subcabinet.
The Secretary of Labor is designated by statute as a member of the newly codified Governor's Artificial Intelligence Subcabinet.
The Director of the Governor's Office of Homeland Security is designated by statute as a member of the newly codified Governor's Artificial Intelligence Subcabinet.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill formally establishes and codifies in statute the Governor's Artificial Intelligence Subcabinet of the Governor's Executive Council.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Service and Civic Innovation
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Specifically highlighted in the fiscal note as anticipating moderate to significant fiscal and operational impacts for specialized AI staff to implement the required inventories and impact assessments.

Specifically highlighted in the fiscal note as anticipating moderate to significant fiscal and operational impacts to obtain specialized AI expertise for compliance with the required inventories and assessments.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands an income tax subtraction modification to include members of any State law enforcement unit. Allows eligible officers to subtract the first $5,000 of earned income from federal adjusted gross income. Limits eligibility to officers residing in a political subdivision with a crime rate exceeding the State crime rate. Applies the modification to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland; Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: State law enforcement officers who reside in Maryland political subdivisions where the crime rate exceeds the State crime rate
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues decrease by $203,000 annually beginning in fiscal 2025 due to additional subtraction modifications. Local income tax revenues decrease by $132,000 annually beginning in fiscal 2025. State and local expenditures are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the state's principal tax collector, the Comptroller is responsible for administering Maryland personal income tax laws, processing the $5,000 income tax subtraction modification, updating tax forms, and receiving certifications of qualifying high-crime subdivisions.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS houses the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission, which is statutorily mandated to calculate crime rates and certify qualifying political subdivisions to the Comptroller. DPSCS also employs law enforcement personnel who may qualify.

As the primary state law enforcement agency in Maryland, its sworn officers are direct beneficiaries of the bill's expansion of the income tax subtraction modification to all state law enforcement units.
The bill explicitly references the Maryland Transportation Authority Police and affects the tax status of its officers and other state law enforcement personnel residing in qualifying areas.
DNR houses the Natural Resources Police, a major state law enforcement unit whose officers become eligible for the state income tax subtraction modification if they reside in qualifying subdivisions.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases the maximum line-of-duty funeral benefit for specified public safety officers from $10,000 to $25,000. Repeals the reduction of public safety funeral benefits by related workers' compensation payments. Raises the line-of-duty death benefit for State employees from $100,000 to $125,000. Establishes a line-of-duty funeral benefit of up to $25,000 for State employees. Indexes these death and funeral benefits to inflation starting in fiscal year 2026. Authorizes retroactive benefits for eligible State employees killed in the line of duty on or after January 1, 2023.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Budget and Management; Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Surviving beneficiaries and estates of Maryland public safety officers, Maryland National Guard members, and State employees across the Executive, Legislative, and Judicial branches
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $340,000 in FY 2025 ($250,000 for DBM and $90,000 for DPSCS) and by at least $206,700 annually thereafter, reflecting increased benefit caps and inflation adjustments. State revenues are not affected. Local government expenditures increase minimally to cover higher funeral benefits for local hazardous material response team employees.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DBM is the primary agency responsible for administering the death and funeral benefits under Section 10-404 of the State Personnel and Pensions Article, determining benefit eligibility, handling retroactive claims, and absorbing a substantial portion of the fiscal expenditure increase.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS administers the line-of-duty death and funeral benefits for public safety officers under Section 1-202 of the Public Safety Article, which sees an increase in the funeral benefit cap from $10,000 to $25,000 indexed to inflation, directly impacting DPSCS general fund expenditures.
Members of the Maryland National Guard serving on state or federal orders are explicitly covered under Section 10-404 for line-of-duty death and funeral benefits.

As the head of the Maryland Military Department overseeing the National Guard, the Adjutant General is directly concerned with benefit enhancements and death/funeral provisions for serving Guard members.
The bill explicitly expands line-of-duty death and funeral benefits to cover Judicial Branch personnel under Section 10-404, directly impacting court system employees and judicial officers.
State Police officers and aviation personnel are among the primary public safety personnel eligible for line-of-duty death and enhanced funeral benefits under the amended statutes.
The bill eliminates the statutory requirement that public safety funeral benefits be offset by related workers' compensation benefits paid under Section 9-689 of the Labor and Employment Article.

qa_results.bill_summary: Extends the timeframe from 10 to 60 days after birth for safely leaving an unharmed newborn without liability or prosecution. Authorizes a person to leave an unharmed newborn at a designated facility or with a responsible adult. Authorizes designated facilities to receive a newborn in an approved newborn safety device with specific monitoring and alert features. Requires the Secretary of Human Services to develop, implement, and maintain a public information program subject to existing funding. Requires the Secretary to submit an annual report on Maryland Safe Haven Program metrics to the General Assembly by December 31.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Human Services
qa_results.stakeholders: parents of newborns, designated facilities, healthcare providers, law enforcement agencies, fire companies, and emergency medical services providers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $250,000 annually beginning in FY 2025 for the Department of Human Services to implement the public information program. State and local agencies can distribute program literature and submit reports using existing budgeted resources. Local expenditures may increase minimally if local governments choose to install newborn safety devices, which cost approximately $15,000 each plus $500 to $5,000 in annual maintenance.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates the Secretary of Human Services as the primary official responsible for adopting regulations, developing and maintaining a statewide public information program, and submitting annual metric reports to the General Assembly. In addition, local departments of social services receive custody notifications and medical history submissions regarding surrendered newborns.

State Police barracks are explicitly designated as authorized facilities where individuals may surrender a newborn, and law enforcement personnel are identified as recipients of Safe Haven program training.

State and local health department offices are mandated to regularly distribute Maryland Safe Haven Program literature, and licensed medical providers and hospitals act as designated surrender facilities.
The bill mandates regular distribution of Maryland Safe Haven Program educational and informational literature at each publicly funded educational institution in the state.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes requirements for newborn safety devices to connect with 9-1-1 and dispatch emergency medical services (EMS) providers, and requires training for EMS providers and 9-1-1 operators.
The legislation amends the Courts and Judicial Proceedings Article to alter provisions governing civil and criminal immunity related to the surrender of newborns.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the period during which the State may recover grant funding under the Federally Qualified Health Centers Grant Program. Prohibits the State from recovering funds more than 15 years after project completion if the center leased the property. Maintains the 30-year recovery limit after project completion if the center owned the property. Applies recovery provisions when property transfers to an unqualified entity or ceases operating as a federally qualified health center. Takes effect October 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Board of Public Works
qa_results.stakeholders: Federally qualified health centers and counties, municipal corporations, or nonprofit organizations sponsoring health center projects
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Indeterminate increase in general fund revenues sooner than expected due to accelerated recovery timelines for certain properties. State agency workload can be absorbed with existing budgeted resources. No direct impact on local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health administers the Federally Qualified Health Centers Grant Program, processes applications, and oversees compliance and grant recovery timelines.
The Board of Public Works awards the grants under the program upon recommendation of the Secretary of Health and must approve property transferees under the program's recovery provisions.
The Office of the Attorney General represents the State in legal recovery proceedings to reclaim grant funds and associated legal fees if an entity falls out of compliance.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters specified annual, supplementary, and renewal application fees for alcoholic beverages licenses in Baltimore City. Increases the license renewal application fee paid to the Director of Finance from $50 to $78. Raises annual license fees across multiple categories, including Class A, Class B, Class C, and Class D licenses. Increases supplementary Sunday license fees from $75 to $120 for eligible license holders. Requires the Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners to set fees for festival, tasting, and Class C per diem licenses.
qa_results.responsible_party: Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: alcoholic beverages license holders, license applicants, and hospitality businesses including bars, restaurants, and breweries in Baltimore City
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Baltimore City licensing and fee revenues increase by approximately $823,200 annually beginning in FY 2025 due to higher license and application fees. City expenditures are not affected, and there is no state fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller is tasked with state-level regulation and oversight of the alcoholic beverages industry in Maryland, although the specific fee increases under this bill are administered locally by the Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners with no direct impact on state revenues.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters licensing fees for Class BWL-VLC (video lottery concessionaire) and Class BWL-VLF (video lottery facility) alcoholic beverage licenses, which apply to Baltimore City's casino gaming facility regulated by the agency.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Baltimore Convention and Tourism Redevelopment and Operating Authority Task Force. Directs the Task Force to study governance, redevelopment, financing, and operation of the Baltimore Convention site and surrounding areas. Requires recommendations on potential entity membership, property acquisition, contracting, rates and charges, regulations, and bonding authority. Mandates consideration of at least one non-public-private partnership option that departs from the status quo. Requires the Task Force to report findings to the Baltimore City Mayor, Governor, and General Assembly by December 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Commerce; Baltimore Convention and Tourism Redevelopment and Operating Authority Task Force
qa_results.stakeholders: Baltimore City hospitality, hotel, and restaurant businesses, local African American business owners and residents within a 0.5-mile radius of the Baltimore Convention site, and convention labor union members
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $100,000 in fiscal 2025 for the Department of Commerce to hire a downtown redevelopment consultant. Task force expense reimbursements are minimal and absorbable within existing resources. Local government finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates the Secretary of Commerce as a task force member, requires the Department of Commerce to provide staff support, and results in a $100,000 general fund expenditure in FY 2025 for Commerce to hire a consultant.

The Chair of the Maryland Stadium Authority (or designee) is designated as a member of the task force, and the authority currently holds statutory responsibilities and bond financing agreements regarding the Baltimore Convention Center.
The Chair of the Maryland Economic Development Corporation (or designee) is appointed as a member of the task force to evaluate redevelopment and governance options.
The Administrator of the Maryland Transit Administration (or designee) is explicitly designated as a member of the task force.
The Chair of the Maryland Tourism Development Board is appointed to the task force, and the task force's core mission focuses on tourism redevelopment and promotion.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates the Baltimore Convention and Tourism Redevelopment and Operating Authority Task Force as a temporary advisory body to study and report on governance and redevelopment strategies.
MDOT is the parent department of the Maryland Transit Administration, whose Administrator is appointed to the task force.
The task force is required to submit its final report of findings and recommendations to the Governor by December 1, 2024.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes higher education researchers conducting academic or policy research to review court records of extreme risk protective orders. Requires the Maryland Judiciary to mandate storage and handling agreements with participating institutions of higher education. Restricts the use of reviewed records solely to approved research projects. Prohibits disclosing extreme risk protective order records to individuals not engaged in the research. Authorizes publication of aggregate statistics that do not disclose individual identities. Authorizes the Maryland Judiciary to seek injunctions against unauthorized disclosures or agreement violations.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary
qa_results.stakeholders: academic and policy researchers affiliated with institutions of higher education; institutions of higher education; respondents and petitioners in extreme risk protective order proceedings
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Judiciary, supported by the Administrative Office of the Courts, is tasked with executing required confidentiality and data-handling agreements with institutions of higher education whose researchers review extreme risk protective order records, and is authorized to seek injunctions for violations of those agreements.

Researchers affiliated with USM member institutions conducting academic or policy research are authorized to review confidential ERPO court records upon entering into formal custody and handling agreements with the Maryland Judiciary.

Researchers affiliated with Morgan State University conducting academic or policy research are eligible under the bill to access confidential ERPO records subject to entering into data handling agreements with the Maryland Judiciary.

Researchers affiliated with St. Mary's College of Maryland conducting academic or policy research are eligible under the bill to access confidential ERPO records subject to data handling agreements with the Maryland Judiciary.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands statewide the authority of local jurisdictions and transit agencies to use automated bus lane monitoring systems. Prohibits a person from driving, standing, or parking an unauthorized motor vehicle in a dedicated bus lane. Permits certain vehicles in bus lanes, including emergency vehicles, transit vehicles, school buses, and bicycles. Establishes a maximum civil penalty of $75 for violations recorded by bus lane monitoring systems. Creates the Workgroup on Curb Space Management to recommend curb space policies and obstruction enforcement strategies.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Transportation; District Court of Maryland; Motor Vehicle Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: motor vehicle drivers and registered owners in Maryland; transit bus passengers; local law enforcement and parking enforcement agencies; Maryland Transit Administration; Washington Metropolitan Area Transit Authority
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $17,298 in FY 2025 only for District Court computer reprogramming. State general fund revenues and Transportation Trust Fund revenues increase minimally. Local government fine revenues increase, potentially significantly, offset by monitoring system implementation and administrative expenditures, with net proceeds dedicated to public safety.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Transit Administration (MTA) is explicitly authorized under the bill as an agency that may operate bus lane monitoring systems, operates mass transit buses in dedicated bus lanes, and is designated to have a representative on the Workgroup on Curb Space Management.

The Maryland Department of Transportation (MDOT) is required to provide staff for the newly created Workgroup on Curb Space Management and serves as the umbrella department for modal administrations involved in the bill, including MTA and MVA.

The District Court of Maryland is tasked with prescribing a uniform citation form, adopting procedures for citation trials and collections, and adjudicating contested citations, incurring fiscal costs for judicial IT reprogramming in FY 2025.

The MVA is authorized to refuse the registration or reregistration of vehicles with unpaid, uncontested bus lane citations and may collect administrative flag fees from vehicle owners resolving unpaid penalties.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates the Workgroup on Curb Space Management, a temporary advisory body tasked with studying curb space regulations, enforcement of dedicated bus lanes, and public education strategies before reporting recommendations to the Governor and General Assembly.
The Governor is responsible for appointing the members of the Workgroup on Curb Space Management, designating the Workgroup chair, and receiving its final report by July 1, 2025.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes operating standards and data privacy requirements for assisted living referrers in the State. Requires referrers to maintain general liability insurance and require employee criminal history records checks. Mandates referrers provide service descriptions and written financial agreements to clients or their representatives. Prohibits referrers from requesting referral fees from programs more than two years after providing a referral. Restricts the disclosure of medical records and sale of personal data without informed consent. Directs the Office of Health Care Quality to maintain a database of licensed assisted living programs.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of Health Care Quality; Office of the Attorney General
qa_results.stakeholders: assisted living referrers, licensed assisted living programs, and individuals seeking assisted living referrals and their representatives
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State operational requirements can be handled with existing budgeted resources, with no effect on revenues. Local governments are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the Office of Health Care Quality (OHCQ), a regulatory unit within the Maryland Department of Health, with registering assisted living referrers and maintaining a user-friendly database of licensed assisted living programs.
The bill explicitly authorizes the Office of the Attorney General to investigate whether an assisted living referrer has violated the subtitle's provisions and seek appropriate legal relief.

The bill establishes consumer protection, privacy, and background check requirements for referrers directing individuals to assisted living programs, aligning closely with the Department of Aging's mission regarding long-term care advocacy and the welfare of older adults.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Climate Technology Founder's Fund within the Maryland Clean Energy Center to support climate technology start-ups. Requires recipients of fund financial assistance to provide matching funds equal to the awarded amount. Directs the Maryland Energy Administration to transfer at least $1,200,000 annually from the Strategic Energy Investment Fund through fiscal 2028. Requires at least 40% of awarded funds for equity investments in minority, women-owned, and veteran-owned businesses. Allocates 40% of Maryland Energy Innovation Institute seed grant funding to start-ups from minority serving institutions. Repeals prior Strategic Energy Investment Fund distributions to the Small, Minority, and Women-Owned Businesses Account and apprenticeship programs.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Clean Energy Center; Maryland Energy Administration
qa_results.stakeholders: Clean energy start-up companies, including small, minority, women-owned, and veteran-owned businesses, and minority serving institutions
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Strategic Energy Investment Fund special fund expenditures increase by $1.2 million annually from fiscal 2025 through 2028, with corresponding increases in nonbudgeted revenues and expenditures for the Climate Technology Founder's Fund.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes and requires the Maryland Clean Energy Center (MCEC) to administer the Climate Technology Founder's Fund, appoint an oversight committee, provide financing to early-stage climate tech companies, and report annually on outcomes.

The bill requires MEA to transfer at least $1.2 million annually from the Strategic Energy Investment Fund (SEIF) to the new Climate Technology Founder's Fund from FY 2025 through FY 2028, while repealing previous mandated SEIF distributions to other programs.

The bill alters provisions governing Commerce's Small, Minority, and Women-Owned Businesses Account by repealing its dedicated SEIF distribution and authorizing the transfer of up to $2.2 million from this account to the new fund.
The bill repeals an existing $8.0 million SEIF funding distribution for clean energy apprenticeship and workforce development programs under the Department of Labor's EARN program.
The fund allocates up to $2.0 million for seed grants through the Maryland Energy Innovation Institute (MEII), which is housed at the University of Maryland, College Park.
The bill authorizes the Governor to transfer up to $2.2 million from the Small, Minority, and Women-Owned Businesses Account to the new fund and mandates an annual report to the Governor.
The bill amends State Finance and Procurement Section 6-226 to exempt the Climate Technology Founder's Fund from the requirement that interest earnings accrue to the General Fund.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires Carroll County Class B and Class D alcoholic beverages licensees or designated supervisory employees to hold alcohol awareness certification. Mandates that a certified individual remain present on the licensed premises whenever alcoholic beverages may be sold. Requires at least one individual listed on the license to maintain current certification while listed. Imposes a $100 fine for a first violation. Authorizes a fine up to $500, license suspension, license revocation, or both for subsequent offenses.
qa_results.responsible_party: Carroll County Board of License Commissioners
qa_results.stakeholders: Class B and Class D alcoholic beverages license holders and designated supervisory employees in Carroll County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No effect on State operations or finances. Carroll County can handle enforcement with existing resources, and county revenues are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland regulates the state's alcohol industry and oversees state standards for alcoholic beverage regulation and awareness programs, although this bill applies specifically to local retail license holders in Carroll County with no direct state fiscal impact.

qa_results.bill_summary: Amends prior authorizations of State debt enacted between 2019 and 2023. Alters authorized uses, project locations, and recipient names for multiple capital grants. Extends expenditure and encumbrance deadlines for several specified projects to June 1, 2031. Removes matching fund requirements for designated local recreational initiatives. Reallocates grant funds among new and existing capital projects across Maryland.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of Public Works; Department of Natural Resources; Department of General Services
qa_results.stakeholders: State capital grant recipients, including local governments, community organizations, and nonprofit entities across Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State grant conditions and deadlines are modified without materially affecting State finances. There is no local fiscal impact unless the grantee is a local government.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends prior capital budget authorizations under the Department of Natural Resources' Capital Grants and Loans Administration (KA05), altering the terms, allocations, and allowable uses for Local Parks and Playgrounds Infrastructure funding.
The bill alters prior capital authorizations to designate the Maryland Stadium Authority as the new grantee for Phase 2 design, surveys, and analysis related to the Fort to 400 Commission.
The bill transfers grant funding previously authorized to the Historic St. Mary's City Fort to 400 Commission to the Maryland Stadium Authority.
The Board of Public Works is responsible for the oversight, approval, and matching fund certification of state debt authorizations and capital grant agreements amended by this omnibus bill.
DGS administers state capital grants and legislative bond initiatives on behalf of the Board of Public Works, directly implementing changes to grant agreements, recipients, and project scopes.
DBM oversees the state's capital budget planning and monitors prior debt authorizations and spend rates affected by this legislation.

The bill specifically alters a grant requirement by exempting a grantee (Johnston Square) from the Maryland Historical Trust's perpetual easement requirement, which falls under the Department of Planning.

qa_results.bill_summary: Codifies the Private Hospital Grant Program to recommend annual State budget funding for capital projects at private hospitals. Requires the Maryland Hospital Association to establish a review committee to develop application processes and recommend projects. Requires the review committee to consult with the Department of Budget and Management and the Department of Legislative Services. Requires the Maryland Hospital Association to submit project recommendations to the Governor and the Secretary of Budget and Management. Authorizes the Governor to include an appropriation of $20,000,000 for the program beginning in fiscal year 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Hospital Association; Department of Budget and Management; Department of Legislative Services
qa_results.stakeholders: private hospitals in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No fiscal effect in fiscal 2025. Discretionary General Obligation bond expenditures may increase by $12.0 million annually beginning in fiscal 2026 if the Governor funds the program at the authorized $20.0 million level, redirecting bond capacity from other capital projects without altering total capital spending. The Department of Budget and Management and the Department of Legislative Services can provide required consultations using existing budgeted resources. No effect on local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly requires the Private Hospital Grant Program review committee to consult with DBM in establishing the funding request process, developing rejection criteria, and making project recommendations. Furthermore, recommendations must be submitted directly to the Secretary of Budget and Management, and the funding authorization impacts DBM's preparation of the annual state operating and capital budgets.

The bill establishes that the program's review committee must submit final funding recommendations directly to the Governor, and authorizes the Governor to include up to $20,000,000 annually for the program in either the capital or operating budget bill beginning in fiscal year 2026.

The legislation amends the Health - General Article governing hospitals and healthcare facilities within Maryland. While day-to-day administration involves MHA and DBM, capital funding allocations for private hospitals fall within MDH's broader statutory domain and healthcare infrastructure policy.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Reproductive Health Care Clinic Security Grant Program in the Maryland Department of Health. Requires the Secretary of Health to administer the program and establish application procedures and qualification criteria. Assists reproductive health care clinics with costs associated with physical and operational security improvements. Authorizes the Governor to include an appropriation of $500,000 for the program in the fiscal 2026 budget. Limits administrative expenses to up to 5% of appropriated program funds. Prohibits the department from disclosing personal applicant information or grant details that compromise recipient safety.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: reproductive health care clinics providing legally protected health care in Maryland, clinic staff, and patients
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $28,732 in FY 2025 for contractual staffing to establish the program and by $500,000 in FY 2026 for discretionary grant funding and administrative expenses. Revenues and local government finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Reproductive Health Care Clinic Security Grant Program within the Maryland Department of Health, tasking the Secretary of Health with administering the program, developing application and qualification criteria, and managing grant awards.
The bill authorizes the Governor to include a discretionary appropriation of up to $500,000 for the program in the annual budget bill for fiscal year 2026.

DBM oversees the development of the executive budget, which may incorporate the authorized $500,000 discretionary appropriation in fiscal year 2026, and manages personnel classifications for the contractual staff required to administer the program.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The agency was the originally designated administrator in the bill prior to amendments transferring responsibility to the Department of Health, and was consulted as an information source during the fiscal analysis.

qa_results.bill_summary: Renames the Major Information Technology Development Project Fund to the Information Technology Investment Fund. Increases the baseline cost threshold for major information technology development projects from $1,000,000 to $5,000,000. Requires at least 20% of fund appropriations each fiscal year to be set aside for expedited projects. Directs the Board of Public Works to expedite placement and approval of modernization contracts. Alters the name, duties, and membership of the Modernize Maryland Commission. Requires the Department of Information Technology to inventory legacy systems and develop a State Modernization Plan.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Information Technology; Department of General Services; Board of Public Works; Modernize Maryland Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: units of State government; information technology contractors and vendors; small and minority business enterprises; Maryland residents
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general and special fund expenditures increase by $2.1 million in FY 2025 for two positions, operating expenses, and consultant studies for legacy systems and IT procurement. Future years reflect ongoing personnel expenses and consultant costs of $200,000 every other year beginning in FY 2026. A mandated appropriation begins in FY 2026 to fund two positions in the Department of Information Technology. Local government finances are not directly affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary implementing agency, DoIT's oversight responsibilities are centralized and significantly expanded. The bill alters the Secretary's duties, renames and restructures the Major IT Development Project Fund into the Information Technology Investment Fund, requires legacy system assessments and a State Modernization Plan, and provides additional staff positions.

DGS is directly mandated to hire a consultant to evaluate the State's procurement process for IT modernization projects and recommend improvements, carrying an estimated fiscal impact of $1.0 million in FY 2025.
The bill mandates that contracts to modernize IT systems or proceed with expedited projects must be expedited for approval and placed on the Board of Public Works agenda as soon as practicable.

The Comptroller is required to account for the Information Technology Investment Fund and must be consulted by DoIT on recommendations to transition State agencies off the Annapolis Data Center mainframes consistent with the Comptroller's sunset goal.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill renames the Modernize Maryland Oversight Commission to the Modernize Maryland Commission and alters its membership, terms, purpose, and reporting duties regarding legacy systems and modernization best practices.

The Secretary of Budget and Management advises on major IT development projects and receives recommendations from the Secretary of Information Technology to withhold project funds if agencies fail to report or encounter implementation issues.
The State Treasurer is designated to hold the Information Technology Investment Fund separately and manage the investment and reinvestment of money within the fund.

The Governor appoints members to the Modernize Maryland Commission, receives required reports and modernization strategies, and is required to submit budget appropriations, set-asides, and positions for IT modernization.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Language Assistance Services Pilot Program in the Behavioral Health Administration. Authorizes competitive grants to local behavioral health authorities to reimburse behavioral health providers for language assistance services. Applies to interpretation and translation services for children with limited English proficiency and their parents or legal guardians. Requires participating providers to submit a current, written language access plan with each reimbursement request. Mandates an annual State appropriation of $120,000 in fiscal years 2025 and 2026 to fund grant awards.
qa_results.responsible_party: Behavioral Health Administration; Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: children with limited English proficiency, parents and legal guardians making health care decisions for those children, local behavioral health authorities, and licensed and accredited behavioral health providers
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by an estimated $201,100 in FY 2025, $190,800 in FY 2026, and $36,900 in FY 2027 to cover $120,000 in annual grant funding and 1.0 contractual position. Local revenues and expenditures increase for local behavioral health authorities receiving grant awards and reimbursing providers.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Language Assistance Services Pilot Program within the Behavioral Health Administration (BHA), a division of the Maryland Department of Health. MDH is responsible for administering the program, adopting regulations, awarding competitive grants to local behavioral health authorities, hiring staff, and submitting annual implementation reports.

The bill mandates that the Governor include an appropriation of $120,000 in the annual budget bill for fiscal years 2025 and 2026 to fund the pilot program and requires annual implementation reports to be submitted to the Governor.

DBM is responsible for state budget preparation and personnel administration, and this legislation mandates state budget appropriations for the program as well as state general fund expenditures for contractual personnel.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Governor to make recess appointments to the State Board of Elections and the Accountability and Implementation Board. Requires the Governor to submit nominations within 40 days of legislative session commencing for terms ending during recess. Allows later nominations submitted before sine die adjournment only if the Senate consents to examine the nominee. Prohibits an executive officer from continuing to serve more than four years after the officer's term ends. Clarifies reappointment, acting capacity, and voting restrictions for rejected nominees and unconfirmed recess appointees.
qa_results.responsible_party: Office of the Governor; Maryland Senate
qa_results.stakeholders: gubernatorial nominees and appointees to Maryland offices requiring Senate confirmation, incumbent executive officers, and members of State boards and commissions
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No direct state or local fiscal impact, as the bill largely clarifies existing constitutional and statutory requirements. The Governor's Office anticipates operational costs of approximately $270,745 in fiscal 2025 for two positions and a tracking system to achieve compliance.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly governs the Governor's constitutional and statutory authority and procedures for making executive appointments requiring Senate advice and consent, imposing strict nomination deadlines and limits on holdover and acting service, which results in operational and staffing impacts.

Housed within the Executive Department, the Office of Appointments manages the vetting and nomination process for over 600 boards and commissions. The fiscal note highlights significant operational impacts on this office to comply with nomination deadlines, including the need for additional personnel and a new tracking system.

The bill explicitly includes a specific exception authorizing the Governor to appoint members to the State Board of Elections during Senate recess regardless of whether the term of office ends during the upcoming recess.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Senate-confirmed positions across various state boards and commissions are directly subject to the bill's four-year holdover service cap, acting capacity restrictions, and rules invalidating votes and quorum counts for individuals serving in violation of these provisions.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires an alcoholic beverages retailer in Baltimore County to obtain written approval from the Board of License Commissioners. Mandates this approval before applying to the Executive Director of the Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission for a permit. Authorizes a permit holder to establish a warehouse to store alcoholic beverages titled to the holder. Maintains the individual storage permit fee of $50. Takes effect July 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore County; Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: alcoholic beverages retailers in Baltimore County
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state fiscal effect. Baltimore County can implement the bill with existing budgetary resources, and local revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill concerns requirements for obtaining individual storage permits for alcoholic beverages. While the permit application is submitted to the Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission, the Comptroller's office is charged with broad regulatory and revenue administration over the alcohol industry.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires each State unit to submit an annual procurement forecast for contracts over $100,000 to the Office by June 30. Mandates that units submit a prior-year reconciliation by August 15 and report forecast changes within 15 days. Directs the Office of Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs to publish all submitted forecast information online. Requires the Office to consult with primary procurement units to identify contracting opportunities and assist small businesses with bidding. Creates a compliance officer position within the Office to carry out these requirements.
qa_results.responsible_party: Governor's Office of Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs
qa_results.stakeholders: Small businesses seeking State contracts and State procurement units
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $77,900 in FY 2025 for one new compliance officer position within the Governor's Office of Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs, growing to $105,500 by FY 2029. Other State procurement units can fulfill reporting requirements using existing resources. Revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOSBA is the primary implementing agency responsible for consulting with primary procurement units, developing outreach and assistance programs for small businesses, receiving and publishing annual procurement forecasts and reconciliations, and receives a new staff position (compliance officer) under the bill.

As a designated primary procurement unit and the state's central procurement agency, DGS must consult with GOSBA to identify small business opportunities, collaborate on the outreach program, and submit procurement forecasts and annual reconciliations.

As a designated primary procurement unit, MDOT must consult with GOSBA to identify small business opportunities and develop outreach initiatives, as well as submit annual procurement forecasts and reconciliations for contracts over $100,000.

The State Treasurer is designated by statute as a primary procurement unit required to consult with GOSBA to identify small business contracting opportunities and develop outreach programs, in addition to submitting procurement forecasts.

USM is a designated primary procurement unit required to consult with GOSBA on small business contracting opportunities and outreach programs, and must submit annual procurement forecasts and reconciliations.

Morgan State University is a designated primary procurement unit required to consult with GOSBA regarding small business contracting opportunities and submit annual procurement forecasts and reconciliations.
St. Mary's College of Maryland is an independent primary procurement unit required to consult with GOSBA on small business contracting and submit annual procurement forecasts and reconciliations.

The Maryland Port Commission is statutorily designated as a primary procurement unit and oversees the Maryland Port Administration, which conducts procurements subject to the forecast and consultation requirements.
The Board of Public Works exercises overarching authority over state procurement regulations and oversees the primary procurement units impacted by this legislation.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the Circuit Administrative Judge of the Sixth Circuit to establish a Truancy Reduction Pilot Program in Frederick County. Applies the program only to the extent funds are provided in the annual State budget. Authorizes the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of Maryland to accept gifts or grants to implement the program. Takes effect October 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Circuit Administrative Judge of the Sixth Circuit; Supreme Court of Maryland; Maryland Judiciary
qa_results.stakeholders: truant students and their parents or guardians in Frederick County; Frederick County Public Schools; Frederick County juvenile court
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $155,000 annually beginning in fiscal 2025 for Judiciary reimbursable grant funding. Frederick County grant revenues and corresponding expenditures increase by $155,000 annually. The Office of the Public Defender may experience an operational workload increase.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the Judiciary by authorizing the Circuit Administrative Judge of the Sixth Circuit to establish a Truancy Reduction Pilot Program in Frederick County. The Administrative Office of the Courts (through the Office of Problem-Solving Courts) provides administrative oversight and $155,000 in annual reimbursable grants to support the program.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The creation of a truancy reduction program in Frederick County may have an operational impact on the Office of the Public Defender due to increased caseloads involving representation of juveniles and charges brought against parents in truancy and related delinquency matters.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes direct delivery permits authorizing licensed Maryland breweries, wineries, and distilleries to deliver alcohol directly to adult consumers. Limits annual direct deliveries per address to 18 cases of wine, 3,456 ounces of beer, or 24 liquor bottles. Requires delivery drivers to be at least 18 years old and certified in alcohol awareness. Repeals limits on alcoholic beverages an individual may purchase for off-premises consumption when visiting licensed manufacturers. Mandates annual production and sales reporting by licensed distilleries, wineries, and breweries to the Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission.
qa_results.responsible_party: Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission; Comptroller of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: Licensed Maryland breweries, wineries, and distilleries; adult consumers of alcoholic beverages in Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues increase by at least $8,400 annually beginning in fiscal 2025 from $200 permit and renewal fees. The Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission can handle monitoring and enforcement with existing budgeted resources. Local operations and finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires direct alcoholic beverage delivery and shipping permit holders to file quarterly tax returns with the Comptroller, pay quarterly sales and excise taxes directly to the Comptroller, provide copies of permits to the agency, and allow the Comptroller to perform audits of permit holder records.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits licensed retailers and vape shop vendors from displaying cigarettes, other tobacco products, or electronic smoking devices unless located behind a counter. Requires retailers to verify through government-issued photo identification that purchasers are at least 21 years old. Repeals exceptions that allowed sales of tobacco products and electronic smoking devices to active-duty military members under age 21. Increases county retail license fees for cigarettes and electronic smoking devices to $300 to fund enforcement. Mandates that the Maryland Department of Health or its designee conduct annual unannounced inspections of licensed retailers. Increases penalties for distributing tobacco products to underage individuals and authorizes court-ordered license suspensions.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health; Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: licensed retailers of cigarettes, other tobacco products, and electronic smoking devices; vape shop vendors; individuals under age 21; local health departments
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues and expenditures increase by $1.2 million in FY 2025 and $1.6 million annually thereafter from increased license fees dedicated to enforcement. General fund expenditures increase by $44,761 in FY 2025 for Judiciary computer programming. General fund revenues may increase by $24,000 in FY 2025 and $32,000 annually from higher fines. Local health departments receive approximately $1.0 million in FY 2025 and $1.5 million annually in MDH grants to conduct inspections, while Montgomery County revenues increase by $82,688 in FY 2025 and $110,250 annually from retained license fees.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDH is a primary implementing agency under the bill. It is mandated to conduct annual unannounced compliance inspections (and follow-up inspections) of licensed tobacco and electronic smoking device retailers, authorized to issue civil citations, receives $275 of each license fee collected to fund enforcement and local health department grants (totaling over $1.2M to $1.6M annually), and must collaborate on a comprehensive study and report.

Circuit court clerks collect and distribute the revised license fees, and the District Court and circuit courts adjudicate civil citations and criminal violations under the bill. Courts are required to order license suspensions or revocations upon certain convictions, and the fiscal note reflects a direct fiscal impact of $44,761 in FY 2025 for Judicial computer programming modifications.

The bill explicitly requires the Comptroller to coordinate with the Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission, MDH, and MSDE to submit a report on tobacco and electronic smoking device retailers, licensing density, and youth impacts. The agency also administers state sales and use taxes, which may be affected by changes in retail sales.

The bill statutorily requires the State Department of Education (MSDE) to collaborate with the Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission, MDH, and the Comptroller on an evaluation and legislative report regarding tobacco retail density near schools and youth tobacco and vaping usage.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expresses legislative intent that the Department of Information Technology evaluate artificial intelligence capabilities. Focuses the evaluation on creating a statewide virtual 3–1–1 portal. Envisions the portal providing Maryland residents nonemergency government information and services. Urges the Department to prioritize portal creation if deemed feasible. Takes effect July 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Information Technology
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland residents seeking nonemergency government information and services
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures may increase if the Department of Information Technology implements a statewide virtual 3–1–1 portal, but any potential implementation costs are currently indeterminate. The initial feasibility evaluation is conducted using existing departmental resources. Local government finances have no direct impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly expresses the intent of the General Assembly for the Department of Information Technology (DoIT) to evaluate the potential of artificial intelligence to create a statewide virtual 3-1-1 portal for nonemergency government information and services, and to prioritize its development if determined feasible.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes local school systems to use Safe Schools Fund grants for school security employees. Clarifies that eligible school security employees provide school safety services and are not school resource officers. Maintains existing annual grant funding requirements and distribution formulas under the Maryland Safe to Learn Act. Takes effect July 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: School Safety Subcabinet; Maryland Center for School Safety
qa_results.stakeholders: Local school systems, public school security employees, and Maryland public school students and staff
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No State or local fiscal impact; expanding the authorized uses of the Safe Schools Fund has no effect on total revenues or expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Center for School Safety (MCSS) provides staff to the School Safety Subcabinet, which administers the Safe Schools Fund, and is responsible for statewide school safety coordination, reporting, and guidance regarding school resource officers and security personnel.

The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) oversees public education and local school systems, houses the Maryland Center for School Safety as an independent unit, and the State Superintendent of Schools chairs the School Safety Subcabinet which administers the Safe Schools Fund.

qa_results.bill_summary: Increases the annual motor vehicle registration emergency medical system surcharge from $17 to $40. Allocates at least $9 of each surcharge to the R Adams Cowley Shock Trauma Center. Directs $6.50 of the surcharge and at least 20% of specified impaired driving fines to trauma physician services. Expands Maryland Trauma Physician Services Fund eligibility to cover licensed trauma health care practitioners. Increases maximum criminal fines for specified driving while impaired offenses by $200 for first and second offenses. Requires the Governor to appropriate at least $16,500,000 annually to the Amoss Fund beginning in fiscal year 2026.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Health Care Commission; Health Services Cost Review Commission; Maryland Department of Transportation; Comptroller; Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland motor vehicle owners, trauma physicians and trauma health care practitioners, trauma centers and specialty referral centers, local fire and rescue organizations, and individuals convicted of impaired driving offenses.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues increase by approximately $104.8 million annually beginning in FY 2025 from the vehicle surcharge increase, distributed to MEMSOF, Shock Trauma, and MTPSF. Special fund expenditures increase by $3.4 million in FY 2025 and $4.9 million annually thereafter for transaction processing fees, grants, and mandated Amoss Fund funding. General fund and local fine revenues decrease minimally due to diverting at least 20% of impaired driving fines to MTPSF.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MHCC is a primary administering agency for the Maryland Trauma Physician Services Fund (MTPSF). The bill expands the fund's purpose, alters reimbursement methodologies and parameters for trauma physicians and practitioners, requires annual pediatric trauma grants, and expands annual reporting duties.

HSCRC jointly administers the Maryland Trauma Physician Services Fund with MHCC, collaborates on reimbursement methodologies and grant processes, and must report on hospital global budget costs related to trauma services.

MVA is responsible for collecting the motor vehicle registration emergency medical system surcharge, which is increased under the bill from $17 to $40 per vehicle across multiple vehicle classifications.

MDOT is the parent department of the MVA and is fiscally impacted; the Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) incurs an estimated $2.2 million annually in credit card processing fees associated with the increased surcharge collections.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MIEMSS receives core funding from MEMSOF (which receives significant additional revenue under the bill), designates trauma centers and protocols that govern MTPSF disbursements, and consults on trauma center equipment grant awards.

The Comptroller statutorily administers the Maryland Emergency Medical System Operations Fund (MEMSOF), including accounting for all transactions and performing year-end reconciliations for the tens of millions in newly allocated surcharge revenue.
MDEM administers the Senator William H. Amoss Fire, Rescue, and Ambulance Fund, which receives a mandated annual budget appropriation of at least $16.5 million beginning in FY 2026.
