The medically oriented aviation functions of the MSP Aviation Command are a primary statutory recipient of funding from MEMSOF, which receives up to $45.6 million annually in additional surcharge revenues under the bill.

The state court system adjudicates impaired driving offenses for which fines are increased, requires one-time computer reprogramming costs ($18,543 in FY 2025), and must divert at least 20% of collected fines to MTPSF.
MDH receives transfers from MTPSF to fully cover the State's share of undercompensated care costs for Medicaid enrollees treated in trauma centers, and serves as the umbrella department housing MHCC.

The bill mandates that the Governor allocate at least $9.00 of each annual vehicle registration surcharge to the Shock Trauma Center and include a mandatory appropriation of at least $16.5 million in the annual state budget for the Amoss Fund beginning in FY 2026.
DBM is responsible for state budget preparation and execution, and must operationalize the Governor's mandated annual appropriation of at least $16.5 million to the Amoss Fund starting in FY 2026.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes the Workgroup on Home Detention Monitoring to study pretrial home detention systems. Requires the workgroup to examine the costs and availability of publicly and privately provided monitoring systems. Directs the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services to provide staff for the workgroup. Requires the workgroup to adopt a member code of conduct at its first meeting. Mandates an annual report of findings and recommendations to the General Assembly by December 31 each year.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services; Workgroup on Home Detention Monitoring
qa_results.stakeholders: Pretrial defendants subject to home detention, private home detention monitoring agencies, local detention centers, and county pretrial release programs
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures for Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services staffing and workgroup member expense reimbursements are minimal and absorbable within existing budgeted resources. Local government finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates the Secretary of Public Safety and Correctional Services as a member of the Workgroup and requires the Department to provide staff support and administrative resources for the Workgroup.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly designates the Public Defender of Maryland (or the Public Defender's designee) as a member of the Workgroup on Home Detention Monitoring.
The bill requires the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of Maryland to appoint a representative of the Judiciary to serve as a member of the Workgroup.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill formally creates and establishes the Workgroup on Home Detention Monitoring to study and make recommendations regarding pretrial home detention systems.
The bill authorizes the Governor to appoint multiple members to the Workgroup representing law enforcement, detention centers, pretrial release programs, and private monitoring agencies.
The office assists the Governor in vetting and appointing qualified individuals to serve on the newly established Workgroup.

qa_results.bill_summary: Prohibits an incarcerated individual serving a sentence for first-degree rape from earning diminution credits to reduce confinement. Applies this prohibition to offenses that occur on or after October 1, 2024. Bars diminution deductions for any presentence or postsentence confinement in local correctional facilities. Prohibits diminution deductions for individuals committed to the custody of the Commissioner of Correction. Clarifies that an individual cannot be required to serve longer than the authorized statutory maximum sentence.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
qa_results.stakeholders: Individuals convicted of first-degree rape committed on or after October 1, 2024, victims of sexual offenses, and State and local correctional facilities.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No material impact on State finances over the initial five-year period. In the future, State general fund incarceration expenditures increase, potentially significantly over time, as individuals serve longer sentences. Local correctional finances are not expected to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS is the primary implementing agency responsible for calculating and administering diminution credits for incarcerated individuals across State correctional facilities. The bill directly impacts their operations and will increase confinement expenditures as offenders convicted of first-degree rape serve longer sentences without the ability to earn credits.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: OPD represents indigent defendants in criminal proceedings, including first-degree rape cases. The elimination of diminution credits impacts defense strategy, client counseling, and plea bargaining considerations regarding the actual time a defendant will serve.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires public buildings to co-locate up to two doses of naloxone with each automated external defibrillator. Applies to publicly funded transit accommodations, public gathering or amusement areas, and secondary or higher education facilities. Directs the State Emergency Medical Services Board and the Maryland Department of Health to jointly adopt implementation regulations. Grants civil liability immunity to public building operators and individuals who administer co-located naloxone during suspected overdoses. Authorizes the use of the Opioid Restitution Fund to finance the co-location initiative.
qa_results.responsible_party: State Emergency Medical Services Board; Maryland Department of Health
qa_results.stakeholders: Owners and operators of public buildings, secondary schools, higher education institutions, public transit facilities, recreation centers, emergency medical responders, and individuals at risk of opioid overdose
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund expenditures from the Opioid Restitution Fund increase by at least $74,100 in FY 2025 and ongoing for personnel, plus additional unquantified costs for naloxone doses, storage packaging, and information technology updates. Local government expenditures are absorbable within existing resources. State and local revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MIEMSS operates the Public Access Automated External Defibrillator (AED) Program on behalf of the EMS Board and is directly tasked with developing, implementing, and adopting joint regulations for the AED and naloxone co-location initiative, as well as upgrading tracking systems.

MDH is statutorily required to collaborate with the EMS Board to develop and implement the initiative, jointly adopt regulations, coordinate with its Overdose Response Program, and utilize Opioid Restitution Fund resources.
The bill applies to public secondary schools under its definition of 'public building', requiring public secondary education facilities to co-locate naloxone with on-site AEDs.

Public mass transportation accommodations supported by public funds, such as transit stations and passenger terminals operated under MDOT, fall under the definition of public buildings required to co-locate naloxone with AEDs.

DNR manages public parks and recreation facilities, which are defined as public buildings under the bill and required to co-locate naloxone with any AEDs placed in public gathering or amusement areas.
USM institutions are public higher education facilities covered under the bill's definition of 'public building' and must comply with requirements to co-locate naloxone with AEDs on their campuses.
As a public higher education institution, Morgan State University facilities are defined as public buildings and must co-locate naloxone with AEDs on campus.
As an independent public higher education institution, St. Mary's College facilities are subject to the bill's requirements to co-locate naloxone with AEDs placed on campus.
MSD operates secondary education facilities supported by public funds and is subject to the co-location mandate for AEDs placed in its school buildings.
The bill references protocols established by the Maryland State Police Medical Director regarding civil immunity for individuals administering approved overdose treatments.

qa_results.bill_summary: Expands eligibility for the Maryland Police Officers and Probation Agents Scholarship Program to include community colleges in the State. Authorizes scholarship recipients to use tuition assistance awards at Maryland community colleges in addition to public senior higher education institutions. Supports students pursuing degree programs that further their intent to become police officers or probation agents after graduation. Extends scholarship benefits to current police officers and probation agents seeking degrees that advance their careers. Takes effect immediately as an emergency measure.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Higher Education Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Current police officers and probation agents, prospective police officers and probation agents, and Maryland community colleges
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures do not change, as the expansion of eligibility can be accommodated within the existing $5.0 million general fund appropriation. Local community college revenues and expenditures are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MHEC is the primary implementing agency for the Maryland Police Officers and Probation Agents Scholarship Program and the Office of Student Financial Assistance, responsible for administering the program and incorporating community colleges into the eligible institutions.

As the state's coordinating and financial aid regulatory body, the commission administers the Maryland Police Officers and Probation Agents Scholarship Program, which this bill alters by expanding eligible institutions to include community colleges.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS employs the state's probation agents within the Division of Parole and Probation. The bill expands educational scholarship opportunities for current and prospective probation agents to include community colleges.
The bill expands tuition assistance eligibility for current police officers and individuals preparing to become police officers to attend community colleges under the scholarship program.

qa_results.bill_summary: Alters the definition of hospital outpatient facility fees and the required contents of written disclosures provided to patients. Requires hospitals to disclose both a fee range and a specific fee estimate when outpatient facility fees are unknown. Requires the Maryland Health Services Cost Review Commission to study hospital outpatient facility fees in consultation with designated stakeholders. Mandates a preliminary report by December 1, 2024, and a final report by December 1, 2025. Requires the Commission to convene a workgroup on expanding facility fee notice requirements to all outpatient services.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Health Services Cost Review Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Patients receiving outpatient medical services, Maryland hospitals, out-of-state hospitals operating outpatient facilities in Maryland, physicians and nonphysician clinicians, commercial health insurers, and employer groups.
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Maryland Health Services Cost Review Commission special fund expenditures increase by $75,000 in FY 2025 and $75,000 in FY 2026 for contractual services to conduct the study and complete required reports. Revenues are unaffected. Local governments are not impacted.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HSCRC is the primary implementing agency tasked with conducting an extensive study and submitting reports on hospital outpatient facility fees, convening an advisory workgroup, receiving annual lists of outpatient services, and handling unresolved consumer complaints.

The bill was requested by the Office of the Attorney General. Its Health Education and Advocacy Unit (HEAU) is explicitly listed on the required patient notice form to mediate facility fee disputes, receives annual reporting from HSCRC, and is mandated to participate in the study and workgroup.

HSCRC is an independent commission within MDH. In addition, the bill specifically requires MDH to be consulted in the study on hospital facility fees and to participate as a member of the outpatient facility fee notice workgroup.

MIA is statutorily designated to receive annual lists of hospital-based, rate-regulated outpatient services from HSCRC and is required to be consulted by HSCRC during the study on outpatient facility fees.

qa_results.bill_summary: Corrects technical errors, omissions, obsolete cross-references, and outdated terminology across multiple articles of the Annotated Code of Maryland. Authorizes publishers of the Annotated Code to make specified nonsubstantive stylistic and grammatical corrections. Requires Department of Legislative Services approval for code publisher revisions and effectuation of statutory termination provisions. Updates archaic terminology by replacing references to mental retardation with intellectual disability in court and criminal procedure statutes. Takes effect immediately as an emergency measure upon enactment.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Legislative Services; publishers of the Annotated Code of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: legal practitioners, state agencies, Maryland courts, and users of the Annotated Code of Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact, as the bill is technical in nature.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: SB 1106 makes technical corrections to the Courts and Judicial Proceedings Article regarding judicial titles (Justices of the Supreme Court of Maryland), judicial salary commissions, and juvenile court terminology.
The bill updates technical terminology and statutory cross-references involving the accounting and distribution of funds and tax withholding under the Natural Resources Article.

The bill makes nonsubstantive statutory corrections to several sections of the Education Article, including county superintendent selection committees, education funding formulas, and school construction provisions.

The bill makes technical and terminology corrections to the Health - General Article and Health Occupations Article, as well as provisions governing criminal competency commitments and the Office of the Chief Medical Examiner.
The bill updates obsolete statutory cross-references in the Labor and Employment Article regarding the state minimum wage.

SB 1106 makes nonsubstantive drafting, stylistic, and cross-reference corrections to several Natural Resources Article sections covering the Chesapeake and Atlantic Coastal Bays Trust Fund, scenic river advisory boards, vessel registration, and hunting licenses.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill makes minor drafting and stylistic corrections to sections of the Correctional Services Article and Public Safety Article, including references to inmate identification and criminal justice information checks.
The bill updates obsolete departmental administration titles (Water and Science Administration) and corrects cross-references within the Environment Article.
The bill corrects an obsolete cross-reference in the Insurance Article regarding motor vehicle liability coverage for family child care providers.
The bill corrects a tabulation error in Public Safety Article § 5-310 regarding handgun permit revocations and reviews conducted by the Secretary of State Police.
The bill corrects internal cross-references in the State Personnel and Pensions Article.
The bill corrects terminology and statutory references regarding delegated fiduciary duties and the holding and investment of the Chesapeake and Atlantic Coastal Bays 2010 Trust Fund.
The bill updates obsolete federal agency nomenclature (referencing the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs) in Transportation Article § 13-903 concerning vehicle registration fee exemptions.
The bill updates an obsolete cross-reference in State Government Article § 2-1220 regarding performance audits of local alcoholic beverage and cannabis licensing boards.
The bill corrects drafting errors and cross-references in the Public Utilities Article regarding generating station certificate exemptions and offshore wind project pricing schedules.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires commercial fish packers, dealers, and catchers to submit required reports under Department of Natural Resources regulations. Replaces statutory requirements that commercial fishery reports be submitted on department-prescribed forms. Requires individuals holding an angler's license for nontidal waters to submit required reports under department regulations. Requires individuals holding a Chesapeake Bay and coastal sport fishing license to submit required reports under department regulations. Takes effect July 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
qa_results.stakeholders: Commercial fish packers and dealers, licensed commercial fishers, and recreational anglers holding an angler's license or Chesapeake Bay and coastal sport fishing license
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No direct effect on State or local finances. Future costs from expanding electronic reporting would depend on implementation methods and would be addressed during regulatory adoption.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: SB 1118 directly regulates fish and fisheries reporting under the Department of Natural Resources (DNR). It authorizes DNR to adopt regulations specifying how commercial dealers, packers, and harvesters, as well as recreational anglers, must submit required fishery harvest and catch reports.

qa_results.bill_summary: Authorizes the University System of Maryland to issue up to $30,000,000 in academic facilities bonds. Allocates $5,000,000 to finance campuswide building systems and infrastructure improvements at the University of Maryland, College Park. Dedicates $25,000,000 to finance systemwide capital facilities renewal projects across constituent institutions and centers. Establishes that the issued bonds do not constitute a debt or pledge of the State of Maryland. Takes effect June 1, 2024.
qa_results.responsible_party: University System of Maryland
qa_results.stakeholders: University System of Maryland institutions, students, faculty, and staff, particularly at the University of Maryland, College Park
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: State bond revenues and expenditures increase by $30.0 million in FY 2025. Higher education expenditures increase by an estimated $2.5 million annually beginning in FY 2026 for debt service payments over 20 years. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly authorizes the University System of Maryland (USM) to issue, sell, and deliver $30.0 million in academic facilities revenue bonds to finance facility renewal and capital improvement projects across its campuses.

qa_results.bill_summary: Requires the Comptroller to distribute $500,000 annually from abandoned property funds to the Tax Clinics for Low-Income Marylanders Fund. Increases the mandated annual budget appropriation for the CASH Campaign of Maryland to $800,000 starting in fiscal 2026. Requires $150,000 of that appropriation to fund grants for on-demand or mobile tax clinics. Requires those clinics to serve senior populations, rural communities, or under-resourced communities, including new American populations. Requires designated tax clinics to interact with the CASH Campaign of Maryland at least once each year.
qa_results.responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland; Governor
qa_results.stakeholders: Low-income Maryland residents; senior populations; rural communities; under-resourced communities; new American populations; University of Maryland School of Law; University of Baltimore School of Law; Maryland Volunteer Lawyers Service; CASH Campaign of Maryland
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Decreases general fund revenues by $500,000 annually beginning in FY 2025 from redirected unclaimed property funds. Increases special fund revenues and expenditures for the Tax Clinics for Low-Income Marylanders Fund by $500,000 annually, including $333,300 for higher education institutions. Increases general fund expenditures by $300,000 annually beginning in FY 2026 for the CASH Campaign appropriation.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller administers both the abandoned property fund from which $500,000 is distributed annually and the Tax Clinics for Low-Income Marylanders Fund, being responsible for accounting and distributing grant awards.

Two constituent institutions (the University of Maryland School of Law and the University of Baltimore School of Law) receive two-thirds of the fund's annual grant distributions ($333,300) to operate low-income tax clinics and are statutorily required to interact with the CASH Campaign of Maryland annually.
The State Treasurer is statutorily required to hold the Tax Clinics for Low-Income Marylanders Fund separately and manage the investment of the money held in the fund.
The bill mandates that the Governor include an increased appropriation of $800,000 for the CASH Campaign of Maryland in the annual state budget bill beginning in fiscal year 2026.
As the principal budget agency, the Department of Budget and Management is responsible for implementing the statutory budget mandate of $800,000 starting in fiscal year 2026.

qa_results.bill_summary: Repeals the service terminal dates required for eligibility in the Douglas J. J. Peters Veterans of the Afghanistan and Iraq Conflicts Scholarship. Expands eligibility to qualified uniformed service members serving on or after October 24, 2001, in Afghanistan or March 19, 2003, in Iraq. Preserves eligibility for qualifying veterans, active-duty service members, activated reservists, and Maryland National Guard members. Extends scholarship benefits to qualifying children, stepchildren, and spouses of eligible service members. Takes effect immediately as an emergency measure upon enactment.
qa_results.responsible_party: Maryland Higher Education Commission
qa_results.stakeholders: Maryland resident veterans, active-duty armed forces members, activated reservists, and Maryland National Guard members who served in the Afghanistan or Iraq conflicts, as well as their eligible children, stepchildren, and spouses
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. Expanding eligibility does not necessitate additional state spending, as awards remain subject to annual state budget appropriations and can be managed through waiting lists. The Maryland Higher Education Commission can implement administrative changes with existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MHEC directly administers the Douglas J. J. Peters Veterans of the Afghanistan and Iraq Conflicts Scholarship through its Office of Student Financial Assistance and is responsible for adjusting applicant eligibility criteria and managing scholarship awards.
As the state coordinating board administering financial aid, the commission oversees and implements the eligibility changes and application process for this state scholarship program.
DVMF assists Maryland veterans, active-duty military personnel, and their families in identifying and accessing state education benefits and scholarships for which they are eligible.
National Guard members activated for service in Iraq or Afghanistan and their dependents are directly eligible beneficiaries of this expanded scholarship program.
The maximum scholarship award is calculated based on undergraduate tuition and fees at USM institutions, and member universities enroll eligible scholarship recipients.

qa_results.bill_summary: Establishes a Class B–CAEVC (College Athletic Event Venue Concessionaire) beer, wine, and liquor license in Prince George’s County. Authorizes the Board of License Commissioners for Prince George’s County to issue the license to qualifying athletic venue concessionaires. Authorizes license holders to sell beer, wine, and liquor for on-premises consumption in designated athletic event areas. Requires a separate license for each venue in which the concessionaire operates. Sets an annual license fee of $3,500 payable on or before May 1.
qa_results.responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Prince George's County
qa_results.stakeholders: athletic event venue concessionaires at the University of Maryland, College Park and Bowie State University, and event attendees
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: Prince George's County license fee revenues increase by approximately $10,500 annually beginning in fiscal 2025 based on an estimated issuance of three licenses. Additional local enforcement activity can be absorbed within existing resources, and State finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly applies to athletic event venues located on the campuses of University of Maryland, College Park (UMCP) and Bowie State University, which are both constituent member institutions of the University System of Maryland.

qa_results.bill_summary: Affirms the General Assembly's opinion that the federal Equal Rights Amendment meets Article V constitutional requirements. Urges the presidential administration to publish the Equal Rights Amendment without delay as the Twenty-eighth Amendment. Urges Congress to pass a joint resolution affirming the amendment. Calls on other state legislatures to adopt similar resolutions. Directs the Department of Legislative Services to forward copies to specified federal officials and state legislative leaders.
qa_results.responsible_party: Department of Legislative Services
qa_results.stakeholders: individuals protected by legal prohibitions against sex-based discrimination, the President of the United States, the United States Congress, the Archivist of the United States, and state legislatures
qa_results.fiscal_impact_summary: The joint resolution does not directly affect State or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The resolution specifically references legal action taken by the Maryland Attorney General, who filed an amicus brief in federal court in 2022 supporting the certification and publication of the Equal Rights Amendment.
The Commission on Civil Rights enforces Maryland's anti-discrimination protections, which align with the subject matter and intent of the federal Equal Rights Amendment addressed in the resolution.
The Governor's Office coordinates state executive policy initiatives and intergovernmental relations with the federal government, which are urged to act by this joint resolution.
